chapters.title: Chapter 351
paragraphs: Waiting was nerve-racking, and time crawled by.
If I had been one of the countless twenty-somethings living in twenty-first-century Korea, I might have been half a wreck by now.
After all, I would have had to endure ten days in a gloomy underground prison without a smartphone or Wi-Fi.
But I had something those ordinary twenty-somethings didn’t.
Martial arts.
System Successfully completed Circulate Qi! Internal energy rises slightly!
“Phew.”
I slowly drew a deep breath and gathered the qi inside me.
While I’d been circulating my qi, Cheongpung—standing guard, my ass; he’d been snoring away beside me—blearily opened his eyes.
“Oh, are you finished?”
“Phewww.”
“Benefactor?”
“Phewwwww.”
“Benefactor, are you hurt?”
Why did this guy keep ruining my concentration?
He looked ready to keep asking until I answered, so I reluctantly replied.
“Don’t talk to me.”
“Why not?”
“I’ll lose qi.”
There was a reason gym rats constantly went on about losing muscle.
Finishing circulating my qi didn’t mean I could simply get up the instant it ended. I also needed time to gather my qi, savor the afterglow, and meditate.
“Oh, I’m sorry.”
“Come on. You know all this, don’t you?”
Cheongpung scratched the back of his head.
“I didn’t know there was anything like that...”
“Huh? Then what have you been doing all this time?”
“I just got up and went out to play when I finished.”
“From the very beginning?”
“Yes.”
“...Did Great Hero Mae Jonghak never teach you?”

“Grandpa said that no matter how much dust you gathered, all you’d have was a pile of dust. He said it was more important to spend that time doing whatever I wanted. Apparently, those experiences might eventually provide a clue to enlightenment.”
Was this some kind of YOLO cultivation method?
The more stories like this I heard, the more certain I became that Sword Saint Mae Jonghak was an eccentric.
No, wait.
That guy has more internal energy than I do.
I currently possessed just over a hundred years of internal energy.
That put me far above my peers; it was the kind of level someone could reach only if a prestigious great sect on the level of the Nine Sects and One Gang committed itself to supporting them.
And I had only managed it because I’d obtained the Blazing Flame Divine Pill and stumbled into various other fortuitous encounters while repeatedly surviving life-or-death situations in the Murim.
So how did Cheongpung have more internal energy than me?
“Elixirs! You ate Huashan’s elixirs!”
Cheongpung’s official sponsors were none other than the Sword Saint and Huashan. If he’d received their help, it wasn’t impossible.
But Cheongpung’s answer to my entirely reasonable suspicion was simple.
“No, I didn’t. Grandpa doesn’t like people coming to visit him.”
“Oh, right. Then how did you build up that much internal energy?”
Cheongpung thought for a moment before answering.
“It just sort of accumulated on its own.”
“Oh, and when I was little, I often had my sinews cleansed and my marrow washed. Hehe.”
What the hell? Why was he talking about cleansing the sinews and washing the marrow as if he were merely washing his face?
I stared blankly at Cheongpung as he smiled awkwardly.
This guy really was born a protagonist.
Natural talent and fortuitous encounters. Everything came so naturally to him that he took it all for granted.
The phrase I just did it, and it worked might as well have been invented for Cheongpung.
“What a rotten world.”
“Benefactor, what is?”
“Nothing. Just something.”
“Yes.”
My chest had already felt stifled lately. Now it felt as though someone had piled another hundred sweet potatoes on top of it.
I’d run into the so-called “wall” that Murim warriors often spoke of, and I had been thinking about asking Cheongpung for advice...
But there’s no point asking him.
I had just let out a quiet sigh when—
Grrrrrind.
“...Benefactor?”
A heavy scraping sound bored into my ears. Cheongpung stared past my shoulder, his eyes wide, and my heart sank before beginning to pound.
No way. No way.
It’s only been ten days.
I slowly turned my head. At the far end of the corridor, an iron door was slowly opening, filling my entire field of vision.
When two people finally emerged, I asked in a trembling voice,
“How... did it go?”
There was no answer.
But that was enough.
The Divine Physician and Mungyeong—the exhausted master and Disciple—were looking at me with radiant smiles.
Smiles bright enough to illuminate the dark underground prison.
“The treatment was a success. There were several difficult moments along the way, but we managed to overcome them safely and finish the treatment sooner than expected...”
The Divine Physician continued speaking, but his voice sounded as though it were coming from far away. Only his first words kept echoing in my ears.
The treatment was a success.
Yes, it had ended successfully. I’d heard the words I wanted to hear more than anything, and that was enough.
Old Master.
Without realizing it, I tightened my grip on Jeok Cheongang’s hand.
He still lay there with his eyes closed, perhaps not yet ready to regain consciousness. But I could feel it clearly.
His vitality has returned.

That wasn’t all. Jeok Cheongang’s appearance had changed considerably over the past ten days. His age spots had vanished, his wrinkled skin had grown taut, and flesh had returned to the body that had been wasting away by the day.
Compared to before, he looked a good ten years younger. No, perhaps twenty.
“Could it be...?”
My voice trailed off as I looked at the Divine Physician.
Noticing the question in my eyes, he smiled faintly.
“Unfortunately, it is not Bone Transformation. However, the medicinal ingredients used during the treatment and the energy of the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng greatly benefited Sir Jeok.”
“Oh, I see.”
Disappointment and joy washed over me at the same time.
It would have been wonderful if he had used this treatment as an opportunity to advance to an even higher realm, but perhaps I had expected too much for a moment.
“You seem disappointed.”
“Oh, no.”
Startled, I quickly waved my hands. These two had successfully completed the difficult treatment without a single complaint. It would have been rude to look disappointed.
“I was only...”
“Heh heh. I did not mean to blame you. How could I not understand Young Master Jin’s feelings for his Master? Is that not right?”
“Of course. You are absolutely right, Master.”
Mungyeong answered politely, then continued speaking to me.
“Sir Jeok will regain consciousness within three days at the latest. The treatment has only just ended, so his qi needs time to settle properly. You need not worry too much.”
“Three days at the latest.”
“Yes. Of course, even after he awakens, he must avoid exerting himself too heavily for a while. Sir Jeok is renowned throughout the Murim, so he should recover quickly.”
“I’m sure he will. He’s always been overflowing with energy. Then, does that mean everything really is...”
“Yes.”
Mungyeong smiled and nodded.
“The Yin and Yang have regained their balance, and no Formless Ultimate Poison remains. The treatment is over.”
“...Phew.”
I released the breath I’d been holding. All the strength drained from my body, leaving me with the strange sensation that I was floating.
How long had I waited to hear those words?
When my legs gave out and I slumped to the floor, the Divine Physician spoke with a mischievous expression.
“It seems this old quack was not very trustworthy to you, Young Master Jin.”
“N-no, it wasn’t that I didn’t trust you, Old Man Dong. It was just... You know how it is. Cheongpung knows what I mean, right?”
“I don’t!”
“...Never mind. My mistake for asking you.”
The Divine Physician laughed even louder.
He watched us fondly, as though enjoying his grandchildren’s antics, then patted me on the shoulder.
“Everything is fine now. This old man will remain here as a precaution, so put any worries you still have away for good.”
“What?”
The Divine Physician saw my expression and hurriedly waved his hands.
“There is no need to make that expression. I am only staying to watch the patient awaken after treatment.”
“Phew, you scared me. You should have led with that.”
I had thought there was something else left to worry about.
Mungyeong grinned at his flustered Master, then spoke.
“Sorry to interrupt, but I think I should leave now.”
His sudden announcement startled me.
“What? Already?”
“Yes. Venerable Myoryeong should have regained consciousness by now, so I would like to go check on her.”
“You must be tired. Stay and rest for a while.”
“No, it is fine. I hardly did anything anyway. If I still have energy to spare, then as the younger one—even if only by a year—I should be the one to go. Isn’t that right, Master?”
“You little rascal!”
“Hahaha.”
I was worried about him, but it seemed they had already settled the matter between themselves.
No sooner had he finished speaking than Mungyeong slung his travel pack over his shoulder. Watching him, I suddenly remembered something I had forgotten.
“Mungyeong.”
“Yes?”
“Thank you. Truly.”
Mungyeong gazed at me for a moment, and a smile touched his lips.
“That is the finest praise a medical apprentice could receive.”
“Family Head, the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi requests an audience.”
Ssssss.
At the voice from outside the door, the snow-white snake slipped back into Tang Sadok’s robes.
Tang Sadok frowned at the interruption to one of the few peaceful moments in his day.
“Jin Taekyung, you mean?”
“Yes.”
“For what reason?”
“He says the treatment is over. And...”
The guard continued, confusion evident in his voice.
“He said he would like to keep using the item he borrowed for a few more days.”
“The item he borrowed.”
“Yes. Those were his exact words. He also asked to remain in the underground prison for a few more days.”
It was an indirect way of referring to the Myriad-Poison Ring. Tang Sadok let out a short laugh and muttered,
“What a brazen brat...”
“Pardon?”
“I was not speaking to you. Pay it no mind. Tell Jin Taekyung I give him permission, and continue watching him.”
“Yes, Family Head.”
Tang Sadok listened to the guard’s footsteps fade away and tapped the table.
He was neither a Great Hero of Benevolence and Righteousness who helped others without seeking anything in return nor a chivalrous hero who could not tolerate injustice.
He had lent Jin Taekyung the clan’s sacred treasure as part of their bargain, but it was only natural that he would continue keeping a close watch on him.
I am the Family Head of the great Sichuan Tang Clan. I trust no one.
One shichen earlier, even the young medical apprentice attempting to leave the clan had been thoroughly searched and questioned.
They had only allowed him to leave because his identity was guaranteed. Had he been a Disciple of some ordinary lesser sect, he would not have been permitted to take a single step outside.
In any case, the Fire King’s successful treatment is good news. The Divine Physician truly lives up to his name.
Tang Sadok had already heard from his late father that Fire King Jeok Cheongang was an exceedingly eccentric old man.
He had also heard that Jeok Cheongang was so proud that he would repay any gratitude or grudge he incurred, no matter what it took.
You bastard... your days are numbered.
A green glint flashed through Tang Sadok’s eyes.

The murderer who had killed his father and the Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun was definitely said to be one-armed. That was not especially rare in the Murim, but it was not a feature one saw every day, either.
A maimed man stood out wherever he went.
Run. Run wherever you can. The Sichuan Murim will hunt you until the day you breathe your last.
Grind.
Tang Sadok was quietly grinding his teeth when—
“Uncle!”
With an urgent shout, the pavilion doors flew open. Tang Sadok’s face twisted at the same instant.
It wasn’t the Master of the Gatekeeper Pavilion’s unannounced intrusion that disturbed him, but the martial artist standing beside the man.
His green martial uniform was torn and covered in blood, and the words Tang Family were embroidered across it.
There was no mistaking it.
He was a member of the Green Shadow Squad.
A member of the Green Shadow Squad who should never have appeared here in such a state.
Facing the rigid Tang Sadok, the Green Shadow Squad martial artist cried out, blood choking his voice.
“They—they’re coming!”

chapters.title: Chapter 352
paragraphs: They’re coming.
The Green Shadow Squad martial artist had blurted out a disjointed sentence.

But insight struck Tang Sadok like a flash of lightning. It gave form to the small unease he had harbored in his heart, and it was the conclusion drawn from all the experience he had accumulated over the years.
The murderer isn’t alone!
The one-armed man who had killed his father and the Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun was coming to the Sichuan Tang Clan with his subordinates.
Who the true mastermind was, how many men they had, and how they had managed to move through Sichuan as freely as their own backyard—none of that mattered now.
The next moment, Tang Sadok’s voice erupted like a thunderbolt.
“One Origin, Three Divisions, and Five Squads—prepare to meet the enemy!”
Rumble!
The pavilion trembled beneath the enormous shout, laden with powerful internal energy.
The disturbance had occurred in none other than the Family Head’s Hall. The first to react were Tang Sadok’s guards surrounding the pavilion.
“Family Head!”
Bang!
By the time the guards burst inside, smashing through the pavilion, the clan members who had heard Tang Sadok’s shout were already spreading his orders throughout the family compound.
Within fifteen minutes, hundreds of Tang Family members, united by venomous resolve and resentment, would assemble.
And then...
I’ll show you what the Tang Family’s revenge looks like.
Despite the fury boiling in his chest, Tang Sadok’s eyes had grown as cold as the northern wind and bitter snow.
“Family Head, what in the world is—”
“The men who deserve to die are coming. That is all.”
He waved away the bewildered guards and fixed his gaze on the Green Shadow Squad martial artist.
The man’s uniform was torn and soaked in blood, unmistakable evidence of battle.
“What happened? Tell me everything you saw and heard. Leave nothing out.”
The Green Shadow Squad martial artist finally caught his breath and began his report in an exhausted voice.
“It began when we discovered a suspicious group while searching near the Golden Hall.”
“A suspicious group?”
“Yes.”
“The Golden Hall is barely half a day from our family. The Beggars’ Sect and the government troops have already completed every inspection and search in the area. How could...”
Tang Sadok trailed off, his gaze turning grim.
“...The government troops. It was the government troops.”
The Green Shadow Squad martial artist stared wide-eyed at the Family Head, then nodded.
“Y-yes! They were definitely wearing government uniforms.”
“A disguise.”
Tap. Tap.
Tang Sadok drummed his bony fingers against the table.
They had been caught completely off guard.
The Beggars’ Sect and the government troops had confirmed Chengdu’s safety several times, and it had been only two days since they expanded their search area.
The enemy had slipped into Chengdu through the gap left when the net loosened.
It wouldn’t have been difficult.
The elite were always deployed to the front lines. The most experienced and sharp-eyed members of the Beggars’ Sect and government troops had already left Chengdu.
Besides, wasn’t this after several thousand government troops had spent nearly ten days roaming around Chengdu? Anyone wearing their uniforms could have blended in naturally.
“How many were there?”
“Perhaps to avoid suspicion, they were moving in several groups. But from what we were able to determine, there seemed to be at least three hundred of them.”
“Three hundred?”
“Yes. I’m certain.”
The Master of the Gatekeeper Pavilion had been listening to the report with an anxious expression. Now he spoke in a triumphant tone.
“Ha! Only three hundred? They must have a death wish. Isn’t that right, Uncle?”

“Our family alone has more than three hundred martial artists ready to fight at a moment’s notice. And that isn’t all. Isn’t this exactly why we built an impregnable fortress? They won’t even make it over the walls before our poison and hidden weapons kill them.”
Tang Sadok finally opened his mouth.
“Shut up.”
“Pardon?”
“I said shut up.”
“U-Uncle, why are you acting like this? It’s only three hundred. We could wipe out that many in the blink of an eye...”
“Only three hundred?”
The fingers drumming against the table stopped dead.
Tang Sadok stared at his only nephew with utter contempt.
“You haven’t forgotten the Gyeongwol Year Bloodbath, have you?”
“...How could I?”
The Gyeongwol Year Bloodbath was practically taboo within the Tang Clan.
Fifty years ago, the Sichuan Tang Clan had been forced to abandon the land it had occupied for centuries and flee in disgrace.
That day, Tang Sadok had lost his only older brother, and the Master of the Gatekeeper Pavilion had lost his father before he was even born.
“But things are different now!”
Tang Sadok answered his nephew’s impassioned shout in a cold voice.
“Yes. Exactly what is different?”
“The Demonic Cult’s forces numbered two thousand, while our family had only three hundred martial artists!”
“You’re more or less correct so far. Go on.”
“Although we were defeated and forced to retreat, our family suffered barely more than a hundred casualties, while the Demonic Cult lost over a third of its forces.”
“That is also true. Those losses delayed the Demonic Cult’s conquest of Sichuan. Our family lost its home, but gained even greater fame in exchange.”
“Then why?”
Bang!
The Master of the Gatekeeper Pavilion slammed his fist down, denting the iron table. He glared at his uncle with blazing eyes.
“Why are you afraid of a mere three hundred enemies? Fifty years ago, even the Demonic Cult’s vicious fiends—several times more numerous than this—had to shed untold blood to overcome our family!”
His ringing shout shook the air inside the pavilion.
Tang Sadok’s answer to his furious nephew was short and simple.
“So? Is that all?”
“...What?”
“You pathetic fool.”
Tang Sadok sighed as his nephew’s eyes wavered.
“The Gyeongwol Year Bloodbath is a humiliating chapter of our history that must never be forgotten. But it is also the day our family proved its strength to the entire world.”
“Y-yes. That is why martial artists throughout the world still praise our family’s martial might and righteous spirit.”
“Ha... Hahahaha!”
Ignorance this profound was practically a disease. Tang Sadok let out a hollow laugh as he looked at his nephew, who still failed to understand.
“Yes. The entire world knows. Do you think our enemies don’t?”

“After the Great Faction War, our family built an impregnable fortress that no one could breach. We increased our numbers and armed our clan members thoroughly. Is there anyone under heaven who doesn’t know that? Is there anyone who doesn’t know the strength and determination our family displayed during the Gyeongwol Year Bloodbath?”

Only now did he understand that the three hundred enemies invading the Sichuan Tang Clan were not men anyone could dismiss as only three hundred.
By contrast, the old and experienced Family Head’s judgment was swift and decisive.
“Sound the Tang War Drum.”
A stir passed through the guards, who had been frozen like stone at the Family Head’s command.
“Y-you mean the Tang War Drum?”

“Distribute poison and hidden weapons to everyone, regardless of age or sex. Retired elders, craftsmen who have never learned martial arts, women—no one is exempt. Our family will commit its full strength to this battle.”
“A-as you command!”
The blade-sharp order wiped the color from the guards’ faces. They hurried into motion.
A short while later, when the Tang War Drum’s thunder rolled throughout the Sichuan Tang Clan, everyone would know.
Their family stood on the brink of destruction.
And no one felt that danger more keenly than Tang Sadok.
This is dangerous.
The experience and instincts he had honed over years of leading the family whispered a warning.
A sea of corpses and blood surpassing even the Gyeongwol Year Bloodbath might be waiting for the Sichuan Tang Clan.
Then came the sound that announced the beginning of everything.
Boom. Boom. Boom!
The majestic sound alone was enough to set hearts pounding. The Master of the Gatekeeper Pavilion murmured,
“So this is the Tang Clan drum...”
The Tang Clan drum had not sounded since before he was born. He was still struggling to contain his emotions upon hearing it for the first time when Tang Sadok spoke.
“They beat us to it.”
“U-Uncle?”
The Master of the Gatekeeper Pavilion spun toward him and saw the fathomless depths of Tang Sadok’s eyes.
At the same time, several gray-flecked figures entered the pavilion with swift movement techniques.
“Family Head!”
“It’s the enemy! They’re coming while beating a war drum!”
“They launch an attack while sounding their own war drum. Impressive bastards. Truly impressive.”
Tang Sadok burst into laughter.
The ten people staring at him looked dumbfounded.
“This is no time to laugh!”
“Family Head, please give us your orders!”
They varied widely in appearance. One was a young man who seemed to be in his thirties, another was a graying middle-aged man, and there was even an old man around Tang Sadok’s age.
Whatever their ages, each had proven their martial prowess among the clan’s hundreds of members.
That was why Tang Sadok had given them another name.
“The Tang Clan’s Ten Wonders. Perfect timing. I was waiting for you.”
“Family Head, what in the world is happening? We should attack them at once—”
“You can ask that fellow over there for the details.”
The gazes of the Tang Clan’s Ten Wonders followed Tang Sadok’s.
Finding himself under the scrutiny of so many powerful figures, the Green Shadow Squad martial artist swallowed hard.
“I-I’ll tell you anything I know!”
“That is good to hear. Then let this old man ask you...”
Tang Sadok continued in a gentle voice.
“Weren’t you one-armed?”
At that moment, time seemed to stop.
The majestic thunder of the Tang War Drum, which had finally begun to sound. The frantic movements and shouts of the clan members.
Unlike the time outside, which continued to flow unchanged, everything inside the pavilion had come to a complete halt.
Amid the silence and shock, only one person moved backward through time.
Crack. Crrrck.
Bones lengthened and contracted. Muscles swelled.
The blood-soaked uniform tore apart, splitting the two characters embroidered across its chest—Tang Family—in half.
The Green Shadow Squad martial artist slowly rose to his feet.
He was no longer a young man in his twenties.
Nor was he a member of the Green Shadow Squad.
“You have a sharp eye. The Poison King raised his son well.”
The middle-aged man smiled faintly and rubbed his left arm. The color of his skin differed subtly around the elbow, as if the arm had been removed and attached again.

A green light flickered in Tang Sadok’s eyes as he stared at the middle-aged man.
“So it was you. You were the one who harmed my father.”
“Poison King Tang Taesang truly lived up to his reputation. I was honestly impressed. That was when I lost my arm, too.”
The middle-aged man clenched and unclenched his left fist, making a show of frowning.

“Do not worry. This old man will personally cut off your head so you never have to concern yourself with it again.”

Yet even in the face of deadly poison capable of killing a person with a single breath, the middle-aged man—the Western Heaven Demon Lord—smiled calmly.
“If you can, by all means.”
Roar!

The elite were always deployed to the front lines.
The most experienced and sharp-eyed members of the Beggars’ Sect and government troops had already left Chengdu.
Besides, wasn’t this after several thousand government troops had spent nearly ten days roaming around Chengdu?
Anyone wearing their uniforms could have blended in naturally.
“How many were there?”
“Perhaps to avoid suspicion, they were moving in several groups.

“Three hundred?”
“Yes.
I’m certain.”
The Master of the Gatekeeper Pavilion had been listening to the report with an anxious expression.

Only three hundred?
They must have a death wish.

Tang Sadok finally opened his mouth.
“Shut up.”

chapters.title: Chapter 353
paragraphs: Boom. Boom. Boom!
Listening to the thunderous drumbeats, an old man muttered,
“It’s been a while since I heard that.”
He was short and stocky, with coarse, unruly features. To ordinary eyes, he was nothing more than an ugly, ill-tempered old man.
But anyone who had faced him even once called him by another name.
Fiend.

The old man curled the corners of his mouth upward. Seeing the wet-behind-the-ears pups waiting for him atop the walls surrounding the Sichuan Tang Clan like an impregnable fortress, roughly three hundred yards ahead, put him in an excellent mood.
“I can almost smell the blood already. This is how I felt when we first came down from the Qilian Mountains.”
He had come into the world after a difficult birth, cursed with ugly features.

How could his two brothers, born from the same womb on the same day, have been any different? When even their father disappeared, the three brothers had nowhere left to turn. Fleeing the contempt of others, they hid in the Qilian Mountains.
“We were so young back then. Bastard or bitch, we killed them all, then killed some more...”
They had been born into an age of chaos, and so they became fiends.
By the time they finally looked around, everyone who had despised their ugliness and pelted them with stones lay submerged in pools of blood.
Then they joined the Demonic Cult’s invasion of the Central Plains and stained the world red. People came to know and fear them as the Qilian Three Fiends.
“Remembering our prime is exhilarating. Don’t you think?”
The old man, the First Fiend, turned his head with a smile, only to click his tongue when he realized his mistake.
“Good grief. Maybe it’s because I’m getting old, but I keep forgetting things.”
The two younger brothers who had followed him like shadows their entire lives were not here.
The Second Fiend had left to take charge of Qingcheng, while the Third Fiend had gone to take charge of Emei.
Before long, the two famous mountains counted among the greatest in the world would be covered in a sea of corpses and blood.
And then...
Kwahhhhhng!
At last, the signal announcing the beginning of everything rang out.
The First Fiend let out a hearty laugh at the thunderous boom coming from beyond the walls of the Sichuan Tang Clan. The time promised by the Western Heaven Demon Lord had arrived.
“The Demon Lord is calling us. Don’t you agree?”
Shing-shing-shing!
Hundreds of weapons were drawn, slicing through the dawn air.
Behind the First Fiend stood three hundred black-clad men in a long formation. They had already discarded their government-troop uniforms and donned black leather armor.
“The time has come. Raise the flag!”
The instant the First Fiend’s shout rang out, the Tang Clan martial artists atop the walls saw it.
Flap.
A flag rose high beyond the pale dawn mist.
Two characters billowed in the fierce wind.
“Dark Heaven...?”
Someone on the wall muttered the words, but the booming drums swallowed them.
Boom. Boom. Boom!
The drumbeats grew stronger, and the black-clad men began to advance in time with them.
Hot breath spilled from between their lips, but their eyes were cold. Razor-sharp killing intent rolled off their bodies.
And at their head stood a single fiend.
“By command of the Lord of Heaven...”
His blood-red eyes shone with joy.
What a magnificent day this was. The orthodox Murim would remember it. Everyone would gaze upon Dark Heaven’s flag hanging over the world and tremble with fear.
Quivering with elation, the First Fiend shouted,
“Destroy the Sichuan Tang Clan!”
“As you command!”
Boom. Boom-boom. Boom-boom-boom-boom-boom!

The drums quickened amid fierce battle cries. Three hundred black-clad men charged toward the walls, while dark clouds rolled across the sky and smothered the sunlight that had only just begun to shine.
That was when a powerful shout erupted from atop the walls.
“These villains dare invade our family! Don’t leave a single one alive!”
“Everyone, fire!”
Shhhhhhhk! Thud!
An arrowhead shot with tremendous force pierced someone’s body and buried itself in the ground. Blood mist bloomed, followed by a scream.
“Gaaaaah!”
But there were very few casualties. Most of the black-clad men deflected the arrows with their weapons, while others emerged unharmed thanks to their armor.
“Wh-what?”
“Even the crossbows can’t pierce it? What kind of armor is that...?”
Even crossbow bolts capable of punching through thick iron plates proved useless against the armor.
As the Tang Clan martial artists faltered, a small figure streaked forward at dazzling speed.
Fwoooosh!
“Ha-ha-ha-ha! Excellent! Excellent!”
No one atop the walls knew the First Fiend’s identity. But everyone who heard his crazed laughter felt their hair stand on end.
“The Myriad-Poison Formation! Activate the Myriad-Poison Formation!”
The panicked order rang out, but the First Fiend had already vanished like a ghost and reached the gate.
His face twisting into a fiendish grin, he threw a single punch. Two jiazi of internal energy spiraled into his fist like a whirlwind.
“Let’s see how Tang Family blood tastes.”
Whoom—Kwahhhhhng!
The battle had begun.
“Hm?”
“What?”
Cheongpung and I looked at each other at the same time. Then, at the same time, we realized we were thinking the same thing.
“Did you hear that?”
“Benefactor, did you hear it?”
The Divine Physician, who was checking the still-unconscious Jeok Cheongang’s pulse, looked at us in confusion.
“What are you talking about?”
“Just a moment.”
I raised a hand to stop the Divine Physician from continuing and quietly focused my mind.

My body might have been in the underground prison, but my senses were another matter. Amplified several times over by the power of my internal energy, my hearing escaped the labyrinthine prison corridors and rose upward, higher and higher.
And then...
Boom.
This time, I heard it clearly.
Cheongpung set down the food he had been holding and spoke.
“Benefactor, could this be...”
“That’s right.”
I looked up at the ceiling of the prison and continued,
“It’s a drum.”
Boom. Boom. Boom.
As though agreeing with me, the drums sounded again at that exact moment.
Ting.
System An unexpected Quest has been generated. - You cannot refuse. The Quest has been automatically accepted! - Would you like to view the Quest information?
I stared wordlessly at the holographic window filling my vision.
The sudden drumbeats and an unexpected Quest. Neither could possibly be a good sign.
Shit, I’ve already got goose bumps all over my arms.
“This is driving me crazy.”
But there was no turning back now. The only thing I could do was find out what kind of path lay ahead of me.
View Quest information.
Ting.
A new holographic window appeared with the System’s characteristically cheerful notification sound.
Unlike the notification, of course, the contents of the Quest window were anything but cheerful.

System Quest Uninvited Guest Dark Heaven’s dark clouds have finally spread across Sichuan. The battle has already begun, and the Sichuan Tang Clan is surrounded. May fortune favor you in battle. Grade: ??? Limit: ??? Mission: ??? Reward: ??? Failure: Death
I read it exactly three times from beginning to end. Then I thought,
What kind of fucked-up situation is this?
I was so dumbfounded that I could barely speak.
The whole thing was absurd. Enemies had invaded. We were surrounded and couldn’t escape. It wished us luck. The end.
Goddamn, it’s disgustingly simple.
Grade, limit, mission, reward. Every last one was a question mark.
Well, at least it had made one thing perfectly clear.
If I failed this Quest, I would die.
What a revelation. If we couldn’t stop the enemies who had invaded, I would die. Such wonderfully useful information almost made me slap my balls in amazement.
Is this a Quest information window or just a Quest notification window?
Boom. Boom. Boom.
My vision swam. As the drumbeats grew louder and fiercer, cold sweat gathered on my back.
My mind, on the other hand, had gone cold as ice.
I dismissed the Quest window, took a deep breath, and spoke.
“Old Man Dong, we have a problem.”
The Divine Physician had learned martial arts, but his realm was far below ours.
Unlike Cheongpung and me, he had not heard the drumbeats. He asked with a puzzled expression,
“A problem? What do you mean?”
“Enemies have invaded.”
“Enemies? Here, at the Sichuan Tang Clan?”
“Yes. There’s no doubt. We’re already surrounded.”
The Divine Physician looked as if he could hardly believe it. That was a perfectly normal reaction. What kind of lunatics would attack the Sichuan Tang Clan?
But if those lunatics were Dark Heaven, that changed everything. They were the very people responsible for staining Shaolin Temple with blood.
Still, every second mattered. There was no time for a detailed explanation.
“We don’t know what’s going to happen, so steel yourself.”
“...I understand.”
The Divine Physician nodded grimly.
Perhaps because he had traveled throughout the world and experienced countless things, he seemed to accept reality more quickly than expected.
I looked at Jeok Cheongang, who still lay there with his eyes closed.
“How is my Master’s condition?”
“As I told you before, his qi has not yet stabilized. If he suffers an external shock in this condition...”
The Divine Physician did not finish, but I had heard enough.
Jeok Cheongang’s condition was still unstable. According to the Quest window, Dark Heaven had already surrounded the Sichuan Tang Clan.
What if we broke through their encirclement and escaped?
The thought flashed through my mind, but I quickly shook my head.

Jeok Cheongang’s safety was one concern, but our chances of success were slim to begin with. Considering the forces Dark Heaven had deployed against Shaolin Temple, trying to escape might only lead us straight into a deathtrap.
Especially if a monster like the Blood Lord is out there. We have to avoid that at all costs.
After thinking it through, I arrived at a single answer.
I slowly opened my mouth.
“Cheongpung.”
Cheongpung answered in a subdued voice.
“Yes, Benefactor.”
“Can I ask you for one favor?”
“Anything.”
Cheongpung was endlessly innocent and carefree, but every once in a while, he showed a serious side.
And whenever he did, I found him more dependable than anyone else.
That was why I could make this request of him.
“Stay here and protect Old Master—protect my Master. That’s my request.”
“As you heard, we can’t get out right now. Someone has to leave and help the Sichuan Tang Clan.”
“Benefactor.”
“Benefactor.”
I swallowed the words I had been about to say. Cheongpung was looking at me with clear eyes.
“I’ll stay if you tell me to stay, and I’ll go if you tell me to go. But, Benefactor...”
His quiet voice reached my ears.
“You have someone you need to protect, don’t you?”
“When there was someone I had to protect, I was too scared to fight. I couldn’t protect the people I cared about. That’s why I’m such a fool.”
I hadn’t known.
I hadn’t known Cheongpung carried such thoughts.
Even afterward, he had remained cheerful and talkative, living as though he were the happiest person in the world.
That was how he had always been. It suited him. It was only natural for him.
But it wasn’t.
As if recalling what had happened in Henan, Cheongpung turned his gaze toward some distant, dark corner of the underground prison.
Then he turned back to me.
A smile appeared on his lips. The same as always, yet somehow different.
Only then did I understand.
The time had come to make a real decision.
One person stays. One person leaves.
I slowly shifted my gaze.
Cheongpung, still smiling.
The Divine Physician, his face filled with concern.
Someone’s screams and shouts, drawing closer by the moment.
And then...
Jeok Cheongang’s face beneath the shadows of the flickering torchlight.
The next moment, my lips moved before I knew it.
“Cheongpung. I have a favor to ask.”
Cheongpung’s gaze met mine.
I pointed toward the ceiling and flashed him a grin.
“Go land one on those sons of bitches and come back.”
“Yes, Benefactor!”
His answer was brighter than ever.

Seeing the wet-behind-the-ears pups waiting for him atop the walls surrounding the Sichuan Tang Clan like an impregnable fortress, roughly three hundred yards ahead, put him in an excellent mood.
“I can almost smell the blood already.
This is how I felt when we first came down from the Qilian Mountains.”
He had come into the world after a difficult birth, cursed with ugly features.
How could his two brothers, born from the same womb on the same day, have been any different?
When even their father disappeared, the three brothers had nowhere left to turn.
Fleeing the contempt of others, they hid in the Qilian Mountains.
“We were so young back then.
Bastard or bitch, we killed them all, then killed some more...”
They had been born into an age of chaos, and so they became fiends.
By the time they finally looked around, everyone who had despised their ugliness and pelted them with stones lay submerged in pools of blood.
Then they joined the Demonic Cult’s invasion of the Central Plains and stained the world red.
People came to know and fear them as the Qilian Three Fiends.
“Remembering our prime is exhilarating.
Don’t you think?”
The old man, the First Fiend, turned his head with a smile, only to click his tongue when he realized his mistake.
“Good grief.
Maybe it’s because I’m getting old, but I keep forgetting things.”
The two younger brothers who had followed him like shadows their entire lives were not here.
The Second Fiend had left to take charge of Qingcheng, while the Third Fiend had gone to take charge of Emei.
Before long, the two famous mountains counted among the greatest in the world would be covered in a sea of corpses and blood.
And then...
Kwahhhhhng!
At last, the signal announcing the beginning of everything rang out.
The First Fiend let out a hearty laugh at the thunderous boom coming from beyond the walls of the Sichuan Tang Clan.
The time promised by the Western Heaven Demon Lord had arrived.
“The Demon Lord is calling us.
Don’t you agree?”
Shing-shing-shing!
Hundreds of weapons were drawn, slicing through the dawn air.
Behind the First Fiend stood three hundred black-clad men in a long formation.
They had already discarded their government-troop uniforms and donned black leather armor.
“The time has come.
Raise the flag!”
The instant the First Fiend’s shout rang out, the Tang Clan martial artists atop the walls saw it.
Flap.
A flag rose high beyond the pale dawn mist.
Two characters billowed in the fierce wind.
“Dark Heaven...?”
Someone on the wall muttered the words, but the booming drums swallowed them.
Boom.
Boom.
Boom!
The drumbeats grew stronger, and the black-clad men began to advance in time with them.
Hot breath spilled from between their lips, but their eyes were cold.
Razor-sharp killing intent rolled off their bodies.
And at their head stood a single fiend.
“By command of the Lord of Heaven...”
His blood-red eyes shone with joy.
What a magnificent day this was.
The orthodox Murim would remember it.
Everyone would gaze upon Dark Heaven’s flag hanging over the world and tremble with fear.
Quivering with elation, the First Fiend shouted,
“Destroy the Sichuan Tang Clan!”
“As you command!”
Boom.
Boom-boom.
Boom-boom-boom-boom-boom!
The drums quickened amid fierce battle cries.
Three hundred black-clad men charged toward the walls, while dark clouds rolled across the sky and smothered the sunlight that had only just begun to shine.
That was when a powerful shout erupted from atop the walls.
“These villains dare invade our family!
Don’t leave a single one alive!”
“Everyone, fire!”
Shhhhhhhk!
Thud!
An arrowhead shot with tremendous force pierced someone’s body and buried itself in the ground.
Blood mist bloomed, followed by a scream.
“Gaaaaah!”
But there were very few casualties.
Most of the black-clad men deflected the arrows with their weapons, while others emerged unharmed thanks to their armor.
“Wh-what?”
“Even the crossbows can’t pierce it?
What kind of armor is that...?”
Even crossbow bolts capable of punching through thick iron plates proved useless against the armor.
As the Tang Clan martial artists faltered, a small figure streaked forward at dazzling speed.
Fwoooosh!
“Ha-ha-ha-ha!
Excellent!
Excellent!”
No one atop the walls knew the First Fiend’s identity.
But everyone who heard his crazed laughter felt their hair stand on end.
“The Myriad-Poison Formation!
Activate the Myriad-Poison Formation!”
The panicked order rang out, but the First Fiend had already vanished like a ghost and reached the gate.
His face twisting into a fiendish grin, he threw a single punch.
Two jiazi of internal energy spiraled into his fist like a whirlwind.
“Let’s see how Tang Family blood tastes.”
Whoom—Kwahhhhhng!
The battle had begun.
“Hm?”
“What?”
Cheongpung and I looked at each other at the same time.
Then, at the same time, we realized we were thinking the same thing.
“Did you hear that?”
“Benefactor, did you hear it?”
The Divine Physician, who was checking the still-unconscious Jeok Cheongang’s pulse, looked at us in confusion.
“What are you talking about?”
“Just a moment.”
I raised a hand to stop the Divine Physician from continuing and quietly focused my mind.
My body might have been in the underground prison, but my senses were another matter.
Amplified several times over by the power of my internal energy, my hearing escaped the labyrinthine prison corridors and rose upward, higher and higher.
And then...
Boom.
This time, I heard it clearly.
Cheongpung set down the food he had been holding and spoke.
“Benefactor, could this be...”
“That’s right.”
I looked up at the ceiling of the prison and continued,
“It’s a drum.”
Boom.
Boom.
Boom.
As though agreeing with me, the drums sounded again at that exact moment.
Ting.
System An unexpected Quest has been generated. - You cannot refuse.
The Quest has been automatically accepted! - Would you like to view the Quest information?
I stared wordlessly at the holographic window filling my vision.
The sudden drumbeats and an unexpected Quest.
Neither could possibly be a good sign.
Shit, I’ve already got goose bumps all over my arms.
“This is driving me crazy.”
But there was no turning back now.
The only thing I could do was find out what kind of path lay ahead of me.
View Quest information.
Ting.
A new holographic window appeared with the System’s characteristically cheerful notification sound.
Unlike the notification, of course, the contents of the Quest window were anything but cheerful.
System Quest Uninvited Guest Dark Heaven’s dark clouds have finally spread across Sichuan.
The battle has already begun, and the Sichuan Tang Clan is surrounded.
May fortune favor you in battle.
Grade: ???
Limit: ???
Mission: ???
Reward: ???
Failure: Death
I read it exactly three times from beginning to end.
Then I thought,
What kind of fucked-up situation is this?
I was so dumbfounded that I could barely speak.
The whole thing was absurd.
Enemies had invaded.
We were surrounded and couldn’t escape.
It wished us luck.
The end.
Goddamn, it’s disgustingly simple.
Grade, limit, mission, reward.
Every last one was a question mark.
Well, at least it had made one thing perfectly clear.
If I failed this Quest, I would die.
What a revelation.
If we couldn’t stop the enemies who had invaded, I would die.
Such wonderfully useful information almost made me slap my balls in amazement.
Is this a Quest information window or just a Quest notification window?
Boom.
Boom.
Boom.
My vision swam.
As the drumbeats grew louder and fiercer, cold sweat gathered on my back.
My mind, on the other hand, had gone cold as ice.
I dismissed the Quest window, took a deep breath, and spoke.
“Old Man Dong, we have a problem.”
The Divine Physician had learned martial arts, but his realm was far below ours.
Unlike Cheongpung and me, he had not heard the drumbeats.
He asked with a puzzled expression,
“A problem?
What do you mean?”
“Enemies have invaded.”
“Enemies?
Here, at the Sichuan Tang Clan?”
“Yes.
There’s no doubt.
We’re already surrounded.”
The Divine Physician looked as if he could hardly believe it.
That was a perfectly normal reaction.
What kind of lunatics would attack the Sichuan Tang Clan?
But if those lunatics were Dark Heaven, that changed everything.
They were the very people responsible for staining Shaolin Temple with blood.
Still, every second mattered.
There was no time for a detailed explanation.
“We don’t know what’s going to happen, so steel yourself.”
“...I understand.”
The Divine Physician nodded grimly.
Perhaps because he had traveled throughout the world and experienced countless things, he seemed to accept reality more quickly than expected.
I looked at Jeok Cheongang, who still lay there with his eyes closed.
“How is my Master’s condition?”
“As I told you before, his qi has not yet stabilized.
If he suffers an external shock in this condition...”
The Divine Physician did not finish, but I had heard enough.
Jeok Cheongang’s condition was still unstable.
According to the Quest window, Dark Heaven had already surrounded the Sichuan Tang Clan.
What if we broke through their encirclement and escaped?
The thought flashed through my mind, but I quickly shook my head.
Jeok Cheongang’s safety was one concern, but our chances of success were slim to begin with.
Considering the forces Dark Heaven had deployed against Shaolin Temple, trying to escape might only lead us straight into a deathtrap.
Especially if a monster like the Blood Lord is out there.
We have to avoid that at all costs.
After thinking it through, I arrived at a single answer.
I slowly opened my mouth.
“Cheongpung.”
Cheongpung answered in a subdued voice.
“Yes, Benefactor.”
“Can I ask you for one favor?”
“Anything.”
Cheongpung was endlessly innocent and carefree, but every once in a while, he showed a serious side.
And whenever he did, I found him more dependable than anyone else.
That was why I could make this request of him.
“Stay here and protect Old Master—protect my Master.
That’s my request.”
“As you heard, we can’t get out right now.
Someone has to leave and help the Sichuan Tang Clan.”
“Benefactor.”
“Benefactor.”
I swallowed the words I had been about to say.
Cheongpung was looking at me with clear eyes.
“I’ll stay if you tell me to stay, and I’ll go if you tell me to go.
But, Benefactor...”
His quiet voice reached my ears.
“You have someone you need to protect, don’t you?”
“When there was someone I had to protect, I was too scared to fight.
I couldn’t protect the people I cared about.
That’s why I’m such a fool.”
I hadn’t known.
I hadn’t known Cheongpung carried such thoughts.
Even afterward, he had remained cheerful and talkative, living as though he were the happiest person in the world.
That was how he had always been.
It suited him.
It was only natural for him.
But it wasn’t.
As if recalling what had happened in Henan, Cheongpung turned his gaze toward some distant, dark corner of the underground prison.
Then he turned back to me.
A smile appeared on his lips.
The same as always, yet somehow different.
Only then did I understand.
The time had come to make a real decision.
One person stays.
One person leaves.
I slowly shifted my gaze.
Cheongpung, still smiling.
The Divine Physician, his face filled with concern.
Someone’s screams and shouts, drawing closer by the moment.
And then...
Jeok Cheongang’s face beneath the shadows of the flickering torchlight.
The next moment, my lips moved before I knew it.
“Cheongpung.
I have a favor to ask.”
Cheongpung’s gaze met mine.
I pointed toward the ceiling and flashed him a grin.
“Go land one on those sons of bitches and come back.”
“Yes, Benefactor!”
His answer was brighter than ever.

chapters.title: Chapter 354
paragraphs: Clang! Krrr-kang!
“They’re vile bastards we could chew to pieces and still not be satisfied! Show no mercy!”
“The Lord of Heaven wills it! Destroy the Tang Clan!”
Sword clashed against sword. Ragged breathing mingled with hoarse cries. The killing intent and stench of blood from hundreds of people locked in battle flooded the air.
Amid the dawn mist, blackened by poison smoke, those intent on killing raised their weapons and charged at one another.
Pfft!
“Gaaah!”
A young man screamed.

Born into a collateral branch of the great Sichuan Tang Clan, he had reached the First Rate realm without much difficulty. His considerable martial talent and composure beyond his years had earned him high expectations from everyone around him.
But now, the young man’s bright future was extinguished by a flash of black Sword Energy.
Fwoooosh! Slash!
The Sword Energy carved diagonally through his upper body.
That was the end.
The black-clad man stared at the young man’s collapsing body, his face pale as blood and entrails spilled out.
The kid was vicious.
The fight had been decided in only three exchanges.
Yet the unknown Tang Clan martial artist had staked his life on leaving them both grievously wounded.
The ox-hair needle that had somehow burrowed beneath the black-clad man’s collarbone was proof.
So this is the Sichuan Tang Clan.
Clicking his tongue, the black-clad man pulled out the needle.
It was so fine that he had to look closely to make it out, and its tip had turned black. There was no question that it had been coated in poison.
“Ghk!”
His vision blurred for an instant. The poison that had entered near his collarbone was rapidly spreading throughout his body.
At this rate, even his Peak-level internal energy could do no more than buy him time.
On a chaotic battlefield like this, being struck by one of the Sichuan Tang Clan’s deadliest poisons meant he was as good as dead.
But the black-clad man did not panic.
No—he smiled.
“The Lord of Heaven is... great.”
The muffled words slipped between his clenched teeth.
When he opened his mouth for the first time, a small bead lay inside.
An eerie light flowed from the bead and streamed down his throat like a river.
Ssssss.
The change was instantaneous. His blurred vision cleared, and strength and vitality returned to his weakening body.
As every trace of poison vanished from his body, the black-clad man shuddered.
The Lord of Heaven, nobler and greater than any other.
The life force bestowed upon him by his god filled his entire body.
“The Lord of Heaven has descended upon me!”
With a cry of ecstasy, the black-clad man turned in search of another victim.
That was when—
“Wrong. The one descending upon you bastards is Yama.”
Crack!
A throwing blade flew from somewhere and buried itself between his eyebrows.
The internal energy carried by the blade tore through flesh and bone, reducing his brain to pulp. He died instantly.
Thud. Crash!
The bead that rolled from the dead man’s mouth was drawn into someone’s hand.
An old man studied it with wizened gray eyes and muttered, “These bastards... They’re carrying artifacts.”
An ordinary martial artist would have assumed the bead was a poison-warding pearl.

But the old man, Tang Jinhu, was a direct descendant of the Sichuan Tang Clan and a veteran of the Great Faction War. He instinctively realized that this bead was something different from a poison-warding pearl.
What is this?
Poison-warding pearls were normally clear. The more transparent they were, the more effective they were at neutralizing poison—and the more valuable they became.
But the bead the black-clad man had possessed shone with an ominous black light, as though it held storm clouds within it.
Even so, it had been powerful enough to neutralize one of the Tang Clan’s deadliest poisons.
The greater problem was...
Every last one of them has an artifact of this quality. At this rate, neither our family’s poison techniques nor the poison formations we prepared in advance will be of any use.
On top of that, they wore leather armor that ordinary swords and blades could not pierce.
Tang Jinhu finally understood why the Tang Clan drum had sounded.
At this rate, the bloodbath would be even more horrific than the one in the Gyeongwol Year.
“These bastards...”
Crunch.
Tang Jinhu crushed the bead in his hand and thrust out both arms, his face brimming with killing intent.
The silver threads wound around his wrists drank in his internal energy and snapped taut.
The next instant, a dazzling white flash filled the battlefield.
Screeeech—thud-thud-thud!
“Ghk!”
“Gaaah!”
Only a handful of those struck managed even a final scream. Death came equally to First Rate and Peak masters alike.
Raising their weapons to block was useless. The threads Tang Jinhu unleashed lived up to the name Soul-Severing Thread, slicing through everything in their path.
Blades. Bone and flesh. Even the lives of his enemies.
Tang Jinhu felled more than ten black-clad men with a single move, then released an azure dragon’s roar.
“Don’t retreat! Aim your hidden weapons at their vital points and attack them together!”
“Head Elder! This old man has come as well!”
“Would you look at these fucking bastards! How dare they invade our family? Do you not see the Heaven-Poison Wanderer before you?”
Tang Jinhu was a Supreme Peak master who had retired more than a decade ago, as well as the head of the Council of Elders.
The sight of veteran masters joining the battlefield one after another at precisely that moment brought color back to the faces of the Tang Clan martial artists who had begun to falter.
“G-Grandfather!”
“The Head Elder is here! The Council of Elders has mobilized!”
But their joy lasted only an instant.
Krrr-kang! Slash!
“Gaaah!”
“Tang Hwi!”
“Brat! Is this the time to be looking away?”
Pfft-pfft-pfft!
“Help me... Ghk!”
“Lord of Heaven!”
“The great Lord of Heaven is with us! Kill them all!”
The black-clad men were more skilled than the Sichuan Tang Clan martial artists, while their armor and bizarre poison-warding pearls rendered the Tang Clan’s famed poisons and hidden weapons useless.
A dozen Elders, including Tang Jinhu, and dozens of Peak masters whom the Tang Clan had painstakingly trained fought desperately.
But their limits were clear.
Screeeech—thud!
Tang Jinhu severed the throats of two black-clad men charging at him with the Soul-Severing Thread and ground his teeth.
“Where did these bastards come from...?”
The sight before him was appalling.
The black-clad men swung their weapons while crying out to the Lord of Heaven as if possessed.
Each time they blocked swords and hidden weapons with their armor and pressed onward through the poison smoke, blood sprayed and corpses piled up.

In the vacant eyes of a Tang Clan martial artist whose breath had stopped, red flames that had sprung up somewhere flickered. The hot fire and acrid smoke drove away the poison mist and consumed the fallen corpses.
Tang Jinhu roared, his voice raw enough to spit blood.
“No! You bastards! How dare you—how dare you lay hands on my own flesh and blood!”
Even the mighty forces of the Demonic Cult had suffered more than a thousand casualties to overcome the Tang Clan.
How could a mere three hundred enemies wreak such horrific devastation?
“Ghk! H-Head Elder...”
“Hyung!”
Pfft-pfft-pfft!
Even the Elders who had once roamed the martial world could not escape death.
They had not reached the exalted Supreme Peak realm as Tang Jinhu had, but every one of them was a veteran master who had reached the very edge of Peak.
Yet whenever they cut down one enemy, five more charged in. When they cut down those five, ten more rushed forward.
Among those ten black-clad men who charged forward without regard for their lives, a Peak master was hiding.
Slash. Crash!
After sacrificing dozens of his subordinates to behead another Elder, the black-clad man laughed triumphantly.
“So much for a Tang Clan Elder.”
“You bastard!”
Screeeech! Thud!
Despite Tang Jinhu’s furious efforts, the situation did not improve.
More than a hundred clansmen had already lost their lives, and half the Outer Hall had fallen into enemy hands.
“Huff, huff.”
Worse, his internal energy and stamina were rapidly running dry.
The battle had already reached a point where one aging Supreme Peak master could no longer turn the tide.
A lament slipped from Tang Jinhu’s lips as he realized the truth.
“What are the Family Head and the Tang Clan’s Ten Wonders doing?!”
If they were here, things would be different. Tang Sadok, the head of the family and its strongest master, along with the Tang Clan’s Ten Wonders.
If they joined the battle, they could turn the tide.
But—
“Heh-heh. They’re probably quite busy by now.”
The sudden voice in his ear made Tang Jinhu’s heart drop.
“Who are you?”
“As for who this old man is... Damn it. I can’t see a thing. Get the hell out of my way.”
Boom!
With a tremendous blast of displaced air, three or four black-clad men were hurled away as bloody pulp.
An old man drenched in blood strode into the newly cleared space and flashed Tang Jinhu a wide grin.
“Much better. Now I can see.”
He was short and ugly.
Tang Jinhu’s eyes trembled as he stared at him.
“Hm? Do you know me?”
“...I never expected the Fiend of Qinghai to still be alive.”
First Fiend stared at Tang Jinhu for a moment, then his eyes widened.
“Ah, now I remember. You’re that youngster from the Tang Family. So, have you gotten any better at using the Soul-Severing Thread?”
“Good enough to cut off your head.”
“I always thought the Sichuan Tang Clan was fairly practical for an orthodox faction. Looking at you, I suppose that isn’t entirely true. Not if you still indulge in such foolish fantasies.”
“Youngster, you still don’t understand, do you? Then this old man will tell you himself.”
First Fiend cackled.
“You, your Family Head, and those idiots called the Tang Clan’s Ten Wonders will all die. Whether they bear the Tang surname or are nothing but dogs, I’ll kill and burn every last one of them.”
“You—!”
“Don’t be too upset. The Lord of Heaven treats all people equally. He has bestowed the same punishment upon the Buddhist nuns and those Daoist bastards. Heh-heh-heh.”
Tang Jinhu froze, forgetting even his anger.
Only then did he realize that First Fiend’s two younger brothers, who had always followed him like shadows, were nowhere to be seen.
...Emei and Qingcheng.
The carnage of corpses and blood had not been limited to the Tang Clan.
The Sichuan Tang Clan, Emei, and Qingcheng.
He could feel the people’s screams and deaths.
Today, the three factions that ruled Sichuan would fight for their very survival.
Inside the hellscape those men had painted.
“Even after all these years... You truly are a Fiend.”
Tang Jinhu spat out the words.
First Fiend answered with a radiant smile.
“How kind of you. Could there be any greater praise for this old man?”
“I’ll kill you.”
“Your body has grown old, but your dreams remain ambitious.”
First Fiend burst into mad laughter and raised the twin axes in his hands.
“Now, shall we have another taste of blood?”
As if those words were a signal, hundreds of black-clad men who had already occupied the Outer Hall poured forward like a wave.
The surviving Tang Clan martial artists stood in their path, resolved to fight to the death.
“Go! Kill everything you see!”
“Stop them! We must never let them into the Inner Hall!”
Those trying to break through and those trying to stop them.
At the forefront, two men charged straight at each other.
Screeeech!
Tang Jinhu unleashed the Soul-Severing Thread with every ounce of his strength, firm resolve burning in his eyes.
Family Head, please be safe.
Kwahhhhhng!
“Cough!”
Tang Sadok stared at his palm with trembling eyes. Small pieces of his organs lay amid the dark-red blood.
“How... How could this...”
His head slowly rose as the exhausted words left him.
At that very moment, another life was extinguished.
Crunch! Thud!
A headless body toppled like a rotten log.
Considering the fame the man had enjoyed in life, it was a pitifully meaningless death.
“Were they called the Tang Clan’s Ten Wonders? They’re more capable than I expected.”
A few steps from the corpse, a middle-aged man wiped the blood spattered across his face and continued.
“Of course, we’ll have to call them something else now. Let me see... Yes. The Tang Clan’s Three Skills seems appropriate.”
Tang Sadok stared at the middle-aged man through blurred eyes.

The man had introduced himself as the Western Heaven Demon Lord. This enemy who had killed Tang Sadok’s father was overwhelmingly powerful. Neither Tang Sadok’s poison arts nor the combined assault of the Tang Clan’s Ten Wonders had been of any use.
Is this how it ends?
Tang Sadok still had the strength to fight. So did the other three surviving members of the Tang Clan’s Ten Wonders.
But...
How can we possibly stand against that monster?
What raised him from the depths of despair was the mettle he possessed as the Family Head—and the blood of the Tang Family flowing through his veins.
“Not yet. It isn’t over yet.”
“Why not remain seated? You cannot have much strength left.”
“I don’t know why, but I know you have no intention of killing this old man.”
“...Hm. As I said, the Poison King raised his son well.”
“Then kill me.”
“That won’t do. But I suppose I should wear you down a little more.”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord frowned and reached toward Tang Sadok.
That was when—
“Wait! Please, wait!”
A young man rushed in with a shout, then let out a sigh of relief.
“Phew. I’m not too late. Thank you for waiting!”
As the Western Heaven Demon Lord stared at Cheongpung, a single thought crossed his mind.
What kind of lunatic is this?
