Tang Jinhu crushed the bead in his hand and thrust out both arms, his face brimming with killing intent.
The silver threads wound around his wrists drank in his internal energy and snapped taut.
The next instant, a dazzling white flash filled the battlefield.
Screeeech—thud-thud-thud!
“Ghk!”
“Gaaah!”
Only a handful of those struck managed even a final scream.
Death came equally to First Rate and Peak masters alike.
Raising their weapons to block was useless.
The threads Tang Jinhu unleashed lived up to the name Soul-Severing Thread, slicing through everything in their path.
Blades.
Bone and flesh.
Even the lives of his enemies.
Tang Jinhu felled more than ten black-clad men with a single move, then released an azure dragon’s roar.
“Don’t retreat!
Aim your hidden weapons at their vital points and attack them together!”
“Head Elder!
This old man has come as well!”
“Would you look at these fucking bastards!
How dare they invade our family?
Do you not see the Heaven-Poison Wanderer before you?”
Tang Jinhu was a Supreme Peak master who had retired more than a decade ago, as well as the head of the Council of Elders.
The sight of veteran masters joining the battlefield one after another at precisely that moment brought color back to the faces of the Tang Clan martial artists who had begun to falter.
“G-Grandfather!”
“The Head Elder is here!
The Council of Elders has mobilized!”
But their joy lasted only an instant.
Krrr-kang!
Slash!
“Gaaah!”
“Tang Hwi!”
“Brat!
Is this the time to be looking away?”
Pfft-pfft-pfft!
“Help me...
Ghk!”
“Lord of Heaven!”
“The great Lord of Heaven is with us!
Kill them all!”
The black-clad men were more skilled than the Sichuan Tang Clan martial artists, while their armor and bizarre poison-warding pearls rendered the Tang Clan’s famed poisons and hidden weapons useless.
A dozen Elders, including Tang Jinhu, and dozens of Peak masters whom the Tang Clan had painstakingly trained fought desperately.
But their limits were clear.
Screeeech—thud!
Tang Jinhu severed the throats of two black-clad men charging at him with the Soul-Severing Thread and ground his teeth.
“Where did these bastards come from...?”
The sight before him was appalling.
The black-clad men swung their weapons while crying out to the Lord of Heaven as if possessed.
Each time they blocked swords and hidden weapons with their armor and pressed onward through the poison smoke, blood sprayed and corpses piled up.
In the vacant eyes of a Tang Clan martial artist whose breath had stopped, red flames that had sprung up somewhere flickered.
The hot fire and acrid smoke drove away the poison mist and consumed the fallen corpses.
Tang Jinhu roared, his voice raw enough to spit blood.
“No!
You bastards!
How dare you—how dare you lay hands on my own flesh and blood!”
Even the mighty forces of the Demonic Cult had suffered more than a thousand casualties to overcome the Tang Clan.
How could a mere three hundred enemies wreak such horrific devastation?
“Ghk!
H-Head Elder...”
“Hyung!”
Pfft-pfft-pfft!
Even the Elders who had once roamed the martial world could not escape death.
They had not reached the exalted Supreme Peak realm as Tang Jinhu had, but every one of them was a veteran master who had reached the very edge of Peak.
Yet whenever they cut down one enemy, five more charged in.
When they cut down those five, ten more rushed forward.
Among those ten black-clad men who charged forward without regard for their lives, a Peak master was hiding.
Slash.
Crash!
After sacrificing dozens of his subordinates to behead another Elder, the black-clad man laughed triumphantly.
“So much for a Tang Clan Elder.”
“You bastard!”
Screeeech!
Thud!
Despite Tang Jinhu’s furious efforts, the situation did not improve.
More than a hundred clansmen had already lost their lives, and half the Outer Hall had fallen into enemy hands.
“Huff, huff.”
Worse, his internal energy and stamina were rapidly running dry.
The battle had already reached a point where one aging Supreme Peak master could no longer turn the tide.
A lament slipped from Tang Jinhu’s lips as he realized the truth.
“What are the Family Head and the Tang Clan’s Ten Wonders doing?!”
If they were here, things would be different.
Tang Sadok, the head of the family and its strongest master, along with the Tang Clan’s Ten Wonders.
If they joined the battle, they could turn the tide.
But—
“Heh-heh.
They’re probably quite busy by now.”
The sudden voice in his ear made Tang Jinhu’s heart drop.
“Who are you?”
“As for who this old man is...
Damn it.
I can’t see a thing.
Get the hell out of my way.”
Boom!
With a tremendous blast of displaced air, three or four black-clad men were hurled away as bloody pulp.
An old man drenched in blood strode into the newly cleared space and flashed Tang Jinhu a wide grin.
“Much better.
Now I can see.”
He was short and ugly.
Tang Jinhu’s eyes trembled as he stared at him.
“Hm?
Do you know me?”
“...I never expected the Fiend of Qinghai to still be alive.”
First Fiend stared at Tang Jinhu for a moment, then his eyes widened.
“Ah, now I remember.
You’re that youngster from the Tang Family.
So, have you gotten any better at using the Soul-Severing Thread?”
“Good enough to cut off your head.”
“I always thought the Sichuan Tang Clan was fairly practical for an orthodox faction.
Looking at you, I suppose that isn’t entirely true.
Not if you still indulge in such foolish fantasies.”
“Youngster, you still don’t understand, do you?
Then this old man will tell you himself.”
First Fiend cackled.
“You, your Family Head, and those idiots called the Tang Clan’s Ten Wonders will all die.
Whether they bear the Tang surname or are nothing but dogs, I’ll kill and burn every last one of them.”
“You—!”
“Don’t be too upset.
The Lord of Heaven treats all people equally.
He has bestowed the same punishment upon the Buddhist nuns and those Daoist bastards.
Heh-heh-heh.”
Tang Jinhu froze, forgetting even his anger.
Only then did he realize that First Fiend’s two younger brothers, who had always followed him like shadows, were nowhere to be seen.
...Emei and Qingcheng.
The carnage of corpses and blood had not been limited to the Tang Clan.
The Sichuan Tang Clan, Emei, and Qingcheng.
He could feel the people’s screams and deaths.
Today, the three factions that ruled Sichuan would fight for their very survival.
Inside the hellscape those men had painted.
“Even after all these years...
You truly are a Fiend.”
Tang Jinhu spat out the words.
First Fiend answered with a radiant smile.
“How kind of you.
Could there be any greater praise for this old man?”
“I’ll kill you.”
“Your body has grown old, but your dreams remain ambitious.”
First Fiend burst into mad laughter and raised the twin axes in his hands.
“Now, shall we have another taste of blood?”
As if those words were a signal, hundreds of black-clad men who had already occupied the Outer Hall poured forward like a wave.
The surviving Tang Clan martial artists stood in their path, resolved to fight to the death.
“Go!
Kill everything you see!”
“Stop them!
We must never let them into the Inner Hall!”
Those trying to break through and those trying to stop them.
At the forefront, two men charged straight at each other.
Screeeech!
Tang Jinhu unleashed the Soul-Severing Thread with every ounce of his strength, firm resolve burning in his eyes.
Family Head, please be safe.
Kwahhhhhng!
“Cough!”
Tang Sadok stared at his palm with trembling eyes.
Small pieces of his organs lay amid the dark-red blood.
“How...
How could this...”
His head slowly rose as the exhausted words left him.
At that very moment, another life was extinguished.
Crunch!
Thud!
A headless body toppled like a rotten log.
Considering the fame the man had enjoyed in life, it was a pitifully meaningless death.
“Were they called the Tang Clan’s Ten Wonders?
They’re more capable than I expected.”
A few steps from the corpse, a middle-aged man wiped the blood spattered across his face and continued.
“Of course, we’ll have to call them something else now.
Let me see...
Yes.
The Tang Clan’s Three Skills seems appropriate.”
Tang Sadok stared at the middle-aged man through blurred eyes.
The man had introduced himself as the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
This enemy who had killed Tang Sadok’s father was overwhelmingly powerful.
Neither Tang Sadok’s poison arts nor the combined assault of the Tang Clan’s Ten Wonders had been of any use.
Is this how it ends?
Tang Sadok still had the strength to fight.
So did the other three surviving members of the Tang Clan’s Ten Wonders.
But...
How can we possibly stand against that monster?
What raised him from the depths of despair was the mettle he possessed as the Family Head—and the blood of the Tang Family flowing through his veins.
“Not yet.
It isn’t over yet.”
“Why not remain seated?
You cannot have much strength left.”
“I don’t know why, but I know you have no intention of killing this old man.”
As I said, the Poison King raised his son well.”
“Then kill me.”
“That won’t do.
But I suppose I should wear you down a little more.”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord frowned and reached toward Tang Sadok.
That was when—
“Wait!
Please, wait!”
A young man rushed in with a shout, then let out a sigh of relief.
“Phew.
I’m not too late.
Thank you for waiting!”
As the Western Heaven Demon Lord stared at Cheongpung, a single thought crossed his mind.
What kind of lunatic is this?

chapters.title: Chapter 355
paragraphs: “Phew. I’m not too late. Thank you for waiting!”
What kind of lunatic is this?
At the sight of the young man strolling in as casually as if he belonged there, the Western Heaven Demon Lord let out an involuntary, hollow laugh.
I emerge after all this time, and now I’m running into all kinds of strange people.
He considered himself a man who had lived a fairly extraordinary life, but the young man before him easily surpassed anything he had imagined.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord found that rather unfortunate. He had wasted time, and the young man had hastened his own death.
“What’s there to thank me for? Farewell.”
Swish!
Even livestock called for different blades.
If Tang Sadok and the Tang Clan’s Ten Wonders were pigs, that brat was an ant.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord did not even feel the need to draw his favored weapon. He flicked a finger toward the young man’s brow, then started to turn his head toward Tang Sadok.
Or rather, he was about to when—
“Whoa. That nearly scared the life out of me.”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord stared at the young man, eyes widening.
The brat should have been lying dead by now, yet he was looking back at him with an innocent grin.
In the iron pillar exactly half a step to his side was a hole the size of an egg.
Right where the young man’s head had been only a moment before.
...He dodged it? The eighth-stage Ghost Prison Finger?
It should not have happened. It could not have happened.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord wondered if something had gone wrong with his body without his noticing.
Then—
“Stand back.”
Tang Sadok spoke, his face rigid. Pale from his internal injuries, his expression held a trace of dismay.
“This is no place for a greenhorn like you to interfere... Cough!”
“Gasp! Blood! You’re bleeding!”
When Tang Sadok suddenly vomited blood, the young man stepped forward with a worried look.
“Grandpa Tang, are you all right?”
Swish!
In the blink of an eye, the young man flipped through the air as a flash of light sprang from his waist.
Drawing his sword at the same time, he deflected the slash that came flying through the air. Then he panted heavily.
“Huff, huff. That startled me. Why did you do that without saying anything?”
“Ha-ha. Ha-ha-ha!”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord looked from the sword in his right hand to the young man, then burst into hearty laughter.
Though he had not used his full strength, that single exchange had taught him two things.
First, the mysterious young man was not merely a lunatic.
And second—
“You must be the Disciple Sword Saint Mae Jonghak took in during his later years. Your name was... Cheongpung, wasn’t it?”
Cheongpung stared at the Western Heaven Demon Lord with round eyes.
“Oh? You know me?”
“How could I not, when the scent of Huashan’s plum blossoms pours from your footwork? It has been a long time since I saw such an exceptional Dark Fragrance Drift.”
“Wow! You know Dark Fragrance Drift! But how do you know my name...?”
“I have many unseen eyes and ears.”
Dark Heaven had spent many years planting spies throughout the world, and Sichuan Province was no exception.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord had already known for ten days that Cheongpung was staying at the Tang Clan.
He had not expected them to meet at such a perfect moment.
To have reached this realm at his age... The Sword Saint has raised a monster.
There was a reason he had failed to recognize Cheongpung at first glance.
As the Western Heaven Demon Lord examined Cheongpung from head to toe with a peculiar look in his eyes, Tang Sadok parted his bloodstained lips.
“You vicious bastard. Was attacking our family not enough? Now you mean to harm that boy as well?”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord answered gently.
“No. Not at all.”
“He has nothing to do with our family... What?”
The unexpected answer made Tang Sadok and even the three surviving members of the Tang Clan’s Ten Wonders doubt their ears.
But the Western Heaven Demon Lord, the man at the center of it all, remained impassive.
“I have no intention of taking prey someone else has already marked. Personally, I am not particularly fond of him, but we serve the same master.”
“...What are you talking about?”
“An acquaintance of mine became quite angry recently. It seems the wound to his pride hurt more than losing his arm. He is determined to kill that young man with his own hands.”
Tang Sadok’s expression twisted at the incomprehensible explanation.
Then Cheongpung suddenly spoke.
“The Blood Lord. It’s him.”
“So you do remember him. He’ll be delighted when I tell him.”
“I don’t like him.”
Anyone who knew Cheongpung—especially Jin Taekyung—would have stared at him with his mouth hanging open.
Cheongpung’s nature was as clear as a mountain stream, and he had never once declared that he liked or disliked someone.
Not even those who had approached him with ill intent.
But now, unmistakable hostility had appeared in Cheongpung’s transparent eyes.
“Is he here right now?”
“Unfortunately, he is far away. But he would be very pleased to see you. Ah, and of course...”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord continued smoothly.
“The same goes for the Fire King being treated at the Tang Clan and the young man named Jin Taekyung.”
“I told you. I have many eyes and ears.”
A smile formed at the corner of the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s mouth.
“Do not worry too much. I intend to take all three of you alive. Whether my friend the Blood Lord feels the same, however, I cannot say.”
Cheongpung sensed the chilling edge hidden beneath the man’s gentle voice.
Without realizing it, he tightened his grip around his sword hilt. A different tone and voice than usual slipped through his lips.
“It won’t be easy.”
“I wonder if that’s really—”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s voice never finished.
A tremendous boom split the air, and dozens of flashes filled the pavilion reduced to rubble.
Swish, swish-swish-swish!
Tang Sadok and the Tang Clan’s Ten Wonders—or rather, the three who should now be called the Tang Clan’s Three Skills—shot toward a single target like arrows, as if they had planned it together.

Dozens of hidden weapons filled the air from every direction, each aimed at a lethal acupoint, while Tang Sadok drew on every last ounce of strength and drove his fist into the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s chest.
“You bastard—!”
Kwahhhhhng! Rumble, rumble!
The aftermath was powerful enough to be called an earthquake.
Tang Sadok and the three Tang Clan martial artists had personally experienced the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s might.
They had no intention of squandering their one chance. Their final assault, launched by drawing even upon their innate qi, was devastating.
We did it.
Within the cloud of dust so thick he could not see an inch ahead, Tang Sadok smiled brightly despite coughing up blood.
He had realized that the punch he had unleashed with all his strength had crushed the enemy’s flesh and bones and pierced through his chest.
This is the Tang Family’s revenge.
That was when—
“Did you think this would be enough?”
Crack!
A powerful hand closed around Tang Sadok’s neck as the calm voice reached him.
As the dust dispersed, he saw one of the Tang Clan’s Three Skills dead with a massive hole through his chest. The Western Heaven Demon Lord stood behind the corpse, reaching over its shoulder.
At the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s feet, two people who had once possessed human shapes lay shattered across the ground.
How?
That single thought filled Tang Sadok’s mind.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord smiled gently as he held the dazed Tang Sadok by the throat. Then he swung the sword in his other hand.
Kwahhhhhng!
A wave of Sword Energy surged outward like a tide.
The thirty blades of Sword Energy flying toward him like flower petals were swallowed by the wave and vanished.
But though the petals disappeared, their fragrance remained.
From the foot of the young man driving into the air at the speed of a flash, the scent of plum blossoms planted by Huashan and brought into bloom by the Sword Saint rose up.
Sssshing!
“The Meteor Chasing the Moon Sword!”
A single sword thrust forward, leaving a pale afterimage.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord let out a brief cry of surprise and brought his sword down.
His sinuous Snake Sword collided with Cheongpung’s plum-blossom-engraved blade.
Kwang! Kwang-kwa-kwa-kwang!
Every clash of the two swords unleashed a deafening boom like an exploding shell.
It did not take long for one side to gain the upper hand.
Swish—bang!
A figure went flying under the force of the impact.
Cheongpung twisted in midair and landed, then stared at the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
“I expected you to be strong, but... you really are.”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s martial prowess was extraordinary.
He had seized an overwhelming advantage with only one hand, all while holding Tang Sadok captive.
At Cheongpung’s apparently awed remark, the Western Heaven Demon Lord let out a quiet laugh.
What an impudent brat. He’s hiding quite a bit, too.
Irritated, he briefly considered teaching the brat a lesson himself.
But he had more urgent business.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord clicked his tongue softly, then called in a low voice.
“First Fiend.”
“Yes, Demon Lord.”
Cheongpung was not surprised when First Fiend appeared with a deferential answer. He had sensed the man nearby for the past fifteen minutes.
That meant the attackers had already passed through the Outer Hall and entered the Inner Hall.
The screams were drawing closer.
“Handle that one.”
“You mean the Sword Saint’s successor? I couldn’t be more grateful...”
First Fiend grinned, baring his bloodstained teeth.
He had already claimed nearly a hundred lives, including Tang Jinhu, the Sichuan Tang Clan’s Head Elder.
But intoxicated by his first taste of slaughter in so long, he had found it nowhere near enough.
“You know of the Blood Lord’s request, I assume.”
“Of course. The Sword Saint’s youngest Disciple, whom he cherishes like his own child... Heh-heh. This should be fun. I’ll leave him barely breathing.”
“Keeping him alive would be preferable, but if that proves impossible, you may kill him.”
“What?”
“He is dangerous. If you cannot handle him, cut him down before he can grow.”
“He’s nothing but a greenhorn. I never knew the Demon Lord made jokes. Ha-ha-ha!”
First Fiend’s booming laughter rapidly faded.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s gaze had turned cold.
The instant their eyes met, First Fiend felt his heart drop. He hurriedly threw himself facedown on the ground.
“Y-Your orders.”
For a moment, he had forgotten what kind of man the Western Heaven Demon Lord was.
He was a man who hid a grim reaper behind a gentle voice, soft manner, and mild expression.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord silently looked down at the sweating First Fiend, then walked past him.
Tang Sadok struggled in pain with the hand around his neck, but the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s arm did not move an inch.
“No!”
“Heh-heh. Do you have any idea whose path you’re blocking?”
Swish—boom!
Cheongpung charged forward with a desperate shout, and First Fiend moved to intercept him.
Leaving their thunderous clash behind, the Western Heaven Demon Lord continued walking.
The Inner Hall, where craftsmen had forged weapons and children once walked beside martial artists, was now covered in blood and corpses.
Screams and death overflowed from every direction.
And here, only a short distance away, one man watched the destruction of his family with tears streaming down his face.
“Can you feel it? Everything in the Tang Clan is collapsing.”
Tang Sadok’s hollow eyes trembled.
The Tang Clan was not the only thing collapsing. His firm convictions and his heart were crumbling with it.
Then, as tears continued to stream down his face, a quiet voice slipped into his ear.
“Answer me. Where is the Myriad-Poison Ring?”

Cheongpung twisted in midair and landed, then stared at the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
“I expected you to be strong, but... you really are.”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s martial prowess was extraordinary.
He had seized an overwhelming advantage with only one hand, all while holding Tang Sadok captive.
At Cheongpung’s apparently awed remark, the Western Heaven Demon Lord let out a quiet laugh.
What an impudent brat.
He’s hiding quite a bit, too.
Irritated, he briefly considered teaching the brat a lesson himself.
But he had more urgent business.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord clicked his tongue softly, then called in a low voice.
“First Fiend.”
“Yes, Demon Lord.”
Cheongpung was not surprised when First Fiend appeared with a deferential answer.
He had sensed the man nearby for the past fifteen minutes.
That meant the attackers had already passed through the Outer Hall and entered the Inner Hall.
The screams were drawing closer.
“Handle that one.”
“You mean the Sword Saint’s successor?
I couldn’t be more grateful...”
First Fiend grinned, baring his bloodstained teeth.
He had already claimed nearly a hundred lives, including Tang Jinhu, the Sichuan Tang Clan’s Head Elder.
But intoxicated by his first taste of slaughter in so long, he had found it nowhere near enough.
“You know of the Blood Lord’s request, I assume.”
“Of course.
The Sword Saint’s youngest Disciple, whom he cherishes like his own child...
Heh-heh.
This should be fun.
I’ll leave him barely breathing.”
“Keeping him alive would be preferable, but if that proves impossible, you may kill him.”
“What?”
“He is dangerous.
If you cannot handle him, cut him down before he can grow.”
“He’s nothing but a greenhorn.
I never knew the Demon Lord made jokes.
Ha-ha-ha!”
First Fiend’s booming laughter rapidly faded.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s gaze had turned cold.
The instant their eyes met, First Fiend felt his heart drop.
He hurriedly threw himself facedown on the ground.
“Y-Your orders.”
For a moment, he had forgotten what kind of man the Western Heaven Demon Lord was.
He was a man who hid a grim reaper behind a gentle voice, soft manner, and mild expression.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord silently looked down at the sweating First Fiend, then walked past him.
Tang Sadok struggled in pain with the hand around his neck, but the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s arm did not move an inch.
“No!”
“Heh-heh.
Do you have any idea whose path you’re blocking?”
Swish—boom!
Cheongpung charged forward with a desperate shout, and First Fiend moved to intercept him.
Leaving their thunderous clash behind, the Western Heaven Demon Lord continued walking.
The Inner Hall, where craftsmen had forged weapons and children once walked beside martial artists, was now covered in blood and corpses.
Screams and death overflowed from every direction.
And here, only a short distance away, one man watched the destruction of his family with tears streaming down his face.
“Can you feel it?
Everything in the Tang Clan is collapsing.”
Tang Sadok’s hollow eyes trembled.
The Tang Clan was not the only thing collapsing.
His firm convictions and his heart were crumbling with it.
Then, as tears continued to stream down his face, a quiet voice slipped into his ear.
“Answer me.
Where is the Myriad-Poison Ring?”

chapters.title: Chapter 356
paragraphs: The underground prison beneath the Sichuan Tang Clan was dark and damp by nature.
The few torches spaced along the walls gave off less light than fireflies, and the floor was covered in stagnant water of unknown origin that squelched underfoot.
Just like now.
“What a foul smell. Prison or not, how can they lock people up in a place like this?”

“People? This is where they keep beasts. Haven’t you heard that the Sichuan Tang Clan captured fiends from the Great Faction War and subjected them to every torture imaginable? A place like this should hardly surprise you.”
Squelch. Squelch.
There were two voices, but far more sets of footsteps.
I quietly extended my Qi Sense and counted them.
Fifteen.
The two men at the front, presumably the group’s leaders, continued their conversation.
“But where are all the prisoners? There are bars everywhere, but the cells are empty.”
“Everyone imprisoned here is an old monster from the days of the Great Faction War. It wouldn’t be strange if they’d died long ago, especially after being tortured in a place like this.”
“Fair point.”
Their guess was half right and half wrong.
Many of the underground prison’s original residents had indeed passed on to the next world, but more than ten prisoners still remained.
What they had failed to anticipate was that someone unseen had used Pressure-Point Strike on the prisoners and moved them elsewhere.
“I can’t see even a single ant. Wouldn’t it be better to go back upstairs and kill at least one more person?”
“I don’t think we’ve searched even half the place yet.”
“Now that you mention it, what could there possibly be farther in? The others will come through and search every last corner anyway.”
“Don’t be ridiculous. Have you forgotten the Lord of Heaven’s command? What if someone of the Tang bloodline is hiding down here...?”

“No one would be stupid enough to hide in an underground prison. The battle isn’t even over yet, so why would they hide here? I could understand trying to break through the encirclement and escape, but this?”
The man let out a low groan, then spoke in a firm voice.
“No. We have been entrusted with the revered Lord of Heaven’s command. The Demon Lord himself is leading by example, yet you intend to shirk your duty?”
“Phew. Damn it.”
“Stop complaining and follow me.”
The Dark Heaven martial artist whose face I did not know had no idea that his fate had been decided by those words.
At his firm response, the other man grumbled.
“You ought to learn some flexibility. Keep living like such a stickler and you’ll die before your time.”
“Don’t say such ill-omened things. I’ll live longer than someone who half-asses everything like you, so worry about yourself.”
“Want to bet?”
“Fine. Why wouldn’t I—”
Long story short, the man who half-assed everything won their bet over who would live longer.
Though only by a fraction of a second.
Shnk!
It was a perfect ambush.
I had concealed my presence and waited in the darkness of the maze-like passage. The instant I drove the dagger in my left hand into one man’s eye, I swung the sword in my right.
I had smeared mud over the blade beforehand to keep it from catching the light. It sheared through flesh and bone.
Slash! Splat!
The two Peak masters died without so much as a scream, collapsing like rotten logs.
Suddenly drenched in blood and filthy water, the black-robed men stared blankly between their leaders’ bodies and me.
“W-What...?”
Thirteen left.
Instead of answering, I swung my sword again. With another grisly sound of parting flesh, a severed head flew into the air.
“Twelve.”
A single emotion surfaced in their vacant eyes.
Fear.
“Dead end, huh? The layout down here is pretty fucked up. Apparently, they built it this way in case anyone tried to escape.”
“Eek!”
I walked toward the rat trapped at the end of the passage.
Granted, he was rather large for a rat. But despite his size, he had been the first to run. Apparently, he was a coward.
“All right. Time to join your friends in hell.”
“F-Fiend!”
“You crazy bastard. When you do it, it’s romance, but when I do it, it’s adultery?”
Thud.
The black-robed man dropped to his knees, his face deathly pale. He still had his weapon in hand, but by now he knew perfectly well that it was useless against me.
In the end, he resorted to begging for his life.
“P-Please, spare—”
“F-Fuck off.”
Crack.
I snapped the black-robed man’s neck without hesitation. His tongue lolled out as his head tilted at an unnatural angle.
Instant death. No question.
“You people always make me do the same job twice. It’s not like you were going to get far.”
With a sigh, I slung him over my shoulder and retraced my steps. It did not take long to return to the site of my initial ambush.
The man had not made it very far, and over the past ten days I had become familiar with the underground prison’s labyrinthine layout.
“Bastards. What the hell are you crawling all the way in here for? Is there something to eat?”
This was the second time the black-robed men had infiltrated the underground prison.
About thirty minutes ago, seven of them had come in. I had killed every last one.
I had helped thin the enemy’s ranks for the Sichuan Tang Clan, but I could not feel happy about it. I knew what their presence meant.
The battle is going badly.
The underground prison was located on the outskirts of the Tang Clan’s Inner Hall. That meant the Outer Hall, which could be considered the front line, had already been breached.
Then what about Cheongpung...?
I shook my head as an ominous thought flashed through my mind.
No way. Even if you dropped Cheongpung into the middle of hell, he’d be the kind of guy who came back alive.
No. He had to be.
Damn it. If only I could at least log out. Then there’d be a little hope.
I had held out some hope, but no such luck.
The System had disabled Logout the instant the Quest began.
Besides, even if Logout suddenly became available, I could not risk returning to the modern world.
The enemy had already broken in twice within the past thirty minutes. If they stormed the place while I was gone, even briefly...
Not only me, but Jeok Cheongang and the Divine Physician would be finished.
I have no choice. I have to stop them here.
They had numbers. I was alone.
I needed to keep making the most of ambushes, as I had just done, while conserving my strength for an emergency.
The whole plan goes to hell if they walk in and find corpses everywhere.
I began moving the scattered bodies one by one.
The place I had chosen as my temporary morgue lay in the deepest, darkest reaches of the underground prison.
Creeeak.
“Long time no see. What’s it been, half an hour?”
“I brought you some new friends so you wouldn’t get lonely.”
At the center of the prison, where not a single ray of light could reach, an old man festooned with restraints glared at me with blazing eyes.
The Heavenly Power Demon.
“What?”
“What are you going to do, glare me to death? If you’ve got something to say, say it.”
“Oh, right. Your pressure points.”
I had struck his Paralysis Acupoint and Mute Acupoint, so of course he could not speak.
I walked over and released them. His furious voice immediately burst out.
“What the hell do you think you’re doing?”
“Can’t you tell? I’m moving corpses.”
“I can see that! Why the hell are you bringing them here?”
“Keep your voice down. Shout one more time and I might strike a lethal acupoint instead of your Mute Acupoint.”
Good. He was quiet now.
Leaving the silenced Heavenly Power Demon behind, I began stacking the bodies I had brought into the prison.
Thump. Rumble-rumble.
“Could you pick up that head over there?”
“...Are you speaking to this old man?”
“Oh, right. You’re in restraints.”
“Huff! Huff!”

The Heavenly Power Demon’s face flushed crimson as he snorted through his nose. Still, he apparently had no desire to get struck in a lethal acupoint, because he just barely swallowed the shout rising in his throat.
“What in the world is wrong with you...?”
“All done. I’m leaving.”
“What? Something you want to say?”
The Heavenly Power Demon had refused to utter a word despite my efforts to coax information out of him over the past several days.
A man who had seen enough corpses during the Great Faction War to last a lifetime would not be complaining now without a reason. My suspicion had clearly hit the mark, and he began to stammer.
“N-No. Nothing.”
“Then we’re done.”
“W-Wait. Wait a moment.”
“Last chance. If you have something to say, spit it out.”
The Heavenly Power Demon’s lips worked silently for a moment before he let out a deep sigh.
“Why did you leave only this old man here? Where are the other prisoners?”
“You don’t need to know.”
“Then what are these corpses?”
He tried to sound unconcerned, but the way he studied my expression made it obvious that this was what he had really wanted to ask.
For the past several decades, his only visitor had been Old Man Gung bearing instruments of torture. Now nearly twenty naked corpses had suddenly been piled in front of him. Of course he was curious.
“Has some calamity befallen the Tang Clan?”
“Yeah.”
I added one brief sentence.
“Dark Heaven invaded.”
It was the same expression I had seen on his face a few days ago.
Pretending not to notice how the words Dark Heaven had made the Heavenly Power Demon freeze, I continued.
“The Outer Hall has already been breached. There’s probably a fierce battle raging in the Inner Hall as we speak. Things are going worse than expected.”
“Who did you say it was?”
“What?”
“You must have interrogated your captives. This old man is asking who leads them.”
“Pretty sharp.”
I had already squeezed information out of one of the seven who first entered the prison.
He had been terrified, but he severed his own heart meridian and killed himself before I could learn much. Still, I had managed to get one man’s title from him.
“The Western Heaven Demon Lord.”
Clatter! Clank!
Just four words.
But their effect on the Heavenly Power Demon was tremendous.
The old man had always hung limply from his restraints, his gaunt body reduced to skin and bone. Now he hauled at the chains as though he might tear himself free at any moment.
He even glared at me with bloodshot eyes.
“Did you just say... the Western Heaven Demon Lord?”
“You know him?”
“I-Is he still alive? Then the Cult Leader! What happened to the Cult Leader?”
What was wrong with this old man all of a sudden?
Caught off guard, I answered.
“...At this hour? He’s probably eating breakfast.”

It was my first time hearing the title Western Heaven Demon Lord, so how would I know what had happened to the Demonic Cult’s Cult Leader? It was not as if the Demonic Cult had an official Twitter account.
“So it has finally come to this. In the end... it has come to this. Ha. Ha-ha-ha!”
After babbling words I could not understand, the Heavenly Power Demon began laughing like a man who had lost his mind.
I stared at him for a moment, then suddenly spoke.
“Spill it. What’s the connection between the Demonic Cult and Dark Heaven? And what kind of fucking bastard is this Western Heaven Demon Lord?”
The laughter echoing through the prison abruptly stopped.
The Heavenly Power Demon’s hollow gaze settled on me.
“He—the man you call the Western Heaven Demon Lord—was one of the four Protectors of the Divine Cult. He served closer to the Cult Leader than anyone...and led him astray.”
“Then...”
“One day, he began calling himself the Western Heaven Demon Lord. That was the beginning of everything. And now it has come to this. In the end, it has come to this. Ha-ha... Hahahaha!”
At that very moment, the Heavenly Power Demon erupted into crazed laughter.
Boom! Rumble-rumble!
A tremendous roar sounded in the distance, and the underground prison shook.

chapters.title: Chapter 357
paragraphs: A serene expression. An unhurried gait. A spotless yellow robe.
He alone stood apart—the only person whom the aura of death filling the Sichuan Tang Clan could touch.
“They’re no more than a handful of men at best. Push them back!”
“Fight to the end! We are the Sichuan Tang Clan!”
“Waaaaah!”
With a tremendous roar that shook the earth, two waves crashed into each other. Screams and battle cries mixed together as a thick mist of blood began to form.
It was a savage battle fought with utter disregard for life. The outcome was decided just as swiftly.
“Surround them! Don’t let a single one survive!”
“Gaaaah!”
The black wave of men dressed in black swallowed the wave of green.
When it passed, all that remained in its wake were green-clad corpses scattered like foam.
Watching it all from more than a thousand feet away, the Western Heaven Demon Lord suddenly spoke.
“It’s over.”
Their resolve to stand and fight without retreating was worthy of respect, but they had been hopelessly outnumbered from the start.
Even the poison and hidden weapons that formed the foundation of the Sichuan Tang Clan had been rendered largely ineffective.
The battle—or rather, the war—belonged to Dark Heaven.
“It seems I won’t be able to keep my promise. My apologies, Family Head Tang.”
The more desperate people became, the more their judgment faltered. Tang Sadok had been no exception.
After extracting the answer he wanted by promising to preserve the Tang Family’s lineage, the Western Heaven Demon Lord had taken a simple and cruel course of action.
Rather than kill Tang Sadok immediately, he had seated him against a tree atop a hill overlooking the Sichuan Tang Clan.
There, Tang Sadok could watch his family perish until his own last breath.
“Everything according to the will of the Lord of Heaven.”
Drip. Drip-drip.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord looked up at the sky as rain began to fall, then turned away.
The mouth of a cave yawned open like a black maw. Beside a fallen brazier lay a hunchbacked old man, dead with his eyes wide open.
What caught the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s interest were the wounds carved into the old man’s body.
The Black Blood Sword Technique.
The Black Blood Sword Technique was permitted only to Dark Heaven martial artists.
Having recognized the identity of those who had arrived before him, the Western Heaven Demon Lord descended the stone steps leading underground.
Footprints stained with blood and mud stood out clearly upon the stairs. At least twenty of his subordinates had passed this way before him.
And most likely...
They’re all dead.
There were tracks leading down, but none coming back up.
The moment he entered the underground prison, suspicion became certainty.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord had lived a life steeped in blood. He could feel the lingering heat of battle in the dark corridor and smell the metallic reek of blood beneath the stench.
Who did this?
He studied the fine droplets of blood spattered across the wall.
Skilled. They were cut down before they could put up any real resistance.
With the Sichuan Tang Clan in mortal peril, there was no chance any of its masters would remain here merely to guard outsiders.
If Tang Sadok had told the truth, only three people remained in the underground prison.
The Divine Physician was hardly a fighting force, and Fire King Jeok Cheongang had yet to regain consciousness. That left only one person.
Jin Taekyung, the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord recalled what the Blood Lord had said about Jin Taekyung.
The most arrogant and tenacious young bastard under heaven, with more guts than sense.
For some reason, the Blood Lord had wanted to kill Jin Taekyung even more than the Sword Saint who had cut off his arm or the Fire King.
So he’s skilled enough to survive an encounter with the Blood Lord?
But Jin Taekyung would not be so lucky twice.
The Sword Saint was not here, and the Fire King was in no condition to fight.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord intended to capture the rats trapped in the jar and return without difficulty.
Along with the Myriad-Poison Ring in their possession.
Squelch. Squelch.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord strolled onward, then abruptly stopped.
A solid stone wall stretching down from the ceiling blocked his path.
“Well, now. They certainly made this place complicated.”
He regarded the wall for a moment, then closed his hand into a fist. Dark-red mist coiled around his arm and enveloped it.
Gooooooong.
Everything happened in an instant.
The manifestation of qi. Its compression. Its explosion.
Nothing could stand in the path of his Fist Force.
Rumble-rumble-rumble!
Walls shattered and collapsed. The entire prison shook.
The immense concentration of qi shot forward in a straight line, punching through dozens of walls. Stalactites rained from the ceiling like hail, and a dense cloud of dust billowed into the air.
Much better.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord surveyed the path he had created, then spoke.
“Why don’t you come out now?”
His only answer was a piercing shriek through the air.
Whoosh!
The dust cloud split apart. The Western Heaven Demon Lord plucked the dagger flying toward his throat from the air and smiled.
“Are you Jin Taekyung?”
“You already know. Why ask?”
Step. Step.
A tall young man—Jin Taekyung—emerged from the cloud of dust and stared at the Western Heaven Demon Lord with an impassive gaze.
I tried to look unfazed.
Half of any fight was momentum. You couldn’t let your guard down because your opponent looked weaker, and you couldn’t let yourself be intimidated because he looked stronger.
Especially when you were facing the real deal.
What kind of monster is this guy?
I stared at the middle-aged man before me, inwardly clicking my tongue.
If Moses had parted the sea with his staff, this man had carved a new path through the underground prison with a single punch.
And that wasn’t all. He stood there with a faint smile, the very picture of tranquility.
Even the air around him smells different.
The Blood Lord had been openly insane. This middle-aged man, on the other hand, was dangerous simply by existing.
Their martial arts might have been comparable in strength, but they were completely different in nature.
“I’ve heard a great deal about you. You’re an amusing young man, just as I was told.”
I lowered White Flame’s spearhead at an angle.
“I’m pretty entertaining myself.”
“I also heard you lack manners.”
“You’ve got the wrong man. My nickname is Mr. Manners.”
“Well, I would have to spend more time with you to know for certain. But according to an acquaintance of mine, it’s true.”
“You don’t look like you have any friends. Who’s the acquaintance?”
The smile on the middle-aged man’s lips deepened.
“The Blood Lord.”
“He’s very eager to see you.”
“I never want to see that fucking bastard again.”
“That young man Cheongpung said the same thing. In a different tone, of course.”
This bastard has already met Cheongpung.
And yet he was here...
I felt my face stiffen despite myself.
“You, by any chance...”
The middle-aged man smiled and waved a hand.
“There’s no need to worry. I won’t kill you. I intend to take you, Cheongpung, and the Fire King back alive.”
I asked with a dumbfounded expression.
“Take us?”
“I told you. The Blood Lord wants to see you. So you’ll be safe, at least until then.”
“Of course, what happens afterward will be up to the Blood Lord.”
The middle-aged man had given me two pieces of good news and one piece of bad news.
The good news was that Cheongpung was alive and the Blood Lord wasn’t here. The bad news was that if I lost this fight, we’d all be attending a group get-together with him.
Of course, the chances of us having a drink over grilled intestines before parting ways were close to zero.
The odds that I’ll become the grilled intestines instead are probably around fifty percent.
The other fifty percent was the chance I’d end up as grilled tripe.
Damn it. Just thinking about it was making my mouth water.
I swallowed dryly and looked the middle-aged man up and down.
A man who could call the Blood Lord, presumably one of Dark Heaven’s highest-ranking figures, an acquaintance. A man who could unleash that much destructive power with a single punch.
A title came to mind.
“You’re the Western Heaven Demon Lord, aren’t you?”
“Ah, come to think of it, I haven’t introduced myself yet. It’s a pleasure to meet you.”
Pleasure, my ass.
I stared at the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s two perfectly functional arms and muttered.
“I heard you only had one arm.”
“That was true until ten days ago.”
“What?”
“I had another attached. It wasn’t originally mine, so it still doesn’t move quite as well as I’d like. If you intend to try something, aim for my left arm.”
What the hell was this guy?
Even if some kind of suturing operation was possible, he had replaced an arm as if it were a computer component.
Aside from the subtle difference in skin tone, it moved perfectly naturally.
Is that even possible? And in only ten days?
I couldn’t make any sense of it, but I had to set my shock and questions aside for now.
His last remark bothered me even more.
He even told me his weakness.
There could only be one reason for something that absurd.
It was the kind of arrogance only someone certain of his overwhelming strength could display.
And the Western Heaven Demon Lord was strong enough to make arrogance look like composure.
“Damn it.”
I drew a deep breath and fixed him with a cold, level stare.
“Can’t you just pretend you came to visit a patient and turn around?”
“That would be difficult. Setting you people aside, there’s something I have to take with me.”
“Something?”
Instead of answering, the Western Heaven Demon Lord posed a question of his own.
“This old man will ask you this time. Will you surrender? Peacefully.”
“Could you kill yourself for me? Peacefully.”
“Then there’s only one answer.”
Roughly a hundred yards separated us.
The instant our gazes collided across that distance—
Whoosh! Swish!
We both reached out at the same time.
No. When it came to launching our attacks, at least, I was faster.
The only problem was that the Finger Qi the Western Heaven Demon Lord fired reached its target one step before my dagger did.
Striking second, hitting first.
A red warning light flashed in my head. At the same time, my sharpened senses took in everything around me.
The Finger Qi was formless and invisible, yet I could clearly feel its approach. It was a new sense I had acquired while fighting Hwangbo Eom, the Taeeul Merciless Sword.
Now!
I twisted my head and shot forward. Something faster than a bullet grazed my ear.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord watched me with open surprise.
“To evade a Ghost Prison Finger at eighty percent power... You certainly have a talent for surprising people as well—”
“Yeah, Ghost Prison Finger.”
Whoosh!
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s voice cut off.
Within that slowed instant, his widening pupils reflected me closing in right before his eyes.
My speed lay beyond anything he had imagined—far beyond the limits of a Peak master.
Stamina, Strength, Agility. And the Flamefire Path.
I poured everything into a single step. I erased the distance and tore through the air.
The fire dragon crouched within my qi sea spread its wings and soared. White Flame’s transparent spearhead became the dragon’s claw, plunging toward my enemy.
Heavenly Strike.
Kraaaaaash!
Rumble-rumble-rumble!
It was a tremendous reverberation.
As if to attest to the ferocity of the fighting, the corpses of enemies and allies piled together in tangled heaps collapsed.
The pavilion shook as though struck by an earthquake. Even those swinging weapons at one another staggered as they momentarily lost their balance.
“An earthquake! It’s an earthquake!”
“Damn it, why now...?”
An earthquake was a calamity no human strength could stop.
The tremor lasted only a moment, but it was enough to fill everyone with fear.
Everyone except the two men facing each other in the ruined Family Head’s Hall of the Sichuan Tang Clan.
“Ha-ha-ha-ha-ha!”
The old man, the First Fiend, threw back his head and roared with laughter, then turned toward Cheongpung.
“You felt that just now, didn’t you?”
Cheongpung nodded, looking dazed.
“Yes.”
Of course he had. The tremor had been an immense wave of qi, powerful enough to be felt from hundreds of yards away.
The First Fiend continued with a sneer.
“It seems the Demon Lord has finally made up his mind. Heh-heh.”
“I know. It’s really amazing.”
“He has finally cast aside his last shred of mercy and embraced killing intent. Neither the Fire King nor that disciple of his will survive. Do you understand what that means?”
“Yes. My Benefactor really is amazing.”
“Now that we no longer need to worry about the Blood Lord’s feelings, even I won’t show you any mercy from here on—what?”
The First Fiend paused and frowned.
He couldn’t begin to understand what the greenhorn before him had just said.
“Your Benefactor? You mean the Fire King’s disciple?”
But Cheongpung’s next words were not directed at the First Fiend.
In fact, none of his answers had been directed at him from the start.
A quiet murmur slipped from Cheongpung’s lips.
“At first, I thought I was far ahead of him. But before I knew it, he’d already come this far...”
Cheongpung gazed toward the distant source of the tremor, his eyes shining with joy and ruefulness.
No one else in the Sichuan Tang Clan could have guessed the truth—not even the First Fiend standing before him.
But Cheongpung knew.
“There’s no doubt. It’s my Benefactor.”
Cheongpung had been happy on Huashan, but he had also been lonely.
The beautiful scenery, the animals he could play with, and even the grandfather he revered more than anyone else could not fill a certain emptiness within him.
“There are many young prodigies your age in the Murim. The Ten Dragons and Phoenixes are the best among them.”
“Hmm. Then are the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes stronger than me?”
“Huh? What kind of question is that? Of course you, Pung, are—”
“Grandpa?”
“Ahem. Of course you’re still lacking, Pung.”
“Gasp! Really?”
“O-Of course! The world is vast, and there are many masters. So you’ll have to keep working hard at your martial arts from now on, right?”
“Yeees...”
From the single thoughtless remark his grandfather had let slip, Cheongpung felt the unfamiliar emotion in one corner of his heart grow stronger.
Only later did he learn its name.
Competitive pride.
Which of us is stronger?
He wanted to find out. He wanted to pit his martial arts against theirs and spend time with them.
And so Cheongpung left Huashan and ventured into the world. Then, on a sunny winter day, he met him.
“If it wouldn’t be too much trouble, may I have one candied hawthorn skewer?”
“...Mujin. Give him one.”
That was Cheongpung’s first meeting with Jin Taekyung.
His Benefactor in name, his friend in truth—and now, his one and only true rival.
A gentle smile touched Cheongpung’s lips.
“I know. My Benefactor feels the same way I do.”
Flames rose in the First Fiend’s eyes as he watched this.
This greenhorn would have died long ago if not for the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s orders, yet he dared to ignore him. That alone had sealed his fate.
“You little bastard...”
The First Fiend raised his twin axes, their blades caked with scraps of human flesh.
Then he saw what was happening before him and froze like a statue.
Swooshhh.
The wind was blowing.
A scarlet wind of qi flowed from Cheongpung’s body, slid down his wrist, and streamed into his sword.
It passed over the plum blossom engraved upon the hilt, coiled around the blade, and finally bloomed into a single crimson plum blossom.
Crackle-crackle-crackle!
A halo of light, more brilliant and destructive than anything else.
A dazed voice escaped between the First Fiend’s lips as he stared at the unbelievable sight.
“...Sword Force.”
The product of great martial artists. Proof that its wielder had reached the exalted realm known as Supreme Peak.
Yet the twenty-three-year-old young man’s face wore an innocent smile wholly unsuited to a great martial artist.
“So, shall we begin?”

paragraphs: Kraaaaaash!

It was the claw of a fire dragon descending from the heavens—a force of destruction that could erase anything in its path.
This is...
In a moment split into ever-smaller fragments, the Western Heaven Demon Lord thought,
I can’t evade it.
This was no strike he could avoid by retreating a few steps.
Then what could he do? Before he could even form the question, the body that had survived countless life-and-death duels was already moving.
Whoosh!
Dark-red Sword Force surged from his waist and collided with the blue flames.
Boom!
A tremendous roar erupted, and a shock wave swept through my entire body. My ears went numb, and the breath caught in my throat.
Sword and spear collided in a burst of dark-red light. The next instant, I went flying as though someone had yanked me backward.
Bang! Bang! KABOOM!
The thick wall of sedimentary rock crumbled like castella the moment my back struck it.
I knocked away a stalactite falling toward my eyes and twisted around in midair.
The instant my feet hit the ground, they plowed furrows through the solid stone floor.
Krrrrrk!
Damn it. I must have flown at least thirty feet.
I tore off my leather shoes, their soles completely gone, tossed them aside, and glared at the bastard in the distance.
“Fucking bastard. You’re pretty good, huh?”
Even through the thick cloud of dust, I could see the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s stiff expression.
He silently looked down at the sword blade broken clean in half and his blood-soaked grip before opening his mouth.
“That spear is a divine weapon.”
“Divine? That’s a bit much.”
“What martial art was that?”
I answered without hesitation.
“Get Hit and Fucking Die Technique.”
“I’m beginning to understand why the Blood Lord called you arrogant. And... why he wanted to kill you so badly.”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s gaze swept over me.
“You’re dangerous.”
“I am kind of dangerous. Maybe that’s why all the women avoid me.”

“Cheongpung is certainly remarkable, reaching Supreme Peak at such a young age, but even he cannot compare to you. To be honest, you have far exceeded my expectations. Despite being only at Peak, you managed to wound me.”
I wasn’t surprised. I had already sensed that Cheongpung had broken through the wall and reached Supreme Peak.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s accurate assessment of my martial arts realm followed the same logic.
“Was that a compliment?”
“Of course. But do not be too pleased. I do not like people who exceed my expectations.”
Speaking in a low voice, the Western Heaven Demon Lord clenched and unclenched his bloodied palm. Sticky blood dripped down, wetting the rocks and sand.
“My execution of Four Ounces Deflecting a Thousand Catties was flawless. Yet I still failed to redirect your strike completely. A strike from a green young man who has not even advanced beyond Peak.”
Four Ounces Deflecting a Thousand Catties—the martial principle of controlling a thousand catties with only four ounces.

And just as he said, the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s use of Four Ounces Deflecting a Thousand Catties had been flawless. Even after being caught off guard, his attempt to calmly and precisely redirect Heavenly Strike had been impressive enough to earn my secret admiration.
But if there was one thing he had failed to anticipate...
“I’m a little stronger than I look.”
He wasn’t facing an ordinary Peak master.
A Third Rate could not contend with a Second Rate, and a Second Rate could only kneel before a First Rate.
The higher the realm, the wider the gulf and the more overwhelming the difference in strength. That was common sense in this world—the common sense of the Murim.
But I defied common sense.
“Call me a physical Supreme Peak master.”
“A physical Supreme Peak master. I have no idea what that means, but if you say so, then so be it. Understood.”
I stared at the nodding Western Heaven Demon Lord in disbelief.
“...What exactly do you understand?”
“Live long enough and you experience all manner of things. Compared to the supernatural powers I know of, what you’ve shown is merely a drop in the bucket.”
With a faint smile, the Western Heaven Demon Lord raised one arm.
The movement was so natural that it was hard to believe he had been one-armed until only ten days ago.
That arm had to be one of the supernatural powers he was talking about.
“Everything shall unfold according to the will of the most exalted Lord of Heaven. Why not abandon your futile hopes and surrender?”
“Surrender?”
“If you do, I will personally petition the Lord of Heaven to put your talents to good use. Even the Blood Lord will not dare touch you.”
“Wow. You’ve got it all planned out.”
“May I take that as your consent?”
“Hmm, wait a second. I just thought of something better.”
I slowly walked toward the Western Heaven Demon Lord as I continued.

“Stories like this always end with good triumphing over evil anyway. So stop screwing around in Dark Heaven or Cheonggyecheon or whatever and come over to the orthodox faction. I’ll put in a good word with Grandpa Sword Saint and get you an easy job.”
“Heh. Well, this is something.”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord stepped forward with a faint smile.
“What a pity. Don’t regret this when you meet the Blood Lord.”
“Every bastard who’s said that to me is kneeling with his head planted before Yama by now.”
“Perhaps it’s your youth, but you’re far too hot-blooded. If you expect the same stroke of luck you enjoyed at the start, forget it. I know that strike was your full strength.”
“That’s the best bullshit I’ve heard all year. Have you been taking bullshit lessons from the yellow dog next door?”
I answered casually, but unfortunately, the Western Heaven Demon Lord was right.
A surprise attack had to end everything in one strike. Either cripple the opponent or kill them.
Breaking his weapon and tearing open his hand wasn’t enough.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord was a master far above me. Showing him my full strength without inflicting any significant injury had been a painful mistake.
Should I have used One Annihilation from the start?
What would have happened if I’d gone all in from the beginning?
I cast the thought aside. Even if I could return to that moment, I probably still wouldn’t be able to stake everything on one move.
I had to avoid gambles that left only total victory or utter ruin—especially when lives other than my own hung in the balance.
Besides... I haven’t played all my cards yet.
Step. Step.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord and I. He and I. We slowly approached each other.
Unlike our first clash, neither of us launched Finger Qi or daggers.
We measured the distance, watched each other’s hands and feet, and waited for the right moment.
A moment exactly like this one.
Snap!
The Western Heaven Demon Lord moved first.
He erased thirty feet in a single step, his hand blurring. Ink-black Sword Force burned along his crooked, serpentine Snake Sword.
Avoid a direct clash at all costs.
If there was one gap even the System couldn’t bridge, it was enlightenment.
The difference between someone who had attained the insight required to reach Supreme Peak and someone who had not was as vast as heaven and earth.
No matter how great my strength was, if I repeatedly clashed with Sword Force, I would inevitably suffer internal injuries.
Whoosh! Boom!
The Sword Force split the ground, blasting out a crater that looked like something from a movie. If I hadn’t barely dodged the strike, it would have cut me in half.
I retreated and flicked my hand.
Inventory open. Summon.
Shhk-shhk-shhk!
I had never formally learned the art of throwing blades, but with enough force and speed behind them, the daggers were deadly in their own right.
Not that it mattered against the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
Slice!
A single horizontal line flashed through the air.
Ink-black Sword Energy shot from his blade, slicing through the daggers and flying straight at me.
I tilted my head, and searing heat and Sword Energy grazed past me.
Boom!
Ignoring the roar and tremor behind me, I planted my foot.
Grind. Crack!
The solid stone floor split like a spiderweb. The next instant, I shot forward like a streak of light.
I moved with enough speed to rival a Supreme Peak movement technique—perhaps even surpass one.
“As expected!”
With a short exclamation, the Western Heaven Demon Lord brought his sword down.
Ink-black Sword Force, so dark that it dimmed the very air around it, swept across my body.
It would have cut me apart, if not for the thought that had flashed through my mind a fraction of an instant earlier.
Thirty points each into Agility and Strength.
Swoosh.
The change came with dazzling speed. My whole body grew lighter, while my muscles gained density and elasticity, squeezing out every last bit of strength.
As I stepped upon the wind, the ink-black Sword Force sliced through empty air.
Kraaaaaash!
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes flew wide.
It was already too late for him to pull back his sword. He thrust out his other hand, trying to seize the spear hurtling toward his chest.
His reflexes were astonishing.
Just as astonishing was the fact that my prediction had been exactly right.
Inventory open. Store.
Whoosh!
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s Force-wreathed hand swept through empty air.
The spear that had seemed certain to fall into his grasp—White Flame—was now safely tucked away somewhere in my inventory.
This was the moment I had been waiting for.
Flame Divine Palm.
My right hand, wreathed in blue flames, slammed into the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s abdomen.
Boom!
His body lifted slightly into the air amid the tremendous heat. At that exact moment, I drove my waiting left fist forward.
Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist.
Crack!
The strike that had brought down a cliff buried itself in the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s side.
The impact ran back through my fingertips. His body flew like a cannonball and smashed into the wall.
Bang! KRA-KA-BOOM!
The entire underground prison shuddered. At the same time, unbearable weakness and hunger washed over me.
I had poured everything I had into every movement of that exchange. No wonder ragged breaths spilled from my lips.
“Whew.”
Rumble.
I steadied my breathing and slowly walked forward through the stones raining down around me.
Driven deep into the solid rock, the Western Heaven Demon Lord stared at me with unfocused eyes.
“I was definitely trying to catch the spear... How did you...”
“It’s probably something like those supernatural powers you believe in.”
“Cough. I see. Then is that also how you suddenly became faster?”
“Yeah. A few perfectly good lives were wasted because of you. They were bastards who deserved to die anyway, though.”
“What do you mean?”
“This is an underground prison. Haven’t you noticed anything strange?”
After a brief silence, the Western Heaven Demon Lord answered.
“...There are no prisoners.”
“Correct.”
“How did you do it? Did you perhaps use the Essence-Siphoning Great Technique on them?”
“You could say that, in a way.”
The difference was that the Essence-Siphoning Great Technique absorbed an opponent’s qi, while I sucked up EXP.
Thanks to those guys, I earned sixty points. It was a stroke of genius.
Instead of destroying the prisoners’ dantians, the Sichuan Tang Clan had chosen to suppress their internal energy and shackle them.
That way, they could live longer. That way, the clan could make them taste hell through prolonged torture.
Thanks to that, the dozen or so prisoners other than the Heavenly Power Demon had become nourishment for me.
“Cough. The Essence-Siphoning Great Technique. I see. So that was it.”
“Are you satisfied now?”
“If I ask, will you answer?”
“Yeah. So...”
I looked down at the Western Heaven Demon Lord as he weakly nodded.
“Drop the lousy act and get up. And enough with the coughing when you’re not even bringing up blood.”
“Well, this is something.”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes, which had seemed ready to go out at any moment, curved into crescents.
“Apparently, I’m really no good at this sort of thing.”
Fucking bastard.

chapters.title: Chapter 359
paragraphs: Rustle.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord brushed the bits of stone from his body, then rolled his neck from side to side. His brow furrowed as his bones ground against one another.
“Your fists pack quite a punch. Without my Body-Protecting Qi, I might have been seriously injured.”
Quite a punch, my ass.
I let out a deep sigh as I watched him get up as though nothing had happened after taking both my full-powered Flame Divine Palm and Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist.
“Forget the Body-Protecting Qi. Isn’t it cheating for someone like you to equip gear too?”
“Gear? What is that?”
I pointed at the black-scaled armor visible through the tears in his yellow robe.
“That thing you’re wearing underneath, you bastard.”
“Ah. You mean the Black Dragon Armor.”
“The Black Dragon Armor?”
Now that was one hell of a cool name.
I didn’t know exactly what the Black Dragon Armor was, but its defensive capabilities were so impressive that even calling it a divine weapon didn’t seem like enough.
It had blocked two full-powered attacks, yet all it had lost were a few scales.
With that level of defense, fists and palms won’t cut it.
The armor worn by Dark Heaven’s ordinary martial artists had been formidable too, but it was nothing compared to the Black Dragon Armor.
An eye for an eye. A tooth for a tooth. A divine weapon for a divine weapon.
As long as he had the Black Dragon Armor, I needed White Flame to inflict a fatal wound on him.
Unless...
My gaze probed him for another opening. The Western Heaven Demon Lord smiled faintly.
“The more I see of you, the more interesting you become. Your strange techniques are one thing, but I like your refusal to back down.”
“So? Want to date?”
“I must politely decline. I already have a lover I’ve been with for many years.”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord gently stroked his sword’s winding blade. Ink-black Sword Force rose from the clean break where half the blade had snapped off.
“I’ve seen all your cards. Now it’s my turn.”
With that quiet murmur, the Western Heaven Demon Lord stepped forward. A suffocating aura rippled behind him like wings.
Only then did I realize it.
His martial arts had reached a realm far beyond what I’d imagined.
“...Damn it.”
Deng.
I could almost hear a bell ringing somewhere to announce the start of round two.
But this wasn’t a boxing match that ended after twelve rounds. There were no spectators to cheer or groan, no staff to throw in the towel.
This match would end only when one of us staked his life—nothing less.
Inventory open. Summon.
The cold spear shaft settled into my grip. I drew a deep breath and leveled the spearhead at the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
“Come at me.”
He didn’t hesitate.
Snap!
The Western Heaven Demon Lord extended one foot.
Shifting Form and Position.
His vanished figure reappeared in midair above my head.
Every hair on my body stood on end as I leaned backward.
Saaak! Boom!
His heel missed the bridge of my nose by a hair and slammed into the ground. The floor caved in, sending fragments of stone flying in every direction.
Blood trickled from the bridge of my nose where the wind pressure had sliced it, but I wasn’t given even a moment to wipe it away.
Shh-shh-shh-shhk!
Ink-black Sword Energy rained down from every direction, slashing and sweeping toward my waist, chest, and stomach without distinction.
They were attacks I could never have dodged in the past.
But not anymore.
I can see them.
In the slowed world, I sensed the Sword Energy hurtling toward me.
I could picture where that destructive energy was headed and how I needed to move to evade it.
My body was already moving ahead of my thoughts.
Kra-kra-kra-kaboom!
I dodged some attacks and knocked others aside with my spear. Thick clouds of dust billowed into the air, and craters like something out of a war movie pockmarked the ground.
And then...
Whooong!
Ink-black Sword Force gleaming with a murky light burst through the dust cloud. His gaze calm and steady, the Western Heaven Demon Lord brought his sword down in a diagonal slash.
I had no way of knowing what martial art or form he was using.
But I knew one thing.
If I backed down here, all that awaited me was death.
I have to strike back.
I needed power strong enough to stand against Sword Force. This was the moment to use the best move I had.
The answer had been there from the beginning.
One Annihilation.
Grind.

Every muscle in my body drew taut like a bowstring. My foot shot forward first, and my waist, bent as far back as it could go, snapped forward. The rotational force flowed through my shoulder and arm and poured into the spearhead.
Kraaaaaash!
It was a concentration of energy far too massive to be called mere Spear Energy.
The spearhead surged forward, wreathed in blue flames. It burned through the air and devoured the dust cloud as it hurtled toward a single man.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes widened. At the same time, his blade trembled, and an even greater mass of Sword Force erupted from it.
The next instant, blue flame and black darkness collided.
KABOOOOOM!
A roar unlike anything I had ever heard erupted as everything within a radius of over a hundred feet shattered and exploded.
Part of the ceiling collapsed under the impact, and the incredibly solid rock was pulverized into drifting dust.
Amid it all, one man remained standing.
“Damn it.”
Even my full-powered One Annihilation hadn’t worked.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord shook his head at my dejected expression. Blood ran down from his shoulder. That was all One Annihilation had left behind.
“There’s no need to be disappointed. It was a sufficiently powerful form. For a moment, it even sent a chill through my heart.”
“Let me ask you one thing.”
“Anything.”
“If I hadn’t wasted my strength earlier and had opened with that strike... could I have killed you?”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord considered it carefully before answering.
“I believe you could have taken one of my arms. Perhaps even more than that. But you would have been the one to die.”
“Damn it. I knew it.”
“I think it’s time to end this.”
Whooooosh.
It didn’t even surprise me anymore. Sword Force surged like water from an inexhaustible spring and lashed toward me like a whip.
I gritted my teeth as the drain on my internal energy left me weak to the point of collapse.
“It’s... not over yet.”
I drew up every last bit of internal energy I had and unleashed the Fire Dragon Divine Spear.
The blue flames were visibly smaller than before. They shot toward the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s exposed throat.
Screeeeeech!
The next instant, I met his unwavering gaze and realized it.
He read me.
By the time the realization flashed through my mind, it was already too late. The Sword Force that had seemed poised to cut me down abruptly changed course in midair and struck the spearhead.
Boom!
A roar like the sky splitting apart rang out. I clenched my teeth and held on to the spear shaft as it bucked violently in my hands.
My ankles were already buried deep in the ground when the Sword Force swept toward me.
Shh-shh-shh-shh-shhk!
Above, below, left, and right.
Terrifying energy hurtled in from thirty-six directions around me.
Every nerve in my body screamed as I swung my spear like a madman.
Boom! Kra-kra-kra-kaboom!
My body staggered and my breath caught with every strike I deflected.
This wasn’t a matter of speed or strength.
It was martial arts—and internal energy.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s martial arts occupied a distant realm beyond my reach, and the terrifying internal energy transmitted through my spear battered me from within.
What the hell...!
Blood sprayed between my clenched teeth. My torn hands had been covered in blood for some time already.
I squeezed out every last ounce of strength and swung my spear at the ink-black Sword Force cleaving toward my chest.
The second form of the Fire Dragon Divine Spear.
Heavenly Strike.
Screeeeeech! Boom!
But unlike before, the fire dragon’s claw was pitifully weak, while the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s ink-black Sword Force hadn’t lost even a fraction of its power.
Krrrrk!
I was driven backward, carving a long furrow through the ground.
Before me, the underground prison shook as though caught in an earthquake, thick clouds of dust filling the air.
He’s gone.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord was nowhere to be seen. Not ahead of me, to either side, or above.
That left only one possibility.
I spun around and unleashed a palm strike.
Bang! Boom!
Two sounds rang out at once.
The heat of the Flame Divine Palm burned through the air, while the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s palm struck my chest.
My vision went white. Then came the agony of my heart meridian tearing apart strand by strand. I swallowed the blood surging up my throat and regained control of my body as I was hurled backward.
“That was remarkable. I mean it.”
It was pure instinct.
At the quiet voice that suddenly came from beside me, my arm moved on its own. The hand blade shooting toward the back of my neck struck my forearm instead.
Crack!
Pain flooded through me with the sound of bone shifting out of place. Then the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s foot lashed out like a whip and buried itself in my side.
Thud! Boom!
I smashed through the rock and became embedded in the wall. The Western Heaven Demon Lord slowly walked toward me.
Admiration and delight filled his eyes.
“Incredible. Truly incredible. Do you know what you just did?”
I spat out a mouthful of bloody phlegm.
“No, you fucking bastard.”
“You should be proud. You lasted more than three hundred moves against me while I was fighting at full strength.”
“Three hundred moves. I’m crying tears of joy.”
“You don’t seem particularly happy, so let me put it another way. What if I told you the Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun and her Elders lasted more than five hundred moves?”
“Nope. Still not happy.”
“Why not?”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord looked genuinely baffled. I tossed him a curt answer.
“They died anyway.”
Three hundred moves, five hundred moves, a thousand moves—it didn’t matter. If you lost the fight, all that awaited the loser was death.
The Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun and the Poison King had been no exception.
And...
Neither was I, probably.
“Cough.”
Blood seeped between my parted lips.
I wanted to get up as casually as the Western Heaven Demon Lord had earlier, but my body was in no condition for that.
Internal injuries aside, my left arm is fractured, and I think I’ve cracked some bones in my chest.
I’d really taken one hell of a beating. No wonder breathing had been difficult for a while now.
Panting, I planted White Flame like a cane and dragged myself upright.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes lit up.
“Do you still have something left to show me?”
“Of course.”
“That must also be the power of those supernatural powers. Show me. Quickly! Quickly!”
“I was planning to.”
I leveled my spear at the Western Heaven Demon Lord, who was practically bouncing with excitement like a child.
And that was all I did.
“What are you waiting for? Come at me.”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord stared at me in confusion.
“What did you just do?”
“I’m showing you. The supernatural powers you wanted to see.”
“What?”

“I’m good with my body, but hopeless with my head. I’m such a dumbass that I even failed the Level Eight Hanja exam. Then I came across the term ‘supernatural powers’ in a martial-arts novel. I didn’t know what it meant, so I looked it up.”
Even if I explained it like this, he probably wouldn’t understand half of what I was saying.

My vision wavered. Every time I exhaled, my lungs prickled as though they were being stabbed with needles, and the spear shaft that had always felt light now seemed like a boulder weighing ten thousand geun.
Even so...
“‘Supernatural powers.’ Mysterious beings or phenomena that are difficult to explain through reason. That’s what it meant.”
I neither staggered nor collapsed. I simply stared at the Western Heaven Demon Lord and continued speaking slowly.
“What’s so special about supernatural powers? A bastard who keeps fighting even after he’s been reduced to this—that’s supernatural powers.”
Remaining Stat Points? None.
Physical condition? It was a miracle I could still stand.
Now that everything had flown out like the contents of Pandora’s box, the one thing left inside me wasn’t hope.
Sheer grit.
Hope could make someone rise again, but it could also make them weak.
But as long as that grit remained—as long as I still possessed the will to fight to the bitter end—I wouldn’t fall.
No.
I had decided not to fall.
Because there were people I had to protect. The Fire King and Cheongpung had fought for my sake, so even if I had to become a ghost instead of some supernatural being, I had to stop this bastard.
I gathered every last scrap of internal energy. The meager handful of qi flowed unsteadily toward the spearhead.
A faint wisp of Spear Energy lit the darkness like a firefly.
“Quit spouting bullshit and come at me, you bastard with a supernatural-powers fetish.”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord fell silent.
Countless emotions passed across his face. When they were gone, only a pair of deeply solemn eyes remained.
Swish!

The Western Heaven Demon Lord brushed the bits of stone from his body, then rolled his neck from side to side.
His brow furrowed as his bones ground against one another.

What is that?”

You mean the Black Dragon Armor.”

Now that was one hell of a cool name.

It had blocked two full-powered attacks, yet all it had lost were a few scales.
With that level of defense, fists and palms won’t cut it.
The armor worn by Dark Heaven’s ordinary martial artists had been formidable too, but it was nothing compared to the Black Dragon Armor.
An eye for an eye.
A tooth for a tooth.
A divine weapon for a divine weapon.
As long as he had the Black Dragon Armor, I needed White Flame to inflict a fatal wound on him.
Unless...

The Western Heaven Demon Lord smiled faintly.

Your strange techniques are one thing, but I like your refusal to back down.”

Want to date?”

I already have a lover I’ve been with for many years.”

His martial arts had reached a realm far beyond what I’d imagined.

Deng.

There were no spectators to cheer or groan, no staff to throw in the towel.
This match would end only when one of us staked his life—nothing less.
Inventory open.
Summon.
