He didn’t hesitate.
Snap!
The Western Heaven Demon Lord extended one foot.
Shifting Form and Position.
His vanished figure reappeared in midair above my head.
Every hair on my body stood on end as I leaned backward.
Saaak!
Boom!
His heel missed the bridge of my nose by a hair and slammed into the ground.
The floor caved in, sending fragments of stone flying in every direction.
Blood trickled from the bridge of my nose where the wind pressure had sliced it, but I wasn’t given even a moment to wipe it away.
Shh-shh-shh-shhk!
Ink-black Sword Energy rained down from every direction, slashing and sweeping toward my waist, chest, and stomach without distinction.
They were attacks I could never have dodged in the past.
But not anymore.
I can see them.
In the slowed world, I sensed the Sword Energy hurtling toward me.
I could picture where that destructive energy was headed and how I needed to move to evade it.
My body was already moving ahead of my thoughts.
Kra-kra-kra-kaboom!
I dodged some attacks and knocked others aside with my spear.
Thick clouds of dust billowed into the air, and craters like something out of a war movie pockmarked the ground.
And then...
Whooong!
Ink-black Sword Force gleaming with a murky light burst through the dust cloud.
His gaze calm and steady, the Western Heaven Demon Lord brought his sword down in a diagonal slash.
I had no way of knowing what martial art or form he was using.
But I knew one thing.
If I backed down here, all that awaited me was death.
I have to strike back.
I needed power strong enough to stand against Sword Force.
This was the moment to use the best move I had.
The answer had been there from the beginning.
One Annihilation.
Grind.
Every muscle in my body drew taut like a bowstring.
My foot shot forward first, and my waist, bent as far back as it could go, snapped forward.
The rotational force flowed through my shoulder and arm and poured into the spearhead.
Kraaaaaash!
It was a concentration of energy far too massive to be called mere Spear Energy.
The spearhead surged forward, wreathed in blue flames.
It burned through the air and devoured the dust cloud as it hurtled toward a single man.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes widened.
At the same time, his blade trembled, and an even greater mass of Sword Force erupted from it.
The next instant, blue flame and black darkness collided.
KABOOOOOM!
A roar unlike anything I had ever heard erupted as everything within a radius of over a hundred feet shattered and exploded.
Part of the ceiling collapsed under the impact, and the incredibly solid rock was pulverized into drifting dust.
Amid it all, one man remained standing.
“Damn it.”
Even my full-powered One Annihilation hadn’t worked.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord shook his head at my dejected expression.
Blood ran down from his shoulder.
That was all One Annihilation had left behind.
“There’s no need to be disappointed.
It was a sufficiently powerful form.
For a moment, it even sent a chill through my heart.”
“Let me ask you one thing.”
“Anything.”
“If I hadn’t wasted my strength earlier and had opened with that strike... could I have killed you?”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord considered it carefully before answering.
“I believe you could have taken one of my arms.
Perhaps even more than that.
But you would have been the one to die.”
“Damn it.
I knew it.”
“I think it’s time to end this.”
Whooooosh.
It didn’t even surprise me anymore.
Sword Force surged like water from an inexhaustible spring and lashed toward me like a whip.
I gritted my teeth as the drain on my internal energy left me weak to the point of collapse.
“It’s... not over yet.”
I drew up every last bit of internal energy I had and unleashed the Fire Dragon Divine Spear.
The blue flames were visibly smaller than before.
They shot toward the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s exposed throat.
Screeeeeech!

He read me.

The Sword Force that had seemed poised to cut me down abruptly changed course in midair and struck the spearhead.

chapters.title: Chapter 360
paragraphs: I didn’t know how much time had passed.
Time crawled for me, while the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s rushed by as swift and violent as the Yangtze’s current I had seen a few weeks ago.
One thing was certain: even now, at this very moment, time kept moving.
Thud!
I saw neither a windup nor the movement itself. By the time I realized the Western Heaven Demon Lord had taken a step, my head had already snapped back.
Before I could even regain my balance, the sound of splitting air pierced my ears.
Shhk, thud! Thud-thud-thud!
Shoulder, chest, stomach.
Palm and fist, each laden with internal energy, hammered my upper body in fluid succession.
My bones shifted with sickening cracks, and agony washed my vision white. I gritted my teeth.
Crk.
A molar shattered, and for a brief moment, my mind cleared.
“Raaaagh!”
Whoosh!
With a cry squeezed from the depths of my lungs, I swung my fist.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord caught my hopelessly slow, wide-open punch and clicked his tongue.
“You still have strength left?”
Crack!
Even muscles and bones hardened like steel were nothing more than kindling before the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
His hook-like hand seized my wrist and twisted. Flesh and bone were crushed together.
The bones in my already broken left arm splintered, sending horrific pain through me.
“Gaaaaaagh!”
“Don’t worry. I’ll summon some skilled healers to treat you later.”
“Go... fuck yourself!”
I thrust my still-usable right arm at the Western Heaven Demon Lord as he wiped the blood splattered across his face.
White Flame’s spearhead, wreathed in faint Spear Energy, stabbed toward his lower body.
Whoosh. Clack.
But the spearhead was stopped with absurd ease.
Not by the Black Dragon Armor or Body-Protecting Qi, but by the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s bare hand.
“Futile.”
His hand, wrapped in ink-black Force, tightened around the spearhead. The faint energy gathered there vanished as though swallowed by darkness.
“Give up. The outcome won’t change.”
With those quiet words, the Western Heaven Demon Lord yanked on the spearhead.
I clung desperately to the shaft as it tried to slip from my flayed, blood-soaked grip.
Searing pain surged through me, but it was bearable.
Pain was something I’d endured more than enough of, both in the past and now.
Whoosh, crash!
I tumbled forward with the spear shaft. A handful of dirt entered my mouth and mixed with the blood.
The ice-cold, foul-smelling floor of the underground prison somehow felt more comfortable than ever.
I’m sleepy.
If I closed my eyes now, I felt as though I could fall asleep immediately.
Maybe after dreaming one long dream for days on end, I would wake up in the modern world instead of Murim.
A plush seat on a private plane bound for Sichuan, China, would be fine. So would my room at Hope Goshiwon, steeped in the musty smell of a bachelor living alone.
Maybe all of this is a dream.
I had been through too much in the space of little more than a year.
From F-rank Hunter Jin Taekyung to the Third Young Master of the Jin Family of Taiyuan. From a disgrace who dragged his family’s name through the mud to the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi.
I had witnessed brutal wars and countless deaths. I had met so many people.

Jin Wikyung, who absolutely doted on his younger brother, and Jin Mukyung, who would have loved to kill his. Hyuk Mujin, who had shared life and death with me while always remaining at my side. Cheongpung, who was both my friend and my rival.
And...
Old Master.
My eyelids, which had been slowly sliding shut without my realizing it, stopped.
That's right. The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.
He was behind me, and I stood before him.
That was why I could neither fall nor run away.
That arrogant bastard. Taekyung, go on ahead.
H-hyung!
I’ll catch up soon.
Three years had already passed, but I would never forget what happened that day.
I had failed to protect the people precious to me, and I had survived through their sacrifice.
Yet even after gaining power beyond anything my past self could have imagined, I had repeated the same mistake.
What do you think? The Dance of the Fire God and Demon. Pretty damn incredible, isn’t it?
Jeok Cheongang had been smiling then.
That smile held the joy of avenging his closest friend—and the relief of protecting one little brat he couldn't tell was his disciple or his enemy.
“Yes. It’s incredible...”
A small voice escaped through my torn, swollen lips.
The floor of the underground prison no longer felt comfortable.
Feeling its bitter cold and stench, I began to push myself up.
I braced my still-usable right arm against the floor and supported myself on both knees.
My body felt ready to break apart at any moment, and every movement was slow, but I refused to give up.
When I finally stood upright on my trembling legs, the first thing I encountered was a pair of deeply sunken eyes.
“Impressive. Almost foolishly so.”
Thud!
My nose broke, and my head snapped backward. But I did not fall or stagger back.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s hand held my shoulder like a shackle.
“How many times must I tell you? It’s already over.”
Crunch.
The bones in my shoulder were crushed. The spear shaft slipped limply from my weakened grip.
Horrific pain should have followed, but what I actually felt was faint and distant.
“If you’re waiting for help, you’ve miscalculated. The Sichuan Tang Clan will be destroyed. No, it may all be over already.”
Crack!
This time, it was my legs.
Both shins—the only parts of me still intact—broke at once, and I lost my balance.
Ironically, the only reason I remained upright was that the Western Heaven Demon Lord had not let go.

“Who could possibly come to your aid as they did in Henan? The Sword Saint, who won’t hear this news for another half month? The Sword Saint’s successor, who is likely fighting desperately even now? Or perhaps...”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord turned his head.
Beyond the empty underground prison, shattered and collapsed by our clash, his gaze settled upon a tightly shut iron door.
“Your master, who still hasn’t regained consciousness?”
“Cough.”
“Nothing will change. Today, the Tang Clan, Qingcheng, and Emei will be destroyed. And all of you...”
“Cough!”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s words cut off.
A sticky liquid of dirt and blood covered his face.
He clearly had not expected someone with all four limbs crushed to do such a thing.
For one fleeting instant, he froze with his hand around my neck.
I drove my head forward with every ounce of strength I had left.
Thud!
The heavy impact snapped the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s head back.
My internal energy had run dry long ago, and my severe Internal Injuries made it difficult to move even a single finger. I did not know where that strength had come from. I did not even know myself.
And...
It’s not like I have time to think about it anymore.
That had been my final act of defiance.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord rubbed his reddened forehead and let out a quiet laugh.
“You truly are... a dangerous man.”
I answered in a faint, unfocused voice.
“I should’ve cracked your skull.”
“If I hadn’t raised my Body-Protecting Qi at the last moment, you might have.”
“You monstrous bastard.”
“Hah. It feels strange hearing that from you.”
Unfathomable emotions flickered through the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes as he looked at me.
At first glance, they seemed like anger. At the same time, they felt almost like admiration.
Before I could make sense of them, an unexpected roar rang out.
Rumble-rumble-rumble, boom!
The sound had come from neither me nor the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
The underground prison.
The entire vast space, thousands of feet across, shook. Fist-sized stones fell from the ceiling, and cracks spread across the ground.
The noise and tremors soon subsided, but a deep furrow appeared between the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s brows.
“...I’d better hurry.”
The instant he muttered those words and glanced at the ceiling, heaven and earth flipped.
A moment later, a slight impact traveled through my back.
Boom!
A wall.
He had thrown me against it.
“Cough.”
As I spat up blood, his calm voice reached my ears.
“Sit there for a while. I’ll be back soon.”
“If you’re still alive by then, I’ll take you with me. If you happen to be dead...”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord paused before continuing.
“That wouldn’t be so bad either. You’re a dangerous man.”
“W-wait.”
I reached with all the strength I had left toward the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s retreating back.
I had to stop him. I had to keep him from capturing Jeok Cheongang and the Divine Physician.
But not a single part of my body would move as I wanted.
“Cough. Bleegh!”
Dark-red blood gushed from my open mouth.
The chunks mixed in with it were...
Damn it. Pieces of my organs.
It was neither my first time seeing such a thing nor an unexpected sight, but crushing despair weighed down my entire body.
My limbs were crippled, and I had suffered a fatal Internal Injury.
In my heart, I had already thrown myself into the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s path. But with my arms and legs crushed, I couldn’t take a single step.
“Ah.”
I raised my head blankly with a groan.
The corridor where the Western Heaven Demon Lord had disappeared stood empty.
The place, devastated by our clash, was filled with traces of craters large and small, collapsed walls, and other destruction.
The prison where prisoners had still been confined half a day earlier was now strewn with bent bars, fallen rocks, and things like broken chains.
The sight made me realize it.
It’s over.
I had fought, and I had lost.
I had tried to stop him, but I couldn’t. I had tried to protect them, but I had failed.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord had been telling the truth.
The kind of luck we had seen in Henan would not happen again. The Tang Clan, Emei, and Qingcheng were headed for destruction, and Cheongpung could not handle them all alone.
He’ll probably die or be captured.
I wished he would run instead, but that would never happen.
That was the kind of person Cheongpung was. Even drenched in blood, he would return to the underground prison to save his Benefactor.
I stared into the darkness beyond, where the exit lay, and laughed weakly.
Damn it...
It all felt like my fault.
Cheongpung. Jeok Cheongang. Even the Divine Physician, who had been dragged into this mess for no reason and would suffer because of it.
At least Hyuk Mujin and Gung Gibang had not come with me. That was the only thing I could be grateful for.
Rumble-rumble-rumble.
A slight tremor ran through the ground, accompanied by a roar that seemed to rise from the depths of the earth.
The sound announcing the end of the match.
There had been no need to go twelve rounds like in boxing. I had fallen after only three, and I would probably die soon.
I’m sorry. All of you.
The capsule’s instruction manual had contained one simple rule.
If you die in the Murim, you die in reality, too.
Everything I had built while traveling between those two worlds was crumbling little by little, just like this underground prison.
“I never thought I’d die like this...”
My vision blurred. The pain throughout my body and the sounds reaching my ears slowly faded away.
Then, just as I was about to slip free of every sensation, an old man’s face suddenly appeared before me.
A chain with marks where something had torn it away.
An unusually tall body, so gaunt that every bone stood out.
I called to him in a feeble voice.
“...Heavenly Power Demon.”

sentences.text: I didn’t know how much time had passed.
Time crawled for me, while the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s rushed by as swift and violent as the Yangtze’s current I had seen a few weeks ago.
One thing was certain: even now, at this very moment, time kept moving.
Thud!
I saw neither a windup nor the movement itself.
By the time I realized the Western Heaven Demon Lord had taken a step, my head had already snapped back.
Before I could even regain my balance, the sound of splitting air pierced my ears.
Shhk, thud!
Thud-thud-thud!
Shoulder, chest, stomach.
Palm and fist, each laden with internal energy, hammered my upper body in fluid succession.
My bones shifted with sickening cracks, and agony washed my vision white.
I gritted my teeth.
Crk.
A molar shattered, and for a brief moment, my mind cleared.
“Raaaagh!”
Whoosh!
With a cry squeezed from the depths of my lungs, I swung my fist.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord caught my hopelessly slow, wide-open punch and clicked his tongue.
“You still have strength left?”
Crack!
Even muscles and bones hardened like steel were nothing more than kindling before the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
His hook-like hand seized my wrist and twisted.
Flesh and bone were crushed together.
The bones in my already broken left arm splintered, sending horrific pain through me.
“Gaaaaaagh!”
“Don’t worry.
I’ll summon some skilled healers to treat you later.”
“Go... fuck yourself!”
I thrust my still-usable right arm at the Western Heaven Demon Lord as he wiped the blood splattered across his face.
White Flame’s spearhead, wreathed in faint Spear Energy, stabbed toward his lower body.
Whoosh.
Clack.
But the spearhead was stopped with absurd ease.
Not by the Black Dragon Armor or Body-Protecting Qi, but by the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s bare hand.
“Futile.”
His hand, wrapped in ink-black Force, tightened around the spearhead.
The faint energy gathered there vanished as though swallowed by darkness.
“Give up.
The outcome won’t change.”
With those quiet words, the Western Heaven Demon Lord yanked on the spearhead.
I clung desperately to the shaft as it tried to slip from my flayed, blood-soaked grip.
Searing pain surged through me, but it was bearable.
Pain was something I’d endured more than enough of, both in the past and now.
Whoosh, crash!
I tumbled forward with the spear shaft.
A handful of dirt entered my mouth and mixed with the blood.
The ice-cold, foul-smelling floor of the underground prison somehow felt more comfortable than ever.
I’m sleepy.
If I closed my eyes now, I felt as though I could fall asleep immediately.
Maybe after dreaming one long dream for days on end, I would wake up in the modern world instead of Murim.
A plush seat on a private plane bound for Sichuan, China, would be fine.
So would my room at Hope Goshiwon, steeped in the musty smell of a bachelor living alone.
Maybe all of this is a dream.
I had been through too much in the space of little more than a year.
From F-rank Hunter Jin Taekyung to the Third Young Master of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
From a disgrace who dragged his family’s name through the mud to the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi.
I had witnessed brutal wars and countless deaths.
I had met so many people.
Jin Wikyung, who absolutely doted on his younger brother, and Jin Mukyung, who would have loved to kill his.
Hyuk Mujin, who had shared life and death with me while always remaining at my side.
Cheongpung, who was both my friend and my rival.
And...
Old Master.
My eyelids, which had been slowly sliding shut without my realizing it, stopped.
That's right.
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.
He was behind me, and I stood before him.
That was why I could neither fall nor run away.
That arrogant bastard.
Taekyung, go on ahead.
H-hyung!
I’ll catch up soon.
Three years had already passed, but I would never forget what happened that day.
I had failed to protect the people precious to me, and I had survived through their sacrifice.
Yet even after gaining power beyond anything my past self could have imagined, I had repeated the same mistake.
What do you think?
The Dance of the Fire God and Demon.
Pretty damn incredible, isn’t it?
Jeok Cheongang had been smiling then.
That smile held the joy of avenging his closest friend—and the relief of protecting one little brat he couldn't tell was his disciple or his enemy.
“Yes.
It’s incredible...”
A small voice escaped through my torn, swollen lips.
The floor of the underground prison no longer felt comfortable.
Feeling its bitter cold and stench, I began to push myself up.
I braced my still-usable right arm against the floor and supported myself on both knees.
My body felt ready to break apart at any moment, and every movement was slow, but I refused to give up.
When I finally stood upright on my trembling legs, the first thing I encountered was a pair of deeply sunken eyes.
“Impressive.
Almost foolishly so.”
Thud!
My nose broke, and my head snapped backward.
But I did not fall or stagger back.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s hand held my shoulder like a shackle.
“How many times must I tell you?
It’s already over.”
Crunch.
The bones in my shoulder were crushed.
The spear shaft slipped limply from my weakened grip.
Horrific pain should have followed, but what I actually felt was faint and distant.
“If you’re waiting for help, you’ve miscalculated.
The Sichuan Tang Clan will be destroyed.
No, it may all be over already.”
Crack!
This time, it was my legs.
Both shins—the only parts of me still intact—broke at once, and I lost my balance.
Ironically, the only reason I remained upright was that the Western Heaven Demon Lord had not let go.
“Who could possibly come to your aid as they did in Henan?
The Sword Saint, who won’t hear this news for another half month?
The Sword Saint’s successor, who is likely fighting desperately even now?
Or perhaps...”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord turned his head.
Beyond the empty underground prison, shattered and collapsed by our clash, his gaze settled upon a tightly shut iron door.
“Your master, who still hasn’t regained consciousness?”
“Cough.”
“Nothing will change.
Today, the Tang Clan, Qingcheng, and Emei will be destroyed.
And all of you...”
“Cough!”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s words cut off.
A sticky liquid of dirt and blood covered his face.
He clearly had not expected someone with all four limbs crushed to do such a thing.
For one fleeting instant, he froze with his hand around my neck.
I drove my head forward with every ounce of strength I had left.
Thud!
The heavy impact snapped the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s head back.
My internal energy had run dry long ago, and my severe Internal Injuries made it difficult to move even a single finger.
I did not know where that strength had come from.
I did not even know myself.
And...
It’s not like I have time to think about it anymore.
That had been my final act of defiance.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord rubbed his reddened forehead and let out a quiet laugh.
“You truly are... a dangerous man.”
I answered in a faint, unfocused voice.
“I should’ve cracked your skull.”
“If I hadn’t raised my Body-Protecting Qi at the last moment, you might have.”
“You monstrous bastard.”
“Hah.
It feels strange hearing that from you.”
Unfathomable emotions flickered through the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes as he looked at me.
At first glance, they seemed like anger.
At the same time, they felt almost like admiration.
Before I could make sense of them, an unexpected roar rang out.
Rumble-rumble-rumble, boom!
The sound had come from neither me nor the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
The underground prison.
The entire vast space, thousands of feet across, shook.
Fist-sized stones fell from the ceiling, and cracks spread across the ground.
The noise and tremors soon subsided, but a deep furrow appeared between the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s brows.
“...I’d better hurry.”
The instant he muttered those words and glanced at the ceiling, heaven and earth flipped.
A moment later, a slight impact traveled through my back.
Boom!
A wall.
He had thrown me against it.
“Cough.”
As I spat up blood, his calm voice reached my ears.
“Sit there for a while.
I’ll be back soon.”
“If you’re still alive by then, I’ll take you with me.
If you happen to be dead...”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord paused before continuing.
“That wouldn’t be so bad either.
You’re a dangerous man.”
“W-wait.”
I reached with all the strength I had left toward the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s retreating back.
I had to stop him.
I had to keep him from capturing Jeok Cheongang and the Divine Physician.
But not a single part of my body would move as I wanted.
“Cough.
Bleegh!”
Dark-red blood gushed from my open mouth.
The chunks mixed in with it were...
Damn it.
Pieces of my organs.
It was neither my first time seeing such a thing nor an unexpected sight, but crushing despair weighed down my entire body.
My limbs were crippled, and I had suffered a fatal Internal Injury.
In my heart, I had already thrown myself into the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s path.
But with my arms and legs crushed, I couldn’t take a single step.
“Ah.”
I raised my head blankly with a groan.
The corridor where the Western Heaven Demon Lord had disappeared stood empty.
The place, devastated by our clash, was filled with traces of craters large and small, collapsed walls, and other destruction.
The prison where prisoners had still been confined half a day earlier was now strewn with bent bars, fallen rocks, and things like broken chains.
The sight made me realize it.
It’s over.
I had fought, and I had lost.
I had tried to stop him, but I couldn’t.
I had tried to protect them, but I had failed.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord had been telling the truth.
The kind of luck we had seen in Henan would not happen again.
The Tang Clan, Emei, and Qingcheng were headed for destruction, and Cheongpung could not handle them all alone.
He’ll probably die or be captured.
I wished he would run instead, but that would never happen.
That was the kind of person Cheongpung was.
Even drenched in blood, he would return to the underground prison to save his Benefactor.
I stared into the darkness beyond, where the exit lay, and laughed weakly.
Damn it...
It all felt like my fault.
Cheongpung.
Jeok Cheongang.
Even the Divine Physician, who had been dragged into this mess for no reason and would suffer because of it.
At least Hyuk Mujin and Gung Gibang had not come with me.
That was the only thing I could be grateful for.
Rumble-rumble-rumble.
A slight tremor ran through the ground, accompanied by a roar that seemed to rise from the depths of the earth.
The sound announcing the end of the match.
There had been no need to go twelve rounds like in boxing.
I had fallen after only three, and I would probably die soon.
I’m sorry.
All of you.

If you die in the Murim, you die in reality, too.
Everything I had built while traveling between those two worlds was crumbling little by little, just like this underground prison.
“I never thought I’d die like this...”
My vision blurred.

Then, just as I was about to slip free of every sensation, an old man’s face suddenly appeared before me.
A chain with marks where something had torn it away.
An unusually tall body, so gaunt that every bone stood out.
I called to him in a feeble voice.
“...Heavenly Power Demon.”

chapters.title: Chapter 361
paragraphs: Step. Step.
There was not the slightest trace of urgency or hesitation in the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s stride.
Not even fragments of rock falling from the ceiling to herald the collapse, nor the pitch-black darkness blocking his path, could change that.
The Four Great Demon Lords were beings entitled to walk that way.
Only one thing concerned him: the possibility that he might fail to carry out the exalted Lord of Heaven’s command.
Jin Taekyung. That child held me up for quite some time.
He had never imagined Taekyung would delay him for so long.
As Jin Taekyung came to mind, the Western Heaven Demon Lord unconsciously rubbed his forehead.
He felt a swollen lump beneath his fingers, throbbing with pain. It bothered him more than his torn palm or the blood running down his forearm.
A lump.
Jin Taekyung had been hanging there with all four limbs broken.
His internal energy had clearly been exhausted, and his Internal Injury was severe enough that it would not have been strange for an ordinary Peak master to have died already...
“To think my Body-Protecting Qi couldn’t completely stop it.”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord let out a hollow laugh.
Jin Taekyung had pierced his Body-Protecting Qi with his mere flesh and wounded him. By ordinary common sense, such a thing was utterly impossible.
Two words surfaced in the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s mind.
With everything he had.
Prepared to die.
Is this not supernatural powers in its truest form?
It was unbearably fascinating. At the same time, it sent a chill through his heart.
In terms of martial arts realm, Cheongpung, who had already reached the Supreme Peak, was unquestionably ahead.
But Jin Taekyung felt dangerous for a different reason.
He is strong simply because he is human.
Martial arts far beyond what any Peak master should possess. Tenacity that surpassed all imagination.
Had Jin Taekyung’s strength not run out when it did, the Western Heaven Demon Lord would have ended his life without hesitation.
But now, everything was proceeding smoothly toward its conclusion.
“Is this the place?”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord stopped before a firmly shut iron door. In an underground prison made up mostly of barred cells, the treatment room’s enormous iron door stood out immediately.
Of course, even without such an obvious landmark, it could never have escaped the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s Qi Sense.
No mistake.
Without hesitation, he brought down a hand blade.
The Force coating its edge sliced effortlessly through the handspan-thick steel door and its locking mechanism.
Shhk! Boom!
The bisected iron door crashed to the floor with a deafening roar.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord strode into the treatment room. He spotted someone and smiled faintly.
“Are you the Divine Physician?”
An old man sat in a chair beside a bed made of Cold-Ice Stone. He opened his eyes.
His voice was calm.
“That is merely an empty title bestowed upon me by the people of this world.”
“I have heard plenty of rumors about you. They say no one knows your name or age—not even whether you are a man or a woman. I have wanted to meet you at least once.”
“And now that you have, what do you think?”
“You look much as I imagined. More like an immortal, even, than those Daoist bastards who put on lofty airs as though they lived above the clouds.”
The Divine Physician sighed.
“I wish that were true. If this old man were an immortal, I would also possess the power to drive away fiends.”
“Do I look like a fiend?”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord spread his arms wide and spun in a circle.
He had an ordinary face and an ordinary build. Were it not for his long robe, torn to shreds and soaked in blood, he could have been any unremarkable middle-aged man.
“When the Lord of Heaven descends from the heavens to the mortal realm, four loyal servants stand beneath His almighty power.”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord continued in a gentle voice.
“I am neither a fiend nor an immortal. I am merely a servant who follows His command.”
The sincerity in his voice made the Divine Physician’s eyelids tremble.
The Lord of Heaven? A servant? Whatever the man meant, there could be no doubt that he was utterly insane.
“What nonsense! If you are not a fiend despite slaughtering people without hesitation, then what are you?”
“It is unfortunate. But what can I do? Erasing those who oppose His will is part of my duty.”
“Y-you are...”
The Divine Physician was struck speechless as the Western Heaven Demon Lord gave a quiet sigh.
The thick scent of blood soaked into every word he spoke and every small movement he made, enough to make nausea rise in the Divine Physician’s throat.
“Get out.”
“Hm? What did you say?”
“I said get out. No one is permitted to enter while I am treating a patient. Especially a fiend like you.”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord stared at the Divine Physician’s rigid face, then laughed aloud.
“I thought you were an inflexible physician, but you know how to joke. Divine Physician, the treatment is already over.”
“It is not over.”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord advanced with an amused expression. At the end of his path lay Jeok Cheongang, motionless as a corpse.
“I believe the patient should be moved somewhere else.”
“Before that... you should ask the physician’s permission.”
The Divine Physician rose from his seat, his expression hard.
At that very moment—
Pa-pa-pat!

Dozens of streaks of light shot from his billowing sleeves. Needles large and small flew in straight lines or curved through the air toward the lethal acupoint behind the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s neck.
Yet as he watched them hurtle toward him, the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s smile only deepened.
“How interesting.”
Tudududuk!
He did not move.
The formidable Body-Protecting Qi surrounding him simply did its job.
Dozens of needles struck the Body-Protecting Qi and trembled violently.
“And unfortunate.”
Crunch.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord closed his hand, then opened it again. Invisible energy obeyed its master’s will, seizing the needles and crushing them into a mangled mass.
The Divine Physician might have learned martial arts, but the gulf between him and the Western Heaven Demon Lord was as vast as the distance between heaven and earth.
“I’ll say it again. The treatment is over.”
At the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s quiet declaration, the Divine Physician’s body rose into the air.
Seizing an Object Through Empty Space—a feat possible only for someone possessing terrifying internal energy.
The Divine Physician flew forward as if something had flung him. His face turned deathly pale as the Western Heaven Demon Lord caught him by the throat.
“F-fiend...”
“That hardly seems like something a physician who just unleashed a killing technique should say. Come to think of it, wouldn’t that make you a fiend as well?”
“If I think of the blood that will stain your hands, I will gladly become one!”
Whoosh. Thunk.
The Divine Physician’s palm strike, thrust out with a shout that brought up blood, was blocked with ease.
Crack-crack.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord tightened his grip and broke the old physician’s hand. A strange glint passed through his eyes.
“The Tang Family Head was right. You had it.”
His gaze had settled on the Divine Physician’s hand.
Around one wrinkled finger was something wholly unsuited to a physician.
“So this is the Myriad-Poison Ring...”
A band glowing softly, set with a jewel that seemed to contain both light and darkness.

The Western Heaven Demon Lord gazed at the objective of his mission with rapture, as though bewitched. He carefully removed the Myriad-Poison Ring from the Divine Physician’s finger and slipped it onto his own.
“The Lord of Heaven will be pleased.”
The Divine Physician, who had watched everything unfold, let out a suppressed groan.
“W-what are you planning to do?”
“Don’t concern yourself with it. Your role ends here anyway.”
Whoosh! Thud!
A palm strike that shot forward like a blade pierced the Divine Physician’s abdomen.
His lower dantian shattered. The Divine Physician was hurled across the room, vomiting blood.
“Bweeeeegh!”
“It seems I no longer need the physician’s permission. Wouldn’t you agree?”
The Divine Physician despaired, and the Western Heaven Demon Lord laughed heartily.
It was over. At last, he had obtained the Myriad-Poison Ring desired by the Lord of Heaven and erased from this land three great sects whose influence spanned the realm.
Nothing remained that could stand in his way.
It was time to finish everything and return.
“Come. Let us go together. There is someone who wishes to see you.”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord whispered to Jeok Cheongang, who slept peacefully atop the Cold-Ice Stone, then used Seizing an Object Through Empty Space to draw him closer.
Or rather, he was about to.
Woooooong.
A low, faint sound, like a swarm of bees buzzing.
Only the Western Heaven Demon Lord could have noticed it. It was a tremor in the air, a faint vibration that slowly drew nearer.
Could the collapse have already begun?
The Western Heaven Demon Lord turned toward the source.
Beyond the treatment room, its iron door now gone, a faint light flickered in the pitch-black darkness.
“What is that...”
He deliberately furrowed his brow.
The next instant, his eyes flew wide.
Woooooong! Rumble-rumble-rumble!
The vibration intensified. Wind and air tore apart.
And then—
KRAAAAAA!
A massive light shot forward, obliterating the space in its path.
No.
No—a spear wreathed in blue flames.
A name flashed through the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s mind, and he could no longer hold back his laughter.
“Supernatural powers! Truly, this is supernatural powers!”
As he threw back his head and laughed, a vast darkness surged up and shot forward.
White Flame, engulfed in blue fire, collided with the darkness.
KABOOOOOM!
Amid the deafening blast that shook the underground prison, a voice rang out.
“The sickroom is off-limits unless you’re family or a Disciple. You fucking bastard.”
Step. Step.
I pushed through the cloud of dust and moved forward.
Neither the rocks pouring from the ceiling like rain nor the pitch-black darkness before me could stop my steps.
I simply continued toward the one person somewhere beyond it.
What a monster. Not that I expected something like that to kill him.
I couldn’t see him, but I could feel him—the immense energy coiled within the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
But it didn’t frighten me as much as before.
I calmly clenched my fist. The powerful internal energy overflowing from my entire body felt almost tangible in my hand.
Heavenly Power Demon.
My clash with the Western Heaven Demon Lord had presented him with a new opportunity.
The falling rocks from the collapsing ceiling had broken his restraints, allowing the old man known as a fiend to leave the underground prison for the first time in decades.
And the Heavenly Power Demon’s first words to me had been completely unexpected.
You killed all the other prisoners.
Cough. So?
You bastard. Why did you leave me alive?
Did that bother you so much?
Answer the question. I can cut off your breath right now.
Wait a few more moments. It’ll give out on its own.
You bastard!
It had been a conversation between two cripples.
One with all four limbs crushed. The other with his Sinews and Meridians already severed.
But the Heavenly Power Demon had one advantage over me.
At least his internal energy remained intact.
I was already dying, and the approaching death frightened me.
I wanted one last conversation with the person watching me die.
I didn’t want to kill you.
Why not?
Because at least the man I knew wasn’t a fiend.
The way I see it, a good man from the Demonic Cult is better than a bad man from the orthodox faction. If I killed someone like you, I felt like I’d become no different from a fiend myself.
In truth, I had hesitated over and over. Killing the Heavenly Power Demon would have earned me a massive amount of EXP and several level-ups.
After agonizing over it, I had chosen to give that up.
Looking back, it had probably been for the best. The Western Heaven Demon Lord wasn’t someone I could defeat with one or two level-ups.
Rather than dying with an unpleasant feeling in my chest, I thought it was better to leave this world feeling relieved.
Well... this isn’t so bad either.
The Heavenly Power Demon had stared at me for a long while, his expression complicated, before making me an offer.
An offer I couldn’t possibly refuse.
Remembering the Heavenly Power Demon’s final words, I swept my hand through the air.
The tremendous wind pressure scattered the cloud of dust, revealing the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
“Your big brother’s here.”
“Kha! Khahahaha!”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord doubled over like a shrimp, roaring with laughter.
I looked past his shoulder.
A dozen or so meters behind him, someone stood unsteadily inside the treatment room where the door had been.
The Divine Physician.
His face was deathly pale, but he nodded.
Jeok Cheongang was safe.
Thank goodness. I made it in time.
As I breathed a sigh of relief, the Western Heaven Demon Lord finally stopped laughing and raised his head.
“You’ve changed so much that I hardly recognize you.”
“I got a gift. From someone I never expected.”
“A gift?”
“Yeah. I received internal energy.”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord exclaimed in realization.
“Transmitting Internal Energy Across the Body!”
“Apparently, that’s what some people call it.”
“Did you use that power you spoke of? The one resembling the Essence-Siphoning Great Technique?”
“No.”
“Then you had a fortuitous encounter. Ha-ha!”
“It wasn’t free. He asked me for one favor.”
“A favor?”
“Yeah.”
I quietly nodded. I remembered the Heavenly Power Demon’s words as he transferred his internal energy to me.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord...
“He asked me to kill you.”
Tudududuk. Grab.
When I reached out, White Flame was pulled free from deep within the wall and caught in my hand.
The fire dragon, swollen by three jiazi of internal energy, spread its wings.
“You’re... dead.”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord smiled broadly.

The Lord of Heaven?
A servant?
Whatever the man meant, there could be no doubt that he was utterly insane.
“What nonsense!
If you are not a fiend despite slaughtering people without hesitation, then what are you?”
“It is unfortunate.
But what can I do?
Erasing those who oppose His will is part of my duty.”
“Y-you are...”
The Divine Physician was struck speechless as the Western Heaven Demon Lord gave a quiet sigh.
The thick scent of blood soaked into every word he spoke and every small movement he made, enough to make nausea rise in the Divine Physician’s throat.
“Get out.”
“Hm?
What did you say?”
“I said get out.
No one is permitted to enter while I am treating a patient.
Especially a fiend like you.”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord stared at the Divine Physician’s rigid face, then laughed aloud.
“I thought you were an inflexible physician, but you know how to joke.
Divine Physician, the treatment is already over.”
“It is not over.”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord advanced with an amused expression.
At the end of his path lay Jeok Cheongang, motionless as a corpse.
“I believe the patient should be moved somewhere else.”
“Before that... you should ask the physician’s permission.”
The Divine Physician rose from his seat, his expression hard.
At that very moment—
Pa-pa-pat!
Dozens of streaks of light shot from his billowing sleeves.
Needles large and small flew in straight lines or curved through the air toward the lethal acupoint behind the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s neck.
Yet as he watched them hurtle toward him, the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s smile only deepened.
“How interesting.”
Tudududuk!
He did not move.
The formidable Body-Protecting Qi surrounding him simply did its job.
Dozens of needles struck the Body-Protecting Qi and trembled violently.
“And unfortunate.”
Crunch.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord closed his hand, then opened it again.
Invisible energy obeyed its master’s will, seizing the needles and crushing them into a mangled mass.
The Divine Physician might have learned martial arts, but the gulf between him and the Western Heaven Demon Lord was as vast as the distance between heaven and earth.
“I’ll say it again.
The treatment is over.”
At the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s quiet declaration, the Divine Physician’s body rose into the air.
Seizing an Object Through Empty Space—a feat possible only for someone possessing terrifying internal energy.
The Divine Physician flew forward as if something had flung him.
His face turned deathly pale as the Western Heaven Demon Lord caught him by the throat.
“F-fiend...”
“That hardly seems like something a physician who just unleashed a killing technique should say.
Come to think of it, wouldn’t that make you a fiend as well?”
“If I think of the blood that will stain your hands, I will gladly become one!”
Whoosh.
Thunk.
The Divine Physician’s palm strike, thrust out with a shout that brought up blood, was blocked with ease.
Crack-crack.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord tightened his grip and broke the old physician’s hand.
A strange glint passed through his eyes.
“The Tang Family Head was right.
You had it.”
His gaze had settled on the Divine Physician’s hand.
Around one wrinkled finger was something wholly unsuited to a physician.
“So this is the Myriad-Poison Ring...”
A band glowing softly, set with a jewel that seemed to contain both light and darkness.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord gazed at the objective of his mission with rapture, as though bewitched.
He carefully removed the Myriad-Poison Ring from the Divine Physician’s finger and slipped it onto his own.
“The Lord of Heaven will be pleased.”
The Divine Physician, who had watched everything unfold, let out a suppressed groan.
“W-what are you planning to do?”
“Don’t concern yourself with it.
Your role ends here anyway.”
Whoosh!
Thud!
A palm strike that shot forward like a blade pierced the Divine Physician’s abdomen.
His lower dantian shattered.
The Divine Physician was hurled across the room, vomiting blood.
“Bweeeeegh!”
“It seems I no longer need the physician’s permission.
Wouldn’t you agree?”
The Divine Physician despaired, and the Western Heaven Demon Lord laughed heartily.
It was over.
At last, he had obtained the Myriad-Poison Ring desired by the Lord of Heaven and erased from this land three great sects whose influence spanned the realm.
Nothing remained that could stand in his way.
It was time to finish everything and return.
“Come.
Let us go together.
There is someone who wishes to see you.”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord whispered to Jeok Cheongang, who slept peacefully atop the Cold-Ice Stone, then used Seizing an Object Through Empty Space to draw him closer.
Or rather, he was about to.
Woooooong.
A low, faint sound, like a swarm of bees buzzing.
Only the Western Heaven Demon Lord could have noticed it.
It was a tremor in the air, a faint vibration that slowly drew nearer.
Could the collapse have already begun?
The Western Heaven Demon Lord turned toward the source.
Beyond the treatment room, its iron door now gone, a faint light flickered in the pitch-black darkness.
“What is that...”
He deliberately furrowed his brow.
The next instant, his eyes flew wide.
Woooooong!
Rumble-rumble-rumble!
The vibration intensified.
Wind and air tore apart.
And then—
KRAAAAAA!
A massive light shot forward, obliterating the space in its path.
No.
No—a spear wreathed in blue flames.
A name flashed through the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s mind, and he could no longer hold back his laughter.
“Supernatural powers!
Truly, this is supernatural powers!”
As he threw back his head and laughed, a vast darkness surged up and shot forward.
White Flame, engulfed in blue fire, collided with the darkness.
KABOOOOOM!
Amid the deafening blast that shook the underground prison, a voice rang out.
“The sickroom is off-limits unless you’re family or a Disciple.
You fucking bastard.”
Step.
Step.
I pushed through the cloud of dust and moved forward.
Neither the rocks pouring from the ceiling like rain nor the pitch-black darkness before me could stop my steps.
I simply continued toward the one person somewhere beyond it.
What a monster.
Not that I expected something like that to kill him.
I couldn’t see him, but I could feel him—the immense energy coiled within the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
But it didn’t frighten me as much as before.
I calmly clenched my fist.
The powerful internal energy overflowing from my entire body felt almost tangible in my hand.
Heavenly Power Demon.
My clash with the Western Heaven Demon Lord had presented him with a new opportunity.
The falling rocks from the collapsing ceiling had broken his restraints, allowing the old man known as a fiend to leave the underground prison for the first time in decades.
And the Heavenly Power Demon’s first words to me had been completely unexpected.
You killed all the other prisoners.
Cough.
So?
You bastard.
Why did you leave me alive?
Did that bother you so much?
Answer the question.
I can cut off your breath right now.
Wait a few more moments.
It’ll give out on its own.
You bastard!
It had been a conversation between two cripples.
One with all four limbs crushed.
The other with his Sinews and Meridians already severed.
But the Heavenly Power Demon had one advantage over me.
At least his internal energy remained intact.
I was already dying, and the approaching death frightened me.
I wanted one last conversation with the person watching me die.
I didn’t want to kill you.
Why not?
Because at least the man I knew wasn’t a fiend.
The way I see it, a good man from the Demonic Cult is better than a bad man from the orthodox faction.
If I killed someone like you, I felt like I’d become no different from a fiend myself.
In truth, I had hesitated over and over.
Killing the Heavenly Power Demon would have earned me a massive amount of EXP and several level-ups.
After agonizing over it, I had chosen to give that up.
Looking back, it had probably been for the best.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord wasn’t someone I could defeat with one or two level-ups.
Rather than dying with an unpleasant feeling in my chest, I thought it was better to leave this world feeling relieved.
Well... this isn’t so bad either.
The Heavenly Power Demon had stared at me for a long while, his expression complicated, before making me an offer.
An offer I couldn’t possibly refuse.
Remembering the Heavenly Power Demon’s final words, I swept my hand through the air.
The tremendous wind pressure scattered the cloud of dust, revealing the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
“Your big brother’s here.”
“Kha!
Khahahaha!”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord doubled over like a shrimp, roaring with laughter.
I looked past his shoulder.
A dozen or so meters behind him, someone stood unsteadily inside the treatment room where the door had been.
The Divine Physician.
His face was deathly pale, but he nodded.
Jeok Cheongang was safe.
Thank goodness.
I made it in time.
As I breathed a sigh of relief, the Western Heaven Demon Lord finally stopped laughing and raised his head.
“You’ve changed so much that I hardly recognize you.”
“I got a gift.
From someone I never expected.”
“A gift?”
“Yeah.
I received internal energy.”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord exclaimed in realization.
“Transmitting Internal Energy Across the Body!”
“Apparently, that’s what some people call it.”
“Did you use that power you spoke of?
The one resembling the Essence-Siphoning Great Technique?”
“No.”
“Then you had a fortuitous encounter.
Ha-ha!”
“It wasn’t free.
He asked me for one favor.”
“A favor?”
“Yeah.”
I quietly nodded.
I remembered the Heavenly Power Demon’s words as he transferred his internal energy to me.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord...
“He asked me to kill you.”
Tudududuk.
Grab.
When I reached out, White Flame was pulled free from deep within the wall and caught in my hand.
The fire dragon, swollen by three jiazi of internal energy, spread its wings.
“You’re... dead.”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord smiled broadly.

chapters.title: Chapter 362
paragraphs: The Western Heaven Demon Lord spoke with a laugh.
“I admit it. You are supernatural powers incarnate.”
He had crushed all four of Jin Taekyung’s limbs with his own hands and inflicted severe Internal Injuries.
Crippled? He would have been fortunate if that were all. His wounds had been more than enough to kill him.
And yet the young man, Jin Taekyung, had survived.
He had returned to stand before the Western Heaven Demon Lord with his limbs restored without a single scar and even greater internal energy than before.
Even dozens of sorcerers working together couldn’t achieve a recovery like this.
If this wasn’t supernatural powers—an outright miracle—what was?
The Western Heaven Demon Lord trembled with a sudden surge of excitement and wonder.
Seeing him like that, Jin Taekyung cocked his head and sneered.
“What? Thinking about dying soon making you need to piss? Why are you shaking so much?”
“Do you know how many years I have lived?”
“No. Don’t want to, either.”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord nodded.
“Of course. To be honest, I don’t know myself.”
“Are you an idiot?”
“As I grew older, counting the years began to feel meaningless. Had I gone on living as I was, I might have grown so weary of the boredom that I chose death.”
“Can’t you die now? I’m serious. I’d even get down on my knees and beg.”
“I’m afraid I’m enjoying myself more than ever. Today, I met you, just as I once met the Lord of Heaven.”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord smiled brightly once more.
For him, the past several decades had been tedious years of endurance.
He missed war and blood. He yearned for something he had never experienced before.
Something new that even the Poison King and the Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun had failed to provide.
The young man before him possessed the very thing the Western Heaven Demon Lord had longed for.
“I have only one request.”
The corners of the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s mouth stretched wide.
With his face grotesquely twisted into a smile, he resembled a fiend from the Lotus Sutra.
“Try to hold out as long as you can.”
Rumble-rumble-rumble!
The ground shook violently.
Black qi streamed from the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s entire body, bearing down on everything around him.
The absolute master, possessed of power that could shatter heaven, brought down his darkness-shrouded sword. Ink-black Sword Force surged forward, erasing the space in its path.
Whoooooosh!
“I’ve got one request, too.”
The young man, Jin Taekyung, tightened his grip on his spear.
Blue flames enveloped the spearhead, illuminating the darkness like sacred fire.
“Try to die as fast as you can.”
KABOOM!
A deafening boom shook heaven and earth, and a massive impact traveled down the spearhead.
Krrrk!
A thrill rushed through me as I stared at the ink-black Sword Force clashing with White Flame.
I have a good chance of winning.
That single exchange was enough to convince me.
Sword Force against Spear Energy.
Ask which was superior, and ninety-nine out of a hundred people would answer Sword Force.
The last one would probably give you shit for asking something so obvious.
But...
This is doable.
During my first battle with the Western Heaven Demon Lord, every exchange had inflicted an Internal Injury and forced me back.
But the immense internal energy the Heavenly Power Demon had given me through Transmitting Internal Energy Across the Body changed everything.
I had retreated only one step.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord had once seemed impossibly distant. Now he was close enough to touch if I reached out.
“Internal energy sure is nice, huh? Don’t you think?”
Zzzzzzt.
My absurdly massive Spear Energy showed no sign of dimming, even against the ink-black Sword Force.
Beyond our crossed weapons, the Western Heaven Demon Lord regarded me with open admiration.
“I guarantee there has never been a Peak master like you in the history of the Murim.”
“Of course not. They probably didn’t have more than three jiazi of internal energy.”
I looked him straight in the eye and added,
“Or an ability like this.”
Before I had even finished speaking, I was already issuing a command in my mind.
Assign fifty points each to Strength and Agility.
Internal energy wasn’t the only thing the Heavenly Power Demon had given me.
Ten Level Ups had healed every injury on my body, and I still had all the Stat Points that came with them.
Whoooooosh.
A dazzling halo of light enveloped my entire body.
The change, perceptible only to me, took place in an instant.
Now it was time to see the results for myself.
“Put some real strength into your ‘don’t-go.’”
“Don’t-go?”
“Your asshole, dumbass.”
I was going to make him shit himself.
Clenching my teeth, I poured strength into the hand gripping the spear shaft.
Grrrrrk.
What were my stats now?
I didn’t know the exact numbers, but one thing was certain.
At the very least, this body had already gone far beyond the limits of a human being.
The smile vanished from the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s face beneath the overwhelming pressure.
“This is ridiculously crude...!”
“Way to hit me where it hurts.”
It was crude enough to leave anyone speechless, but it was also brutally effective.
The spear, which had been slowly giving way beneath the Sword Force, began to tilt ever so slightly toward the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
If my martial arts aren’t enough, I’ll make up the difference with my body.
It was a method only I could use in this world.
At the same time, it proved that the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s martial arts stood far above mine.
“Ha!”
Krrrk!
The instant a sharp shout burst from the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s mouth, his sword traced a strange arc and coiled around the spearhead.
He was redirecting my attack with the principle of Four Ounces Deflecting a Thousand Catties.
The spearhead plunged into empty air, releasing an explosion of compressed air.
As I staggered, the Western Heaven Demon Lord thrust out his hand.
Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh!
Invisible, formless qi.
I couldn’t see it, but I could sense it—where it would strike and when.
With that realization, my body flowed into motion.
I bent backward until my back nearly touched the ground.
Pfft!
Five strands of Finger Qi shot from the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s hand and grazed my philtrum.
Blood sprayed, filling my nose with its coppery smell.
By the time I sprang upright with a carp-leaping maneuver, the ink-black Sword Force was already slicing diagonally across my body.
Whoooooosh! Shhk!
It missed me by a hair and tore through space.
That alone brought down a pillar three zhang away and split the bars of the underground prison like tofu.
We were too close for me to swing my spear.
But I already knew what to do.
Inventory open. Store.
White Flame vanished from my hand, and I thrust both arms toward the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s chest.
Whooosh!
Scorching heat mingled with my breath.
My palms, imbued with the power of Flame Divine Palm, shot forward. At the same moment, the Western Heaven Demon Lord released his sword.
His hands blurred as he slammed both palms into mine.
KABOOM!
The instant our four palms, each carrying tremendous internal energy, collided, a violent gale erupted around us.
The rocky ground caved in, and the force of the impact blasted apart everything nearby.
But the real struggle had only begun.
Hngh!
I smothered the groan rising in my throat.
An immense wave of energy poured through our locked palms and intertwined fingers, making my vision swim.
What the hell is with this bastard’s internal energy...?
I currently possessed a full three jiazi of internal energy.
In terms of sheer internal energy, that was more than enough to stand shoulder to shoulder with the Sect Leaders of the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families.
But the Western Heaven Demon Lord—the monster standing before me—was on an entirely different level.
This is insane.
Hissssss.
The heat gathered in my hands slowly faded as darkness devoured the flames.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord spoke in a low voice.
“There is no need to feel so aggrieved. A tower easily built is just as easily toppled.”
“You are merely a strong child. Such is the limit of those who have failed to cross the wall.”
Limit?
That single word made my teeth clench.
I had heard it until I was sick of it.
A bastard raised without a father. A bastard from a poor family. A bastard doomed to remain an F-rank Hunter until the day he died...
Every cutting remark anyone had ever aimed at me had come with the same word attached like a tag.
Even now, after everything I had accomplished.
“I swear, I’m going to...”
A question mark appeared over the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s face at my suppressed voice.
Holding back the endless torrent of his internal energy, I forced out the words like a groan.
“I’m going to circumcise that mouth of yours.”
It didn’t take long for the question mark on his face to turn into an exclamation mark.
I ground my teeth and summoned every last bit of strength I had. My body, which had been sliding backward, began inching forward.
Then I slowly bent the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s interlocked fingers.
Crack!
Bones shifted out of place, and his brow furrowed.
“When it comes to brute strength, you may well be the best under heaven. But this is as far as you go.”
Crack-crack-crack! Thud!
It happened in an instant.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord stepped on empty air, launched himself upward, and drove his knee into my face.
The bridge of my newly healed nose caved in, and several broken teeth spun through the air.
I hurriedly pulled my hand away and wiped the blood covering my eyes.
“Ghk!”
“Your limit is clear.”
Whoosh—bang!
A fist hurtled toward me with a violent crack of displaced air.
I raised an arm to shield myself, but the shockwave ruptured my eardrums.
As I staggered, punches and kicks rained down.
Thud-thud-thud-thud-thud!
Chest. Stomach. Legs.
The relentless barrage battered my entire body.
But unlike our first battle, I neither let his attacks land so easily nor fell beneath them.
I’ve already been through this once. I won’t let it happen twice.
I reached into a pale afterimage and caught something solid.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s arm—the part even the Black Dragon Armor left exposed.
Without the slightest hesitation, I twisted it.
No.
I wrung it out like wet laundry.
Krrrk!
His skin tore, and shards of splintered bone burst through.
No matter how great the master, he could still feel pain. The Western Heaven Demon Lord let out a stifled groan and threw a punch.
His movement was duller and rougher than before.
There was no reason I couldn’t avoid it.
Bang!
Compressed air exploded half a span from my face.
I shot out my arm like lightning and caught his fist.
That was when I saw it.
“Huh?”
Something familiar caught my eye, and I froze.
A ring set with a small gemstone that radiated a mysterious light.
It was almost strange that I hadn’t noticed it sooner.
Why does he have the Myriad-Poison Ring...?
In that impossibly brief instant, a thousand thoughts flashed through my mind.
And after the flash of insight came the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s attack.
Crack!
I had let myself get distracted in the middle of a fight. Of course I couldn’t dodge it.
The blow sent me tumbling across the ground. I staggered back to my feet, clutching my ringing head.
I had taken the hit, but I couldn’t stop laughing like a madman.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord frowned.
“Why are you laughing? Have you lost your mind?”
“Lost my mind? You’re the crazy one, dumbass.”
Still laughing, I waved the object in my hand.
See this?
A fresh new Item, still warm after being stored in my Inventory and pulled right back out.
“What are you going to do if you lose something important? Huh?”
A host of emotions flashed across the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s face when he saw the Myriad-Poison Ring.
Shock. Surprise. Confusion.
Then anger.
He looked down at his suddenly empty hand and spoke in a heavy voice.
“How?”
“Who knows? Maybe it’s those supernatural powers you love so much.”
A single brush had been enough.
The Myriad-Poison Ring had left the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s hand and been safely stored in my private vault—the Inventory, where no one else could reach it.
Now I slipped it onto my middle finger.
“You can tell it’s a sacred treasure. Look at that shine. Pretty, isn’t it?”
“Give it back. It is not something the likes of you can possess.”
I raised my middle finger at the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
“What do you think? Looks good?”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord trembled with rage.
His usual composure had vanished without a trace.
Seeing him like that finally confirmed it.
“The Myriad-Poison Ring. This was your objective from the very beginning.”

The moment I saw the ring on the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s finger, the first thing that came to mind was the Green Jade Buddha Staff, the sacred treasure of Shaolin Temple that the Blood Lord had stolen during the massacre at Shaolin.

“I figured there had to be something special about it when that bastard clung to it even while running for his life... What, are you people collecting orbs? You think a dragon will appear and grant you a wish if you gather seven?”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes darkened.
“I told you to give it back.”
“Yeah. Fuck off.”
I waved the middle finger wearing the Myriad-Poison Ring right in his face.
At the same time, I muttered inwardly.
Inventory open. Store.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes widened as the Myriad-Poison Ring vanished without a trace, as though erased by an eraser.
Rumble-rumble-rumble.
The qi around him churned violently.
The sword he summoned with Seizing an Object Through Empty Space flew into his grasp.
Tss-tss-tss-tss!
Ink-black Sword Force blazed around the blade, fiercer and more violent than ever.
“This is the last time. Hand it over.”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord was no longer the same now that he had lost what mattered most.
His mind was shaken, and a shaken mind made for a shaken sword.
That might be enough to turn the tide.
“I’ll give you my final answer, then. No.”
The moment the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes sank deeply at my answer—
“You brought this upon yourself.”
At those emotionless words, the ink-black Sword Force coiling around his blade shot forward like an arrow.
But its devastating power wasn’t aimed at my arms, my legs, or my neck.
At the far end of the ruined corridor stood the treatment room.
“No!”
I launched myself forward with a scream.
The muscles throughout my body, swollen to the point of bursting, shrieked in pain.
The internal energy I desperately dragged up clawed at my heart meridian.
But none of that mattered.
As long as I could stop it.
As long as I wasn’t too late.
Old Master!
With the cry trapped inside my throat, I kicked off the ground once more.
KABOOOOOM!
In a world slowed to a crawl, a deafening roar like heaven splitting apart filled my ears, and a blinding flash swallowed my vision.
