“Way to hit me where it hurts.”
It was crude enough to leave anyone speechless, but it was also brutally effective.
The spear, which had been slowly giving way beneath the Sword Force, began to tilt ever so slightly toward the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
If my martial arts aren’t enough, I’ll make up the difference with my body.
It was a method only I could use in this world.
At the same time, it proved that the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s martial arts stood far above mine.
“Ha!”
Krrrk!
The instant a sharp shout burst from the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s mouth, his sword traced a strange arc and coiled around the spearhead.
He was redirecting my attack with the principle of Four Ounces Deflecting a Thousand Catties.
The spearhead plunged into empty air, releasing an explosion of compressed air.
As I staggered, the Western Heaven Demon Lord thrust out his hand.
Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh!
Invisible, formless qi.
I couldn’t see it, but I could sense it—where it would strike and when.
With that realization, my body flowed into motion.
I bent backward until my back nearly touched the ground.
Pfft!
Five strands of Finger Qi shot from the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s hand and grazed my philtrum.
Blood sprayed, filling my nose with its coppery smell.
By the time I sprang upright with a carp-leaping maneuver, the ink-black Sword Force was already slicing diagonally across my body.
Whoooooosh!
Shhk!
It missed me by a hair and tore through space.
That alone brought down a pillar three zhang away and split the bars of the underground prison like tofu.
We were too close for me to swing my spear.
But I already knew what to do.
Inventory open.
Store.
White Flame vanished from my hand, and I thrust both arms toward the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s chest.
Whooosh!
Scorching heat mingled with my breath.
My palms, imbued with the power of Flame Divine Palm, shot forward.
At the same moment, the Western Heaven Demon Lord released his sword.
His hands blurred as he slammed both palms into mine.
KABOOM!
The instant our four palms, each carrying tremendous internal energy, collided, a violent gale erupted around us.
The rocky ground caved in, and the force of the impact blasted apart everything nearby.
But the real struggle had only begun.
Hngh!
I smothered the groan rising in my throat.
An immense wave of energy poured through our locked palms and intertwined fingers, making my vision swim.
What the hell is with this bastard’s internal energy...?
I currently possessed a full three jiazi of internal energy.
In terms of sheer internal energy, that was more than enough to stand shoulder to shoulder with the Sect Leaders of the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families.
But the Western Heaven Demon Lord—the monster standing before me—was on an entirely different level.
This is insane.
Hissssss.
The heat gathered in my hands slowly faded as darkness devoured the flames.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord spoke in a low voice.
“There is no need to feel so aggrieved.
A tower easily built is just as easily toppled.”
“You are merely a strong child.
Such is the limit of those who have failed to cross the wall.”
Limit?
That single word made my teeth clench.
I had heard it until I was sick of it.
A bastard raised without a father.
A bastard from a poor family.
A bastard doomed to remain an F-rank Hunter until the day he died...
Every cutting remark anyone had ever aimed at me had come with the same word attached like a tag.
Even now, after everything I had accomplished.
“I swear, I’m going to...”
A question mark appeared over the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s face at my suppressed voice.
Holding back the endless torrent of his internal energy, I forced out the words like a groan.
“I’m going to circumcise that mouth of yours.”
It didn’t take long for the question mark on his face to turn into an exclamation mark.
I ground my teeth and summoned every last bit of strength I had.
My body, which had been sliding backward, began inching forward.
Then I slowly bent the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s interlocked fingers.
Crack!
Bones shifted out of place, and his brow furrowed.
“When it comes to brute strength, you may well be the best under heaven.
But this is as far as you go.”
Crack-crack-crack!
Thud!
It happened in an instant.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord stepped on empty air, launched himself upward, and drove his knee into my face.
The bridge of my newly healed nose caved in, and several broken teeth spun through the air.
I hurriedly pulled my hand away and wiped the blood covering my eyes.
“Ghk!”
“Your limit is clear.”
Whoosh—bang!
A fist hurtled toward me with a violent crack of displaced air.
I raised an arm to shield myself, but the shockwave ruptured my eardrums.
As I staggered, punches and kicks rained down.
Thud-thud-thud-thud-thud!
Chest.
Stomach.
Legs.
The relentless barrage battered my entire body.
But unlike our first battle, I neither let his attacks land so easily nor fell beneath them.
I’ve already been through this once.
I won’t let it happen twice.
I reached into a pale afterimage and caught something solid.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s arm—the part even the Black Dragon Armor left exposed.
Without the slightest hesitation, I twisted it.
No.
I wrung it out like wet laundry.
Krrrk!
His skin tore, and shards of splintered bone burst through.
No matter how great the master, he could still feel pain.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord let out a stifled groan and threw a punch.
His movement was duller and rougher than before.
There was no reason I couldn’t avoid it.
Bang!
Compressed air exploded half a span from my face.
I shot out my arm like lightning and caught his fist.
That was when I saw it.
“Huh?”
Something familiar caught my eye, and I froze.
A ring set with a small gemstone that radiated a mysterious light.
It was almost strange that I hadn’t noticed it sooner.
Why does he have the Myriad-Poison Ring...?
In that impossibly brief instant, a thousand thoughts flashed through my mind.
And after the flash of insight came the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s attack.
Crack!
I had let myself get distracted in the middle of a fight.
Of course I couldn’t dodge it.
The blow sent me tumbling across the ground.
I staggered back to my feet, clutching my ringing head.
I had taken the hit, but I couldn’t stop laughing like a madman.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord frowned.
“Why are you laughing?
Have you lost your mind?”
“Lost my mind?
You’re the crazy one, dumbass.”
Still laughing, I waved the object in my hand.
See this?
A fresh new Item, still warm after being stored in my Inventory and pulled right back out.
“What are you going to do if you lose something important?
Huh?”
A host of emotions flashed across the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s face when he saw the Myriad-Poison Ring.
Shock.
Surprise.
Confusion.
Then anger.
He looked down at his suddenly empty hand and spoke in a heavy voice.
“How?”
“Who knows?
Maybe it’s those supernatural powers you love so much.”
A single brush had been enough.
The Myriad-Poison Ring had left the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s hand and been safely stored in my private vault—the Inventory, where no one else could reach it.
Now I slipped it onto my middle finger.
“You can tell it’s a sacred treasure.
Look at that shine.
Pretty, isn’t it?”
“Give it back.
It is not something the likes of you can possess.”
I raised my middle finger at the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
“What do you think?
Looks good?”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord trembled with rage.
His usual composure had vanished without a trace.
Seeing him like that finally confirmed it.
“The Myriad-Poison Ring.
This was your objective from the very beginning.”

The moment I saw the ring on the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s finger, the first thing that came to mind was the Green Jade Buddha Staff, the sacred treasure of Shaolin Temple that the Blood Lord had stolen during the massacre at Shaolin.
“I figured there had to be something special about it when that bastard clung to it even while running for his life...
What, are you people collecting orbs?
You think a dragon will appear and grant you a wish if you gather seven?”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes darkened.
“I told you to give it back.”
“Yeah.
Fuck off.”
I waved the middle finger wearing the Myriad-Poison Ring right in his face.
At the same time, I muttered inwardly.
Inventory open.
Store.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes widened as the Myriad-Poison Ring vanished without a trace, as though erased by an eraser.
Rumble-rumble-rumble.
The qi around him churned violently.
The sword he summoned with Seizing an Object Through Empty Space flew into his grasp.
Tss-tss-tss-tss!
Ink-black Sword Force blazed around the blade, fiercer and more violent than ever.
“This is the last time.
Hand it over.”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord was no longer the same now that he had lost what mattered most.
His mind was shaken, and a shaken mind made for a shaken sword.
That might be enough to turn the tide.
“I’ll give you my final answer, then.
No.”
The moment the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes sank deeply at my answer—
“You brought this upon yourself.”
At those emotionless words, the ink-black Sword Force coiling around his blade shot forward like an arrow.
But its devastating power wasn’t aimed at my arms, my legs, or my neck.
At the far end of the ruined corridor stood the treatment room.
“No!”
I launched myself forward with a scream.
The muscles throughout my body, swollen to the point of bursting, shrieked in pain.
The internal energy I desperately dragged up clawed at my heart meridian.
But none of that mattered.
As long as I could stop it.
As long as I wasn’t too late.
Old Master!
With the cry trapped inside my throat, I kicked off the ground once more.
KABOOOOOM!
In a world slowed to a crawl, a deafening roar like heaven splitting apart filled my ears, and a blinding flash swallowed my vision.

chapters.title: Chapter 363
paragraphs: KABOOOOOM!
A tremendous roar and shockwave slammed into my entire body.
My vision swam. The ceiling and floor traded places, and my hair whipped around me. My body flew helplessly through the air and crashed into a corner of the treatment room.
Crack!
A sharp current raced up my spine, and something hot surged up from deep within my lungs.
“Ghk!”
Dark red blood spilled across the floor. It was obvious proof that I had suffered a serious Internal Injury.
And I had.
Damn it. How long has it even been since I recovered?
The only consolation was that my injuries weren’t as severe as before and that I had managed to protect the treatment room from the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s Sword Force.
“Are you all right?”
At my question, the Divine Physician lifted his head from where he had curled up in a corner of the treatment room.
He was covered in pale dust, with Jeok Cheongang cradled in his arms. After letting out a quiet groan, he answered.
“Thanks to Young Master Jin blocking the attack, I am safe.”
But despite his answer, the Divine Physician was clearly far from all right.
His beard, white as an immortal’s, was stained with blood. His wrist was bent at an unnatural angle, and through the tatters of his clothes, I could see dark bruises covering his lower abdomen.
That’s...
There was no doubt about it. The Divine Physician’s dantian was ruined. Having lost all the martial arts he possessed, he was now nothing more than an ordinary old man.
No—with his qi-sea acupoint destroyed and his arm broken, his condition was anything but good.
Even after all that, he still protected Old Master...
Not a single scratch marred Jeok Cheongang’s body. The old physician had disregarded his own safety to protect his patient.
“Old Man Dong.”
“This old man is fine, so do not worry.”
The Divine Physician gave me a faint smile, then looked at me with concern.
“More importantly, I am worried about Young Master Jin’s condition. This old man will come to you, so please wait just a moment—”
Instead of answering, I reached out.
Formless internal energy flowed from my fingertips and gently pushed back the Divine Physician as he tried to approach me.
“Y-Young Master Jin?”
Before the Divine Physician could finish speaking, a streak of Finger Qi shot through the air from somewhere beyond us and pierced the wall.
It had passed through the exact spot where the Divine Physician’s head had been only moments ago.
Shhk! Pfft!
Had I been even one second later—no, even a quarter of a second—the Divine Physician would already have been dead.
I gestured for the physician, now frozen like a rock, to take cover. Then I turned and stared straight ahead.
“That’s pretty low, going after a helpless old man.”
Beyond the clouds of dust parting like the Red Sea, the Western Heaven Demon Lord finally appeared.
A chilling voice slipped between his lips.
“Low? You were the one who threw away the opportunity I gave you.”
His usual composure and refined manner of speaking had long since vanished. Concentrated killing intent burned in his eyes as he stared at me.
“You touched something you should never have touched.”
“Fuck, anyone listening to you would think the Myriad-Poison Ring was an erogenous zone. You’re an old bastard who can’t even get it up anymore.”
I used White Flame as a cane and pushed myself to my feet.
Every bone in my body throbbed as if it were about to break. Judging by the pain, some of them probably had cracked. On top of that, I had suffered a severe Internal Injury.
Damn it. He was already a monster to begin with.
For a moment, I regretted provoking him.
I had never imagined that a Supreme Peak master like the Western Heaven Demon Lord would resort without hesitation to tactics fit for some Third Rate dark-path thug.
But...
“This must be that important to you. Right?”
I waved the Myriad-Poison Ring I had just taken out of my Inventory.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord, who had seemed impossible to stop, halted abruptly.
“Hand it over at once—”
“You want it back? That won’t be difficult.”
“You intend to negotiate?”
“You catch on fast.”
The Myriad-Poison Ring was nothing more than a strange ring to me—no more and no less.
But it was different for the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
He valued this tiny ring more than the destruction of the Sichuan Tang Clan, Qingcheng, and Emei.
Just like the Blood Lord, who had desperately taken the Green Jade Buddha Staff with him even as his arm was severed.
“Take your lackeys outside and withdraw at once. Otherwise, you’ll never see the Myriad-Poison Ring again.”
“Never see it again...”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord brushed back his hair, stiff with blood.
After a brief silence, a low voice slipped from his lips.
“Ridiculous.”
“What?”
“How could it not be ridiculous? I need only kill you all and take it.”
“Nothing will change. Not for you, your master, or the Divine Physician. None of you can escape death.”
Even if I explained it, the Western Heaven Demon Lord wouldn’t properly understand the concepts of subspace or the Inventory.
Maybe he was right. Perhaps killing me really would cause everything inside my Inventory to spill out.
But the Western Heaven Demon Lord had overlooked one thing.
“Well, that sounds plausible enough. But you should’ve considered the possibility that I might destroy the Myriad-Poison Ring first.”
My grip was strong enough to crumple steel like paper. Even without circulating internal energy, reducing this little ring to powder would be easy.
“So don’t get any bright ideas. Back off. If you take even one more step—”
Step.
I could not finish my sentence as I stared at the Western Heaven Demon Lord. He took a step forward without hesitation and smiled.
“What? Are you flustered?”
He didn’t wait for my answer. Looking delighted beyond measure, he continued.
“It is truly amusing. You call it a sacred treasure, yet you do not actually believe it is one.”
“What is that supposed to mean?”
“My mistake. I thought you would understand after hearing that much.”
The smile vanished from the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s lips. His eyes bored into me, filled with scorn and contempt.
“Did you really think a mere human made of flesh and blood could do anything to a sacred treasure imbued with such great power?”
I looked down at the Myriad-Poison Ring resting in my palm.
A sacred treasure passed down through the generations of the Sichuan Tang Clan. One of the old legends of the Murim. A strange ring said to detoxify and absorb any poison under heaven.
And...
The Myriad-Poison Ring can’t even be appraised by the System.
A sacred treasure.
The single word flashed through my mind, and my heart seemed to drop into my stomach. Something ran down my back—whether it was blood or cold sweat, I could not tell.
Drip. Drip.
My fist clenched reflexively, and drops of blood fell from it.
Even beneath my terrifying grip, the Myriad-Poison Ring didn’t so much as bend. Instead, it dug into my palm like a thorn.
“Damn it.”
I muttered under my breath.
There could be no more compromise. No retreat.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord advanced toward me with a jaunty step.
“I regret what this means for the Blood Lord, but...”
Tss-tss-tss-tss!
“I will have to kill you.”
Black mist poured from his entire body and swallowed the treatment room.
Pa-pa-pat!
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s figure vanished.
He erased the distance of several zhang in a single step and swung his ink-black Sword Force. Solid rock split apart like tofu.
I ducked beneath the attack and thrust my spear forward like an arrow.
Bang!
The spearhead stabbed into empty air, and compressed air exploded.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord caught the shaft with a hand wreathed in Force and clicked his tongue.
“You still cannot let go.”
At the same time, the tip of his foot struck my wrist.
The blow targeted not the bone but an acupoint. Pain like a massive needle stabbing into my veins shot through me, and the spear fell from my grip.
But I didn’t give up.
I’d been ready to take him down with me from the very beginning.
I could not fall from something like this.
Either he died, or I did.
And if even that was impossible, I would throw my life away to make sure we died together.
Without the help of the others, it would not have been strange if I had already died several times.
Now it was time to repay that debt—with interest.
“Hngh!”
With a shout that was almost a groan, I grabbed the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s ankle.
He let out a roar and drove a palm into me.
Boom!
A small explosion went off inside my body.
The foul internal energy penetrated through bone and flesh, tearing my heart meridian to shreds.
My vision blurred, and the strength drained from my legs.
But the hand locked around the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s ankle like a shackle kept moving, driven by the will and instinct carved into my mind.
Krrrk!
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes widened in pain.
His Body-Protecting Qi could block my Spear Energy, but it couldn’t stop his ankle from breaking beneath raw physical strength.
Damn it, my hand...
Of course, I had to pay the price for my reckless act.

The hand that had seized his Body-Protecting Qi barehanded was blackened as though it had been shocked by high-voltage electricity. On top of that, I had suffered another Internal Injury that worsened my already terrible condition.
At the moment my grip loosened against my will and my body staggered—
“GRAH!”
A belated scream burst from the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s mouth.
His ankle had been wrung out like wet laundry beneath my tremendous grip. White bone showed through the mangled flesh, all of it drenched in blood.
No matter how far someone had advanced into the Supreme Peak realm, everyone had limits.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord had displayed unbelievable martial prowess, but he didn’t possess infinite internal energy or stamina.
And unlike me, he couldn’t recover through Level Ups.
This is my only chance.
I charged at the staggering Western Heaven Demon Lord.
I endured the pain that made it feel as though my limbs were being torn apart and drew up my internal energy. It flowed into both fists, then blazed into flame.
Whoooooosh!
“Jin Taekyung!”
Heat filled the space.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord stood right in front of me, shouting my name through bloodshot eyes.
Pain had made him drop his sword, leaving his hand empty. It was too late for him to block my attack.
If I reached out—if I merely extended my hand—I could deal the Western Heaven Demon Lord a devastating blow.
But then. Then why...
Why did I feel this way?
A strange sensation seized me.
The world had slowed around me.
Everything moving within it was so slow that it made me want to yawn.
It was the same sensation I had felt while facing Hwangbo Eom, the Taeeul Merciless Sword.
But this time, the sensation was incomparably sharper. An alarm rang in my mind, and at the same time, I sensed something chilling digging into the back of my neck from behind.
Ah.
So that was it.
A flash of insight struck me.
I pulled back the hand reaching toward the Western Heaven Demon Lord and twisted my head aside.
At that moment, time—which had briefly seemed to have its pause button pressed—began moving again.
Swoooooosh!
Like a dam bursting, several things happened at once.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s sword, wrapped in ink-black Sword Force, grazed the back of my neck.
When I thrust both palms forward again, the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s fist smashed into my side.
KRAK!
My ribs broke, and blood surged up my throat.
I was hurled away at bullet-like speed. With great difficulty, I raised my head.
Through my distant, hazy vision, I saw the Western Heaven Demon Lord standing upright.
Perhaps it was because of that strange sensation.
Or perhaps it was the pain.
But the face I saw was filled not with joy or satisfaction, but with shock and fury.
“You dodged my Qi-Controlled Sword?”
Right. The Qi-Controlled Sword.
I’d forgotten he could do that too.
I let out a short laugh as I spat up blood.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes trembled as he stared at me.
“Enlightenment, even at a moment like this... You are someone who must never be allowed to live.”
Enlightenment.
So that was what this was.
I flexed my fingers.
The flow of qi and the sensations running through me were clearer than ever.
Along with the pain that already ruled my entire body.
But it’s too late.
Step. Step.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s approaching footsteps rang like thunder.
I watched him draw closer through hazy eyes.
Amid the darkness, with stone dust and debris raining down around him, the Western Heaven Demon Lord seemed to ripple like a shadow deeper than the night itself.
“Supernatural powers. You truly were such a being.”
I bared my bloodstained teeth and laughed.
My voice stumbled past my lips like a drunkard.
“Fuck off, you... fucking moron.”
“Farewell.”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes flashed red in the darkness.
His hand, wrapped in impenetrable darkness, rose high and slowly descended toward the crown of my head.
Whoooooosh.
And then—
“Do not touch a single hair on his head.”
Fwoosh!
Flames bloomed in the darkness as a hoarse voice rang out, as though its owner hadn’t spoken in ages.
Beyond the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s rigid shoulder, someone was rising to his feet.
“Take your hands off what belongs to this old man.”
A small frame.
But a presence as immense as a giant.
I laughed, and the Western Heaven Demon Lord groaned.
“Fire King...!”

“Damn it.”
I muttered under my breath.
There could be no more compromise.
No retreat.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord advanced toward me with a jaunty step.
“I regret what this means for the Blood Lord, but...”
Tss-tss-tss-tss!
“I will have to kill you.”
Black mist poured from his entire body and swallowed the treatment room.
Pa-pa-pat!
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s figure vanished.
He erased the distance of several zhang in a single step and swung his ink-black Sword Force.
Solid rock split apart like tofu.
I ducked beneath the attack and thrust my spear forward like an arrow.
Bang!
The spearhead stabbed into empty air, and compressed air exploded.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord caught the shaft with a hand wreathed in Force and clicked his tongue.
“You still cannot let go.”
At the same time, the tip of his foot struck my wrist.
The blow targeted not the bone but an acupoint.
Pain like a massive needle stabbing into my veins shot through me, and the spear fell from my grip.
But I didn’t give up.
I’d been ready to take him down with me from the very beginning.
I could not fall from something like this.
Either he died, or I did.
And if even that was impossible, I would throw my life away to make sure we died together.
Without the help of the others, it would not have been strange if I had already died several times.
Now it was time to repay that debt—with interest.
“Hngh!”
With a shout that was almost a groan, I grabbed the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s ankle.
He let out a roar and drove a palm into me.
Boom!
A small explosion went off inside my body.
The foul internal energy penetrated through bone and flesh, tearing my heart meridian to shreds.
My vision blurred, and the strength drained from my legs.
But the hand locked around the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s ankle like a shackle kept moving, driven by the will and instinct carved into my mind.
Krrrk!
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes widened in pain.
His Body-Protecting Qi could block my Spear Energy, but it couldn’t stop his ankle from breaking beneath raw physical strength.
Damn it, my hand...
Of course, I had to pay the price for my reckless act.
The hand that had seized his Body-Protecting Qi barehanded was blackened as though it had been shocked by high-voltage electricity.
On top of that, I had suffered another Internal Injury that worsened my already terrible condition.
At the moment my grip loosened against my will and my body staggered—
“GRAH!”
A belated scream burst from the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s mouth.
His ankle had been wrung out like wet laundry beneath my tremendous grip.
White bone showed through the mangled flesh, all of it drenched in blood.
No matter how far someone had advanced into the Supreme Peak realm, everyone had limits.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord had displayed unbelievable martial prowess, but he didn’t possess infinite internal energy or stamina.
And unlike me, he couldn’t recover through Level Ups.
This is my only chance.
I charged at the staggering Western Heaven Demon Lord.
I endured the pain that made it feel as though my limbs were being torn apart and drew up my internal energy.
It flowed into both fists, then blazed into flame.
Whoooooosh!
“Jin Taekyung!”
Heat filled the space.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord stood right in front of me, shouting my name through bloodshot eyes.
Pain had made him drop his sword, leaving his hand empty.
It was too late for him to block my attack.
If I reached out—if I merely extended my hand—I could deal the Western Heaven Demon Lord a devastating blow.
But then.
Then why...
Why did I feel this way?
A strange sensation seized me.
The world had slowed around me.
Everything moving within it was so slow that it made me want to yawn.
It was the same sensation I had felt while facing Hwangbo Eom, the Taeeul Merciless Sword.
But this time, the sensation was incomparably sharper.
An alarm rang in my mind, and at the same time, I sensed something chilling digging into the back of my neck from behind.
Ah.
So that was it.
A flash of insight struck me.
I pulled back the hand reaching toward the Western Heaven Demon Lord and twisted my head aside.
At that moment, time—which had briefly seemed to have its pause button pressed—began moving again.
Swoooooosh!
Like a dam bursting, several things happened at once.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s sword, wrapped in ink-black Sword Force, grazed the back of my neck.
When I thrust both palms forward again, the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s fist smashed into my side.
KRAK!
My ribs broke, and blood surged up my throat.
I was hurled away at bullet-like speed.
With great difficulty, I raised my head.
Through my distant, hazy vision, I saw the Western Heaven Demon Lord standing upright.
Perhaps it was because of that strange sensation.
Or perhaps it was the pain.
But the face I saw was filled not with joy or satisfaction, but with shock and fury.
“You dodged my Qi-Controlled Sword?”
Right.
The Qi-Controlled Sword.
I’d forgotten he could do that too.
I let out a short laugh as I spat up blood.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes trembled as he stared at me.
“Enlightenment, even at a moment like this...
You are someone who must never be allowed to live.”
Enlightenment.
So that was what this was.
I flexed my fingers.
The flow of qi and the sensations running through me were clearer than ever.
Along with the pain that already ruled my entire body.
But it’s too late.
Step.
Step.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s approaching footsteps rang like thunder.
I watched him draw closer through hazy eyes.
Amid the darkness, with stone dust and debris raining down around him, the Western Heaven Demon Lord seemed to ripple like a shadow deeper than the night itself.
“Supernatural powers.
You truly were such a being.”
I bared my bloodstained teeth and laughed.
My voice stumbled past my lips like a drunkard.
“Fuck off, you... fucking moron.”
“Farewell.”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes flashed red in the darkness.
His hand, wrapped in impenetrable darkness, rose high and slowly descended toward the crown of my head.
Whoooooosh.
And then—
“Do not touch a single hair on his head.”
Fwoosh!
Flames bloomed in the darkness as a hoarse voice rang out, as though its owner hadn’t spoken in ages.
Beyond the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s rigid shoulder, someone was rising to his feet.
“Take your hands off what belongs to this old man.”
A small frame.
But a presence as immense as a giant.
I laughed, and the Western Heaven Demon Lord groaned.
“Fire King...!”

chapters.title: Chapter 364
paragraphs: I had a very long dream. A dream of walking through a hundred years of time.

A vagrant child who had wandered the continent begging for scraps met a master, learned martial arts, and made his name known throughout the world. Then one day, he saw his former self in a young beggar stuffing a dirt-covered dumpling into his mouth.
“What’s your name?”
“...I don’t know.”
“Jangcheon. From now on, your name is Jangcheon.”
They were dark, cold memories. On a day when heavy rain poured from the sky, the disciple who had been like his own flesh and blood left, while his master was left behind.
It was only after a very long time that he returned to the world.
And then...
“You’re an interesting fellow. Who did you say you were?”
“Jin Taekyung. Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
He met someone.
A young brat with an irreverent manner and a rebellious gaze he couldn’t hide. Jeok Cheongang hadn’t liked him.
But why had that been?
Whenever he looked around, the brat was always there beside him. Somehow, he kept catching Jeok Cheongang’s eye.
Perhaps that was when his heart had begun to change.
“This old man is already afflicted with the infirmities of old age. Do you truly believe you can learn martial arts from someone like me?”
“Yes.”
“I’ll say this again...”
“I believe in you, Old Master. That’s enough for me.”
Light and warmth seeped into memories that had once been dark and cold.
He never regretted the decision he made that day. Not even when he performed the Dance of the Fire God and Demon for what would be the last time in his life.
“How was it? The Dance of the Fire God and Demon. Pretty incredible, right?”
“Yes. It was incredible.”
Those few words were enough. He wanted nothing more. He had avenged his friend and saved his one and only Disciple.
But the enemy rose again, impossible though it seemed, and that was where his memories ended.
In the darkness where everything had vanished, he wondered.
Am I dead? Where is this place, where neither Yama nor the dead can be found?
Could I be doomed to wander the underworld?
The question soon faded.
At some point, he lost all sense of time. He even forgot who he was and how he had lived.
No—it was just as he was beginning to forget.
“Old Master. Did you know?”
Someone’s voice echoed faintly in the distance. A voice he had heard somewhere before, speaking words he had never heard that person say.
“I always wanted to call you Master.”
He understood.
At the same time, he remembered the person he had briefly forgotten. The sturdy dam holding back his memories collapsed, and they swallowed him whole.
“I felt the same.”
Fwoosh.
Flames bloomed.
His hands, wreathed in Blazing Flame, tore through the air. The darkness surrounding him in every direction cracked apart, and light seeped through.
The passage was narrow, as though warning him that he was not yet ready to awaken. But without hesitation, he stepped toward the light.
He’s calling me.
Fwoosh!
A blinding white light filled his vision, and the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, opened his eyes.
“Do not touch a single hair on his head.”
His voice was hoarse from long disuse. But when the Western Heaven Demon Lord turned to face him, he felt it.
The heat contained within that small old man’s body.
The flames burning in his eyes.
“Take your hands off what belongs to this old man.”
“Fire King...!”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord let out a low groan.
Of all times, the old monster from Mount Jiuhua had to awaken now.
Under normal circumstances, this might have been manageable. But one of the Demon Lord’s ankles had already been crushed, and he had expended a considerable amount of strength.
His opponent, meanwhile, was a Supreme Peak master hailed as the greatest of the Ten Kings.
This is bad. Very bad.
At this rate, he might have to brace himself for a fight that would leave them both gravely wounded.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord had no intention of dying here after failing the mission personally entrusted to him by the Lord of Heaven.
I have no choice.
It wounded his pride as a martial artist, but he would have to settle this by the easiest means available.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord bit his lip and extended a hand. Jin Taekyung’s limp body, barely clinging to consciousness, flew into his grasp like iron drawn to a magnet.
He seized Jin Taekyung by the throat and shook him for Jeok Cheongang to see.
“You would do well to stop there, if you want your one and only Disciple to live.”
Step.
Jeok Cheongang’s approaching footsteps stopped dead.
He stared at the Western Heaven Demon Lord, then slowly parted his lips.
“Have you ever seen such a motherless, fatherless, fucking son of a bitch...?”
“Did you listen to this old man through your asshole? I told you not to touch a single hair on his head.”
The torrent of profanity left the Western Heaven Demon Lord momentarily stunned.
Then a sneer spread across his lips.
“Oh, did you?”
A stifled groan escaped Jin Taekyung’s lips as the Western Heaven Demon Lord tightened his grip.
Crunch.
The faint sound of bones shifting out of place echoed through the underground prison.
Jeok Cheongang’s eyes darkened.
“You dare...”
“I have many eyes and ears. They all told me the same thing—that the great Fire King cherishes his Disciple as though he were his own flesh and blood.”
“...What do you want?”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord answered without hesitation.
“If you don’t want to lose your Disciple, kill yourself.”
“Kill myself?”
Jeok Cheongang let out a hollow laugh and opened his mouth.
“You’ve got quite a bark. Did you learn it from some marketplace mongrel?”
“They say a master and Disciple grow alike. You sound exactly like him.”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord clicked his tongue softly and tightened his grip.
Crack-crack!
With a louder, sharper crunch, Jin Taekyung’s limp feet thrashed in the air.
Deep furrows appeared between Jeok Cheongang’s brows.
“You bastard!”
“This is my final offer. Accept it, and you can save your Disciple and preserve your martial lineage. Refuse...”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord continued in a chilling voice.
“And I will break this fellow’s neck right now, then fight you in a life-and-death duel. You will most likely be the first to fall.”
This was no empty bluff.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord knew Jeok Cheongang was not in perfect condition either.
That was only natural. He had hovered between life and death for more than a month after fighting the Blood Lord and had only just awakened.
“What will you do?”
Jeok Cheongang’s eyelids trembled.
The old master regarded his Disciple, trapped in the enemy’s grasp, with an indescribable look before opening his mouth.
“Promise me... you will keep your word.”
“Of course.”
It was, of course, a lie.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord had no intention of leaving a single person alive.
Not the Sichuan Tang Clan. Not the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang. Not the Divine Physician, who lay unconscious behind them in the aftermath of the battle. And...
The Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, Jin Taekyung. He, especially, cannot be allowed to live.
The Sword Saint’s successor was dangerous enough, but Jin Taekyung was particularly dangerous.
If they had fought for another half a shichen—no, even another fifteen minutes—the brat might have attained enlightenment and broken through the wall of the Supreme Peak realm.
It was a great stroke of fortune that the Demon Lord had defeated him before his enlightenment could deepen.
The Lord of Heaven is aiding me.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord barely suppressed the corners of his mouth as they tried to curl upward.
Jeok Cheongang, who had been staring at him, abruptly spoke.
“Is that enough now?”
The unexpected question made the Western Heaven Demon Lord frown.
“What are you talking about?”
“You sly bastard. You've become even more of a monster since I last saw you.”
“What nonsense are you—”
But the Western Heaven Demon Lord could not finish.
No, he was unable to.
Grab.
Crack-crack-crack!
Fiery pain erupted from his wrist.
The next moment, reflected in the Western Heaven Demon Lord's widened eyes were his wrist, twisted as though a giant had wrung it, and a young man whose hand clamped around it like a hook.
“Jin Taekyuuung!”
How?
A roar filled with pain, disbelief, and shock thundered through the underground prison.
But Jin Taekyung did not hear him. Could not hear him.
His eyes were hazy, as though he were drunk, and he moved on instinct alone.
Krrrk!
Irresistible strength tore the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s wrist free as easily as uprooting a weed.
Blood fountained into the air amid searing pain.
For an instant, the Western Heaven Demon Lord's vision went white.
Then a streak of flame bloomed before him.
“I told you.”
The old master, wreathed from head to toe in blazing hellfire, spat out each word.
“Do not touch my Disciple. Not even a hair.”
KABOOOOOM!
A massive pillar of fire surged upward.
I felt dazed.
As though I might fall asleep at any moment. Or as though I had only just woken up.
Everything felt blurred and distant.
This has to be a dream.
It definitely was.
The fact that I was alive even though I should have died long ago. The fact that Jeok Cheongang had awakened even though he should have needed several more days before he was ready to wake up.
But...
Is this a dream too?
Ding.

System Jeok Cheongang has awakened from a long sleep! - You have successfully completed all related chain Quests. Your noble devotion and sacrifice will be rewarded! - Level Up! - Level Up! - Level Up! Stamina, Strength, Agility, and Internal Energy have been restored! - A total of three Level Ups has partially healed your physical injuries!
Ding. Ding. Ding.
The bright chime of bells echoed around me.
At the same time, an energy like warm sunlight spread throughout my body.
Broken bones fused together, and torn flesh healed. My damaged organs and shredded acupoints began to mend and settle back into place.
Slowly.
But steadily.
Crack.
My toes stepped on empty air.
Before I knew it, the Western Heaven Demon Lord was holding me by the throat.
My ruptured eardrums should have healed by now, but the conversation between the two men still sounded distant.
What is this feeling?
Hummm. Hummm.
A strange noise beyond description circled inside my head.
Then, in the next moment, Jeok Cheongang’s voice pierced clearly into my ears.
“How long do you intend to hang there?”
I don't really know, Old Master. I just... I just can't summon any strength. I don't even know if this is a dream or reality.
I wanted to answer that familiar face, but no voice came out.
The hand pressing against my throat suddenly felt uncomfortable.
Then... I should get it off me.
By the time the thought crossed my mind, my hand had already moved.
It shot out so quickly that even I didn’t realize it had moved and seized the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s wrist.
Crack-crack-crack!
Hard bones crumpled, and a scream burst forth.
Without hesitation, I twisted and yanked.
Something tore, and blood fountained into the air. Before a single drop could strike the floor, a streak of flame swept past me.
“It’s been a while, you reckless little brat.”
The voice stretched out, carrying a hint of laughter.
Hellfire flickered from Jeok Cheongang's palm as it passed by me.
The Flame Divine Palm, mastered to its utmost limit, slammed into the chest of the Western Heaven Demon Lord as he writhed in agony.
KABOOOOOM!
A massive pillar of fire surged upward, scorching the ceiling.
The flames seemed as though they would burn forever—until ink-black Sword Force extinguished them.
Ssssssssh!
“Die!”
Black clouds shrouded the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s entire body.
His lips were drenched in blood, and every vessel in his eyes had burst, staining them crimson.
He looked like a madman, but the power contained within his sword seemed capable of cleaving the heavens.
Whoooooosh!
Darkness erupted from his blade, splitting the pillar of fire as it shot forward.
“Ugh.”
A small groan escaped Jeok Cheongang’s lips as he tried to draw up his Scorching Yang Qi.
I felt the qi crouched within his still-unrecovered body waver.
I watched it all with vacant eyes.
The darkness rushing toward me through my hazy vision.
Jeok Cheongang’s swaying body.
And then—
“Ah.”
A single exclamation escaped my lips.
I was here, yet at the same time, I was not.
I could feel and see everything.
Everything surrounding me felt vivid and clear.
So that was it. That was what this meant.
A blinding flash pierced my entire body, from the crown of my head to the tips of my toes.
Everything that had blocked my path until now cracked and collapsed.
The world that had looked hazy, as though I were drunk, cleared up. My dazed mind became as clear as a summer sky.
At the end of it all shone a light called enlightenment.
Ding.
System Congratulations. You have finally crossed the wall and stepped into a great realm! - You have reached the Supreme Peak realm!
Ding. Ding. Ding.
The bells rang louder and clearer than ever before.
I took a step.
Space vanished, and the natural qi within it surged.
I drew White Flame into my grasp with Seizing an Object Through Empty Space, and a fire dragon roared from its spearhead.
KRAAOOOOOO!

My toes stepped on empty air.
Before I knew it, the Western Heaven Demon Lord was holding me by the throat.
My ruptured eardrums should have healed by now, but the conversation between the two men still sounded distant.
What is this feeling?
Hummm.
Hummm.
A strange noise beyond description circled inside my head.
Then, in the next moment, Jeok Cheongang’s voice pierced clearly into my ears.
“How long do you intend to hang there?”
I don't really know, Old Master.
I just...
I just can't summon any strength.
I don't even know if this is a dream or reality.
I wanted to answer that familiar face, but no voice came out.
The hand pressing against my throat suddenly felt uncomfortable.
Then...
I should get it off me.
By the time the thought crossed my mind, my hand had already moved.
It shot out so quickly that even I didn’t realize it had moved and seized the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s wrist.
Crack-crack-crack!
Hard bones crumpled, and a scream burst forth.
Without hesitation, I twisted and yanked.
Something tore, and blood fountained into the air.
Before a single drop could strike the floor, a streak of flame swept past me.
“It’s been a while, you reckless little brat.”
The voice stretched out, carrying a hint of laughter.
Hellfire flickered from Jeok Cheongang's palm as it passed by me.
The Flame Divine Palm, mastered to its utmost limit, slammed into the chest of the Western Heaven Demon Lord as he writhed in agony.
KABOOOOOM!
A massive pillar of fire surged upward, scorching the ceiling.
The flames seemed as though they would burn forever—until ink-black Sword Force extinguished them.
Ssssssssh!
“Die!”
Black clouds shrouded the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s entire body.
His lips were drenched in blood, and every vessel in his eyes had burst, staining them crimson.
He looked like a madman, but the power contained within his sword seemed capable of cleaving the heavens.
Whoooooosh!
Darkness erupted from his blade, splitting the pillar of fire as it shot forward.
“Ugh.”
A small groan escaped Jeok Cheongang’s lips as he tried to draw up his Scorching Yang Qi.
I felt the qi crouched within his still-unrecovered body waver.
I watched it all with vacant eyes.
The darkness rushing toward me through my hazy vision.
Jeok Cheongang’s swaying body.
And then—
“Ah.”
A single exclamation escaped my lips.
I was here, yet at the same time, I was not.
I could feel and see everything.
Everything surrounding me felt vivid and clear.
So that was it.
That was what this meant.
A blinding flash pierced my entire body, from the crown of my head to the tips of my toes.
Everything that had blocked my path until now cracked and collapsed.
The world that had looked hazy, as though I were drunk, cleared up.
My dazed mind became as clear as a summer sky.
At the end of it all shone a light called enlightenment.
Ding.
System Congratulations.
You have finally crossed the wall and stepped into a great realm! - You have reached the Supreme Peak realm!
Ding.
Ding.
Ding.
The bells rang louder and clearer than ever before.
I took a step.
Space vanished, and the natural qi within it surged.
I drew White Flame into my grasp with Seizing an Object Through Empty Space, and a fire dragon roared from its spearhead.
KRAAOOOOOO!

chapters.title: Chapter 365
paragraphs: So this is what it feels like.
Supreme Peak. The realm of the great martial artists chosen by heaven.
I had taken a step into a place that had always been beyond my reach, and I felt boundless freedom.
How could I put this...?
This is incredible.
A faint smile had already formed at the corners of my mouth.
Ding. Ding. Ding.
System The realm of Fire Gate Divine Technique has advanced to the eighth stage. - The realm of Fire Dragon Divine Spear has advanced to the eighth stage! Flamefire Path has advanced to...!
System notifications rang out without pause, announcing advances in my martial arts, the resulting Level Ups, and completed achievements.
Qi like molten lava surged from deep within me. I felt not the slightest fear of the darkness bearing down on Jeok Cheongang and me.
“Die!”
A scream-like shout. A face twisted like a fiend.
Nothing remained of the genial, smiling middle-aged man he had once appeared to be.
All that stood before me was a monster consumed by killing intent.
Whoooosh!
Ink-black Sword Force, wreathed in savage killing intent, came crashing down like a lightning bolt. One look was enough to feel the destructive power lurking within it.
But...
In the end, you were human too.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord was already exhausted from his injuries and fatigue, and his excessive rage had scattered his mind.
When the mind wavered, so did the qi. A needle couldn’t pierce a boulder, but it could slip through the gaps between grains of sand.
Sss.
One step.
The instant my toes pushed off the ground, the space between us vanished.
I appeared in front of Jeok Cheongang, blocking his path. He shouted urgently at my back.
“You little bastard, get back—”
His voice cut off.
Cyan-white energy surged over White Flame’s transparent spearhead.
Imbued with the heat of Extreme Yang, strands of energy intertwined like tangled thread, drawing together until they finally assumed a single form.
A beautiful yet destructive concentration of internal energy. The exclusive domain of great martial artists.
Force.
I had finally made it this far.
Trembling with exhilaration, I thrust my arm toward the oncoming darkness.
Ssssh!
A single line traced through the air. Cyan-white flame shot forward like an arrow and met the darkness head-on.
Heavenly Strike.
The fire dragon’s claws tore the ink-black Force to pieces.
KRAAAAAA!
Amid the deafening roar, I saw it clearly.
The darkness scattering—and the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s face twisting with rage and shock.
The backlash from his shattered Force inflicted an Internal Injury. Blood and a furious howl burst from his mouth.
“You dare—you dare!”
“What, motherfucker?”
You’re dead now.
I beamed and kicked off the ground.
But someone else was already streaking toward the Western Heaven Demon Lord, one step ahead of me.
A small figure.
Jeok Cheongang had brought his briefly disordered qi back under control.
—You can tell me what happened later.
A short Sound Transmission followed.
—First, let’s beat the shit out of that goddamn bastard.
It was the kind of comment that made me want to hit the Like button.
Or rather, the kind of Sound Transmission.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord was stunned.
How? How can this be happening?
More than a hundred years. Several jiazi of internal energy.
Everything he had built over all that time was collapsing. Being denied.
And by a mere brat in his twenties!
How is such a thing possible?
What crossed the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s mind at that moment went beyond mere doubt.
Supernatural powers.
A young man barely past twenty had manifested Force. Nor was that all. He possessed the strength of a giant and the speed of the wind.
Nothing short of a ghost’s intervention could explain it.
And yet...
You will be the ones who die.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord ground his teeth and planted his foot on the ground. At the same instant, a tremendous wave of qi erupted from his entire body.
“Come!”
He roared like a wounded tiger.
No—he truly was a wounded tiger.

Fatigue had accumulated over the long battle, and much of his internal energy had been exhausted. One wrist had been torn off, and one ankle was broken. A momentary misjudgment had even left him with an Internal Injury at the hands of a mere brat.
But even so, one fact remained unchanged.
“I am the Lord of Heaven’s loyal servant! So long as that person is with me, even death itself shall pass me by!”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s shout carried an almost heroic grandeur. Two voices—one old, one young—immediately followed.
“What kind of bullshit are you spouting now?”
“Sounds less like Dark Heaven and more like Darkcheonji. Hey, try saying, ‘Lee Man-ui is a son of a bitch.’”
Jeok Cheongang and Jin Taekyung.
Master and Disciple rushed forward like the wind and thrust out their arms together.
KWAANG!
A thunderous roar erupted as a terrifying wave of qi swept through the underground prison.
A moment later, blood trickled from one man’s lips.
“Cough.”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord staggered beneath the tremendous impact he had taken head-on.
Under normal circumstances, perhaps it would have been different. But for a man who had already suffered serious injuries, the joint attack of two Supreme Peak masters was truly threatening.
Even so, the Western Heaven Demon Lord refused to give up.
I’ll bring one of them down first.
The young Disciple overflowed with strength granted by some ghostly aid, while the old Master still suffered from his injuries.
Naturally, the Western Heaven Demon Lord chose the latter.
“Die!”
His leg lashed out like a whip.
Boom!
Jeok Cheongang blocked the terrifying kick with one hand and let out a low groan.
At that very moment—
“How dare you touch him.”
Crack! Crunch!
The spear shaft flashed upward like lightning and smashed into the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s jaw.
His vision went white. The tremendous force, which even his Body-Protecting Qi could not fully absorb, slammed his jaws shut and severed his tongue.
Pain and impact lifted the Western Heaven Demon Lord into the air.
Waiting for him were two hands wreathed in flame.
“This old man is the Fire King, you son of a bitch!”
With that vicious curse, Jeok Cheongang unleashed the Flame Divine Palm.
BOOM!
The already unstable Body-Protecting Qi scattered. The heat of Extreme Yang seeped through the spiderweb of cracks covering the Black Dragon Armor.
A burning agony seized him, and something hot surged up his throat.
“GWAAAAAAGH!”
Black blood mixed with pieces of his organs sprayed out. Before the blood could even reach the ground, a brief sound of something cutting through the air pierced the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s ears.
Ssssh-sh-sh-sh!
Dozens of spear shadows filled his blood-red eyes, their vessels already burst.
Cyan-white flames scorched the air as they closed in from every direction. The Western Heaven Demon Lord dragged up every last shred of strength he possessed.
Ssssss!
Ink-black Sword Force surged along his blade and collided with the spear shadows.
Every clash unleashed a tremendous roar and shock wave, shaking the underground prison and churning the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s insides.
“Graaagh...!”
But it wasn’t over.
“Do you have time to look away?”
The cold voice sounded just as Jeok Cheongang’s Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist drove into the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s side.
Crack! KRRRUNCH!
It was a full-powered blow from Jeok Cheongang, the Fire King acclaimed as the greatest of the Ten Kings.
Unable to withstand the tremendous impact, part of the Black Dragon Armor shattered along with his Body-Protecting Qi. Flesh burned, and bones crumpled.
“GAAAAAH!”
A horrific scream echoed through the prison.
Even as he writhed in agony, the Western Heaven Demon Lord drew up all his remaining internal energy and unleashed it in every direction.
BOOM! KWA-KWAKWANG!
The ground, ceiling, pillars, and rocks. The manifested ink-colored Force shot out without discrimination. Everything it touched turned to dust or was sliced apart like tofu.
Yet the two people who should have been its targets had already torn through the net of Force and reached the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
Shhk!
The Force gathered on the transparent spearhead slashed diagonally through the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s upper body, while the two flame-wreathed palms struck his collapsing chest.
BOOM! KWAANG!
The Western Heaven Demon Lord was hurled away like a cannonball in agony unlike anything he had ever experienced.
His body smashed through solid rock and buried itself deep within the wall.
“Ghk, ghek.”
A grotesque groan escaped him as he blinked.
Through his blurred vision, he saw two figures approaching.
Is this how I die?
The Western Heaven Demon Lord thought blankly.
For many long years, he had reigned over others as one of the strong. He had taken pleasure in trampling the weak and stealing everything they cherished.
Every ordinary martial artist in Murim contemplated death at least once.
But not the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
The only beings beneath heaven who should have been able to take his life were himself and the one supreme and exalted being—the Lord of Heaven.
And yet...
“How dare wretches such as you attempt to kill my servant?”
A voice as dry as desert sand slipped between his blood-soaked lips.
There was neither pain nor reason in the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s voice.
His eyes, now filled entirely with blood-red light, were no longer human.
Nor did they belong to the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
“This body has descended from heaven to earth. Kneel before me, from the lowest to the highest.”
At that moment, Jeok Cheongang and Jin Taekyung shouted like thunder.
“No way...”
“The Lord of Heaven!”
Rumble-rumble!
A terrifying energy spread from the Western Heaven Demon Lord—or rather, from the being temporarily borrowing his body—and shook the ground and ceiling.
An ink-colored current writhed like a tentacle from the stump of his torn-off arm, slowly sealing the wound that had been gushing blood like a waterfall.
“Worship me. Submit before omnipotent power.”
Plop. Plop.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord’s body slowly rose to its feet.
As he approached one step at a time, manifested internal energy spread behind him like wings.
And then—
Everything stopped.
The trembling. The wind. Even the drifting dust and the flow of the air.
Within that frozen world, a streak of darkness shot forward.
Ssssss!
The darkness approached without a sound and swallowed the two of them.
No—it would have.
Had a spearhead not thrust forward, cleaving through a flow of time divided into ever-finer instants.
Gooooooong—
Wind and qi condensed around the spearhead, then erupted.
Wreathed in cyan-white flame, the spearhead advanced, erasing everything in its path.
One Annihilation.
A blinding flash burst forth.
Time began to flow again.
With it came complete exhaustion and pain that made my entire body feel as though it were breaking apart.
I want to collapse just like this.
My arms, my legs, my fingers, every last strand of muscle—every part of my body felt ready to snap.
But I held on through sheer, superhuman strength.
Not yet. Not yet.
At the very least, I didn’t want to fall before he did.
“So just fucking die already, you bastard.”
I raised my head and looked at the Western Heaven Demon Lord—or rather, the thing borrowing his body.
Its entire body had been burned black, and a gaping hole had been blasted through its chest.
After inspecting the damage, the corners of its mouth slowly lifted.
“Interesting. Very interesting.”
Fwoosh.
The moment it finished speaking, its fingers turned to ash and scattered.
A stray breeze swept past, and its body slowly began to crumble.
But the thing borrowing another man’s body felt no pain. Instead, it tossed out a final remark with a laugh.
“We shall meet again.”
I barely managed to raise my middle finger.
“Go eat a dick.”
No answer came.
Beyond the drifting ash, System notifications announcing Quest success and Level Up rang out.
But the mental fatigue caused by the battle did not recover.
I only wanted to collapse right there.
No—I was already falling.
Grab.
A wrinkled hand caught me by the shoulder.
It belonged to Jeok Cheongang, the Fire King. When I saw his welcome face, I suddenly remembered something I needed to say.
“How was it?”
“What?”
“One Annihilation. It was incredible, right?”
The concern filling Jeok Cheongang’s face slowly melted away.
Then a gentle smile appeared on his lips.
“Yes. It was incredible.”
That was enough.
I closed my eyes with the answer I could no longer voice.
In the distance, the sound of the underground prison collapsing echoed faintly.

chapters.title: Chapter 366
paragraphs: Drip. Drip-drip-drip.
The world lay submerged in darkness so deep that it was impossible to tell how much time had passed.
Black clouds filled the sky, and the rain that had seemed like a passing shower showed no sign of stopping.
Within the grounds of the Sichuan Tang Clan, beside an overflowing pool of blood, corpses had piled up into a small hill.
“So? How are things inside?”
At the gates of the Sichuan Tang Clan, a black-clad man sat astride the corpse of an unknown Tang Clan martial artist. A subordinate who had just arrived from the Inner Hall answered him.
“It still isn’t over. I hear about a hundred of them remain.”
“What? That many?”
“Only half are martial artists. The rest are craftsmen who never learned martial arts, women, or children.”
“Then they should wipe them out and be done with it. What the hell are they wasting time for?”
The black-clad man’s irritation was only natural. Being stuck guarding the entrance while the others earned all the glory was bad enough, but this tedious gate duty still wasn’t over.
“Well, you see...”
“Is there some reason?”
At his superior’s frown, the subordinate hurriedly continued.
“The surviving Tang Clan martial artists are elites, for one thing. But the real problem is that they activated a mechanism array, and it’s holding everyone up.”
“A mechanism array? A poison array shouldn’t be difficult to break through.”
“It isn’t poison. It’s explosives. They had Heaven-Shaking Thunder hidden away.”
“...You don’t mean the Heaven-Shaking Thunder from Pyeokryeomun, do you?”
“It seems so. Because some of them charged in carrying Heaven-Shaking Thunder and died in the explosions, quite a few of our brothers suffered serious losses.”
“Ha. Would you look at these lunatics?”

The black-clad man’s mouth fell open. He had wondered what was happening when those ominous booms began echoing through the grounds, but he had never expected the Tang Clan to possess Heaven-Shaking Thunder from the long-destroyed Pyeokryeomun.
He could now understand, to some extent, why the battle had been delayed.
“Wait. Then what has the Demon Lord been doing? He should have been more than capable of slaughtering them all himself.”
The black-clad man’s question reflected his unwavering faith in the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
And for good reason. The Western Heaven Demon Lord was one of the few servants permitted an audience with the exalted Lord of Heaven, and he possessed terrifying martial might.

The black-clad man had only ever heard of Heaven-Shaking Thunder and had no idea how powerful it truly was. But even the grandfather of Heaven-Shaking Thunder itself could never harm the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
“I heard he went to the Tang Clan’s underground prison a shichen ago.”
The subordinate’s answer made the black-clad man nod.
If the Demon Lord had gone there personally, he must have had a reason, and he would resolve the matter without the slightest mistake. The black-clad man felt not a trace of worry or doubt.
Nor was he alone. Everyone felt the same way.
“Then what about the First Captain?”
First Captain was the position First Fiend, the eldest of the Qilian Three Fiends, had assumed upon entering the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s service.
After a brief hesitation, the subordinate answered.

“He’s engaged in a life-and-death duel with the Sword Saint’s successor in the Inner Hall. No one has been able to approach him since one of our brothers who went to deliver news about the Heaven-Shaking Thunder lost his head.”
“...I see.”
The black-clad man said no more.
What he felt toward the Western Heaven Demon Lord was reverence and trust. What he felt toward First Fiend was fear. He had no desire to voice a careless complaint and meet a gruesome end.
“Um, Captain.”
“Do you have something to say?”
“Yes. The deputy captain asked whether we’d heard from the brothers sent to Qingcheng and Emei.”
“A message arrived just before you got here.”
The black-clad man handed him a small tube. The subordinate checked its contents, then looked up in confusion.
“This is...”
“It came from Emei.”
“Is this the only one?”
“Yes. We still haven’t heard anything from Qingcheng.”
“Their message should have arrived by now.”
“That’s true. But you know what the other captains are like.”
The three brothers of the Qilian Three Fiends resembled one another in more than their ugly appearances.
All three were cruel and eccentric fiends who lost their minds at the sight of blood.
Third Fiend, who had been assigned to Emei Sect, was somewhat better than the others. At least he had sent a messenger eagle at the appointed time.
The problem was that, according to his letter, the situation at Emei was not proceeding smoothly.
The Beggars’ Sect got involved.
The letter reported that Beggars’ Sect disciples wielding bamboo staffs and dog-beating clubs had appeared out of nowhere.
Individually, their martial arts were no match for Dark Heaven’s martial artists, but their appearance held greater significance.
They’ve already caught our scent.
The attack had been meticulously planned. The battle should have ended swiftly and decisively, yet it was dragging on.
Even with this unexpected complication, however, the black-clad man had no doubt that his side would prevail.
He had just shaken off the unease that had briefly troubled him when he suddenly looked up.
“Hmm?”
“What is it?”
“What’s that?”
At the black-clad man’s questioning voice, both the subordinate from the Inner Hall and the thirty-odd martial artists stationed at regular intervals along the walls gathered around him.
Then they saw it.
Beyond the collapsed wall, a streak of wind tore through the driving rain.
It moved swiftly enough to be called a ray of light. Then it erupted in a dazzling flash.
Ssshhhhhhk—crack!
The thirty-odd martial artists blinked. When they reflexively touched their faces, their fingers came away sticky with blood.
Slowly—very slowly—their mouths fell open and their heads turned.
In a world that seemed to have slowed to a crawl, they watched their superior collapse like a rotten old tree.
A hole the size of a fingernail had been punched through the center of his forehead.
They felt as though they had been clubbed across the backs of their heads.
Their superior was a Peak master capable of making a name for himself anywhere under heaven. Yet a man of such skill had been killed by a strike none of them had even seen.
Before anyone present could recover from that tremendous shock, a figure sprang up onto the wall.
And then—
Ssssh-sh-sh-sh!
In the darkness, death-laden rays of light plunged down like bolts of lightning.
First Fiend was on the verge of going insane.
No—he had already been insane for more than fifty years. Now he was becoming an even greater lunatic.
“Why! Why! How could this be!”
Boom! Boom! Boom!
Blood-red Force surged from the twin axes in his hands, smashing and cleaving everything around him.
The sturdy pavilion where the Family Head of the Sichuan Tang Clan had once resided had long since been reduced to ruins.
A lone figure darted back and forth through the wreckage.
“Ah! Eeng! Eek! Whoosh!”
Cheongpung hopped and skipped around, dodging the Force while making strange noises. First Fiend’s eyes rolled white.
“You little son of a—!”
It was enough to drive him mad.

His opponent was a mere pup not yet thirty. He might have been an unprecedented monster who had received the Sword Saint’s teachings and reached the Supreme Peak realm in his twenties, but even that could not erase the gulf created by age and experience.
First Fiend was an old monster from two generations back. He possessed immense internal energy, experience, and martial arts of the highest realm.
That was why, although he had been surprised at first, he had felt no real sense of danger.
The Sword Saint raised quite a monster. There was a reason the Demon Lord warned me about him before leaving. But he still has a long way to go before he can challenge this old man. Heh heh heh.
It did not take long, however, for the smile on his lips to twist into fury.
“Die! I said die!”
With a maddened roar, he swept his twin axes down through the air. A vast net of Force unfurled and descended over Cheongpung’s head.
The Red Slaughter Asura Net.
It was one of the signature techniques left behind by the Red Slaughter Demon, who had dyed the martial world in blood three hundred years ago.

That infamous Slaughter Saint, hunted throughout the Central Plains as a public enemy of Murim, had met his end in an unnamed cave in the Qilian Mountains. Three brothers hiding there from the world had discovered the martial arts manual he left behind. After mastering its contents, they had emerged anew as the Qilian Three Fiends.
And now, the perfected Red Slaughter Asura Net—a technique no one since the Red Slaughter Demon had been able to perform—had finally reappeared through First Fiend’s twin axes.
Whoooosh!
That was when Cheongpung’s gaze deepened as he watched the red net of Force close in from every direction.
Shaaah—
A cool breeze blew.
At the same time, purple Sword Force enveloped his blade and sliced diagonally through the net.
Slash!
First Fiend’s mouth fell open as Cheongpung’s One-Character Wisdom Sword dismantled the perfected Red Slaughter Asura Net with absurd ease.
“Y-You knew the Red Slaughter Demon’s martial arts?”
No perfect martial art existed.

Every martial art left by the Red Slaughter Demon deserved to be called a signature technique, but each still possessed weaknesses. Those weaknesses were secrets known only to the Qilian Three Fiends.
Yet the pup before him had identified them precisely.
“Answer me this instant!”
Cheongpung’s reply was short and simple.
“What’s the Red Slaughter Demon? I’ve never heard of him.”
“...What?”
“Oh, is this about what I just did?”
Cheongpung tilted his head.
“I could just see it.”
“Y-You could see it?”
“If you keep watching, you start to understand. You have more internal energy than I do, Grandpa, and your martial arts are more complicated, so it took a little longer.”
“It took longer?”
“Yes. But I don’t think it’ll take that long anymore.”
First Fiend understood what Cheongpung meant the very next moment.
Ssssh!
A purple flash filled his vision.
Caught off guard by the sudden sword strike, First Fiend hurriedly whipped both axes through the air like lightning.
The Red Slaughter Eighteen Axes lacked subtlety, but its destructive power was second to none. Backed by more than two jiazi of internal energy, it carried enough force to split heaven and earth.
And yet—
Kagagagak!
Cheongpung’s smoothly extended blade guided one axe aside, then struck the other as it swept powerfully toward his flank.
KWAANG!
A thunderous boom erupted, and First Fiend staggered. He had effectively smashed his own axes together.
Even as he retreated, he stared in stunned disbelief.
W-What in the world just happened?
Fwoosh!
Cheongpung shot toward him.
His clear eyes had grown deep and still, while sunset-purple qi surged from his sword.
Whooooom!
First Fiend stared blankly at the strike descending toward the crown of his head.
Th-This is...
There was no mistaking it.
The Red Slaughter Eighteen Axes.
No—this martial art should now be called the Red Slaughter Eighteen Swords.
In less than a shichen, Cheongpung had not only seen through and dismantled First Fiend’s martial arts. He was making them his own.
How can this be!
First Fiend swung his twin axes with a silent cry of shock.
The revelation had slowed his reactions, but not enough to keep him from countering.
At least, that was what he believed—until Cheongpung’s sword moved.
Whoooong.
The heavy, destructive sword stroke softened into the fall of a flower. Thirty-six plum blossoms bloomed from its tip and drifted down through the air.
One martial art surfaced in First Fiend’s mind.
The Thirty-Six Plum Blossom Swords.
At the same time, he realized—
I can’t avoid it.
Ssssh-sh-sh-sh!
Thirty-six plum blossoms—or rather, thirty-six streaks of Force—enveloped First Fiend’s entire body.
Blood spread like mist. Slashed from head to toe, First Fiend staggered backward.
Fear filled his eyes as he stared at Cheongpung, whose sword hung loosely at his side.
“Cough. You... You are...”
“Good thing it’s raining.”
Cheongpung stepped forward, his voice calm.
“I don’t like the smell of blood.”
Splash.
Cheongpung stepped into a crimson puddle of rainwater and blood. First Fiend let out a piercing scream.
“Anyone! Is there no one out there? Hurry, get this bastard...!”
At that moment, a low voice slipped into his ear.
“Don’t call out. There’s no one here.”
There had been no footsteps. No hint of anyone’s presence.
And yet he was there.
The raindrops pouring down overhead shattered in midair before they could touch him.
“Who the hell are you—”
Slash!
First Fiend’s head flew into the air.
Cheongpung flicked the blood from his sword, then stared with a rigid expression at him, standing tall before him.
“I’d like to ask you the same thing. Who are you?”
His voice trembled faintly as he continued.
“Mungyeong.”
