chapters.title: Chapter 367
paragraphs: The warning signs had already been there.
And there was more than enough cause.
Rumble-rumble-rumble!

The ground split apart, and the ceiling shook. The underground prison that had symbolized the darkness of the Sichuan Tang Clan for hundreds of years could no longer withstand the aftermath of one battle after another. It was collapsing.
Along with the countless vengeful spirits of prisoners who had died in the prison—and the three people who were still alive and well.
“...What the fucking hell is this?”
Jeok Cheongang looked around in disbelief.
He had definitely been in a forest before closing his eyes. Then he had opened them to find himself in a cave that might or might not be a prison.
And that wasn’t all. He had dragged his still-ailing old body into a fight to the death with some unknown son of a bitch.
Fine. He could understand things up to that point. Jin Taekyung passing out the moment the battle ended? That was entirely possible too.
But...
“Isn’t this taking things too damn far? Fuck.”
It was the kind of situation that made profanity spill out on its own.
Where was this place? Who was I? Why was the ground splitting apart, and why were boulders the size of people raining down from overhead?
Overcome by a sudden wave of profound regret, Jeok Cheongang nearly ascended to immortality on the spot.
“Goddamn it.”
He had no idea what was going on, but first he had to get out of there.
Once he reached that conclusion, he moved with lightning speed.
First, I need to get Taekyung... But who the hell is this old man?
Ah, hell. Whatever.
Jeok Cheongang slung the unconscious Jin Taekyung and the Divine Physician over his shoulders, then shot forward.
Sssshhhk! Boom!
A massive rock that fell from the ceiling grazed Jeok Cheongang by a hair and smashed into the ground. But that was only the beginning.
Boom! Boom! Rumble!
With every step he took, bizarre rocks came pouring down like a rain shower. The spectacle made Jeok Cheongang’s flesh crawl.
One wrong move, and I could end up buried here.
This was no small cave.
If a cliff weighing tens of millions of geun came crashing down on their heads, even Jeok Cheongang could not guarantee his survival.
Especially with the lingering aftereffects of his injuries.
“Cough.”
He staggered as he raced across the fractured ground. Swallowing the blood rising in his throat, Jeok Cheongang smiled bitterly.
I’m in a sorry state.
His limbs were stiff as stone after so long without moving. He was ravenously hungry and utterly drained.

In that condition, he had fought some monstrous bastard who had crawled out of who-knew-where. Of course his body had deteriorated even further. If not for his internal energy, he would have collapsed long ago.
Rumble!
The vibrations suddenly grew even stronger. Jeok Cheongang gritted his teeth.
All right, I get it. Stop rushing me. I’ll find a way out.
There was someone he had to save. His one and only Disciple, who had become light and warmth when Jeok Cheongang wandered through cold, dark memories.
Yes. My one and only Disciple. My Disciple, without a doubt.
His grip tightened on the two men. An unknown strength seemed to surge from somewhere deep within him.
Flamefire Path.
Jeok Cheongang, who had faltered for a moment, became a streak of flame.
Whooosh!
The clash between Jin Taekyung and the Western Heaven Demon Lord had caused the underground prison to collapse, but that destruction actually helped Jeok Cheongang.
The interior had been devastated by their battle. All the walls that had once divided the underground prison into a maze had crumbled, leaving behind one vast cavern.
There!
Jeok Cheongang’s eyes flashed as he raced forward with his movement technique.
Every enclosed space had an entrance.
At the place where he felt a faint breeze blowing from somewhere, Jeok Cheongang saw the entrance to the underground prison—barely wide enough for one person to pass through.
Hurry. Hurry...!
Jeok Cheongang hurled himself forward with every ounce of strength he had.
He bounded across the heaving ground and dodged the rocks falling from overhead.
He passed the corpse of the Heavenly Power Demon, the old man lying dead as though asleep with a peaceful smile on his face, and shot farther and faster.
The time was brief, yet felt like an eternity. At last, Jeok Cheongang was about to take his final step toward the prison entrance.
“Made...!”
Rrrrumble! Krrrrrumble!
A tremor and roar equal to every deafening crash thus far combined—no, greater than all of them—erupted at once.
The ceiling collapsed.
Massive rocks that had accumulated over hundreds, perhaps thousands, of years crashed down over the entrance to the underground prison.
Then—
“Get the hell out of my way!”
An azure dragon’s roar shook the underground prison as Jeok Cheongang drove his blue-white-flame-wreathed fist into the center of the falling rock.
KWAAAANG!
The superheated energy contained in the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist smashed and melted the rocks.
A roar like the sky splitting apart thundered through the cavern, followed by a sudden blast of scorching wind that swept across the underground prison.
“What in the world...?”
The middle-aged man in black who had hurried over after hearing the roar swallowed a groan at the sight before him.
Rrrrrumble!
Nature itself was collapsing. The cliff hundreds of zhang tall that loomed behind the Sichuan Tang Clan was slowly sinking into the earth.
The sight was staggering even from more than a hundred zhang away, but there was a far greater problem.
“D-Deputy Captain. That’s where the Demon Lord is...”
The underground prison!
The middle-aged black-clad man, the deputy captain of Dark Heaven, felt a chill run down his spine at his subordinate’s words.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord. If anything had happened to him...
We’re all finished.
Cold sweat rolled down his forehead. He had not been this nervous even when the Sichuan Tang Clan used Heaven-Shaking Thunder.
He barked an urgent order.
“Gather every brother scattered across the grounds immediately!”
“E-Everyone? But there are still Tang Clan bastards—”
“Those bastards aren’t the problem. Hurry!”
“Y-Yes, sir!”
The subordinate, frozen stiff, pulled a firework from inside his clothes and lit it. With a pop, a red streak of light burst in the air.
At the emergency signal, the black-clad men scattered throughout the Sichuan Tang Clan began converging on the area.
Within moments, well over a hundred had assembled.
“Deputy Captain. Please give us your orders.”
The deputy captain wanted to smash in the skull of the man who had just spoken. The same went for their captain, First Fiend, who had yet to show so much as a hair despite the emergency signal.
Damn it.
The deputy captain’s throat bobbed as he stared at the still-collapsing cliff.
The order he was about to give was tantamount to suicide. He was going to send them beneath a collapsing cliff to search for the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
But there was no other choice. He had to give the order.
“The Demon Lord is in there. As deputy captain, I will lead the way, and every last one of you will—”
Just as the deputy captain struggled to continue his command—
KABOOM!
An unidentifiable roar erupted, and the pile of rocks forming a small hill exploded outward.
The deputy captain and everyone around him saw a large figure burst up through the rubble.
“Demon Lord! The Demon Lord has emerged—!”
The shout cut off unfinished.
Crash! Thud-thud-thud!
The figure bounced a considerable distance from the cliff like a cannonball before rolling across muddy water and sludge and finally coming to a stop.
It was an old man, clutching two people larger than himself beneath his arms. Jeok Cheongang stared up at the dark, cloud-filled sky and drew a deep breath.
“Phaaah!”
Fresh air and rainwater seeped in through his nose and mouth.

The refreshing sensation felt as if it were washing even his soul clean. His internal energy was already exhausted, and his body felt as though it had been smashed to pieces, but Jeok Cheongang smiled with relief at having rescued Jin Taekyung.
Then, in the next instant, he staggeringly raised his upper body—and froze.
A group stood a little over twenty zhang away, staring at him.
Well over a hundred men dressed in black, all holding bloodstained weapons.
Jeok Cheongang groaned under his breath.
“...Goddamn it. No matter how I look at them, they don’t seem like good people.”
A voice behind him confirmed his suspicion.
“They call themselves Dark Heaven.”
Jeok Cheongang was not startled by the unexpected voice.
He had been through every manner of hardship and had just escaped being crushed to death. He had already noticed from the change in his breathing that the unknown old man he had rescued was awake.
“I see. Dark Heaven. I knew it had to be those sons of bitches.”
After muttering a curse, Jeok Cheongang continued without turning around.
“Do you know where we are?”
“The Sichuan Tang Clan. Regrettably, it appears the battle has already been decided.”
“...This is driving me insane.”
That brief remark summed up Jeok Cheongang’s feelings.
He did not have enough time to wonder how any of this had happened.
“What’s your name?”
“Dong Feng. My name is Dong Feng.”
“Your sobriquet?”
“I am not a martial artist, so naturally I have none.”
“Your dantian was damaged. You’re not a martial artist?”
“I only learned a little because my Master would not stop pestering me. Medicine was always where my heart lay.”
Jeok Cheongang’s eyebrow twitched.

Despite his severe injuries, the old man’s calm bearing and manner of speech carried an unmistakable air of wisdom. Why did they remind Jeok Cheongang of a physician whose medical arts were said to have reached the divine realm?
“The Divine Physician?”
“I am merely an old medical apprentice of no consequence.”
Jeok Cheongang let out a hollow laugh at the Divine Physician’s answer. At last, he thought he understood what had happened.
“Thank you for waking an old man who was at death’s door.”
“You awakened on your own. Your will was simply that strong, Sir Jeok.”
“I had no choice. Some reckless fool woke me up.”
“That very reckless fool crossed the Central Plains to find me and begged for my help. He said he would do anything if it meant saving you, Sir Jeok.”
Jeok Cheongang turned his head. Jin Taekyung lay collapsed beside him, covered in blood and mud.
“...What a foolish boy.”
If he could wake the boy now, he would.
Perhaps then they could have one final conversation.
But Jin Taekyung had exhausted every last ounce of strength. He would not awaken. Jeok Cheongang knew that even without the Divine Physician telling him.
Yes. Perhaps... perhaps this is for the best.
Jeok Cheongang slowly rose to his feet. Ignoring the pain stabbing through his entire body, he addressed the Divine Physician behind him.
“Still have any strength left?”
“I did in my younger days. Before meeting my Master, I worked as a carpenter.”
“That’s an unusual past for the Divine Physician. What about now?”
“I am seventy years old.”
“Your dantian is damaged, so it won’t be easy, but squeeze out every last bit of strength you have. Run as far away as you can.”
“With Young Master Jin?”
“I’m glad you understand.”
After a brief silence, the Divine Physician spoke.
“Sir Jeok... You intend to throw your life away.”
“Throw it away?”
A faint smile touched the corner of Jeok Cheongang’s mouth. His gaze settled on the approaching men in black.
“Do you know why a flame dies out?”
Jeok Cheongang did not wait for the Divine Physician’s answer.
Muddy water splashed beneath his advancing feet. At some point, the rain that had seemed as if it would never end had stopped.
His voice rang out, clear and unburdened.
“Because there is nothing left to burn. That is why it slowly dies out atop the ashes.”
Jeok Cheongang was ready to kindle his final flame.
He felt neither fear nor anger at the death striding toward him.
Only regret.
He would no longer be able to remain by his Disciple’s side.
“Take care of Taekyung for me.”
Just as Jeok Cheongang stepped forward after making that heartfelt request, the Divine Physician spoke.

“After witnessing countless births, aging, sickness, and deaths, I began to wonder. Does the underworld truly exist? If so, who is this fellow called Yama? And if I go there, will I meet the patients I failed to save?”

“Whenever such questions troubled me, my Master would say, ‘The underworld must be full from all the people you sent ahead of you. You should ascend to the celestial realm instead and keep the immortals company.’”
The Divine Physician looked at Jeok Cheongang and continued quietly.
“Sir Jeok. The underworld is full. Please wait a little longer.”
At that moment, Jeok Cheongang felt as if every hair on his body had stood on end, and he raised his head.
High above, bathed in sunlight streaming between the retreating dark clouds, stood a boy.
No. Not a boy. That man is...!
Those eyes were clear and bright like a boy’s, yet the gaze itself was ancient and seasoned, betraying no emotion whatsoever.
Jeok Cheongang had seen those eyes only once, a very long time ago.
That was precisely why he could never forget the feeling they evoked.
The boy’s appearance brought someone to mind, and Jeok Cheongang cried out in shock.
“The Slaughter Saint...!”

If not for his internal energy, he would have collapsed long ago.

The vibrations suddenly grew even stronger.

Flamefire Path.

Whooosh!
The clash between Jin Taekyung and the Western Heaven Demon Lord had caused the underground prison to collapse, but that destruction actually helped Jeok Cheongang.
The interior had been devastated by their battle.
All the walls that had once divided the underground prison into a maze had crumbled, leaving behind one vast cavern.

Every enclosed space had an entrance.

The time was brief, yet felt like an eternity.
At last, Jeok Cheongang was about to take his final step toward the prison entrance.

Krrrrrumble!
A tremor and roar equal to every deafening crash thus far combined—no, greater than all of them—erupted at once.
The ceiling collapsed.
Massive rocks that had accumulated over hundreds, perhaps thousands, of years crashed down over the entrance to the underground prison.
Then—

An azure dragon’s roar shook the underground prison as Jeok Cheongang drove his blue-white-flame-wreathed fist into the center of the falling rock.

“What in the world...?”
The middle-aged man in black who had hurried over after hearing the roar swallowed a groan at the sight before him.

Nature itself was collapsing.

The underground prison!

The Western Heaven Demon Lord.

We’re all finished.

He had not been this nervous even when the Sichuan Tang Clan used Heaven-Shaking Thunder.

paragraphs: The boy—or rather, the “he” bearing the name Mungyeong—looked down at the ground below his feet.
Countless eyes stared up at him in disbelief. Among them was a familiar face.
They had met only once, long ago, but it was not difficult to recognize him.
“It has been a long time, Fire King.”
At his greeting, Fire King Jeok Cheongang’s eyes trembled violently.
“So it really was you...”
The greatest assassin under heaven. He had inspired not merely condemnation and contempt in countless martial artists, but awe. Then one day, he had vanished without a trace, never to appear again.
At least, not until moments ago.
“Why are you here...?”
“A great deal has happened. A great deal indeed. Wouldn’t you agree?”
The question was directed at an old man. He gazed at the Divine Physician—or rather, Dong Feng—with indescribable eyes before opening his lips.
“Thank goodness. I wasn’t too late.”
His voice rang out from every direction.
Six-Harmonies Voice Transmission.
A shudder ran through everyone at the unfathomable realm of martial arts displayed before them. The old physician quietly shook his head.
“You were too late.”
His next words carried a note of regret.
“Too late to turn back the years that have passed.”
“What can be done? Once water is spilled, it is not easily gathered again.”
“Do you not regret it?”
“Regret...”
At his Disciple’s words, he raised his head and looked toward the sky.
The rain that had seemed as though it would fall forever was gone, as were the dark clouds that had blotted out the sun. All that remained was the vast azure heaven.
Is this what you intended?
He posed the question to someone who might be looking down upon the mortal realm from above.
But no answer came.
Just as it never had.
What a damned thing this is.
He slowly closed his eyes. In the pitch-black darkness, memories steeped in blood and struggle flashed past.
He had been raised as an assassin and lived as one. His inborn karma was that of an assassin, so he killed—but he had been born human, and he hated killing.
That was why, near the end of the Great War that had stained the continent with blood, the aging assassin had buried his weapons and chosen to live as a physician.
But...
Had it come to this after all?
With a quiet murmur, he opened his eyes.
A boy’s hands, white and soft.
Returned to Youth had transformed his flesh several years ago, but even that could not erase the scent of blood steeped into his hands.
“I lived as a physician for more than forty years. I wished to die as one.”
His voice, laden with immense internal energy, struck their ears like thunder. The black-clad men staggered as though the sound had shaken their very souls.
“And yet, why have you come here?”
His killing intent made every hair stand on end. The deputy captain, frozen as he stared at the figure in the sky, spoke in a trembling voice.
“E-Even if you truly are the Slaughter Saint, this is no concern of yours.”
“No concern of mine?”
He muttered the words in a low voice before throwing down the travel bag he had been holding.
Thud!
Something bounced out of the bag as it struck the ground and rolled to the deputy captain’s feet.
“T-This is...”
They were the severed heads of two men. Though they belonged to different people, their bulging eyes and twisted expressions looked almost identical.
Like twins born at the same hour on the same day.
The deputy captain’s gaze fixed on one of them.
“Captain!”
As the deputy captain stared in horror at First Fiend’s severed head, the Slaughter Saint slowly spoke.
“One question. Was the one at Qingcheng the second or third of the Qilian Three Fiends?”
Only then did the deputy captain understand.
Why no word had come from the Qingcheng Sect—and where the brothers who had failed to return after seeing the emergency signal had gone.
Only one path remained. The realization struck like lightning, and he unleashed a shout imbued with internal energy.
“Everyone, attack! Kill hi—”
Slash!
The deputy captain’s shout was cut short.
A breeze brushed his neck, and suddenly someone was standing behind him.
Can this truly be... the movement of a human being?
That was the last question to cross his mind.
He had failed to recognize the Ghost Illusory Slaughter Step performed by the greatest assassin under heaven—or rather, the greatest assassin in all history.
Only death awaited him.
Fwoosh!
Blood erupted from the severed neck in a fountain. A figure brushed past the collapsing body and took another step, stirring a wind heavy with the scent of blood.
Slash. Slash. Slash!
The heads of the black-clad men who had watched their superior die in a daze flew into the air.
Before the streams of blood could reach the ground, something pale and ghostlike swept through them.
“It was the life I wanted so desperately.”
Murmuring under his breath, he extended both hands. Long, slender threads streamed from his ten fingers.
Threads of Force—beautiful and destructive.
“And yet, why did you...”
Whoosh!
When his ten curved fingers slashed downward through the air, Force tore through space.
Everything that stood in its way was cut apart and split open. Shattered armor and weapons, limbs and heads, flew in every direction.
In a world brought to a standstill by blood and death, only one person moved freely.
“Did you wake me?”
Consumed by sorrow and fury, he was no longer the cheerful boy or the physician who had passed the two-character name Divine Physician down to his Disciple.

He had returned to the person he had been before earning the name Divine Physician, before meeting the young carpenter who had fallen into grief after losing his wife and children to an epidemic, and before burying his weapons and leaving the Murim.
“The Slaughter Saint...!”
Someone screamed the name.
His eyes had sunk deeper than the abyss. He flung out both arms, and the wind—now a raging storm—swallowed more than a hundred black-clad men.
Kwaaang!
A high hill stood east of the Sichuan Tang Clan.
From there, one could see the entire Tang Clan estate at a glance. A small watchtower stood atop it, and martial artists had once taken turns standing guard.
Once.
Drip. Drip.
Drops of blood fell from the watchtower and dampened the grass. Some slid down the hill and touched someone’s hand.
Its back was deeply wrinkled, and its nails had turned green from long years spent practicing poison arts.
The hand belonged to Tang Sadok, the current Family Head of the Sichuan Tang Clan—the Myriad-Poison Asura.
“Cough.”
Blood sprayed from between his parched lips. His eyes, usually cold and forceful, looked ready to go out at any moment.
“Is this how it ends?”
Tang Sadok murmured faintly.
Everything was racing toward its end. His life. The glorious history of the Sichuan Tang Clan.
“Our family, built over centuries... brought down in a single day.”
Tang Sadok’s lament rang hollow. He no longer possessed the strength even to feel anger or sorrow.
His limbs crushed and his internal injuries severe, all the old Family Head could do was lean against an unknown tree and watch his clan perish.
This is my final gift to you.
The smiling face of a middle-aged man flashed before Tang Sadok’s eyes.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord had not kept his promise. To him, the destruction of the Sichuan Tang Clan had been a foregone conclusion from the very beginning.
“Urgh... Blergh!”
The rage flaring within him like wildfire worsened his internal injuries. Tang Sadok vomited nearly half a gallon of blood, then gasped for breath.
“I’m sorry. I’m sorry...”

It was an apology to the ancestors of the Sichuan Tang Clan. To the innocent members of his household who had lost their lives because they had been saddled with an unworthy Family Head. And to Jin Taekyung and his companions, who had likely already met gruesome deaths at the hands of the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
Of course, none of them could hear Tang Sadok’s voice.
If we meet in the afterlife, I will apologize to you myself.
Just as Tang Sadok murmured those words inwardly—
Rustle.
The bushes stirred, and he sensed something approaching.
No. It was not human.
Only when the strange presence had drawn right up to him did Tang Sadok realize who it belonged to.
Hiss. Hiss.
A flicking tongue. A horned, triangular head. A pure-white snake burrowed into Tang Sadok’s arms.
“Ha... hahaha.”
Tang Sadok laughed weakly, both happy and hollow.
“So it was you.”
Hisss.
The Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake, Mimi, hissed as if answering its master. Its cold tongue licked the beard matted with blood.
“Clever creature. How did you find me all the way out here?”
Tang Sadok gazed at his pet snake through clouded eyes.
He had let Mimi loose because he was worried the snake might be injured in the melee. He had never thought they would meet again like this.
Nor had he imagined their final farewell would happen this way.
Rumble!
A tremendous roar shook the hill. The earth rose, and the branches of the trees trembled.
Tang Sadok raised his head and tried to find the source, but his failing eyesight could no longer make out what was happening.
He could infer only one thing.
Has the time come?
It was a roar on an entirely different scale from Heaven-Shaking Thunder.
At last, the destruction of the great Sichuan Tang Clan had reached his doorstep.
Tang Sadok slowly closed his eyes, then opened them again.
“Leave.”
Hiss?
The snake’s triangular snout tilted to one side.
“This old man has little time left. Neither does the Tang Clan. If you stay here, you will be caught up in this calamity as well.”
Tang Sadok was the Family Head of the Sichuan Tang Clan. Even if the Western Heaven Demon Lord did not come himself, someone would certainly come to confirm whether he was alive or dead.
Tang Sadok could easily imagine what those vicious men would do if they saw the Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake guarding its master’s side.
“So go. Hurry!”
He wanted to shout, but the voice he forced out was so thin it seemed ready to break apart.
Yet the spirit creature that had spent so many years beside Tang Sadok understood the final wish of the man who had been both its master and its friend.
Drip. Drip.
Damp drops fell onto Tang Sadok’s wrinkled hand.
Leaving behind a few tears, Mimi slithered away and disappeared, the snake’s white body gliding across the ground.
As her presence receded into the distance, a bitter smile briefly touched Tang Sadok’s lips.
“Yes. Go carefully.”
In his youth, he had roamed the battlefields. After the war, he had devoted his life to helping his father, the Poison King, rebuild the Sichuan Tang Clan.
He had always been expected to remain cold and meticulous. He had no friend with whom he could share his heart, no lover, and no child of his own blood.
Had that spiritual creature not remained by his side all those years, he could never have endured the loneliness.
From today onward, your name is Mimi. Tang Mimi.
On the day he first encountered the tiny Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake, Tang Sadok had given her the Tang family name.
They shared neither blood nor even species, but Tang Mimi was a member of the Sichuan Tang Clan, recognized as such by its Family Head.
I have lost everyone, and you alone are the one I send away alive. Hahaha.
Tang Sadok let out a hollow laugh and blinked.
Through his fading senses, the roar and someone’s screams echoed faintly from below the hill.
It must have been the final struggle of those fighting to stave off the clan’s destruction.
This old man is here, too. I, Tang Sadok, Family Head of the great Sichuan Tang Clan, am here! Come to me!
The cry, as if he were coughing up blood, only hovered at the tip of his tongue.
Tang Sadok felt the strength slowly drain from his entire body. His heavy eyelids sank lower, little by little.
I’m tired.
What if he simply closed his eyes and fell into a deep sleep?
If he took a short nap and awoke in the grand armchair in the Family Head’s Hall, perhaps he would be able to see the familiar faces of his family.
How wonderful it would be if everything that had happened—including his father’s death—were nothing more than a Butterfly Dream.
Yes. If only it were.
His trembling eyelids slowly sank shut.
No—they were just about to close.
“Mimi! Quick Attack!”
Hisssssss!
What the hell is this bullshit?
Tang Sadok’s eyes flew open.
His vision suddenly cleared, revealing a young man racing toward him and Mimi’s white body shooting through the air like an arrow.
“Y-You?”
“Wow! Wild Grandpa Tang spotted!”
Tang Sadok blinked at Cheongpung, who was grinning brightly despite the blood covering his face.
“What... what is going on? How did you...?”
Cheongpung answered energetically.
“Mimi! Whirlwind!”
Whirrrrr!
If Tang Sadok had possessed even a shred of strength, he would have cursed him out.
Cheongpung and Mimi realized their mistake too late and bowed their heads.
“Ah, I’m sorry.”
Hiss.
Tang Sadok forgot that he had been half dead only moments ago and stared blankly at the man and snake before him. At last, he managed to speak.
“Our family... What happened to our family?”
“They all died.”
“Oh. Not the Tang Clan. I meant Dark Heaven’s black-clad men.”
You should have said that first!
As Tang Sadok choked on shock and fury, Cheongpung pressed a finger to his Mingmen acupoint. Warmth like a spring day seeped into his body.
“Cheongpung! True Qi Guidance!”
This bastard is going to keep this up until the very end...
Tang Sadok wanted to ask what had happened, but this time he could not resist the drowsiness washing over him.
Just before his eyelids closed, a voice as gentle as a spring breeze reached his ears.
“It’s all over now. Rest easy.”
It was the voice that announced the end of a day longer and darker than any other.

sentences.text: The boy—or rather, the “he” bearing the name Mungyeong—looked down at the ground below his feet.
Countless eyes stared up at him in disbelief.
Among them was a familiar face.
They had met only once, long ago, but it was not difficult to recognize him.
“It has been a long time, Fire King.”
At his greeting, Fire King Jeok Cheongang’s eyes trembled violently.
“So it really was you...”
The greatest assassin under heaven.
He had inspired not merely condemnation and contempt in countless martial artists, but awe.
Then one day, he had vanished without a trace, never to appear again.
At least, not until moments ago.
“Why are you here...?”
“A great deal has happened.
A great deal indeed.
Wouldn’t you agree?”
The question was directed at an old man.
He gazed at the Divine Physician—or rather, Dong Feng—with indescribable eyes before opening his lips.
“Thank goodness.
I wasn’t too late.”
His voice rang out from every direction.
Six-Harmonies Voice Transmission.
A shudder ran through everyone at the unfathomable realm of martial arts displayed before them.
The old physician quietly shook his head.
“You were too late.”
His next words carried a note of regret.
“Too late to turn back the years that have passed.”
“What can be done?
Once water is spilled, it is not easily gathered again.”
“Do you not regret it?”
“Regret...”
At his Disciple’s words, he raised his head and looked toward the sky.
The rain that had seemed as though it would fall forever was gone, as were the dark clouds that had blotted out the sun.
All that remained was the vast azure heaven.
Is this what you intended?
He posed the question to someone who might be looking down upon the mortal realm from above.
But no answer came.
Just as it never had.
What a damned thing this is.
He slowly closed his eyes.
In the pitch-black darkness, memories steeped in blood and struggle flashed past.
He had been raised as an assassin and lived as one.
His inborn karma was that of an assassin, so he killed—but he had been born human, and he hated killing.
That was why, near the end of the Great War that had stained the continent with blood, the aging assassin had buried his weapons and chosen to live as a physician.
But...
Had it come to this after all?
With a quiet murmur, he opened his eyes.
A boy’s hands, white and soft.
Returned to Youth had transformed his flesh several years ago, but even that could not erase the scent of blood steeped into his hands.
“I lived as a physician for more than forty years.
I wished to die as one.”
His voice, laden with immense internal energy, struck their ears like thunder.
The black-clad men staggered as though the sound had shaken their very souls.
“And yet, why have you come here?”
His killing intent made every hair stand on end.
The deputy captain, frozen as he stared at the figure in the sky, spoke in a trembling voice.
“E-Even if you truly are the Slaughter Saint, this is no concern of yours.”
“No concern of mine?”
He muttered the words in a low voice before throwing down the travel bag he had been holding.
Thud!
Something bounced out of the bag as it struck the ground and rolled to the deputy captain’s feet.
“T-This is...”
They were the severed heads of two men.
Though they belonged to different people, their bulging eyes and twisted expressions looked almost identical.
Like twins born at the same hour on the same day.
The deputy captain’s gaze fixed on one of them.
“Captain!”
As the deputy captain stared in horror at First Fiend’s severed head, the Slaughter Saint slowly spoke.
“One question.
Was the one at Qingcheng the second or third of the Qilian Three Fiends?”
Only then did the deputy captain understand.
Why no word had come from the Qingcheng Sect—and where the brothers who had failed to return after seeing the emergency signal had gone.
Only one path remained.
The realization struck like lightning, and he unleashed a shout imbued with internal energy.
“Everyone, attack!
Kill hi—”
Slash!
The deputy captain’s shout was cut short.
A breeze brushed his neck, and suddenly someone was standing behind him.
Can this truly be... the movement of a human being?
That was the last question to cross his mind.
He had failed to recognize the Ghost Illusory Slaughter Step performed by the greatest assassin under heaven—or rather, the greatest assassin in all history.
Only death awaited him.
Fwoosh!
Blood erupted from the severed neck in a fountain.
A figure brushed past the collapsing body and took another step, stirring a wind heavy with the scent of blood.
Slash.
Slash.
Slash!
The heads of the black-clad men who had watched their superior die in a daze flew into the air.
Before the streams of blood could reach the ground, something pale and ghostlike swept through them.
“It was the life I wanted so desperately.”
Murmuring under his breath, he extended both hands.
Long, slender threads streamed from his ten fingers.
Threads of Force—beautiful and destructive.
“And yet, why did you...”
Whoosh!
When his ten curved fingers slashed downward through the air, Force tore through space.
Everything that stood in its way was cut apart and split open.
Shattered armor and weapons, limbs and heads, flew in every direction.
In a world brought to a standstill by blood and death, only one person moved freely.
“Did you wake me?”
Consumed by sorrow and fury, he was no longer the cheerful boy or the physician who had passed the two-character name Divine Physician down to his Disciple.

He had returned to the person he had been before earning the name Divine Physician, before meeting the young carpenter who had fallen into grief after losing his wife and children to an epidemic, and before burying his weapons and leaving the Murim.
“The Slaughter Saint...!”
Someone screamed the name.
His eyes had sunk deeper than the abyss.
He flung out both arms, and the wind—now a raging storm—swallowed more than a hundred black-clad men.
Kwaaang!
A high hill stood east of the Sichuan Tang Clan.
From there, one could see the entire Tang Clan estate at a glance.
A small watchtower stood atop it, and martial artists had once taken turns standing guard.
Once.
Drip.
Drip.
Drops of blood fell from the watchtower and dampened the grass.
Some slid down the hill and touched someone’s hand.
Its back was deeply wrinkled, and its nails had turned green from long years spent practicing poison arts.
The hand belonged to Tang Sadok, the current Family Head of the Sichuan Tang Clan—the Myriad-Poison Asura.
“Cough.”
Blood sprayed from between his parched lips.
His eyes, usually cold and forceful, looked ready to go out at any moment.
“Is this how it ends?”
Tang Sadok murmured faintly.
Everything was racing toward its end.
His life.
The glorious history of the Sichuan Tang Clan.
“Our family, built over centuries... brought down in a single day.”
Tang Sadok’s lament rang hollow.
He no longer possessed the strength even to feel anger or sorrow.
His limbs crushed and his internal injuries severe, all the old Family Head could do was lean against an unknown tree and watch his clan perish.
This is my final gift to you.
The smiling face of a middle-aged man flashed before Tang Sadok’s eyes.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord had not kept his promise.
To him, the destruction of the Sichuan Tang Clan had been a foregone conclusion from the very beginning.
“Urgh...
Blergh!”
The rage flaring within him like wildfire worsened his internal injuries.
Tang Sadok vomited nearly half a gallon of blood, then gasped for breath.
“I’m sorry.
I’m sorry...”
It was an apology to the ancestors of the Sichuan Tang Clan.
To the innocent members of his household who had lost their lives because they had been saddled with an unworthy Family Head.
And to Jin Taekyung and his companions, who had likely already met gruesome deaths at the hands of the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
Of course, none of them could hear Tang Sadok’s voice.
If we meet in the afterlife, I will apologize to you myself.
Just as Tang Sadok murmured those words inwardly—
Rustle.
The bushes stirred, and he sensed something approaching.
No.
It was not human.
Only when the strange presence had drawn right up to him did Tang Sadok realize who it belonged to.
Hiss.
Hiss.
A flicking tongue.
A horned, triangular head.
A pure-white snake burrowed into Tang Sadok’s arms.
“Ha... hahaha.”
Tang Sadok laughed weakly, both happy and hollow.
“So it was you.”
Hisss.
The Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake, Mimi, hissed as if answering its master.
Its cold tongue licked the beard matted with blood.
“Clever creature.
How did you find me all the way out here?”
Tang Sadok gazed at his pet snake through clouded eyes.
He had let Mimi loose because he was worried the snake might be injured in the melee.
He had never thought they would meet again like this.
Nor had he imagined their final farewell would happen this way.
Rumble!
A tremendous roar shook the hill.
The earth rose, and the branches of the trees trembled.
Tang Sadok raised his head and tried to find the source, but his failing eyesight could no longer make out what was happening.
He could infer only one thing.
Has the time come?
It was a roar on an entirely different scale from Heaven-Shaking Thunder.
At last, the destruction of the great Sichuan Tang Clan had reached his doorstep.
Tang Sadok slowly closed his eyes, then opened them again.
“Leave.”
Hiss?
The snake’s triangular snout tilted to one side.

chapters.title: Chapter 369
paragraphs: “Search every inch of the place. If you half-ass it like you do your martial arts training, you’ll catch hell.”
“Oh, come on, Senior Brother. Anyone listening would think that was actually true. You really will say anything in front of the kids.”
“You spend every waking hour running around pleasure houses... Do I need to beat you senseless right here before you come to your senses?”
“Fine, fine. I get it.”
Even after his Senior Brother’s scolding, Hwangso’s scowl refused to budge.
He was a first-generation disciple of the Gongdao Sect, a martial sect in Sichuan. He had been called out for this mission along with around thirty second- and third-generation disciples.
Damn it. Five days of this bullshit.
Hwangso grumbled inwardly.
Born into a fairly prosperous merchant family, he had grown up wanting for nothing.

It was irritating enough that his father had forced him onto the path of a martial artist—a path that had never been part of his plans—simply because he wanted connections in the Murim. Five days of sleeping rough in the wind and dust had worn away what little patience Hwangso had left.
Whew. I heard the new courtesan at Tengwang Pavilion is an absolute beauty...
Just as Hwangso’s thoughts raced toward his favorite pleasure house—
“You brat! After everything I just said, you’re still letting your mind wander?”
“Ah, yes, I understand. I said I understand!”
Startled by his Senior Brother’s sudden, tiger-like roar, Hwangso trudged off.
His Senior Brother clicked his tongue at the sight, as if he found him hopeless.
“If you don’t want to die a senseless death, keep your wits about you. Surely you understand what kind of situation we’re in.”
“I understand perfectly. Aren’t we going through all this trouble to catch some fiend who isn’t even here?”
“What do you mean, he isn’t here?”
“You know what I mean. That Third Fiend or whatever. The bastard ran off ages ago, and we’re searching for him in completely the wrong place.”
His Senior Brother’s face stiffened at Hwangso’s sullen reply.
“Watch your words. Not since the Great Faction War has the Sichuan Murim united to cast a net over heaven and earth like this. Everything happens for a reason.”
“Who said there wasn’t a reason? I’m not deaf. I’ve heard it all already.”
Hwangso had heard why the net over heaven and earth had been cast so many times that his ears hurt.
Dark Heaven or whatever they were called had invaded and laid waste to the Tang Clan, Qingcheng, and Emei.

At the head of the attack had been a peerless fiend who had slain the Poison King and the Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun single-handedly. The Qilian Three Fiends, old monsters from two generations ago, and hundreds of Fiends had split into three groups and stained Sichuan’s three foremost sects with blood.
And everyone in Sichuan, Hwangso included, knew how that day—now being called the Three-Gate Bloodbath—had ended.
“They defeated them for all to see, didn’t they? Every fiend who could be called a leader was killed except for one, and the rest of the foot soldiers scattered and ran. Isn’t it over?”
“...Whew.”
His Senior Brother’s lips moved as if he were about to reply, but he merely sighed.
Whatever he said would go in one ear and out the other. His Junior Brother had no interest in learning how much luck and sacrifice had gone into their victory.
The unknown master who suddenly appeared and saved Qingcheng Sect. The countless Beggars’ Sect disciples and nearby martial sects who rushed to Emei’s aid when it was in danger. And...
If not for them, who had saved the Sichuan Tang Clan from annihilation, the three illustrious sects with their long histories would have vanished from the Murim five days ago.
The Three-Gate Bloodbath had been a large-scale assault carried out with such thoroughness and suddenness that it had sent a tremendous shock through the entire orthodox martial world.
And this brat calls himself a martial artist with such shallow thinking. Even if he did join only because circumstances forced him to...
Hwangso bristled when his Senior Brother shook his head.
“What?”
“Enough. Pick ten men or so and search beyond that hill.”
“Again? We’ve already searched that place several times over the past five days...”
“The area assigned to our sect must be searched a hundred times—a thousand, if necessary. I’ll search the nearby undergrowth myself, so stop complaining and do as you’re told.”
His Senior Brother cut him off so firmly that Hwangso clamped his mouth shut.
I need to talk to Father and get back home as soon as possible. Seriously, why would the fiend who fled Emei show up here?
Thousands of people had been mobilized for the net over heaven and earth, and it had lived up to its name.
Most of Dark Heaven’s remnants who had fled after their defeat in the Three-Gate Bloodbath had already been hunted down or captured.
Only the Third Fiend—the youngest of the Qilian Three Fiends who had attacked Emei—remained. The area assigned to the Gongdao Sect lay near Chengdu, practically the heart of Sichuan.
I heard the fiend isn’t in good shape, either. Why would he walk straight into the tiger’s jaws when he could head somewhere sensible like Tibet or Yunnan?
Hwangso’s complaint was not entirely unreasonable.
It might be darkest beneath the lamp, but there was still no reason for a fiend branded an enemy of the Murim to break through such a dense net over heaven and earth and head toward Chengdu.
If there were even the slightest chance of that, why would I be here? The Qingcheng Daoists would have been guarding the place.
This was all because his Senior Brother was so rigid that it went beyond stubbornness and became downright suffocating.
Muttering a quiet curse, Hwangso crooked a finger at the third-generation disciples standing around blankly.
“You there, the big-nosed one. Yes, you. Everyone from you to that big-eared fellow over there. Ten of you—follow me.”
What else could he do? When they told him to dig, he had to dig.
But as Hwangso left to search, with his Senior Brother’s contemptuous gaze boring into his back, his head was filled with nothing but idle thoughts.
Just wait. The second this is over, I’m going straight to Tengwang Pavilion and having myself one hell of a time.
With his mind elsewhere, there was no chance of him conducting the search properly.
The third-generation disciples watched Hwangso for cues and lazily scanned their surroundings. During that sloppy search, not one of them noticed the faint traces of blood on the leaves.
Thank goodness they’re all idiots. At this rate, I have nothing to worry about.
The Third Fiend let out a sigh of relief and extended one foot.
Sssshk.
His body shot forward, skimming over the leaves.
A master of considerable skill might have detected him if one were nearby, but judging by the level of everyone he had encountered so far, there was no chance of that.
They never imagined I would double back toward Chengdu.
The thrill of having completely deceived the orthodox faction lasted only a moment. Anger and killing intent surged from deep within the Third Fiend’s chest.
If it hadn’t been for those fucking bastards...!
Five days ago, everything had gone smoothly when he led his subordinates in the attack.

The death of the Sect Leader, the Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun, and the Elders had left a tremendous gap in Emei’s forces, and the Dark Heaven martial artists under the Third Fiend’s command had driven straight into it like a massive harpoon.
Then, amid the brutal battle overflowing with blood and death, they appeared.
You worthless pieces of trash, lower than dogs!
One filthy beggar.
Hyuk Mujin, Vice Squad Leader of the Jin Dragon Squad of the great Jin Family of Taiyuan, the right arm and little toe of the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, Jin Taekyung, has arrived!
A young man whose name seemed to be either Right Arm or Little Toe—it was hard to tell.
Senior Sister! I’m here!
And a middle-aged nun who appeared to be a disciple of Emei Sect.
At first, even the Third Fiend had been dumbfounded by their fearless entrance.
What? Worthless pieces of trash, lower than dogs? Does this filthy beggar have a death wish? Just wait. This old man will tear you limb from limb and—
The Third Fiend approached with a contemptuous snort, only to swallow the rest of his words.
Behind the fearless young beggar, more filthy beggars than he could count were rushing forward.
A veritable wave of beggars!
B-Beggars’ Sect?
The response had come far too quickly for the Third Fiend.
Not even half a day had passed, yet more than a thousand Beggars’ Sect disciples—not dozens, not even a hundred—had assembled and rushed to Emei’s aid.
The Successor Beggar commands you! Beat those dogshit bastards to death like dogs!
Armor! They’re wearing armor!
Hit the exposed parts! Crush their balls!
An Emei nun charged them head-on without regard for her life, while countless Beggars’ Sect disciples surged in endlessly from behind.
The Third Fiend and the black-clad men under his command fought like mad, cutting down enemy after enemy, but the tide of battle had already begun to turn against them.
Brothers of the Beggars’ Sect! Never retreat!
Waaah!
“Avenge Gaettong!”
The sheer force of their human-wave assault was horrifying.
Cut down one beggar, and two did not rush forward in his place. Five or ten did.

And if he dredged up every last ounce of strength and cut them down too? There was no need to worry about what came next. A club flying in from somewhere would smash his balls while an iron staff cracked the back of his skull.
The dead had no future.
Guh...!
Like a body slowly soaked through by drizzle, the black-clad men collapsed one after another as cold corpses.
Even the Third Fiend, who should have turned the tide of battle, had no time to look after his subordinates.
Form the Demon-Subduing Dragon-Taming Formation!
The Seven Fairies, Emei Sect’s finest masters, used a combined formation to bind the Third Fiend’s feet.
Even when seriously wounded, they never retreated. They attacked as if their lives meant nothing, and the Third Fiend gradually grew exhausted from the mounting fatigue and anxiety.
The Third Fiend’s face twisted violently as he recalled what had happened five days earlier.
And then Extinction Divine Nun appeared. That damned old monster brought it all to an end.
The arrival of Extinction Divine Nun shocked not only the Third Fiend but even the disciples of Emei.
Thirty years ago, at the age of one hundred, she had withdrawn from worldly affairs. She was the Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun’s only Senior Aunt, and everyone believed she had since died.
When another Supreme Peak master suddenly appeared, the Third Fiend chose to flee without a moment’s hesitation. The black-clad men under his command scattered and ran after their superior.
It had been an undeniable defeat.
Yet the Third Fiend had survived to the bitter end.
He had concealed himself with a human-skin mask and a disguise technique, found the weakest point in the net over heaven and earth, and made his way here.
To this nameless cliff where no one had set foot.
“At last... Guh!”
As the cliff rapidly drew closer, the Third Fiend suppressed the emotions welling up inside him.
Only now did the grief and fury of losing his only blood relatives strike him all at once.
“Do not feel too aggrieved. Though I must retreat for now, this youngest brother will surely avenge you, my elder brothers.”
The Third Fiend had just sworn his vengeance and reached toward the cliff when—
Shhk!
His eyes flew wide.
A searing sensation, like a burn, blazed through him as his hand fell away at the wrist.
It was agony he had not felt in a very long time. A beat later, a scream burst from his cracked lips.
“Kyaaaaargh!”
At the same time, a chill raced down his spine.
He pressed his acupoints like lightning to stop the bleeding, then jerked his head up.
Where part of the solid cliff face had stood only moments before, there was now an all-too-familiar face.
“B-Big Brother?”
The Third Fiend’s cry held both delight and shock.
But First Fiend’s response was calm.
“So it seems. Your disguise technique was so poor that I suspected as much.”
Crack. Crackle.
At that moment, First Fiend’s hideous face rippled like a wave. His hunched back straightened, and his arms and legs grew long and slender.
In the place of the ugly old man now stood a handsome boy.
“Who the hell are you?”
At the Third Fiend’s shout, a faint smile crossed the boy’s impassive face—the face of the Slaughter Saint.
“Mungyeong.”
A faint smile crossed the boy’s impassive face—the face of the Slaughter Saint.
“Your enemy.”

“Oh, come on, Senior Brother.
Anyone listening would think that was actually true.
You really will say anything in front of the kids.”
“You spend every waking hour running around pleasure houses...
Do I need to beat you senseless right here before you come to your senses?”
“Fine, fine.
I get it.”
Even after his Senior Brother’s scolding, Hwangso’s scowl refused to budge.
He was a first-generation disciple of the Gongdao Sect, a martial sect in Sichuan.
He had been called out for this mission along with around thirty second- and third-generation disciples.
Damn it.
Five days of this bullshit.
Hwangso grumbled inwardly.
Born into a fairly prosperous merchant family, he had grown up wanting for nothing.
It was irritating enough that his father had forced him onto the path of a martial artist—a path that had never been part of his plans—simply because he wanted connections in the Murim.
Five days of sleeping rough in the wind and dust had worn away what little patience Hwangso had left.
Whew.
I heard the new courtesan at Tengwang Pavilion is an absolute beauty...
Just as Hwangso’s thoughts raced toward his favorite pleasure house—
“You brat!
After everything I just said, you’re still letting your mind wander?”
“Ah, yes, I understand.
I said I understand!”
Startled by his Senior Brother’s sudden, tiger-like roar, Hwangso trudged off.
His Senior Brother clicked his tongue at the sight, as if he found him hopeless.
“If you don’t want to die a senseless death, keep your wits about you.
Surely you understand what kind of situation we’re in.”
“I understand perfectly.
Aren’t we going through all this trouble to catch some fiend who isn’t even here?”
“What do you mean, he isn’t here?”
“You know what I mean.
That Third Fiend or whatever.
The bastard ran off ages ago, and we’re searching for him in completely the wrong place.”
His Senior Brother’s face stiffened at Hwangso’s sullen reply.
“Watch your words.
Not since the Great Faction War has the Sichuan Murim united to cast a net over heaven and earth like this.
Everything happens for a reason.”
“Who said there wasn’t a reason?
I’m not deaf.
I’ve heard it all already.”
Hwangso had heard why the net over heaven and earth had been cast so many times that his ears hurt.
Dark Heaven or whatever they were called had invaded and laid waste to the Tang Clan, Qingcheng, and Emei.
At the head of the attack had been a peerless fiend who had slain the Poison King and the Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun single-handedly.
The Qilian Three Fiends, old monsters from two generations ago, and hundreds of Fiends had split into three groups and stained Sichuan’s three foremost sects with blood.
And everyone in Sichuan, Hwangso included, knew how that day—now being called the Three-Gate Bloodbath—had ended.
“They defeated them for all to see, didn’t they?
Every fiend who could be called a leader was killed except for one, and the rest of the foot soldiers scattered and ran.
Isn’t it over?”
“...Whew.”
His Senior Brother’s lips moved as if he were about to reply, but he merely sighed.
Whatever he said would go in one ear and out the other.
His Junior Brother had no interest in learning how much luck and sacrifice had gone into their victory.
The unknown master who suddenly appeared and saved Qingcheng Sect.
The countless Beggars’ Sect disciples and nearby martial sects who rushed to Emei’s aid when it was in danger.
And...
If not for them, who had saved the Sichuan Tang Clan from annihilation, the three illustrious sects with their long histories would have vanished from the Murim five days ago.
The Three-Gate Bloodbath had been a large-scale assault carried out with such thoroughness and suddenness that it had sent a tremendous shock through the entire orthodox martial world.
And this brat calls himself a martial artist with such shallow thinking.
Even if he did join only because circumstances forced him to...
Hwangso bristled when his Senior Brother shook his head.
“What?”
“Enough.
Pick ten men or so and search beyond that hill.”
“Again?
We’ve already searched that place several times over the past five days...”
“The area assigned to our sect must be searched a hundred times—a thousand, if necessary.
I’ll search the nearby undergrowth myself, so stop complaining and do as you’re told.”
His Senior Brother cut him off so firmly that Hwangso clamped his mouth shut.
I need to talk to Father and get back home as soon as possible.
Seriously, why would the fiend who fled Emei show up here?
Thousands of people had been mobilized for the net over heaven and earth, and it had lived up to its name.
Most of Dark Heaven’s remnants who had fled after their defeat in the Three-Gate Bloodbath had already been hunted down or captured.
Only the Third Fiend—the youngest of the Qilian Three Fiends who had attacked Emei—remained.
The area assigned to the Gongdao Sect lay near Chengdu, practically the heart of Sichuan.
I heard the fiend isn’t in good shape, either.
Why would he walk straight into the tiger’s jaws when he could head somewhere sensible like Tibet or Yunnan?
Hwangso’s complaint was not entirely unreasonable.
It might be darkest beneath the lamp, but there was still no reason for a fiend branded an enemy of the Murim to break through such a dense net over heaven and earth and head toward Chengdu.
If there were even the slightest chance of that, why would I be here?
The Qingcheng Daoists would have been guarding the place.
This was all because his Senior Brother was so rigid that it went beyond stubbornness and became downright suffocating.
Muttering a quiet curse, Hwangso crooked a finger at the third-generation disciples standing around blankly.
“You there, the big-nosed one.
Yes, you.
Everyone from you to that big-eared fellow over there.
Ten of you—follow me.”
What else could he do?
When they told him to dig, he had to dig.
But as Hwangso left to search, with his Senior Brother’s contemptuous gaze boring into his back, his head was filled with nothing but idle thoughts.
Just wait.
The second this is over, I’m going straight to Tengwang Pavilion and having myself one hell of a time.
With his mind elsewhere, there was no chance of him conducting the search properly.
The third-generation disciples watched Hwangso for cues and lazily scanned their surroundings.
During that sloppy search, not one of them noticed the faint traces of blood on the leaves.
Thank goodness they’re all idiots.
At this rate, I have nothing to worry about.
The Third Fiend let out a sigh of relief and extended one foot.
Sssshk.
His body shot forward, skimming over the leaves.
A master of considerable skill might have detected him if one were nearby, but judging by the level of everyone he had encountered so far, there was no chance of that.
They never imagined I would double back toward Chengdu.
The thrill of having completely deceived the orthodox faction lasted only a moment.
Anger and killing intent surged from deep within the Third Fiend’s chest.
If it hadn’t been for those fucking bastards...!
Five days ago, everything had gone smoothly when he led his subordinates in the attack.

The death of the Sect Leader, the Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun, and the Elders had left a tremendous gap in Emei’s forces, and the Dark Heaven martial artists under the Third Fiend’s command had driven straight into it like a massive harpoon.
Then, amid the brutal battle overflowing with blood and death, they appeared.
You worthless pieces of trash, lower than dogs!
One filthy beggar.
Hyuk Mujin, Vice Squad Leader of the Jin Dragon Squad of the great Jin Family of Taiyuan, the right arm and little toe of the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, Jin Taekyung, has arrived!
A young man whose name seemed to be either Right Arm or Little Toe—it was hard to tell.
Senior Sister!
I’m here!
And a middle-aged nun who appeared to be a disciple of Emei Sect.
At first, even the Third Fiend had been dumbfounded by their fearless entrance.
What?
Worthless pieces of trash, lower than dogs?
Does this filthy beggar have a death wish?
Just wait.
This old man will tear you limb from limb and—
The Third Fiend approached with a contemptuous snort, only to swallow the rest of his words.
Behind the fearless young beggar, more filthy beggars than he could count were rushing forward.
A veritable wave of beggars!
B-Beggars’ Sect?
The response had come far too quickly for the Third Fiend.
Not even half a day had passed, yet more than a thousand Beggars’ Sect disciples—not dozens, not even a hundred—had assembled and rushed to Emei’s aid.
The Successor Beggar commands you!
Beat those dogshit bastards to death like dogs!
Armor!
They’re wearing armor!
Hit the exposed parts!
Crush their balls!
An Emei nun charged them head-on without regard for her life, while countless Beggars’ Sect disciples surged in endlessly from behind.
The Third Fiend and the black-clad men under his command fought like mad, cutting down enemy after enemy, but the tide of battle had already begun to turn against them.
Brothers of the Beggars’ Sect!
Never retreat!
Waaah!
“Avenge Gaettong!”
The sheer force of their human-wave assault was horrifying.
Cut down one beggar, and two did not rush forward in his place.
Five or ten did.
And if he dredged up every last ounce of strength and cut them down too?
There was no need to worry about what came next.
A club flying in from somewhere would smash his balls while an iron staff cracked the back of his skull.
The dead had no future.
Guh...!
Like a body slowly soaked through by drizzle, the black-clad men collapsed one after another as cold corpses.
Even the Third Fiend, who should have turned the tide of battle, had no time to look after his subordinates.
Form the Demon-Subduing Dragon-Taming Formation!
The Seven Fairies, Emei Sect’s finest masters, used a combined formation to bind the Third Fiend’s feet.
Even when seriously wounded, they never retreated.
They attacked as if their lives meant nothing, and the Third Fiend gradually grew exhausted from the mounting fatigue and anxiety.
The Third Fiend’s face twisted violently as he recalled what had happened five days earlier.
And then Extinction Divine Nun appeared.
That damned old monster brought it all to an end.
The arrival of Extinction Divine Nun shocked not only the Third Fiend but even the disciples of Emei.
Thirty years ago, at the age of one hundred, she had withdrawn from worldly affairs.
She was the Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun’s only Senior Aunt, and everyone believed she had since died.
When another Supreme Peak master suddenly appeared, the Third Fiend chose to flee without a moment’s hesitation.
The black-clad men under his command scattered and ran after their superior.
It had been an undeniable defeat.
Yet the Third Fiend had survived to the bitter end.
He had concealed himself with a human-skin mask and a disguise technique, found the weakest point in the net over heaven and earth, and made his way here.
To this nameless cliff where no one had set foot.
“At last...
Guh!”
As the cliff rapidly drew closer, the Third Fiend suppressed the emotions welling up inside him.
Only now did the grief and fury of losing his only blood relatives strike him all at once.
“Do not feel too aggrieved.
Though I must retreat for now, this youngest brother will surely avenge you, my elder brothers.”
The Third Fiend had just sworn his vengeance and reached toward the cliff when—
Shhk!
His eyes flew wide.
A searing sensation, like a burn, blazed through him as his hand fell away at the wrist.
It was agony he had not felt in a very long time.
A beat later, a scream burst from his cracked lips.
“Kyaaaaargh!”
At the same time, a chill raced down his spine.
He pressed his acupoints like lightning to stop the bleeding, then jerked his head up.
Where part of the solid cliff face had stood only moments before, there was now an all-too-familiar face.
“B-Big Brother?”
The Third Fiend’s cry held both delight and shock.
But First Fiend’s response was calm.
“So it seems.
Your disguise technique was so poor that I suspected as much.”
Crack.
Crackle.
At that moment, First Fiend’s hideous face rippled like a wave.
His hunched back straightened, and his arms and legs grew long and slender.
In the place of the ugly old man now stood a handsome boy.
“Who the hell are you?”
At the Third Fiend’s shout, a faint smile crossed the boy’s impassive face—the face of the Slaughter Saint.
“Mungyeong.”
A faint smile crossed the boy’s impassive face—the face of the Slaughter Saint.
“Your enemy.”

chapters.title: Chapter 370
paragraphs: The Sichuan Tang Clan had always been famous for its reclusive ways.

Even prominent figures could not easily pass through its gates. Fearing that daughters who married out might reveal the clan’s martial arts and secrets, the Tangs instead brought in sons-in-law and had them take the Tang surname.
The gates of the Sichuan Tang Clan, which had endured for hundreds of years in this manner, had been thrown wide open only seven days ago.
“Over there! Get that pillar straight!”
“Pull on three. Ready. One, two—!”
Burly laborers hauled on ropes and carried stone and lumber across the grounds.
Buildings were slowly taking shape over foundation stones still stained dark red with blood.
Farther away, dozens of Buddhist nuns had gathered to chant prayers.
“May I have no other thought at the end of this life, with Amitabha alone beside me, my heart forever bound to the light from the white curl between his brows...”
The nuns, their heads shaved close and their eyes filled with spiritual energy, were from Emei Sect.
Before them, countless wooden coffins burned amid roaring flames.
“May you be reborn in the Pure Land. We will never forget your steadfast devotion or your souls.”
Several days and nights had passed, yet the fires still had not gone out.
That was how many lives had been lost in the Three-Gate Bloodbath. The Sichuan Tang Clan, in particular, had suffered catastrophic casualties.
“Whew...”
“Venerable Myoryeong, you look exhausted. Perhaps you should rest, even if only for a little while...”
“No, Daoist Myeongjin. I am merely doing what must be done, so please do not concern yourself. Let us continue.”
The Daoist studied the middle-aged nun’s pale face, then nodded gravely.
A short while later, martial artists with swords at their waists approached in a line, carrying several dozen wooden coffins.
Among them were Daoists of Qingcheng Sect, disciples from small and mid-sized sects, and beggars streaked with grime.
A group of physicians came running along behind them.
“The patient suddenly started vomiting blood? Weren’t they stable?”
“If I knew that, would I be here right now? The patient clearly suffered serious internal injuries, but I can’t make sense of these symptoms...”
“Spread out and bring the Divine Physician! Quickly!”
Emei nuns, Qingcheng Daoists, Beggars’ Sect beggars, and martial artists dispatched from sects both great and small. Alongside them were ordinary people—carpenters, stonemasons, physicians, and more.
Countless people moved through the grounds of the Sichuan Tang Clan, each diligently carrying out their own task.
From a tall pavilion, a young beggar watched the scene through an open window and muttered wearily.
“I never thought I’d live to see something like this. And in the Sichuan Tang Clan, no less.”
Hyuk Mujin, lying on a bed, answered him.
“Stop watching and go help. Don’t slack off just because you’re the Successor Beggar.”
“Slack off?”
Gung Gibang’s eyes widened as he pointed at himself.
His upper body was tightly wrapped in spotless white bandages, and one leg had been fitted with a makeshift splint. They were glorious wounds earned in battle against the Third Fiend.
“You can look at me and still say that? You call this slacking off? Huh?”
“Are you the only one who got hurt?”
Hyuk Mujin snorted, then deliberately wriggled like an earthworm.
Unlike Gung Gibang, he was wrapped in bandages from head to toe, making him look like a mummy.
“You have to get hurt this badly before people say, ‘Ah, this kid must have had a rough time.’ You understand?”
Gung Gibang trembled.
The fact that his wounds were less severe clearly proved that his martial arts were superior, yet somehow, he felt as though he had lost.
“I had my bandages changed five times!”
“I’m lucky to be alive. Besides, wasn’t that because you were so filthy? I heard a physician tried to scrub you clean, then passed out from exhaustion. Is that true?”

“Forget it. Talking to you any longer will only subject me to more bad breath. Since we’re on the subject, ask them to brush your teeth next time, too. Every time I talk to you, I feel like I’m speaking into a street mutt’s ass.”
What a vicious tongue.
Gung Gibang was speechless for a moment. Then he stared at the ceiling and lamented.
“The Third Fiend should have killed that bastard.”
“Hey. That’s crossing a line.”
“I still don’t understand how someone like you survived that battle.”
“If you’re really that curious, try following our Captain around for two years.”
“...I’ll pass.”
For all their constant bickering, there was one thing Gung Gibang and Hyuk Mujin agreed on: Jin Taekyung.
He seemed to embody every upheaval under heaven. He possessed the tenacious vitality and sheer determination to survive any crisis.
And now, Jin Taekyung had reached such distant heights in martial prowess that they could scarcely believe he was human like them.
There is one more person like that.
Yeah. That guy.
The same thought crossed both their minds, and their heads turned in unison.
“Mimi, Whirlwind!”
Whirrrr!
“Good job, Mimi! Now fly through the air!”
Hiss?
“Oh. You can’t do that. Then this time...”

Hyuk Mujin and Gung Gibang wondered whether the bizarre young man ordering a snake to fly could truly be the Huashan Divine Dragon—the Sword Saint’s successor who had single-handedly defeated First Fiend, the strongest of the Qilian Three Fiends.
“Say, Gung.”
“What?”
“Do you have to be a little unhinged to become a Supreme Peak master?”
“...I don’t know. I really don’t know anymore.”
Gung Gibang avoided the question.
His own master was rather eccentric, but nowhere near as strange as Jin Taekyung or Cheongpung.
Then again, judging by the Sword Saint and the Fire King, perhaps disciples really did take after their masters.
“But what exactly is that snake?”
“A snake with horns that large? Other than an imugi, there’s only one possibility. A Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake.”
“When I was young, I read an encyclopedia of spiritual creatures that described it as a massive, pitch-black venomous beast.”
Cheongpung shouted.
“Mimi! Lie down!”
Hiss!
“Looking at it now, it doesn’t seem like a venomous beast. It just looks like an ordinary animal.”
“That’s what I’m saying.”
“But why is Cheongpung here? He was barely injured.”
“Didn’t you hear that loud crash outside earlier? They say Cheongpung went out to help and ended up destroying a pavilion.”
Both men fell silent. Lying side by side on their beds, they stared up at the ceiling.
Nearly ninety percent of the clan’s buildings had been damaged, but this pavilion had somehow retained its shape. It was now serving as a temporary clinic for the most important patients.
Catching the scent of medicinal decoctions drifting in from somewhere, Hyuk Mujin suddenly murmured,
“It feels like a dream.”
“Tell me about it.”
Seven days had passed since the Three-Gate Bloodbath.

Sichuan’s Murim had united to cast a net over heaven and earth. Most of Dark Heaven’s black-clad men, who had stained every corner of Sichuan with blood, had either been killed or captured. Even the Third Fiend, who had vanished without a trace, had been seized by a mysterious figure.
And with that, the brief war had come to an end.
But...
“I don’t think this is over. What do you think, Gung?”
“Do you even have to ask? If this is really the end, I’ll sear my own palm.”
They were hardly the only ones who sensed the looming danger.
In barely two months, Henan and Sichuan had been stained with blood.
Once news of the Three-Gate Bloodbath spread to the farthest reaches of the continent, everyone under heaven would realize the truth.
The dark cloud called Dark Heaven had already reached their doorstep.
An undeniable age of turmoil was beginning—and heroes were born in such times.
Hyuk Mujin’s gaze naturally turned toward the closed door.
“When do you think our Captain will wake up?”
“Who knows? Do I look like I have an answer? Mungyeong says there’s nothing wrong with him, so all we can do is wait.”
“Speaking of which, Mungyeong may be skilled for his age, but isn’t he a little young for us to entrust the Captain to him?”
“The Divine Physician is busy, I suppose. Great Hero Jeok is still recovering his strength, and there are far too many critical patients, including Great Hero Tang Sadok. There’s no helping it.”
“I understand. I do. But even if he is the Divine Physician’s Disciple, Mungyeong is still... What could a child that young possibly know?”
At Hyuk Mujin’s worried words, Cheongpung’s head snapped up.
“Uh-oh. Don’t say that. You’ll die.”
“Young Hero Cheongpung?”
“What you just said—don’t say it in front of Grandpa Mun. I mean, especially not in front of Mungyeong.”
“What? Why would you suddenly say that?”
“Don’t. Really, don’t.”
Hyuk Mujin and Gung Gibang exchanged bewildered looks.
Then Cheongpung suddenly gasped.
“Mimi! Where did you go, Mimi?”
Cheongpung desperately searched for the Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake that had vanished the moment he looked away.
Just then, a strangled shout erupted from beyond the tightly closed door.
“Ghk! You damn snake!”
The three men’s gazes collided in midair.
At the same time, several voices calling one person’s name rang out all the way outside the pavilion.
“Benefactor!”
“Captain!”
“Jin Taekyung!”
The shout sent the people working outside into an uproar.
“Did you hear that?”
“Could he have woken up?”
“Tell the Sect Leader! Hurry!”
I had a nightmare.
In pitch-black darkness where I couldn’t see an inch ahead, a snake was slowly tightening around my neck.
I couldn’t breathe. My vision turned white.
Then I opened my eyes and expelled the breath trapped in my lungs.
“Ghk!”
Hiss.
Hiss? What the fuck?
My brain stopped working for three seconds.
At last, I realized what my nightmare had been. I grabbed the horn of the snake coiled tightly around my neck.
“You damn snake!”
I didn’t care whether it was called a Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake or Mimi-chan. Starting today, this bastard’s name was Snake Wine.
“You’re living on dew from now on. Chamisul.”
I was about to whirl it around and slam it into the floor when the tightly closed door shattered and someone burst into the room.
“Benefactor!”
Cheongpung’s thunderous shout made my skull ring.
Behind him, Hyuk Mujin came wriggling like an earthworm while Gung Gibang hopped in on one leg.
“Captain!”
“Jin Taekyung!”
“...Why do you two look like that?”
Hyuk Mujin bounced his body vigorously and answered.
“The Third Fiend. That crazy old monster did this to me.”
Gung Gibang helpfully elaborated.
“It’s a miracle he survived. That lunatic Hyuk Mujin threw dirt and rocks at the Third Fiend. If the Seven Fairies hadn’t stepped in to protect him, he would have been torn limb from limb.”
Who the hell was the Third Fiend, and who were the Seven Fairies? Kim Seonja was my high school disciplinarian’s name...
These lunatics.
My relief at surviving the underground prison lasted only a moment. A headache came on, and I pressed a hand to my forehead.
I had clearly told them to stay put at the Divine Physician’s residence, but apparently they hadn’t been able to resist crawling out and fighting to the death.
Thank goodness they had survived. What would have happened if they had died?
“Were you two that desperate to die? What kind of trouble did you cause this time?”
“What? Why are you looking at me like that?”
The three of us—everyone except Cheongpung—exchanged bewildered looks.
“Is there a problem?”
“Of course there is.”
“You told us to go save Emei Sect, Captain.”
The first answer came from Gung Gibang. The second came from Hyuk Mujin.
They were both talking nonsense, so I deliberately frowned.
“What are you talking about? I did?”
“Yes. That’s what Mungyeong told us. Did you hit your head?”
That couldn’t be it.
I had felt it the instant I opened my eyes. Powerful qi boiled throughout my entire body.
Everything within my sight, along with the energy of nature surrounding me, felt clear and vivid.
So this is Supreme Peak...
I wanted to test this power immediately. Not to mention the System messages that must have piled up like a mountain by now.
But before listening to any more of this nonsense, there was one thing I needed to ask.
“Is everyone all right?”
They knew who I meant by everyone.
Instead of answering, Cheongpung threw open the enormous window.
“See for yourself, Benefactor.”
As if in a trance, I slowly walked toward the window.
A warm spring breeze brushed across my face. An oddly quiet atmosphere greeted me as I leaned my head out beyond the window.
“Ah.”
I looked down and found myself speechless.
There were people below.
Nuns, Daoists, craftsmen who appeared to be carpenters, and physicians dressed in spotless white robes. Countless eyes were fixed upon me, all filled with the same emotion.
Awe.
The next moment, they paid their respects as though they had made an agreement beforehand.
Some formed a fist-and-palm salute. Some bowed their heads slightly. Others prostrated themselves and bowed deeply.
Then a vast chorus rose as one.
“We pay our respects to the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon!”
A shudder ran through me from the crown of my head to the tips of my toes.
Ding.
System Your accomplishments and Fame will resound throughout the Central Plains. You have acquired a new sobriquet!
As the System alert rang in my ears, I spotted someone in the distance.
“Well done.”
I smiled back at Jeok Cheongang.
