Then he stared at the ceiling and lamented.
“The Third Fiend should have killed that bastard.”
“Hey.
That’s crossing a line.”
“I still don’t understand how someone like you survived that battle.”
“If you’re really that curious, try following our Captain around for two years.”
“...I’ll pass.”
For all their constant bickering, there was one thing Gung Gibang and Hyuk Mujin agreed on: Jin Taekyung.
He seemed to embody every upheaval under heaven.
He possessed the tenacious vitality and sheer determination to survive any crisis.
And now, Jin Taekyung had reached such distant heights in martial prowess that they could scarcely believe he was human like them.
There is one more person like that.
Yeah.
That guy.
The same thought crossed both their minds, and their heads turned in unison.
“Mimi, Whirlwind!”
Whirrrr!
“Good job, Mimi!
Now fly through the air!”
Hiss?
“Oh.
You can’t do that.
Then this time...”

Hyuk Mujin and Gung Gibang wondered whether the bizarre young man ordering a snake to fly could truly be the Huashan Divine Dragon—the Sword Saint’s successor who had single-handedly defeated First Fiend, the strongest of the Qilian Three Fiends.
“Say, Gung.”
“What?”
“Do you have to be a little unhinged to become a Supreme Peak master?”
“...I don’t know.
I really don’t know anymore.”
Gung Gibang avoided the question.
His own master was rather eccentric, but nowhere near as strange as Jin Taekyung or Cheongpung.
Then again, judging by the Sword Saint and the Fire King, perhaps disciples really did take after their masters.
“But what exactly is that snake?”
“A snake with horns that large?
Other than an imugi, there’s only one possibility.
A Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake.”
“When I was young, I read an encyclopedia of spiritual creatures that described it as a massive, pitch-black venomous beast.”
Cheongpung shouted.
“Mimi!
Lie down!”
Hiss!
“Looking at it now, it doesn’t seem like a venomous beast.
It just looks like an ordinary animal.”
“That’s what I’m saying.”
“But why is Cheongpung here?
He was barely injured.”
“Didn’t you hear that loud crash outside earlier?
They say Cheongpung went out to help and ended up destroying a pavilion.”
Both men fell silent.
Lying side by side on their beds, they stared up at the ceiling.
Nearly ninety percent of the clan’s buildings had been damaged, but this pavilion had somehow retained its shape.
It was now serving as a temporary clinic for the most important patients.
Catching the scent of medicinal decoctions drifting in from somewhere, Hyuk Mujin suddenly murmured,
“It feels like a dream.”
“Tell me about it.”
Seven days had passed since the Three-Gate Bloodbath.
Sichuan’s Murim had united to cast a net over heaven and earth.
Most of Dark Heaven’s black-clad men, who had stained every corner of Sichuan with blood, had either been killed or captured.
Even the Third Fiend, who had vanished without a trace, had been seized by a mysterious figure.
And with that, the brief war had come to an end.
But...
“I don’t think this is over.
What do you think, Gung?”
“Do you even have to ask?
If this is really the end, I’ll sear my own palm.”
They were hardly the only ones who sensed the looming danger.
In barely two months, Henan and Sichuan had been stained with blood.
Once news of the Three-Gate Bloodbath spread to the farthest reaches of the continent, everyone under heaven would realize the truth.
The dark cloud called Dark Heaven had already reached their doorstep.
An undeniable age of turmoil was beginning—and heroes were born in such times.
Hyuk Mujin’s gaze naturally turned toward the closed door.
“When do you think our Captain will wake up?”
“Who knows?
Do I look like I have an answer?
Mungyeong says there’s nothing wrong with him, so all we can do is wait.”
“Speaking of which, Mungyeong may be skilled for his age, but isn’t he a little young for us to entrust the Captain to him?”
“The Divine Physician is busy, I suppose.
Great Hero Jeok is still recovering his strength, and there are far too many critical patients, including Great Hero Tang Sadok.
There’s no helping it.”
“I understand.
I do.
But even if he is the Divine Physician’s Disciple, Mungyeong is still...
What could a child that young possibly know?”
At Hyuk Mujin’s worried words, Cheongpung’s head snapped up.
“Uh-oh.
Don’t say that.
You’ll die.”
“Young Hero Cheongpung?”
“What you just said—don’t say it in front of Grandpa Mun.
I mean, especially not in front of Mungyeong.”
“What?
Why would you suddenly say that?”
“Don’t.
Really, don’t.”
Hyuk Mujin and Gung Gibang exchanged bewildered looks.
Then Cheongpung suddenly gasped.
“Mimi!
Where did you go, Mimi?”
Cheongpung desperately searched for the Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake that had vanished the moment he looked away.
Just then, a strangled shout erupted from beyond the tightly closed door.
“Ghk!
You damn snake!”
The three men’s gazes collided in midair.
At the same time, several voices calling one person’s name rang out all the way outside the pavilion.
“Benefactor!”
“Captain!”
“Jin Taekyung!”
The shout sent the people working outside into an uproar.
“Did you hear that?”
“Could he have woken up?”
“Tell the Sect Leader!
Hurry!”
I had a nightmare.
In pitch-black darkness where I couldn’t see an inch ahead, a snake was slowly tightening around my neck.
I couldn’t breathe.
My vision turned white.
Then I opened my eyes and expelled the breath trapped in my lungs.
“Ghk!”
Hiss.
Hiss?
What the fuck?
My brain stopped working for three seconds.
At last, I realized what my nightmare had been.
I grabbed the horn of the snake coiled tightly around my neck.
“You damn snake!”
I didn’t care whether it was called a Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake or Mimi-chan.
Starting today, this bastard’s name was Snake Wine.
“You’re living on dew from now on.
Chamisul.”
I was about to whirl it around and slam it into the floor when the tightly closed door shattered and someone burst into the room.
“Benefactor!”
Cheongpung’s thunderous shout made my skull ring.
Behind him, Hyuk Mujin came wriggling like an earthworm while Gung Gibang hopped in on one leg.
“Captain!”
“Jin Taekyung!”
“...Why do you two look like that?”
Hyuk Mujin bounced his body vigorously and answered.
“The Third Fiend.
That crazy old monster did this to me.”
Gung Gibang helpfully elaborated.
“It’s a miracle he survived.
That lunatic Hyuk Mujin threw dirt and rocks at the Third Fiend.
If the Seven Fairies hadn’t stepped in to protect him, he would have been torn limb from limb.”
Who the hell was the Third Fiend, and who were the Seven Fairies?
Kim Seonja was my high school disciplinarian’s name...
These lunatics.
My relief at surviving the underground prison lasted only a moment.
A headache came on, and I pressed a hand to my forehead.
I had clearly told them to stay put at the Divine Physician’s residence, but apparently they hadn’t been able to resist crawling out and fighting to the death.
Thank goodness they had survived.
What would have happened if they had died?
“Were you two that desperate to die?
What kind of trouble did you cause this time?”
“What?
Why are you looking at me like that?”
The three of us—everyone except Cheongpung—exchanged bewildered looks.
“Is there a problem?”
“Of course there is.”
“You told us to go save Emei Sect, Captain.”
The first answer came from Gung Gibang.
The second came from Hyuk Mujin.
They were both talking nonsense, so I deliberately frowned.
“What are you talking about?
I did?”
“Yes.
That’s what Mungyeong told us.
Did you hit your head?”
That couldn’t be it.
I had felt it the instant I opened my eyes.
Powerful qi boiled throughout my entire body.
Everything within my sight, along with the energy of nature surrounding me, felt clear and vivid.
So this is Supreme Peak...
I wanted to test this power immediately.
Not to mention the System messages that must have piled up like a mountain by now.
But before listening to any more of this nonsense, there was one thing I needed to ask.
“Is everyone all right?”
They knew who I meant by everyone.
Instead of answering, Cheongpung threw open the enormous window.
“See for yourself, Benefactor.”
As if in a trance, I slowly walked toward the window.
A warm spring breeze brushed across my face.
An oddly quiet atmosphere greeted me as I leaned my head out beyond the window.
“Ah.”
I looked down and found myself speechless.
There were people below.
Nuns, Daoists, craftsmen who appeared to be carpenters, and physicians dressed in spotless white robes.
Countless eyes were fixed upon me, all filled with the same emotion.
Awe.
The next moment, they paid their respects as though they had made an agreement beforehand.
Some formed a fist-and-palm salute.
Some bowed their heads slightly.
Others prostrated themselves and bowed deeply.
Then a vast chorus rose as one.
“We pay our respects to the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon!”
A shudder ran through me from the crown of my head to the tips of my toes.
Ding.
System Your accomplishments and Fame will resound throughout the Central Plains.
You have acquired a new sobriquet!
As the System alert rang in my ears, I spotted someone in the distance.
“Well done.”
I smiled back at Jeok Cheongang.

chapters.title: Chapter 371
paragraphs: “We pay our respects to Great Hero Jin Taekyung, the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon!”
When that awe-filled cry rang throughout the grounds of the Sichuan Tang Clan, Jin Taekyung was not the only one who felt a shiver run through him.
Watching from a distance, his old master had to struggle to contain the emotion welling up inside him.
You rascal...
Jeok Cheongang remembered the day he had first met Jin Taekyung as clearly as if it were yesterday.

The Third Young Master of a frontier martial family. The young man who had only just begun making a name for himself in Shanxi had become a Hidden Dragon, and now, at last, he was spreading his wings and soaring into the blue sky.
Yes. You truly are a Divine Dragon—and a Great Hero.
Their eyes met, and Jin Taekyung grinned. Leaning halfway out the window, he waved both hands wildly.
“What’s my name?”
“Jin Taekyung!”
“And my sobriquet?”
“Blazing Flame Divine Dragon!”
“Louder—!”
“Waaaaaaaah!”
The solemn gathering erupted into a frenzy, and Jeok Cheongang finally burst into the laughter he had been holding back.
“Ha! Ha-ha-ha!”
His hearty laughter mingled with the cheers. The breeze was cool, and the sky was clear.
It was the dawn of an age of turmoil, but the day a new hero was born was warm with spring.
Jeok Cheongang appeared shortly after the frenzy died down.
“You’ve packed quite a crowd into this millet-sized room.”
“Huh? It’s not cramped at all.”
“Great Hero Jeok, there’s an empty seat over there.”
Unlike Cheongpung and Hyuk Mujin, who could die and come back without ever learning to read the room, Gung Gibang was a pure-blooded beggar to his very bones. He moved at once.
“Oh my, now that you mention it, this place is practically bursting at the seams. I’ll wait outside.”
Cheongpung and Hyuk Mujin waved at him.
“Goodbye, Gung Gibang.”
“He’s finally leaving. Captain, haven’t you smelled a stray dog’s ass around here for a while now?”
I nodded cautiously.
“Yeah. It was pretty strong...”
“Stop talking shit and get out, both of you!”
“No, I’m telling you, it really did smell...”
“All right. Don’t get so angry, Gung Gibang.”
Cheongpung lowered his head dejectedly at Gung Gibang’s furious outburst.
“Mimi. Say goodbye with a whirlwind.”
Hiss. Hissss!
“...What the fuck.”
Looks like Mimi had picked up some new tricks in the meantime. After putting on that flashy performance, Cheongpung was the last to leave the room.
Jeok Cheongang finally spoke.
“You reckless little brat. You certainly made quite a ruckus.”
His face was stern, his voice low and subdued.
He really hadn’t changed at all. Seeing Jeok Cheongang act just like his usual self made me want to laugh for some reason.
“You laughing?”
“Of course I’m laughing. What else should I do, cry?”
“Hah, look at this brat. You made a spectacle of yourself in front of everyone and dragged our sect’s reputation through the mud, yet you still have the nerve to say that?”
“You were laughing pretty loudly for someone who thought that.”
“I saw everything.”
The stern expression he had been struggling to maintain collapsed all at once. Jeok Cheongang’s head slowly turned toward the window.
“Ahem. What exactly do you claim to have seen?”
“About fifty people besides me probably saw it too. For a moment, I thought your smile had split your mouth open and you were bleeding from the corners.”
He’d practically looked like the Chinese Joker.
My finishing shot left him no room to escape. Jeok Cheongang hesitated for a long while, unable to continue, before finally muttering one word.
“Huh?”
“I said you did well!”
Jeok Cheongang shouted, his face bright red, then grumbled under his breath.
My smile deepened at the sight.
Yes. That one sentence was enough.
“Thank you. It was all thanks to you, Old Master.”
What was this? His expression seemed strangely off.
His eyes even looked almost hurt. I asked, baffled,
“What’s wrong this time?”
“Nothing. It’s nothing.”
“Your face doesn’t exactly say nothing...”
“I said it was nothing!”
“Why are you shouting? The mood was finally warm and pleasant for once.”
“If I say it’s nothing, then take it as nothing! You keep prying and asking questions, so this is happening!”
“Uh-oh. It’s getting worse?”
What was wrong with this man all of a sudden? Had I screwed something up?
I was tilting my head in confusion when—
Rustle.
Two presences were coming up the stairs.
Their footsteps were so light and graceful that I might never have noticed them if my senses hadn’t grown even sharper after crossing the threshold.
They’re both incredible masters.
Two Supreme Peak masters, just like that?
After all the crises I had weathered lately, my body moved on its own.
But as I clenched my fists, Jeok Cheongang stopped me with a glance and waved one hand.
A thin stream of hot air gently pushed open the closed door.
“You’re all so impatient. Couldn’t even wait fifteen minutes before swarming up here?”
An old Buddhist nun and a Daoist answered Jeok Cheongang’s gruff voice in turn.
“Impatient? Hearing that from a lay devotee gives this poor nun a rather strange feeling.”
“This junior was discourteous. However, given the circumstances...”
The elderly nun, her face covered in fine wrinkles, was a stranger to me. But I immediately recognized the Daoist.
I cupped my hands toward him.
“Greetings, Perfected One.”
“It’s good to see you again, Fellow Daoist Jin.”
The old Daoist was Cheongpung the Ancient Sword, the Sect Leader of the Qingcheng Sect whom I had once visited to ask for help finding the Divine Physician.
Then this nun must be Emei Sect’s new Sect Leader... Who is she?
I knew a fair amount about famous masters by now, but not enough to understand the inner workings of every sect.
Especially when it came to a Sect Leader who had only recently taken office after the death of the Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun.
As if he had read my thoughts, Jeok Cheongang quietly sent me a Sound Transmission.

That old hag is Emei Sect’s Extinction Divine Nun. She may look kindly, but once she loses her temper, she becomes a rakshasa incarnate. Watch your mouth around her. And whatever you do, don’t mention her age.
I replied cautiously through Sound Transmission.
Just how old is she?
Older than this old man. She was also the Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun’s Senior Aunt.
Oh.
I didn’t know Jeok Cheongang’s exact age, but I knew he was over a hundred. Add the sheer force of that sobriquet...
I bowed deeply to the ancient woman who looked like the matriarch of a bossam restaurant.
“Greetings! My name is Jin Taekyung!”
“Good to meet you, Benefactor Jin.”
The Extinction Divine Nun studied me with a strange look in her eyes, then nodded.
“So the rumors were true. No—they fell short.”
Cheongpung the Ancient Sword smiled faintly.
“Isn’t it truly astonishing?”
“The waves behind drive the waves ahead on the Yangtze. It seems the younger generation means to sweep even old people like us aside. To cross the threshold at such a young age...”
“It isn’t only him, Venerable Nun. There is also a young man named Cheongpung.”
“Ah, the Sword Saint’s successor?”
“Yes. This poor Daoist lacks the discernment to judge which of the two is superior, but both young men are unquestionably heaven-sent. They are a great blessing to the Murim.”
Interest and surprise flickered across their weary faces.
I was shifting my eyes awkwardly when Jeok Cheongang stepped in front of me.
Not that it accomplished much, considering the difference in our heights.
“You’ll wear the boy’s face out staring at him. Say what you came to say and hurry along.”
The two Sect Leaders looked embarrassed by his blunt words and finally got to the point.
“A problem has arisen. Could the two of you accompany us for a while?”
“It won’t take long. You have my word.”
“Accompany you? Right now?”
Jeok Cheongang asked in a displeased voice as he turned toward me.
“What will you do?”
Two Sect Leaders from the Nine Sects and One Gang were asking for my help. What exactly was I supposed to do?
“I’ll go.”
My body felt light, and accompanying them would give me a chance to hear everything that had happened. There was no real reason to refuse.
At my ready answer, the two Sect Leaders took the lead.
Then Jeok Cheongang abruptly asked,
“But where’s the other one?”
“He’s waiting below.”
“He said he preferred not to attract anyone else’s attention.”
The other one? If he was important enough to join this group, was it Tang Sadok, the Family Head of the Tang Clan?
Well, whoever it is, I’ll see him soon enough.
But my curiosity vanished the moment we left the pavilion and encountered a familiar face.
A delighted shout burst from me.
“Hey, you little punk! Mungyeong!”
Mungyeong looked exactly as he had before leaving the Sichuan Tang Clan.
Dark Heaven had invaded not long after he left, so I had been worried. Yet, perhaps our paths had simply missed each other, because he had somehow escaped without a scratch.
“When did you get here? You look taller than before. Going through a growth spurt?”
“Why so quiet? Are you in a bad mood? Maybe...”
I ruffled Mungyeong’s hair, then leaned closer and whispered,
“Did you have a wet dream this morning?”
“You did. You totally did.”
Look at the little brat. Too embarrassed to say a word.
I smiled with satisfaction.
That sort of thing happened from time to time at his age. Maybe this was my chance to spread proper sex education throughout this dusty old Murim.
“Your hyung here is going to show you a whole new world. From now on, call me Teacher Jin Seong-ae.”
Teacher Gu Seong-ae, are you watching? Your knowledge is crossing space and time to reach the next generation.
I was proudly patting Mungyeong on the shoulder when—
“Oh dear... We forgot to tell him.”
Forgot to tell me what?
Three long sighs sounded behind me. At the same time, Mungyeong spoke in a flat voice.
“Take your hand off.”
“And I stopped having wet dreams a long time ago.”
“That’s a little problematic, because your secondary sexual development hasn’t completely finished ye—no, that’s not what I mean.”
I swallowed hard.
A terrifying possibility had just flashed through my mind.
“Who... are you?”
Mom, I’m scared.
“...And that is how things came to this.”
“It truly is a bizarre matter.”
Even as the two Sect Leaders raced along using their movement techniques, their voices never wavered.
They looked at me, waiting for an answer. I forced my lips apart.
“Ah, right. So there’s some kind of strange formation where we’re going?”
“According to the Third Fiend, whom we captured and interrogated, that appears to be the case. But the formation itself is so strange...”
Jeok Cheongang answered gruffly.
“This old man and this brat are both hopeless when it comes to formations. Looking at it won’t tell us a damned thing.”
I agreed. The Fire Gate Cavern on Mount Jiuhua contained an extraordinary Mystic Gate Formation, but that didn’t make either of us experts.
We’d be better off calling someone from the Zhuge Clan.
But it would take the Zhuge Clan a considerable amount of time to get here.
For some reason, the two Sect Leaders seemed to have high expectations of us.
Especially me.
“Fellow Daoist Jin, did you notice anything else strange about that man? Anything in his words or behavior?”
“I’ve told you everything. And from what I could tell... I don’t think it was possible for him to get any stranger.”
Dark Heaven was strange by nature. They were fanatics who worshiped the Lord of Heaven as almost—no, simply—as a god.
The Blood Lord and the Western Heaven Demon Lord were no different, with all their bizarre powers and abilities.
One regenerated like a human Troll. Another popped his arm off and stuck it back on like he had double-sided tape under it. And then there was the possession at the end.
The more I thought about it, the more miraculous our victory seemed.
We had fought those lunatics and somehow won.
“Before you awoke, Benefactor Jeok gave us a general account of what happened. Once the messenger eagle we sent to Henan returns with a reply, we should have a clearer idea of how to proceed.”
“If you notice anything strange when you examine the formation, tell us.”
“Yes.”
As I answered, I glanced at the figure racing far ahead of us.
Mungyeong.
No—the man known as the Slaughter Saint.
Fuck. What the hell is the Slaughter Saint doing here?
Honestly, I had nearly pissed myself.
Even if I spent half a day swimming in the Sanzu River valley, grilled meat, and came back, it wouldn’t be this bad.
Mungyeong was the Slaughter Saint. And I asked the Slaughter Saint if he’d had a wet dream!
Teacher Gu Seong-ae, I nearly died because of you.
I had just let out a private sigh of relief when the dense undergrowth around us fell away, revealing towering cliffs ahead.

Cheongpung the Ancient Sword smiled faintly.
“Isn’t it truly astonishing?”
“The waves behind drive the waves ahead on the Yangtze.
It seems the younger generation means to sweep even old people like us aside.
To cross the threshold at such a young age...”
“It isn’t only him, Venerable Nun.
There is also a young man named Cheongpung.”
“Ah, the Sword Saint’s successor?”
“Yes.
This poor Daoist lacks the discernment to judge which of the two is superior, but both young men are unquestionably heaven-sent.
They are a great blessing to the Murim.”
Interest and surprise flickered across their weary faces.
I was shifting my eyes awkwardly when Jeok Cheongang stepped in front of me.
Not that it accomplished much, considering the difference in our heights.
“You’ll wear the boy’s face out staring at him.
Say what you came to say and hurry along.”
The two Sect Leaders looked embarrassed by his blunt words and finally got to the point.
“A problem has arisen.
Could the two of you accompany us for a while?”
“It won’t take long.
You have my word.”
“Accompany you?
Right now?”
Jeok Cheongang asked in a displeased voice as he turned toward me.
“What will you do?”
Two Sect Leaders from the Nine Sects and One Gang were asking for my help.
What exactly was I supposed to do?
“I’ll go.”
My body felt light, and accompanying them would give me a chance to hear everything that had happened.
There was no real reason to refuse.
At my ready answer, the two Sect Leaders took the lead.
Then Jeok Cheongang abruptly asked,
“But where’s the other one?”
“He’s waiting below.”
“He said he preferred not to attract anyone else’s attention.”
The other one?
If he was important enough to join this group, was it Tang Sadok, the Family Head of the Tang Clan?
Well, whoever it is, I’ll see him soon enough.
But my curiosity vanished the moment we left the pavilion and encountered a familiar face.
A delighted shout burst from me.
“Hey, you little punk!
Mungyeong!”
Mungyeong looked exactly as he had before leaving the Sichuan Tang Clan.
Dark Heaven had invaded not long after he left, so I had been worried.
Yet, perhaps our paths had simply missed each other, because he had somehow escaped without a scratch.
“When did you get here?
You look taller than before.
Going through a growth spurt?”
“Why so quiet?
Are you in a bad mood?
Maybe...”
I ruffled Mungyeong’s hair, then leaned closer and whispered,
“Did you have a wet dream this morning?”
“You did.
You totally did.”
Look at the little brat.
Too embarrassed to say a word.
I smiled with satisfaction.
That sort of thing happened from time to time at his age.
Maybe this was my chance to spread proper sex education throughout this dusty old Murim.
“Your hyung here is going to show you a whole new world.
From now on, call me Teacher Jin Seong-ae.”
Teacher Gu Seong-ae, are you watching?
Your knowledge is crossing space and time to reach the next generation.
I was proudly patting Mungyeong on the shoulder when—
“Oh dear...
We forgot to tell him.”
Forgot to tell me what?
Three long sighs sounded behind me.
At the same time, Mungyeong spoke in a flat voice.
“Take your hand off.”
“And I stopped having wet dreams a long time ago.”
“That’s a little problematic, because your secondary sexual development hasn’t completely finished ye—no, that’s not what I mean.”
I swallowed hard.
A terrifying possibility had just flashed through my mind.
“Who... are you?”
Mom, I’m scared.
“...And that is how things came to this.”
“It truly is a bizarre matter.”
Even as the two Sect Leaders raced along using their movement techniques, their voices never wavered.
They looked at me, waiting for an answer.
I forced my lips apart.
“Ah, right.
So there’s some kind of strange formation where we’re going?”
“According to the Third Fiend, whom we captured and interrogated, that appears to be the case.
But the formation itself is so strange...”
Jeok Cheongang answered gruffly.
“This old man and this brat are both hopeless when it comes to formations.
Looking at it won’t tell us a damned thing.”
I agreed.
The Fire Gate Cavern on Mount Jiuhua contained an extraordinary Mystic Gate Formation, but that didn’t make either of us experts.
We’d be better off calling someone from the Zhuge Clan.
But it would take the Zhuge Clan a considerable amount of time to get here.
For some reason, the two Sect Leaders seemed to have high expectations of us.
Especially me.
“Fellow Daoist Jin, did you notice anything else strange about that man?
Anything in his words or behavior?”
“I’ve told you everything.
And from what I could tell...
I don’t think it was possible for him to get any stranger.”
Dark Heaven was strange by nature.
They were fanatics who worshiped the Lord of Heaven as almost—no, simply—as a god.
The Blood Lord and the Western Heaven Demon Lord were no different, with all their bizarre powers and abilities.
One regenerated like a human Troll.
Another popped his arm off and stuck it back on like he had double-sided tape under it.
And then there was the possession at the end.
The more I thought about it, the more miraculous our victory seemed.
We had fought those lunatics and somehow won.
“Before you awoke, Benefactor Jeok gave us a general account of what happened.
Once the messenger eagle we sent to Henan returns with a reply, we should have a clearer idea of how to proceed.”
“If you notice anything strange when you examine the formation, tell us.”
“Yes.”
As I answered, I glanced at the figure racing far ahead of us.
Mungyeong.
No—the man known as the Slaughter Saint.
Fuck.
What the hell is the Slaughter Saint doing here?
Honestly, I had nearly pissed myself.
Even if I spent half a day swimming in the Sanzu River valley, grilled meat, and came back, it wouldn’t be this bad.
Mungyeong was the Slaughter Saint.
And I asked the Slaughter Saint if he’d had a wet dream!
Teacher Gu Seong-ae, I nearly died because of you.
I had just let out a private sigh of relief when the dense undergrowth around us fell away, revealing towering cliffs ahead.

chapters.title: Chapter 372
paragraphs: “This is the place.”
“It’s a cliff, isn’t it? A pretty ordinary one.”
I stopped with the others before the steep cliff and looked around.
It rose over a hundred zhang, a sheer wall of solid rock, but there was nothing particularly remarkable about it.
There’s supposed to be a formation here?
It didn’t take long to find the answer.
Following a sudden sense of déjà vu, I walked slowly forward and stopped before a yellowish-brown section of the cliff face.
“This is...”
Everything has a flow and a grain. Even something as invisible and intangible as qi is no exception.
And the senses I had gained upon reaching the Supreme Peak realm were more than sharp enough to detect the unnatural flow of qi.
“A formation?”
A voice answered my mutter.
“More precisely, an illusion formation.”
Mungyeong—or rather, the Slaughter Saint—gave me a dry look, then stepped forward and extended a hand.
An enormous amount of qi stirred. The solid rock face vanished like mist, revealing the mouth of a pitch-black cavern.
“Your eyes aren’t completely useless, at least.”
“Uh, what?”
“Don’t ask again.”
The Slaughter Saint tossed out those words and headed into the cavern without giving me a chance to respond.
Was that an insult or a compliment?
It left me feeling strangely annoyed.
Still, it would have been awkward to get angry. I sensed no hostility toward me in the Slaughter Saint’s words or actions. He was merely as dry and stiff with me as he was with everyone else.
That made it more embarrassing than infuriating.
Of course, the fact that he was the Slaughter Saint also had something to do with my willingness to let it slide.
If that was how the Slaughter Saint talked, what was I supposed to do? Even if it rubbed me the wrong way, I had to put up with it.
I should be grateful I was still standing after bringing up wet dreams.
I nearly turned the Slaughter Saint into the Rice Saint, so this is practically getting off easy.
As I had that thought, I heard a low chuckle beside me. I turned to find the corners of Jeok Cheongang’s mouth twitching.
“Why are you laughing all of a sudden?”
“No reason. I was just thinking that the Slaughter Saint is remarkably incapable of being honest.”
“What?”
“Don’t ask again.”
What was this? Some new catchphrase?
Jeok Cheongang strode off. The two Sect Leaders and I followed him into the dark cavern.
Still...
I couldn’t believe a place like this had been hidden here.

It was even close enough to reach within half a day from Chengdu, the heart of Sichuan. That was half a day at an ordinary commoner’s pace. For anyone trained in martial arts, it would take far less time.
I looked around as we made our way through the seemingly endless cavern.
Even the entrance is huge. Several times larger than the Sichuan Tang Clan’s underground prison.
I had heard a brief explanation on the way here. The murderous criminals of Dark Heaven had stayed in this very cavern.
So this was where they had hidden while waiting for the right moment. That explained where so many of them had come from.
But how did they get in here to begin with?
More than three hundred enemies had attacked the Tang Clan under the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s command.
Add in the men sent to Qingcheng and Emei, and their numbers were far too great to ignore.
Was security in Sichuan Province really that terrible? No, even so, wouldn’t the Beggars’ Sect and the Lower District Sect have noticed them?
I walked on with that question in mind until the passage—wide enough for ten grown men to walk abreast—finally ended and opened into a vast chamber.
The words slipped out before I knew it.
“...Huh. Would you look at that.”

The chamber could have easily held over a thousand people. Dozens of night-shining pearls embedded in the ceiling cast a soft glow, while jars filled with dry rations and fasting pills stood in one corner alongside piles of weapons.
But none of that was what surprised me most.
What is that?
Strange patterns covered the entire cavern floor.
Carved in regular arrangements like intricate gears, they looked like the ruins of an ancient kingdom forgotten long ago.
“Is that perhaps the thing you mentioned earlier...?”
At my question, Cheongpung the Ancient Sword, Sect Leader of the Qingcheng Sect, nodded gravely.
“That is correct. That is the strange formation I spoke of.”
I had wondered if it could really be a formation, but apparently it was.
I had encountered all kinds of mechanisms and formations at the Star-Array Grand Banquet, but I had never seen one this large or this bizarre.
This goes beyond strange. It’s downright grotesque.
Maybe it was the patterns. There was something both mysterious and dangerous about them.
Jeok Cheongang seemed to share my thoughts.
“But what in the world are those bizarre patterns?”
“We have yet to determine that ourselves.”
Extinction Divine Nun added to Cheongpung the Ancient Sword’s answer.

“We cannot jump to conclusions. We copied part of the formation and showed it to several renowned scholars and distinguished figures, but none recognized it. We cannot entirely rule out the possibility that it is some unknown script from the Western Regions.”
Before I knew it, a remark slipped from my lips.
“Uh, that isn’t writing.”
Every eye turned toward me. The Slaughter Saint, who had remained silent ever since we entered the cavern, abruptly spoke.
“Your basis?”
“My... basis?”
“If you make such a claim, you must have sound grounds for it. Stop asking questions and answer.”

Of course I had grounds. Conclusive grounds that neither a renowned scholar who had devoured tens of thousands of books nor an eminent martial artist who had spent a lifetime roaming the Murim could refute.
The Integrated Language Pack.
The Integrated Language Pack automatically translated every language through the power of the System.
It didn’t just let me communicate. I could read and write any language as well.
It was thanks to the Integrated Language Pack that I had been able to speak with the Skeleton Warlord in the modern world.
Yet despite the interpretation function being constantly active like a passive Skill, the patterns that made up the formation remained unchanged.
That was definitive proof they weren’t writing.
The problem was...
How am I supposed to explain that?
I shouldn’t have said anything. I should have kept my mouth shut.
But it was already too late. As the Slaughter Saint’s gaze grew more intense, I stammered,
“Bo... bo.”
“Boobs?”
The Rice Saint’s eyebrow twitched.
It was the first emotion he had shown. He had clearly remembered the wet-dream incident.
“Ah, no, not boobs.”
“Breasts, then?”
Please. Don’t say things like that with a face completely devoid of emotion.
“No, that’s not what I meant.”
As I frantically waved my hands, Jeok Cheongang suddenly cut in.
“Are you threatening my Disciple? How dare you threaten the Fire King’s heir and the Young Sect Leader of the Fire Gate Clan?”
“Threaten him? There is no need, but neither is it beyond me.”
“I intended to let this pass since I happened to owe you my life, but if this is how you mean to act, Mun, then this old man cannot stand idle.”
The atmosphere grew increasingly hostile. I squeezed my eyes shut and shouted,
“I-I took a guess!”
“I thought I might have seen something like it in a book before... and it just didn’t feel like writing, so I guessed.”
A heavy silence descended.
The Slaughter Saint let out a nearly inaudible sigh, then asked Jeok Cheongang,
“So that fellow is the heir of the Fire King and the Young Sect Leader of the Fire Gate Clan?”
Jeok Cheongang fell silent for a moment before answering.
“Now that I think about it, he never underwent the formal initiation ceremony.”
“So strictly speaking, he isn’t yet an official Disciple of our sect. Which means he should still be considered a member of the Jin Family of Taiyuan...”
Jeok Cheongang’s eyes met mine. He quietly looked away.
“I shall say no more.”
What did he mean, no more? He had already said everything there was to say.
Having witnessed the complete collapse of trust between Master and Disciple, Extinction Divine Nun and Cheongpung the Ancient Sword awkwardly changed the subject.
“Ahem. In any case, it seems we must continue investigating this strange formation.”
“F-Fellow Daoist Jin and Senior Jeok’s insights have been most helpful.”
Heaven knew they hadn’t helped at all. Earth knew it. Everyone here knew it.
Even a stray dog in an alley wouldn’t believe that nonsense.
Having brought the situation to a close with such an obvious lie, Cheongpung the Ancient Sword turned to Extinction Divine Nun with a troubled expression.
“Still, it is truly difficult to believe. To bring so many people here with nothing more than a formation...”
“Indeed. If such a thing is possible, does that not mean they could appear anywhere under heaven?”
Wait. What did they just say?
I had been staring at the ground, frustrated by my inability to explain myself and still suffering from the aftermath of the boob incident. I abruptly raised my head.
“What is it, Benefactor Jin?”
“No, it’s just... I think this is the first I’ve heard either of you mention that part about the formation.”
“Hmm? You mean the Moving Formation?”
“...The Moving Formation?”

“That is correct. According to the Third Fiend, that strange formation is called a Moving Formation. We cannot know how much of his absurd story to believe, but he said Dark Heaven used it to travel hundreds of li.”
A Moving Formation. They said it was a Moving Formation.
Even if a critic in angular horn-rimmed glasses had suddenly walked out and declared, “I give this formation four and a half stars,” I couldn’t have been more bewildered.
This sounds familiar.
A formation capable of transporting hundreds of people across hundreds of li.
The more I thought about it, the harder my heart pounded and the drier my lips became.
What if this so-called Moving Formation was that thing I was thinking of?
No. That can’t be.
But despite my desperate denial, my Adam’s apple bobbed heavily.
“Is this formation still operational?”
I had directed the question at the two Sect Leaders, but the Slaughter Saint answered.
“The Third Fiend. I caught him here myself.”
“...He tried to escape through the Moving Formation.”
“Yes. But that was only his intention.”
“You mean...”
“As he later confessed, he tried to activate the formation. Nothing happened.”
“Oh.”
“One thing is certain. There is no flow of qi whatsoever within that formation. It has completely lost its power. Nothing remains but an empty shell.”
After finishing his explanation in a flat voice, the Slaughter Saint added,

“Judging from the circumstances that have come to light, Dark Heaven is without a doubt the successor to the Demonic Cult. The Demonic Cult possesses countless monstrous martial arts and supreme techniques, so it would not be strange if they had any number of bizarre arts.”
I had heard what kind of place the Demonic Cult was so many times that it had been drilled into my head.
A powerful religious organization that was the very embodiment of demonic, heterodox arts.

Although it had ultimately been defeated in the Great Faction War, it had managed to overwhelm the entire Murim for so long because of the countless monstrous martial arts and supreme techniques it possessed.
So this formation is one of the many bizarre arts passed down from the Demonic Cult?

No matter how much I thought about it, I couldn’t figure it out. Maybe all the fusion-fantasy novels I had read were getting in the way. This sort of thing showed up in them all the time, which somehow only made it more confusing.
They got away with it just fine in Mukhyung. Ugh. I shouldn’t have read a novel that never even got an ending.
Still, just in case, I decided to memorize the formation’s arrangement and patterns.
I was staring intently at the Moving Formation, engraving every detail into my mind, when the Slaughter Saint suddenly spoke.
“Judging by your behavior, you seem to know something. Does anything come to mind?”
What excuse was I supposed to make now?

chapters.title: Chapter 373
paragraphs: The trip back was short.
On the way there, we had at least slowed down to exchange information. But in game terms, this was a deluxe party with no fewer than five Supreme Peak masters traveling together.
The distance that would have taken an ordinary person half a day to cover had shrunk to almost nothing.
“You’ve worked hard, Benefactor Jin.”
“And you must still be tired. Thank you for coming with us.”
As we neared the Sichuan Tang Clan, the two Sect Leaders turned to address me. I shrugged.
“It’s nothing. I didn’t really help much, anyway.”
“True.”
“He certainly didn’t.”
It was true that I hadn’t been much help, but wasn’t that a little harsh?
Cheongpung the Ancient Sword gave me a faint smile, then clasped his hands toward the Slaughter Saint and Jeok Cheongang.
“I’m grateful to both of you Seniors as well. I apologize for making you come all this way for nothing.”
The Slaughter Saint and Jeok Cheongang answered at the same time.
“It was indeed a pointless trip.”
“Next time, don’t do anything you’ll need to apologize for. Understood?”
“...Ah. Yes.”
That was exactly how I felt.
The Slaughter Saint continued, addressing the visibly uncomfortable Cheongpung the Ancient Sword.
“And... I hope you won’t come looking for me again.”
He wasn’t telling them to call on him less often because it was a bother. After briefly returning as the Slaughter Saint, he intended to go back to being Mungyeong, the young medical apprentice.
Everyone present understood what he meant.
The two Sect Leaders were the most flustered of all.
“S-Senior, that...”
“Benefactor, might you reconsider?”
Instead of answering, the Slaughter Saint gave them a dry look.
After a moment of silence, Cheongpung the Ancient Sword and Extinction Divine Nun sighed softly and nodded.
“...We will do so.”
“I shall respect your wishes. For now.”
For now.
The last two words were heavily emphasized. The Slaughter Saint’s quiet voice slipped between his lips.
“My decision has not changed. Coming this time was nothing more than a passing whim.”
It was a firm answer that left not even the slightest room for argument. The Slaughter Saint’s gaze shifted toward Jeok Cheongang and me.
“I trust you two understand that as well.”
Jeok Cheongang suddenly spoke.
“Are you going to pretend to be a medical apprentice again? It doesn’t suit you.”
“It isn’t an act. The Slaughter Saint no longer exists. Only a medical apprentice remains.”
“If a tiger drapes itself in goatskin, does that make it a goat?”
“If it hides its teeth and claws, even a tiger can become a goat.”
“But you revealed your claws in the end. Didn’t you?”
A shallow crease formed between the Slaughter Saint’s brows.
“You’ve grown more talkative with age. You owe me a debt, after all.”
“...Damn. I can’t argue when you’re not wrong.”
“I’ll take that as an answer.”
Having dismissed Jeok Cheongang, the Slaughter Saint glanced at me.
“And you?”
“Me?”
“Who else is left?”
“No, that’s not what I meant. Do I get a choice?”
“Of course. You have two.”
The Slaughter Saint spoke with an impassive expression.

“First, you can loudly announce that the young medical apprentice named Mungyeong is actually the Slaughter Saint, then be found dead without a soul knowing how. Second, you can keep your mouth shut so no one notices, treat me as you did before, and leave quietly.”
“Which will you choose?”
Wow. The choices were so difficult that I was speechless for a moment.
After swallowing hard, I opened my mouth.
“The second one.”
“A wise choice.”
“Yeah.”
The Slaughter Saint had been about to nod at my prompt answer when he suddenly stopped.
“What did you just say?”
“Why?”
“What?”
“No, I mean, why are you acting like that? You told me to treat you as I did before.”
The two Sect Leaders stood there with their mouths hanging open. The Slaughter Saint was silent for a moment before asking Jeok Cheongang, who had begun chuckling.
“Is this fellow insane?”
“He’s always been like that. Gives you a headache, doesn’t he?”
“I want to smash his skull in.”
I bowed deeply before he could make good on that threat.
“Ah, I got confused for a moment. My apologies.”
“Not even a dog would believe that, but I’ll let it slide this once.”
Had it been too obvious that I was trying to mess with him while pretending it was a mistake? The Slaughter Saint glared at me with narrowed eyes before speaking.
“In any case, watch yourself from now on. Aside from those present, no one knows the truth about me. Ah, that boy Cheongpung is an exception. As is my Disciple, of course.”
“Cheongpung knew too?”
“Yes. Aside from him, everyone who saw me that day is dead.”
Now that was a thorough cleanup.
I finally understood why there hadn’t been a single prisoner at the Sichuan Tang Clan.
The Masked Slaughter Saint. Once the mask came off, panelists and audience members alike dropped dead.
The more I think about it, the stranger this feels. Mungyeong was the Slaughter Saint all along.
Memories flashed through my mind, from our first meeting on the Yangtze to the present.
Which of the sides he had shown me was real, and which was a lie?
The innocent young medical apprentice I had known no longer existed. All that remained was the greatest assassin under heaven, his eyes dry and emotionless.
Before I knew it, a question slipped out.
“Why are you so determined to hide who you are?”
The Slaughter Saint, moving toward the Sichuan Tang Clan now visible in the distance, stopped dead.
After a brief silence, he answered with unexpected calm.
“Because I’m sick to death of the Murim.”
“Is that why you left?”
“Yes. I swore to the heavens that I would never take another life.”
In this place—the Murim—assassins were despised.
Neither the orthodox factions nor practitioners of demonic, heterodox arts welcomed them.
They were seen not as martial artists pursuing higher realms of martial arts, but as people born solely to kill.
How much blood had one assassin spilled—and how deeply had he been stained by it—before earning the sobriquet Slaughter Saint?
I thought I understood how he felt, at least to some extent.
But...
“On the other hand, I’m a little curious.”
“What?”
“Why you came back to the Murim you hate so much.”
“...What nonsense are you talking about, saying I returned?”
The Slaughter Saint’s eyes sank deeper.
“I had no choice. It was unavoidable.”
“I don’t know. If that’s how you put it, I have nothing to say. But it seems like you made at least a few choices yourself. For example...”
I scratched the back of my head and continued.

“You asked to travel with some martial artists you met on the Yangtze because you were headed in the same direction. A few days later, you happened to run into them again and casually revealed your identity. Or you borrowed my name to order the Successor Beggar of the Beggars’ Sect to rescue Emei Sect, while you went to Qingcheng...”
“Enough.”
“Yes. I was about to stop anyway. Now that I’ve listed them one by one, there are quite a few.”
“What is it you want to hear? That I should have stood by and watched countless people—including you and your Master—die?”
“Of course not. I’m truly grateful, Great Hero.”
There was no sarcasm in my voice. I meant it with one hundred percent sincerity.
If he hadn’t stepped in at the right moment, countless people would have died or been injured.
Jeok Cheongang and I would certainly have been among them.
But the Slaughter Saint’s response to my words was as dry as desert sand.
“Don’t call me Great Hero.”
“Then what should I call you?”
The Slaughter Saint stared at me without speaking, then turned away.
He took a step toward the Sichuan Tang Clan, now no more than a large speck in the distance, and glided forward like a ghost.
The boy’s voice scattered on the wind.
“Mungyeong. That is enough.”
Was it really enough?
Only he knew the answer.
I shrugged and replied,
“Yeah, got it, Mungyeong.”
At that moment, the figure walking ahead of us stumbled.
When I returned to the pavilion, two leeches latched onto me.
One was Hyuk Mujin, whom I could never decide was my right arm or my pinky. The other was a beggar whose skin had gotten a little whiter, as if he had started scrubbing off some dirt lately.
“Why is Mungyeong like that? He somehow seems a little gloomier.”
“That’s understandable. His Master, the Divine Physician, was injured, and there are so many patients waiting for treatment.”
“Oh, I see. But Captain, where did you go with Mungyeong?”
“Isn’t it obvious? He looked down, so the Captain took him out for some fresh air. Why are you so stupid?”
“Huh. In all my life, I never thought I’d hear that from a beggar. I may look like this, but I’ve read several hundred books. I’ve never been called stupid before.”
As far as I could tell, both of them were just stupid.
I swallowed the words Slaughter Saint hovering on the tip of my tongue. Those two would never discover Mungyeong’s true identity, even if they died and came back to life.
Then again, with acting skills like that, anyone would be fooled.
The instant people’s attention turned toward him, the Slaughter Saint returned to being Mungyeong.
No one suspected his identity just because the cheerful young medical apprentice seemed a little gloomier than usual.
No one could even have guessed.
“I’d give you credit if you’d read the Four Books and Three Classics, but all you’ve done is read martial arts novels nonstop. What books are you talking about?”
“I read romance novels too. Haven’t you heard of Gwiyeommi?”
“Wait. Gwiyeommi? You mean the scholar who wrote The Temptation of a Young Prodigy, That Bastard Was Strong, and all those others?”
“Oh, you know him.”

“Of course I do. When I was a one-knot Disciple, I used the money I’d begged for to rent one of his books, and the beggar chief beat me black and blue. Damn, if I ran into that bastard now, I’d lay into him with the Dog-Beating Staff Technique. I’d—”
Whack!
“Gah!”
“Aagh!”
I kicked both idiots in the ass as they happily reminisced, drove them out, and slammed the door shut.
I already had more than enough to think about. Why had those bastards come here just to make a racket?
Finally, some peace and quiet.
Cheongpung was probably running all over the place by now, and I’d told Jeok Cheongang to rest for the entire day. No one would come looking for me for a while.
I lay down on the soft bed and decided to take care of something I’d been putting off.
Check unread messages.
Ding. Ding. Ding-ding!
System windows filled the air as an endless stream of chimes rang out.
This had happened a few times before, but this had to be a new record.
Momentarily speechless, I began checking the important messages one by one.

System You have reached the Supreme Peak realm! You defeated Lv. 170 No Gunbaek! Quest Uninvited Guest successfully completed! You have acquired a tremendous amount of EXP and Fame! System messages have exceeded the limit. Acquired EXP and Fame are being totaled. You have reached Lv. 120! Your Fame has surpassed the threshold. You acquire a new sobriquet! Through battles that brought you to the brink of life and death, you gained enlightenment on your own. The realms of all martial arts have risen greatly, and you can now use new martial arts! Fire Gate Divine Technique has reached the eighth stage! Flame Divine Palm has reached... Fire Dragon Divine Spear...
Countless requests for handshakes—no, a veritable feast of messages.
My eyes started spinning just from skimming them.
“...Holy shit.”
What was all this?
I was almost stunned to discover that half the unread messages still remained.
Just as I scrolled down to see how many were left, something unusual caught my eye.

System A new Item becomes bound to you. Currently bound Items: White Flame, ??? This Item has not yet been given a name. If you give it a new name, it will become completely bound to you and can be summoned through your Inventory from anywhere.
“This pops up here...”
The Modern World and Murim inventories were separate. However, bound Items like White Flame weren’t restricted by space and could be pulled out and used anywhere.
I’d already felt that White Flame alone wasn’t enough, so this was quite a stroke of luck.
If they’re giving it to me, I’ll gladly take it.
I was just about to check my Inventory, brimming with anticipation, when—
Knock, knock, knock.
A knock sounded on the door, and someone poked their head inside.
“Captain. It’s me, Mujin...”
“Get lost.”
“No, that’s not what I meant.”
“Hyung’s busy. Go read some Gwiyeommi novels.”
“Oh, Captain, you’ve read them too?”
“...You little bastard, seriously.”
This wouldn’t do.
Before cracking open the Item, I’d have to crack that bastard open first.
I shot up from the bed, and Hyuk Mujin hurriedly shouted,
“Henan! It’s Henan!”
“What?”
“An investigation team has arrived from Henan! They’re looking for you, Captain.”
“...An investigation team?”
I frowned at Hyuk Mujin’s completely contextless explanation.
Ding.
A familiar alert reached my ears.

chapters.title: Chapter 374
paragraphs: Tang Horyong, the Master of Poison Dragon Pavilion, rose from his seat to greet his guest.
An imposing man had just opened the door and entered, and an indescribable pressure radiated from him.
“You’ve had a long journey.”
“Compared to what the Sichuan Tang Clan has endured, it was nothing. Allow me to offer my deepest condolences once again.”
Despite his rough features, the man’s voice was low and gentle, yet possessed a force that compelled others to listen.
It was the sort of presence only a leader of men possessed. The man’s gaze was mild yet unfathomably deep, and it suddenly reminded Tang Horyong of someone.
It feels as though I’m facing another older cousin...
That realization left Tang Horyong more than a little unsettled.
He had heard that the man before him was still young—not yet forty.
His older cousin, on the other hand, was an extraordinary figure not only in age but also in his standing within the Murim.
He was an iron-willed Family Head who had accomplished countless military feats during the Great Faction War and rebuilt his fallen family stronger than ever.
Tang Sadok, the Myriad-Poison Asura.
Tang Horyong, the Acting Family Head of the Sichuan Tang Clan, sighed inwardly as he thought of his older cousin, who had yet to regain consciousness.
Please wake soon and lead us, Family Head.
Tang Horyong had been born a martial artist.
He prided himself on having mastered poison and hidden weapons, but leading a family was an entirely different matter.
Especially lately, countless problems had been pouring in from every direction, leaving him no time even to think about the grief and anger caused by the loss of his blood relatives.
If only someone like this were standing in my place.
In that sense, Tang Horyong couldn’t help envying the man before him.
Nor was he judging him solely by his first impression. He had already heard plenty of rumors about the man.
Even if only a quarter of them were true, the man was more than capable of leading a family.
“Sir Tang, is there something on my face?”
“Ah, no. I’ve been so distracted that I forgot my manners. My apologies.”
At Tang Horyong’s hurried apology, the man nodded gravely.
“Not at all. It’s understandable after everything you’ve suffered.”
In truth, even the word devastating fell short of describing the damage the Sichuan Tang Clan had suffered.
Nearly ninety percent of the clan’s people had died, and most of the Tang Clan’s grounds had been destroyed.
Their only consolation was that the family line had survived, but restoring the clan to its former glory would take many years.
“Our fellow martial artists throughout Sichuan have gone out of their way to help us, but... I fear what lies ahead.”
If Tang Sadok, the Family Head, had been in his position, he would never have shown weakness under any circumstances.
Tang Horyong was different.
At his honest words, the man gently ran his long fingers over his teacup.
“I believe you know why I came here, Sir Tang.”
“I understand that you came to investigate the Three-Gate Bloodbath.”

“To be precise, when I first left Henan, my purpose was to find the culprit who murdered the late Poison King Tang Sadok and the Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun. However, the situation changed drastically on the way here.”
“That’s right. Dark Heaven, those bastards beyond the pale, finally revealed their fangs.”
“Although we already had the incident in Henan as precedent, the fact that they dared to attack three renowned clans and sects across the land at once proves that war is already upon us.”
Small disturbances breed greater chaos.
But Dark Heaven’s existence could no longer be concealed, nor was there any reason to hide it.
Seven days and nights had passed since the horrific Three-Gate Bloodbath.
By now, word without feet would have traveled a thousand li, and countless messenger pigeons would be flying to every corner of the realm.
And war—not mere chaos—had brought people together.
“I heard the orthodox Murim has been rallying in Henan since the Shaolin Bloodshed. Then, perhaps...”
“For now, they are still making preparations. But it is already a foregone conclusion.”
The man continued in a weighty voice.
“That brings me to my proposal. Would you consider going to Henan?”
“Henan.”
“Yes. What you’re thinking of will happen soon.”
After a brief silence, Tang Horyong spoke.
“I’m grateful to be invited to such an honorable occasion, but I cannot leave now. As you know, as Acting Family Head, I must remain with the members of our family...”
“Sir Tang.”
“Go on.”
“As you just said, you are the Acting Family Head. Naturally, you cannot leave the members of the Tang Clan behind.”
Only then did Tang Horyong understand what the man was proposing. His mouth fell open.
It was something he had never dared even consider.
“So you’re saying that we should move our family headquarters?”
“Well...”
The man’s clear gaze, as though it could see straight through him, settled on Tang Horyong.
“Great Hero Mae Jonghak told me that a war even greater than the Great Faction War would soon break out.”
“The Sword Saint...”
Tang Horyong swallowed a groan.
That could not be the Sword Saint’s opinion alone.
The Shaolin Bloodshed had awakened the anger and vigilance of countless orthodox martial artists, and the new Murim Alliance was already poised to take shape.
The entire orthodox Murim was preparing for the coming war.
Can our family survive in a situation like this?
The question flashed through his mind, and his heart sank.
The Sichuan Tang Clan had already suffered a blow unprecedented in its history.
Moreover, the Qingcheng Sect and Emei Sect had also lost a considerable portion of their forces.
If the enemy attacked again, there was little hope of stopping them.
As Tang Horyong sighed with a dazed expression, a quiet voice reached his ears.
“Sir Tang, why do you think the Sichuan Tang Clan has endured for the past several hundred years?”
“That is...”
“Because it was the Tang Clan. Even if you remove the first two characters—Sichuan—that fact does not change.”
“If you make the decision, the orthodox Murim will help the Tang Clan.”
Tang Horyong trembled before finally managing to speak.

“We have made countless enemies over the years. Even among the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families, there are those who regard our family with hostility. Will that truly cause no problems?”
“Everything will be handled fairly and openly. Put your mind at ease and establish a new home. Henan, Shaanxi, or...”
A gentle smile touched the man’s lips.
“Shanxi would be a fine choice as well.”
“Shanxi?”
“Just say the word. I have plenty of land to spare.”
Tang Horyong suddenly remembered one fact he had overlooked.
The man before him was the Alliance Leader who had unified the Shanxi Murim, as well as the greatest landowner and wealthiest man in Shanxi Province.
“Thank you. Truly, thank you, Great Hero Jin!”
“Think nothing of it.”
At that moment, Jin Wikyung, the Lesser Family Head of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, returned the Acting Family Head of the Sichuan Tang Clan’s clasped-fist salute with courtesy and dignity.
Clunk.
“Um, I heard you called for me.”
Jin Wikyung spotted a young man poking his head through the gap in the pavilion door and unleashed a lion’s roar.
“My youngest!”
Thud-thud-thud-thud—crash!
He charged like an enraged bull.
As Tang Horyong watched the two brothers reunite in something that fell somewhere between an embrace and a collision, he recalled one of the rumors he had heard about Jin Wikyung.
They say he’s completely helpless when it comes to his younger brothers.
The Alliance Leader who had unified Shanxi Murim and the greatest landowner in Shanxi Province was nowhere to be seen.
In his place stood a hopelessly doting fool.
He’s still young, so he lacks experience. He can’t compare to my older cousin, who remains perfectly levelheaded at all times. Yes, of course.
Tang Horyong had no way of knowing about Mimi-chan.
“My youngest!”
Jin Wikyung charged at me with tears flying from his eyes and swept me into a fierce embrace.
I’d been in the Murim for two years now. I’d endured this kind of thing more times than I cared to remember, so I’d expected a reaction like this.
Crack!
...But I hadn’t expected that.
Seriously, why did I hear my bones shifting?
I sighed as he squeezed my entire body like an anaconda in the Amazon jungle.
Still, since he was happy to see me, I let him hug me without resisting. His reaction had never been this intense before, though.
“Wait, Hyung-nim. Let go and then we can talk. Let go.”
“Hyung-nim? Why are you using such a stiff form of address? Haven’t I told you to just call me hyung? You’ve changed. You’ve really changed!”
“Okay, I get it, so let me go now.”
“You used to speak informally when you were little! Why are you being so polite now? You’ve changed. You’ve really changed!”
“Let go, goddammit.”
“Gasp! You never swore, even at the height of your rebellious phase! You’ve changed—”
“Wow, that refrain is driving me insane.”
Was being a martial artist his main job and being a Dementor his side gig?
Shuddering at the feeling of my soul being sucked out, I reached out.
Whoosh—crash!
Jin Wikyung’s huge body slammed headfirst into the ground with a heavy thud.
A middle-aged man from the Sichuan Tang Clan, who had been watching us, let out a startled groan.
“It’s all right. Really. We’re just playing around.”
“N-No, but...”
“Look. He’s getting right back up.”
Just as I’d said, Jin Wikyung sprang to his feet as if nothing had happened, tears of emotion welling in his eyes.
“You’ve grown even stronger. That’s my youngest.”
His utter lack of change made me snort with laughter.
“You really haven’t changed.”
“Haven’t changed? Do you know how worried I’ve been these past two months? I couldn’t sleep at night, and I lost my appetite until I was nothing but skin and bones.”
I looked over his enormous, muscular frame and muttered, “You seem to have plenty of skin and bones.”
Come to think of it, two months.
That much time had already passed.
It struck me anew that the time for me to return was drawing near.
If spending ten days in one world meant that only an hour or so passed in the other...
About six hours must have passed. The plane might be landing soon.
The timing couldn’t have been better. I’d built up quite a bit of fatigue while overcoming the massive hurdle that was the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
Without wasting any more words, I got straight to the point.
“When are we leaving?”
“My youngest, you must have suffered so much... Hm?”
Jin Wikyung, who had been anxiously looking me over, froze.
“What did you just say?”
“You came to take me with you, didn’t you? Oh, and the Third Fiend too.”
Jin Wikyung’s eyes widened.
“How did you know?”
The middle-aged man, who seemed to hold an important position in the Sichuan Tang Clan, also spoke in surprise.
“Great Hero Jin, did you not come to investigate the full circumstances of the incident?”

“I did, but several members of the investigation team, including myself, will be returning to Henan. Just before we reached Sichuan, we received orders to escort the Third Fiend, one of the chief culprits behind the Three-Gate Bloodbath.”
“Then what about your proposal concerning our family?”
“That offer remains valid, of course. But relocating right away would be difficult for the Tang Clan.”
“That is true. The Family Head is still in no condition to travel such a great distance, and we must obtain the consent of the other clan members.”
“Yes. And...”
After speaking quietly with the middle-aged man for a moment, Jin Wikyung sent me a covert Sound Transmission.
But how did you know?
I can put two and two together. It seemed obvious from the circumstances.
Ah, my youngest. What terrible ordeal did you endure to become smarter as well?
That rubbed me the wrong way.
I hadn’t actually figured it out from the circumstances. I knew because a Quest to escort the Third Fiend had appeared.
“So when are we leaving?”
Having just finished his conversation, Jin Wikyung answered my question.
“If you already knew, that makes this easier. The sooner, the better. Are you ready?”
“I didn’t bring anything but the two balls between my legs. All I have to do is go.”
Plus two bundles wrapped tightly in bandages.
Jin Wikyung nodded and turned to the middle-aged man.
“Sir Tang, where is the Third Fiend?”

The man he had addressed as Sir Tang replied, “We bound their limbs and confined them under close watch. Ever since their testicles were crushed, they’ve tried to kill themselves at every opportunity, so you’ll need to be careful.”
“...Good grief.”
I’d want to die too if that happened to me.
In any case, everything was in place for us to move quickly.
Jin Wikyung considered it for a moment, then answered decisively.
“Then half a shichen. We’ll leave within half a shichen. Is that acceptable?”
“No problem.”
The instant I answered without hesitation, a frantic commotion arose outside the pavilion, followed by someone shouting.
“The Family Head! The Family Head has awakened!”
Jin Wikyung amended his words in a lukewarm voice.
“One shichen. Let’s make it one shichen.”
“...Yes. That sounds better.”
What a shame. I could’ve taken the Myriad-Poison Ring and run.

chapters.title: Chapter 375
paragraphs: There was an order to visiting the sick.
When word spread that Tang Sadok—the Family Head and an elder of the clan—had awakened, the members of the Tang Clan dropped everything and came running.
But not all hundred-plus of them could see him.
“Benefactor, when can we go see Grandpa Tang?”
“Hard to say. The people ahead of us have been in there for a while, so they should be coming out soon.”
“Oh, I see.”
Cheongpung nodded at my answer.
Wait. Cheongpung?
“What are you doing here? When did you get here?”
“Just now.”
He had joined the conversation so naturally that I hadn’t even noticed him. But why had he come here?
As if he had read my mind, Cheongpung pointed at his chest.
“Mimi said she wanted to see him.”
What the hell had I just heard?
Now he could even communicate with a snake. Was this guy from Slytherin instead of Huashan?
Cheongpung tilted his head at my suspicious stare.
“Why are you looking at my forehead all of a sudden? Is there something on it?”
“I was just checking whether you had a lightning-shaped scar on your forehead.”
“What?”
“There is such a thing.”
The instant I finished speaking—
Clunk.
The tightly shut door of the infirmary opened, and about a dozen people emerged.
They were among the few surviving direct descendants of the Sichuan Tang Clan. Tang Horyong, whom I had met before, was among them.
“Whew...”
His eyes bloodshot, he looked up at the sky before walking toward us.
“The Family Head wishes to see you.”
“We’ve been waiting.”
Jin Wikyung nodded and led the way. Cheongpung and I followed him into the infirmary.
We walked through the heavy smell of medicinal decoctions until a physician with a white cloth covering his nose and mouth led us into a treatment room.
At last, we came face-to-face with several familiar people.
“Cough... You came.”
Tang Sadok’s condition was serious at a glance. His limbs were broken, and the qi within him was unstable from his internal injuries.
The Divine Physician, who exchanged a brief glance with us, stopped Tang Sadok as he tried to sit up.
“Family Head, did I not tell you not to move?”
“This old man is a sinner. I committed a crime deserving of death, so it is only right that I ask for punishment.”
Tang Sadok shook his pale head, stared directly at me, and continued.
“I will make no pathetic excuses. The Western Heaven Demon Lord went to the underground prison because I told him about it.”
I folded my arms at an angle.
“Ah. No wonder.”
“Why?”
Tang Sadok asked with a flustered expression.
“Ah, you knew?”
“Of course I didn’t know at first. Things were too hectic back then. But when I thought about it later, I started wondering how the hell that bastard knew where the Myriad-Poison Ring was.”
Only a tiny number of people knew its location.
Cheongpung might have looked as light as a flower petal, but he was as steadfast as the roots of a tree. That left Tang Sadok as the only person who could have revealed it.
“Why did you do it?”
“He said that if I told him where the Myriad-Poison Ring was, he would preserve our family’s bloodline.”
“And you believed him?”
“This old man was foolish. My judgment was clouded for a moment, and I did something I never should have done.”
“At least you realize that much.”
Tang Sadok’s eyes trembled as he looked at me.
“The reason this old man survived must have been Heaven’s will. I was spared so that I might apologize to you and receive my punishment.”
“Then what punishment do you seek, Family Head?”
The cold voice belonged to Jin Wikyung, who had been silently listening to our conversation.
“Are you the Lesser Family Head of the Jin Family of Taiyuan?”
“Yes. I am also the elder brother who raised my two younger brothers as if they were my own sons.”
Unmistakable anger smoldered in Jin Wikyung’s dark eyes.
“It was something no one who walks the righteous path should have done.”
“I know. No... I am well aware. That is why I ask to be punished.”
“What if I order you to take your own life?”
Everyone, myself included, stared at Jin Wikyung in shock.
Everyone except Tang Sadok.
His expression perfectly calm, he answered.

“I betrayed the principles of the Way, yet because all of you risked your lives to fight for us, our family’s bloodline will endure. If this worthless old man’s life can serve as atonement, I will gladly offer it.”
A brief silence followed. Then Jin Wikyung sighed.
“Whew...”
He regarded Tang Sadok with a complicated look before turning to me.
“What will you do?”
“...What? Have him take his own life?”
“Anything.”
Having the hilt of a sword suddenly placed in my hand made my heart clench.
Especially when the life hanging from the other end belonged to the Family Head of the Sichuan Tang Clan.
Look how icy the mood suddenly got.

Of course, this wasn’t something I could just laugh off. I wasn’t some perfectly impartial, broad-minded Great Hero of Benevolence and Righteousness. When I figured out the whole story, anger had quietly begun simmering inside me.
Everyone’s lives had been on the line back then, not just mine.
But...
“Forget it. I don’t want to take it that far.”
The truth was, part of me understood Tang Sadok’s position.
If I had to weigh an outsider I had met only a few times against my own blood—people I was duty-bound to protect as the head of my family—I might have made the same choice.
Besides, I owed him.
Tang Sadok’s help had played a major part in Jeok Cheongang’s awakening.
Even if there had been a certain deal involved, Tang Sadok had still been the one who lent us a divine artifact without telling even his own blood relatives.
“So let’s call it even. No, that’s going too far. Let’s just say the Sichuan Tang Clan owes us a huge debt for what happened.”
When I finished, Cheongpung and the Divine Physician spoke up.
“It was definitely Grandpa Tang’s fault that Benefactor was put in danger... but I’ll follow Benefactor’s wishes, too.”
“I have already forgotten about it. If I have one wish as a physician, it is for the Family Head to recover as soon as possible. There are still clan members who survived, aren’t there?”
Jin Wikyung spoke last. Unlike before, there was no longer any anger in his voice.
No—perhaps he had known what my answer would be from the start.
“So that is what they say. What do you think, Family Head?”
Tang Sadok’s eyes shook with emotion as he looked at us.
After a brief silence, a hoarse voice escaped his lips.
“This old man... The Sichuan Tang Clan owes all of you a tremendous debt of gratitude.”
The instant Tang Sadok bowed his head in heartfelt thanks—
Ding. Ding. Ding.

System Confessing one’s sins is difficult, but something else requires even greater courage: Forgiveness. Hidden Quest Atonement and Forgiveness successfully completed! Lv. 115 Tang Sadok expresses his profound gratitude for your goodwill. He and the Sichuan Tang Clan will never forget the kindness and aid you showed them today. The people of the Sichuan Tang Clan will remember you as their Benefactor! You have acquired the Title: Tang Clan’s Benefactor! You have received a tremendous amount of EXP and Fame as a reward for completing the Hidden Quest! Level Up!
What the hell? A Hidden Quest out of nowhere?
While I stood dazed by the unexpected System notifications, something cold brushed between my legs and slipped past.
Sssrikk, sssriririk.
“Mimi, you little rascal.”
Seeing Mimi and Tang Sadok reunited after so long reminded me of something I had momentarily forgotten.
“Oh, right. About the Myriad-Poison Ring... Luckily, I’ve kept it safe all this time—”
“Is that so?”
Tang Sadok cut in before I could finish.
“Then continue keeping it.”
“Yes, then I’ll keep it... Wait, what?”
“I entrust our family’s divine artifact to you. Consider it a token of our gratitude to our Benefactor, and please do not refuse.”
Ding.

What was with today?
I was starting to get nervous. What kind of fucked-up shit was waiting for me if the System was showering me with rewards like this?
Seeing me open and close my mouth like a goldfish, Tang Sadok smiled faintly.
“If there is anything you desire, tell me. So long as it lies within our family’s power, I will grant it.”
The Divine Physician smiled along with him and answered,
“All I desire is for the patients to recover as soon as possible.”
“Oh?”
An answer worthy of the Divine Physician. Or should I call him Dong Feng now?
One thing was certain: he too was a Divine Physician in every sense of the title.
“What do you desire?”
Cheongpung jumped at the sudden question.
“M-Me?”
Tang Sadok nodded. Cheongpung twisted his hands and feet awkwardly as he answered.
“I... Well... Hmm. Nothing.”
“Are you sure?”
“Yes. I don’t think there’s anything.”
Hey, you little bastard. Take your eyes off Mimi-chan and talk.
I wanted to bring him a mirror and show him what he looked like. His eyes were filled with aching longing and desire for Mimi-chan.
At this rate, he’s going to bore a hole through her scales.
Just then, Tang Sadok spoke.
“This little one is an old friend of mine. For the past several decades, she has been the only one with whom I could share the joy, anger, sorrow, and delight I could never reveal to anyone else.”
Cheongpung looked at Tang Sadok with pity.
“Grandpa Tang, you don’t have any other friends.”
“I did not make any. Being the Family Head of the Tang Clan was that kind of position.”
“So you don’t have any friends.”
“It is not that I had none. I could have made them, but...”
“You didn’t have a single friend. How sad.”
The Divine Physician hurriedly grabbed Tang Sadok by the shoulder.
“Family Head, calm yourself. You’re breathing far too quickly!”
“Huff... Hoo, huff...”
“Take deep, slow breaths. Now, follow me. One, two...”
“Whoooosh...”
After narrowly surviving a bout of high blood pressure, Tang Sadok looked at Cheongpung and spoke.
“But I could entrust Mimi to you...”
Cheongpung covered his mouth with both hands.
“No, Grandpa Tang. I can’t take your only friend away from you.”
“...I haven’t said I would entrust her to you yet.”
“Oh. Ohhh.”
Tang Sadok let out a deep sigh. For a moment, he had undoubtedly wondered whether it was really safe to entrust Mimi-chan to someone like that.
“Yes, you guessed correctly. Since we do not know what will become of our family, I wish to entrust Mimi to you. Temporarily, of course.”
“Yaaay!”
“Did you hear that last part? Temporarily.”
“Yaaay!”
I’ll bet Hyuk Mujin’s right wrist he didn’t hear it.
Cheongpung was beside himself with joy at becoming Mimi’s temporary guardian.
“Don’t worry. I’ll take good care of her!”
“From what I saw last time, Mimi does seem to follow you well. However, she is naturally quite fussy and very wary of strangers, so...”
“Mimi. Whirlwind, then spin around and around and say hello!”
Sssriririk!
“Oh, shit.”
She busted out a new move right here.

An earthquake struck Tang Sadok’s eyes.

No—one more person had just been added.
