“Of course not!
The pressure-sealing system won’t even let you open it, and the aircraft would be damaged by the pressure difference!
You wouldn’t be able to breathe properly either!”
Team Leader Choi fiddled with the ring on his finger and cut in.
“I think I can block the pressure.
I don’t know what you have in mind, but give it a try.”
“Okay.”
“Don’t!
You bangzi bastards!
Are you trying to kill us all?!”
“...What, bangzi?”
How dare he insult Koreans in front of a proud Korean Kimchi Man?
The captain’s face went pale when he realized what had slipped out.
“No, that’s not what I meant.”
“You chink bastard.
Damn it.”
“Hey, Captain!”
“Y-Yes?”
“Should I open it?”
“Ah!
Aah!”
Before the captain could stop me, I opened the door.
No—I cut it open.
Slice!
Force—the phenomenon known as an Aura Blade in the modern world—sliced through the sturdy alloy, creating a small opening.
It was the kind of overwhelming power only a Supreme Peak master could display in Murim, or an S-rank Hunter here.
Team Leader Choi’s eyes widened in shock.
“Mr.
Jin Taekyung, this is...!”
“Team Leader!”
Whoooosh!
This was no time to stand around gawking.
The tremendous wind and pressure had sent the aircraft lurching and thrown the cabin into chaos.
The passengers’ screams and my shout brought Team Leader Choi back to his senses.
He rubbed his ring.
“A flawless barrier surrounds us.
Barrier!”
“Oh.”
Along with the incantation, a transparent mana barrier blocked the new opening without leaving so much as a gap.
So that was one way to do it.
With a brief exclamation of admiration, I stuck my upper body outside the cabin.
Team Leader Choi’s Barrier spell recognized me as an ally and let me pass through without resistance.
Rumble, rumble, rumble!
The wind pressure battered my upper body as if trying to crush me to death.
I grinned.
This is no joke.
But it wasn’t unbearable.
No, it would have been stranger if I couldn’t endure it.
Compared to the waves of energy the Western Heaven Demon Lord had unleashed, this was no more than a gentle spring breeze.
—Kyaoo-o-o-o!
A monster’s shrill cry mingled with that spring breeze.
The pack of Wyverns had already drawn close.
I judged the distance between us.
About a hundred meters.
I’ve never tried this before...but at this distance, it should be enough.
Inventory, open.
Equip.
Sssshk.
A spear I’d bought at a discount from the Hunter Market slid into my hand.
Like a javelin thrower, I drew my shoulder as far back as it would go.
From my waist to my wrist, every necessary muscle and tendon pulled taut like a bowstring.
—Kyaoo!
Sensing something was wrong, the leader Wyvern at the front shrieked and threw back its head.
I could see a mass of pure-white air being sucked toward its snout.
That’s...
—Breath!
It’s using Breath!
Dodge it, wicked human!
The Skeleton Warlord was right.
Of all the countless monsters in existence, Breath was a power granted only to the dragonkin.
I could clearly see it taking shape inside the Wyvern’s gaping maw.
Gooooom.
A gigantic sphere of wind.
The instant the Air Breath, powerful enough to shred metal like paper, fully took shape—
“Hey, Wyvern!”
—Kyaoo?
“I’m putting it in!”
With a thunderous shout, I whipped my drawn-back shoulder forward.
Fwoosh!
Sssshaaa!
Flaming Force enveloped the spearhead, scorching the air and slicing through the wind.
The Wyvern’s bright-yellow eyes widened as the blue-white streak of light shot straight toward it.
—Kiiiiik!
Whoooosh!
Compressed air erupted from the spear’s tip.
A pure-white cloud burst outward, and then—
Crunch!
Boom-boom!
The gigantic body plummeted toward the ground like a kite with its string cut.
—Kyaoo?
—Kiiit?
More than ten pairs of bright-yellow eyes looked at one another.
Wyverns were ferocious from the moment they were born, but right now, they were so bewildered that they had no idea what to do.
—Kikik?
—Kiiik...
What?
Is the boss dead?
I think so...
After exchanging words among themselves, the Wyverns were dumbfounded.
Their leader had been exceptional even among its own kind, powerful enough to earn the name “Black Star.”
And now, the Black Star had become a black dot plummeting toward the distant ground.
—Kiririk?
—Grrrrk.
None of them had even gotten a proper look at how it died.
They could only guess that the tiny human had thrown a spear and struck it.
But that was absurd.
How could a mere human dare to attack a descendant of the great dragon—
“Hey, Green Wyvern!”
—Kik?
“I’m putting it in!”
Crunch!
This time, they saw it clearly.
Their comrade’s head burst apart in the streak of light.
—Kik!
—Kyaoo-o-o!
After their leader, another of their bloodline had died!
The enraged Wyverns swore revenge on that accursed human.
—Kiiit!
Of course, not today.
They would take revenge later.
A little later.
“Hey, Blue Wyvern!”
Crunch!
...Could they actually get their revenge?
More than ten pairs of wings began flapping for dear life.

chapters.title: Chapter 379
paragraphs: Rumble, rumble, rumble!
A tremendous roar shook the air, while vibrations traveled through the ground.
Xiao Shen stared toward the horizon, unable to believe what was happening.
The monsters are supposed to be thousands of kilometers away. How did they...?
The twenty-year-old was not the only one wondering.

More than a thousand Hunters from the Public Security Armed Forces Department and five thousand members of the Chinese People’s Liberation Army had been dispatched to Chengdu International Airport to maintain public order. Every one of them had the same question, and every one of them was stunned by the reality bearing down on them.
—Screeech!
—Graaaar!
From low-level monsters such as goblins and Orcs to higher-tier monsters like Trolls, ogres, and Lycanthropes...
An army of monsters filled the horizon, charging forward with hideous shrieks.
The one-kilometer gap was closing by the second. Panicked cries rang out.
“Form ranks by unit! Assemble! Form up—!”
“Fire! Fire!”
Rat-a-tat-tat! Boom!
The People’s Liberation Army hurriedly formed ranks and unleashed their firepower at their commanders’ orders, but the effect was negligible.
No one had expected an army of monsters to attack.
The soldiers were ordinary people without any special abilities. Fear paralyzed them, and their weapons were effective only against low-level monsters at best.
“There are too many! There are too many monsters!”
“Pilots!”
“Get the fighter jets in the air! Bomb them from above—!”
The commanders’ frantic shouts were drowned out by a ferocious roar from the sky.
—Kyaaaao-o-o!
“W-What is that?”
“Wyvern! It’s a Wyvern!”
A gigantic shape flew toward them with the setting sun at its back.
A Wyvern, known as the terror of the skies, led the charge, followed by dozens of Griffons and Gargoyles.
The A-rank monsters angled their wings, each several meters long, and dove upon the fighter jets that had yet to take off.
Crunch! Boom!
Their powerful wingbeats rocked the several-ton machines, while magical-power-infused claws tore through the aircraft hulls like paper.
Metal fragments blasted outward with tremendous force, mowing down the pilots running frantically toward their planes.
Boom! Crunch!
They died instantly, without even the chance to scream.
The commanders regained their senses and ordered the soldiers to open fire, but even hundreds—thousands—of bullets left no more than scratches on the monsters’ magical-power-infused skin and hides.
—Kikikik.
The monsters laughed at the helpless humans.
A shock of terror swept through the soldiers, making every hair on their bodies stand on end.
“H-How can this be?”
An army of monsters filled the ground and sky. Even firearms barely affected them.
They were monsters in every sense of the word.
“M-Monsters...”
“I-I have to live. I don’t want to die like a dog in a place like this!”
The fear of death spread faster than any epidemic.
As the People’s Liberation Army began backing away, one person strode forward instead.
“Don’t retreat!”
Xiao Shen shouted, his youthful face still not quite rid of its boyishness and his eyes blazing.
The Five-Starred Red Flag, the national flag of the People’s Republic of China, was emblazoned across the chest of his armor.
“Who are we?”
Those who had been about to flee stopped in their tracks at the young man’s question.
Xiao Shen glared at the army of monsters charging from several hundred meters away. His voice thundered once more from beneath his low-pulled helmet.
“Who are we?”
The shout made their blood boil.
With every eye upon him, Xiao Shen raised his spearhead high.
“We are the descendants of Zhonghua! We are brothers of the People’s Liberation Army and the Public Security Armed Forces Department!”
Aura the color of sunset blazed from the spearhead thrust toward the heavens.
Hissss!
“Let’s go! Let’s wipe out every last one of those monsters!”
“Waaaaaaah!”
A tremendous roar numbed the ears and shook the earth.
Led by Xiao Shen, the Hunters of the Public Security Armed Forces Department gripped their weapons and charged the monster army like ferocious tigers.
“Don’t retreat! Show them the strength of Zhonghua!”
“Uaaaaah!”
—Graaaar!
—Awooooo!
Human cries filled with the resolve to face death mingled with the monsters’ shrieks. The two groups collided and became entangled in one mass.
Kwagwagwagwang!
The collision shook heaven and earth. Death rained down from every direction.
“Gyaaaah!”
—Kweeeek!
Squish! Crack!
Screams and thunderous impacts rang out across the battlefield.
An A-rank Hunter’s aura-coated blade sliced through a Lycanthrope’s neck, while a single swing of an ogre’s iron club reduced three or four Hunters to bloody pulp and sent them flying.
Two Hunters combined their strength to bring down a monster. As they raised their weapons against their next foe, a gigantic shadow fell over them.
—Kiiiiiit!
Slice!
A Griffon plunged from the sky, its claws shredding the Hunters’ bodies along with their armor.
As it searched for its next prey, a large ball of fire hurtled toward it.
“Fire Ball!”
Boom!
The Griffon’s body reeled amid the acrid smoke. The ranged units on the ground had been watching for just such an opportunity, and they did not let it pass.
“Now!”
Bang! Boom-boom-boom!
All manner of spells and arrows brimming with mana pierced the Griffon.
It plummeted with a dying shriek, and the other flying monsters let loose ferocious cries.
—Kyaaaao-o-o!
Modern weapons made of lead and iron blocked the flying monsters as they plunged toward the ranged units.
“Concentrated fire!”
Rat-a-tat-tat-tat! Boom!
Countless rifles and heavy weapons opened fire. Dozens of tanks unleashed their cannons at once.
Modern weapons could not compare to mana, the natural counter to a monster’s magical power, but so much concentrated fire still forced the flying monsters to falter.
—Kiiit!
“It’s working!”
“Anywhere else is useless! Aim for their eyes!”
The flesh of monsters, saturated with magical power from birth, easily shrugged off most physical force.
But there was one exception: the eyes.
Covered only by a thin membrane, their eyeballs could be damaged by heavy weapons.
At the sight of the monsters hesitating, the divisional commander who had been watching the battle excitedly waved his command baton.
“More! Pour it on! Pin those monsters down—”
Rooooar!
His voice cut off.
Poison Breath from a Green Wyvern blanketed an area over a hundred meters in radius. The divisional commander and his command staff were drenched in powerful acidic poison and melted away.
“C-Commander!”
“The command staff...!”
The People’s Liberation Army lost hundreds of soldiers and high-ranking officers in the blink of an eye. Panic swept through its ranks.
Officers, noncommissioned officers, and enlisted soldiers alike stared at the horrific scene before them, crying out in shock.
“This can’t be happening...”
“N-No. This isn’t right. It can’t be! This isn’t my mission!”
That scream spoke for all of them.
They had deployed in force as a precaution, but their primary mission was to meet and escort the foreign Hunters arriving at Chengdu International Airport, then follow their superiors’ orders.
No one had said anything about an army of monsters thousands of kilometers away invading the airport.
“What the hell is happening...?”
“We’re going to die. We’re all going to die.”
The fear they had briefly forgotten descended upon the People’s Liberation Army once more.
They were not the Hunters of the Public Security Armed Forces Department fighting at the front. They were only ordinary people carrying modern firearms.
And their ominous suspicion soon became reality.
A nightmare worse than anything they had imagined.
—Om. Neu. Ha. So. Yu.
A voice spoke in broken, disconnected syllables. The eerie sound, like static from a radio with a poor signal, echoed across the battlefield.
Black fog that had gathered from somewhere spread over the people’s heads.
—Yen. Wi. Ga. Ji. Ke!
That was when the horrific change occurred.
Swoooosh!
Dark magical power, black as storm clouds, spread through the blood and corpses like a spiderweb.
It breathed new power and souls into the bodies growing cold, binding and subjugating them with chains.
Crack. Crack-crack-crack.
An army of skeletons slowly rose from pools of death, granted new life.
Those beings bound the countless dead with invisible chains and made them their slaves.
They laughed in satisfaction.
—Kik, kikikik.
—Grrk. Kihihih.
—Grrrrrk.
With a bubbling sound, a man rose to his feet.
Clad in armor emblazoned with the Five-Starred Red Flag and carrying a massive ax, he looked exactly like the A-rank Hunter Xiao Shen remembered.
...Mr. Yao Wei.
But Xiao Shen could not say the man’s name aloud.
He could not bring himself to.
Because he knew that the person standing before him was no longer the man he had known.
Ah... ahhh.

If Xiao Shen had not witnessed his decapitation a little over ten minutes earlier—if the man had not risen with his own severed head tucked under one arm—he would still have thought of him as a colleague and friend.
But Yao Wei no longer existed.
His new name slipped from Xiao Shen’s lips.
“Dullahan...”
A headless knight.
A Dullahan.
Xiao Shen bit his lip at the sight of his former colleague transformed into a high-level undead monster. Something hot ran down his cheek.
“I’m sorry. I truly am.”
—Graaaar!
The Dullahan charged with a shriek.
Xiao Shen shot forward like the wind.
The two of them had often sparred like this. What began as simple competitive pride became a daily routine, and after every bout, Xiao Shen had to endure Yao Wei’s complaints.
You little punk. Where are your manners? Would it kill you to let me win once?
Ha-ha. Let’s go get something to eat. The loser pays, so I guess you’re buying again today, Mr. Yao Wei.
You’ve got plenty of money at home, and you’re still so greedy. One day, I’ll make you buy me a meal.
But that had never happened, and now it never would.
Xiao Shen had always won.
Goodbye. Thank you for everything.
Whoosh! Slice!
The ax cleaved through empty air.
Aura blazed from Xiao Shen’s spearhead and tore through the Dullahan’s torso from the waist. The headless knight slowly crumpled.
Thud. Crash.
Xiao Shen stared down at the face of the fallen Dullahan—no, Yao Wei—and his eyes burned.
“How dare you... How dare you do this...”
Only half a day ago, these friends and colleagues had been laughing and talking with him.
Now they were undead monsters.
The Hunters of the Public Security Armed Forces Department were famous for their strict discipline, but they were not cold-blooded people without a drop of blood in their veins.
They had entered battle prepared to die. Now, for the first time, they faced the fear born of their attachment to one another.
“Get a grip! It’s me, Liu Yinqin! Liu Yinqin!”
“H-Hyung...!”
—Grrrrrk!
Crack! Boom!
Screams and death rained down from every direction.
The Public Security Armed Forces Department had lost nearly half its strength. The monster army, on the other hand, had only grown in number and continued pouring forward without end.
Am I going to die here, like this?
For the first time in his life, Xiao Shen contemplated his own death.
The situation was desperate enough to make even someone as bright and cheerful as him think that way.
We never received a warning signal, so communications are probably down. There won’t be any reinforcements either... This really is the end.
Slice!
Xiao Shen cut down one charging undead monster after another, then laughed hollowly and looked up at the sky.
The sunset was beautiful.
Once the sun went down and darkness came, he would never see a sight like it again.
At least the last sky I see isn’t half bad...
Huh?
Xiao Shen blinked, his thought cut short.
Something enormous was hurtling toward the battlefield from high above.
An airplane?
Roooooar!
A gigantic aircraft wreathed in flames.
Then someone’s shout rang across the vast sky.
“Hey! Monsters!”
Am I hearing things?
Not only Xiao Shen but everyone on the battlefield looked up.
Someone’s voice, carrying an almost palpable madness, rang out like thunder.
“I’m going to ram it!”
Ram what?
Xiao Shen soon understood.
Rumble, rumble, rumble!
The airplane’s enormous fuselage plowed straight across the battlefield.

At least the last sky I see isn’t half bad...
Huh?
Xiao Shen blinked, his thought cut short.
Something enormous was hurtling toward the battlefield from high above.
An airplane?
Roooooar!
A gigantic aircraft wreathed in flames.
Then someone’s shout rang across the vast sky.
“Hey!
Monsters!”
Am I hearing things?
Not only Xiao Shen but everyone on the battlefield looked up.
Someone’s voice, carrying an almost palpable madness, rang out like thunder.
“I’m going to ram it!”
Ram what?
Xiao Shen soon understood.
Rumble, rumble, rumble!
The airplane’s enormous fuselage plowed straight across the battlefield.

chapters.title: Chapter 380
paragraphs: Xiao Shen realized something for the first time.
Roooooar!
The sight of an airplane diving toward the ground with both wings engulfed in flames inspired terror that transcended species.
—Graaaar!
The supposedly ferocious ogres and Trolls screamed.
—Gweeeaaah!
Even the notoriously sluggish Ghouls ran hard enough to work up a sweat on the soles of their feet.
—Squeeeeee!
“Uh, uh, uhhh...”
The monsters capable of screaming were the lucky ones.
Xiao Shen and most of the others could only stand frozen like statues, staring at the airplane hurtling toward the ground.
I have to run...
His hands and feet refused to move.
More importantly, Xiao Shen and the Hunters of the Public Security Armed Forces Department were surrounded in the middle of the battlefield. They had no chance to escape.
Is this really the end?
The same thought crossed everyone’s mind at that moment.
Rumble, rumble, rumble!
With a deafening roar, the airplane’s enormous fuselage swept across the battlefield.
The earth-shaking collision began at the rear of the monster army as it scattered like a swarm of ants.
Crunch! Crack!
The massive steel hulk, weighing dozens of tons, crushed and burst apart everything in its path.
Green monster blood sprayed like fountains, and limbs of every size flew in all directions.
W-What the hell is this...?
No matter how powerful the monsters’ physical defenses were, they had their limits. Nothing could stop the airplane now that it had transformed into a monster blender.
—Graaaar...!
—Kiiiiek!
Krrrunch!
The monsters’ screams vanished beneath the grisly sounds of flesh being torn apart. It was a scene of carnage beyond anything they had ever seen or heard.
As Xiao Shen and the Hunters stared blankly at the unimaginable sight, someone’s frenzied shout pierced their ears.
“Monsters! Ram them! Kill them!”
Even amid all this chaos, they could clearly hear their native language. A single word flashed through the minds of the Public Security Armed Forces Department Hunters.
Reinforcements.
Xiao Shen was stunned.
An incredible powerhouse!
The voice carried tremendous mana. The speaker was unquestionably an S-rank Hunter.
“Go for it! Airplaaaaane!”
And unquestionably a slightly insane S-rank Hunter.
To think he’d resort to a tactic those island bastards used in World War II. Did he not consider that his own allies might die?
He seems to have been sent by the Central Military Commission... But did our country have an S-rank Hunter like that?
The question suddenly occurred to Xiao Shen, but it was about to become irrelevant.
The gigantic steel hulk that had ground its way across half the battlefield was now charging straight toward him and the other Hunters.
—K-Kiiit!
“Run!”
There was no distinction between friend and foe in the struggle to survive.
Forgetting the humans right in front of him, Xiao Shen drove his dagger into a monster that barreled into him.
Schunk!
—Grrrk.
The monster’s lifeless body collapsed toward Xiao Shen.
He could not move a single step with monsters surging in from every direction. As the crushing weight fell upon him, Xiao Shen shouted.
“The battle isn’t over! Fight until the very end!”
He was right. The battle was not over yet. A Hunter was someone who had to kill monsters until the final moment, until their own breath ran out.
The Hunters who heard Xiao Shen’s shout gritted their teeth and swung their weapons.
This will do.
With lightning-fast skill, Xiao Shen buried his dagger in the back of a fleeing ogre’s head, then drew a deep breath.
The airplane’s massive body was already less than twenty meters away.
It had slowed considerably, but with everyone trapped in place, avoiding it seemed impossible.
I have no regrets.
If he died fighting for the people as a proud Hunter of Zhonghua, that was enough.
Xiao Shen closed his eyes as screams rained down from every direction. At that moment, he heard:
“Heave-ho.”
Krrrunch! Splat!
Drenched in a sticky liquid he assumed was blood, Xiao Shen thought:
...Heave-ho?
Wasn’t a person’s dying cry usually more like “Aaaah”?
The strange sound was an odd choice for a dying cry, so Xiao Shen slowly raised his eyelids.
At last, he saw it.
The airplane had stopped dead only a few steps away. Two men stood beside it, chatting casually.
“All right, we’ve arrived. It might explode, so get everyone off quickly.”
“...Mr. Jin Taekyung. They’re all unconscious.”
“Really? How weak.”
“...They would have died if not for the Barrier magic.”
“Then carry them out, Team Leader Choi. Oh, right. Is that bastard who called us bangzi earlier alive, too?”
“Yes. He’s... alive, at least.”
“Then keep a close eye on that bastard. I’ll keep giving him hell for it when we head back.”
“...I’ll do my best.”
Xiao Shen could not make sense of the situation at all.
Who, when, where, what, why, and how—this bizarre sight defied even the five Ws and one H.
How did the airplane suddenly stop, and who are those people? Weren’t they Hunters sent by the Central Military Commission?
The two men were even speaking in another language.
Xiao Shen could not understand the words of the clean-cut man who looked like a young master, but he knew what country the language belonged to.
It belonged to Korea, their longtime neighbor.
Wait. If they’re Korean...!
Xiao Shen hurriedly wiped the blood from around his eyes. Only then did he recognize one of the men.
A muscular young man who stood a full head taller than everyone else.
The man Xiao Shen had only ever seen on television—his idol—was standing right in front of him.
“C-Could you possibly be Mr. Jin from Korea?”
“Huh?”
The young man, Jin Taekyung, tilted his head as he looked at Xiao Shen.
“I’m not a teacher.”
“Then... Lord Fuck...”
“...Fuck. What?”
It really is him!
Relief and hope washed over Xiao Shen, making his entire body tremble.
How the hell does a Chinese guy know about Lord Fuck?
Articles about me had caused a brief stir in the foreign media, but I never expected even that nickname to spread this far.
Lord Fuck, making the five oceans and six continents tremble.
If I ever went to the United States, some huge Yankee bros might walk up to me holding beer bottles and act like they knew me.
Hey, you. Lord Fuck?
I’m fine, thank you. Fuck. What kind of deranged bastards came up with a nickname like this?
Anyway...
“What a mess.”
That was my brief assessment as I looked around.
Team Leader Choi, who had strung the unconscious flight attendants together like dried fish, and the Skeleton Warlord, whom I had shoved into my Inventory, both answered me.
“It is a horrifying sight.”
—You wicked human. This commander rather likes this place. It feels familiar and comforting.
The fact that a named undead monster—death itself, for all intents and purposes—found the sight pleasing said more than enough.
“We get thrown into actual combat the moment we arrive.”
As if responding to my complaint, a System notification rang.
Ding.
System —An unexpected Quest, Unexpected Attack, has been generated.
Was this why they said they were paying so much?
I clicked my tongue and spoke.
“Team Leader Choi, protect the civilians first. After that, fight as you see fit. Don’t push yourself too hard.”
“Yes. That was already my intention.”
Team Leader Choi was a smart man. Learning the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique had made him incomparably stronger than before, but he would never show off.
“And you there, young man.”
“Y-Yes, Mr. Jin.”
Mr. Jin? What am I, a schoolteacher?
I looked the young man who had answered so quickly up and down.

His face was young, but he was obviously a Hunter. A powerful one, too—probably around A-rank. Unlike the surrounding Hunters, who all wore identical armor as if they had come off a factory line, he also had a red insignia on his shoulder.
“You look like you hold a pretty significant rank, so take good care of your men. Let’s save even one more person.”
“Y-Yes?”
“This is only the beginning.”
As I answered, I thrust out my fist.
Boom!
Streams of Scorching Yang Qi shot toward the monsters standing blankly in place.
Searing heat swept through the area, leaving behind dozens of monster corpses.
“Why are you all staring? Did someone hit the pause button?”
At my single remark, the silence pressing down on the battlefield shattered.
—Graaaar!
“K-Kill them! Stop the monsters!”
Humans against monsters. Monsters against humans.
The battle to kill or be killed began anew. I pulled White Flame from where it was embedded deep in the ground and swung it.
Shing!
Forget half water, half fish. Monsters packed every inch of the battlefield.
A crescent of Force extending from the spearhead brushed against a tightly packed cluster of monsters.
Ding.
System —Defeated Lv. 15 Undead Goblin! —Defeated Lv. 78 Undead Lycanthrope! —Defeated Lv. 93 Dullahan! —Defeated Lv. 30 Skeleton! —... —... —There is a large Level gap. You gained negligible EXP!
System notifications announcing monster kills and EXP gains rang out without pause.
Under normal circumstances, I would have let them go in one ear and out the other or simply ignored them.
But this time, they provided an important clue.
“Don’t tell me these things are...”
—Ah, that’s right. Wicked human! What a powerful undead army!
The Skeleton Warlord’s delighted shout was enough to turn my suspicion into certainty.
No wonder something felt strange.
I had already been puzzled by the fact that I could not sense any life force from them.
There were still quite a few living monsters, but more than half were undead. Altogether, they formed a massive army nearly two thousand strong.
“And undead monsters are...”
The Skeleton Warlord shouted, brimming with excitement.
—Beautiful! Magnificent! Heroic!
Thwack!
I cut down five monsters and muttered.
“Want to be erased like that thing just now? Beautifully, magnificently, and heroically?”
—...I misspoke. I apologize, wicked human.
The Skeleton Warlord, who had briefly forgotten its situation, hurriedly added:
—Wait. If that is the case, then they must be under someone’s control!
I thought so, too.
There was only one thing I was not certain about.
“The Lich. Did that bastard come here in person?”
—Hmm. If you mean the Lich from that holographic video you showed me last time, then probably not.
As I listened to the Skeleton Warlord’s answer, I took half a step forward.
Boom!
A massive iron club passed within inches of my shoulder and smashed into the ground. It was an ordinary ogre, still carrying the vitality of a living creature.
—Graaaar!
“Sure. I’ll grill you.”
Boom!
The Flame Divine Palm struck the ogre in the chest, sending dark green blood spurting from its seven apertures.
I passed its collapsing bulk and brought White Flame down at an angle.
Shiiiiing! Slice!
Space itself split apart, and the monsters caught within it were chopped to pieces.
Leaving behind the Chinese Hunter who stared blankly at me while covered in blood and bodily fluids, I clenched my fist.
Whoooom.
Extreme heat surged into my fist, then blasted forward.
Boom!
Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist.
A massive pillar of fire swallowed the monsters.
The ones that somehow survived shrieked in agony amid the foul stench of burning flesh.
The destructive power made monsters and Hunters alike forget to fight for a moment.
The Skeleton Warlord spoke in a faltering voice.
—W-Wicked human. You have become even more of a monster.
“It feels strange hearing that from a monster. Anyway, if it wasn’t the Lich, then what kind of bastard is causing all this?”
—How should this commander know? But I can guarantee you one thing.
“Guarantee what?”
—His control over the undead is a notch below mine. Wahaha! Legion! This commander has missed you!
Should I kill this bastard or let him live?
As I considered the question, an idea suddenly flashed through my mind, and I stopped dead.
“Hey. What did you just say?”
—Wahahaha! Have you finally felt the majesty of this commander, wicked human?
“Talk, or be erased.”
—...I will talk. But what are you asking about?
“That part about controlling the undead.”
—Isn’t it obvious? This commander is a Skeleton Warlord. Compared to them, of course I’m... Huh?
A brief silence followed.
The Skeleton Warlord must have reached the same conclusion I had. I swallowed hard and broached the subject casually.
“Try it. That thing you do.”
“Do it, or be erased.”
The Skeleton Warlord opened its mouth.
—Grow, grow, skeletons, skeletons...
At that moment, the undead monsters locked in fierce battle suddenly froze in place.
...It works.

chapters.title: Chapter 381
paragraphs: Whoooosh.
I couldn’t see it, but I could feel it.
Centered on me—or rather, flowing from the Skeleton Warlord inside the subspace known as my Inventory—a sticky energy spread in every direction.
The change was immediate.
—Kirik?
—Gwoo?
The ferocious monsters abruptly stopped moving.
Orcs, Trolls, goblins, Lycanthropes, every kind of monster I had only ever seen in monster encyclopedias, and even fallen Hunters.
They had only one thing in common: they had already died once and been resurrected as undead.
Gulp.
I swallowed dryly and muttered, “It works.”
—Wow. It really works.
Wait. What did he just say?
My brain froze for a moment. Then I whispered, “What kind of dog-bone bullshit is that? Didn’t you try it because you knew it would work?”
The Skeleton Warlord answered hesitantly.
—The truth is... even this commander did not expect it to work so easily.
“You said your control was much stronger.”
—Ah, that? I just said it in the heat of the moment.
“What?”
—My pride would not allow me to sit around doing nothing...
Isn’t this guy completely insane?
I was dumbfounded, but regardless, the result was undeniable.
The undead monsters within a radius of several dozen meters had all stopped moving at once, bringing the fierce battle raging around us to a temporary lull.
“T-The monsters have stopped moving!”
“What in the world is going on?”
“Don’t let your guard down! Some of them are still moving!”
Just as someone shouted, it was still too early to relax.
Only some of the nearby undead monsters had come under the Skeleton Warlord’s control. Those farther away, along with the ordinary monsters that were not undead, were unaffected.
—Gwoooooar!
—Chiiik!
“Haaah!”
Clang! Stab!
The uncontrolled monsters were briefly bewildered by the sudden change in their own kind, but they soon began rampaging again, and the battle resumed.
The two sides were hopelessly mismatched in numbers.
But from this moment onward, that was about to change.
I called out in a deliberately hushed voice.
“Go, Warlordmon!”
Warlordmon—no, the Skeleton Warlord—shouted back in outrage.
—Wicked human! Do not call this commander that!
“How about Warlordmon Who’s Desperate to Be Erased?”
—...Damn it.
Despite being a skeleton that couldn’t even breathe, he let out a deep sigh before chanting a spell.
—Fight, Skeleton Skeleton.
That bastard had definitely started enjoying the whole Skeleton Skeleton thing. It was hardly an impressive incantation, but its effect was undeniable.
—Gwoo?
At the Skeleton Warlord’s command, ferocity filled the eyes of the undead monsters that had been standing blankly. Then, in the next moment—
Crunch!
An undead ogre’s iron club crushed a Troll’s skull.
That was only the beginning.
The undead monsters who had gained a new master charged at their own kind.
—Gwoooooar!
—Ch-Chirik?
Crack! Slice! Stab-stab-stab!
An unexpected ambush from behind.
One flank of the monster army surrounding the Chinese Hunters collapsed helplessly.
—Chiiiiiik!
“W-What the hell!”
“Why are those monsters suddenly...?”
The monsters betrayed by their own kind were not the only ones thrown into confusion.
The Chinese Hunters were just as bewildered by the sudden turn of events.
I shouted to the young Hunter who had been racing across the front lines, swinging his spear.
“Xiao Shen!”
“M-Mr. Jin?”
His eyes widened as he looked at me.
“H-How do you know my name?”
I had just used Qi Sense to check his Level window, but that wasn’t important right now.
“What are you doing? Why aren’t you switching to an all-out offensive?”
“But what is going on here...?”
“Are you really curious about that right now? Do you want to grab an undead monster and make it explain why it’s helping us using the five Ws and one H?”
“N-No, sir!”
“Then what should you be doing?”
Xiao Shen snapped to his senses and thrust his spear into the air.
“Attack formation! Everyone in the Public Security Armed Forces Department, from this moment on, attack everything except the undead monsters!”
“Yes, sir!”
Now that was an excellent decision.
Along with their unified shout, the momentum of the roughly five hundred Hunters who had been driven into a corner changed.
“Kill them!”
“Avenge our fallen comrades!”
Shish-shish-shishik! Slice!
—Awooooo!
A Lycanthrope charged at a Hunter who had just beheaded an Orc.
Its jaws opened, yellow fangs poised to tear out the Hunter’s throat, but a massive fist slammed into its mouth.
Crunch!
—Gwoooooar!
The ogre that had crushed the Lycanthrope’s skull let out a savage roar.
High above the ogre, a Griffon plunged into a steep dive, its razor-sharp claws flashing.
—Kiiiieeeek!
Just as the A-rank monster’s mana-infused claws were about to rake across the ogre’s eyes—
“Ice Ball!”
“Lightning Bolt!”
The ranged Hunters waiting nearby unleashed their magic. The electrocuted Griffon convulsed in midair.
At that moment, a figure stepped off a Troll’s shoulder, launched himself into the air, and swung his weapon at the Griffon.
“Custom-made by J Company, widely considered one of Germany’s finest weapon manufacturers—!”
Slice!
A single clean, effortless strike split the Griffon’s head in two.
Team Leader Choi landed gracefully and gazed at the transparent blade, not a single drop of blood staining it, with a satisfied smile.
“A longsword I won at auction for 5.2 billion won. It certainly earns its price.”
It looks stupid, but it’s cool.
It’s cool, but it looks stupid.
After watching the whole thing, the Skeleton Warlord asked dubiously,
—Wicked human, did you say that man was your superior?
“No, well... Technically, as far as our Guild positions go, he is, but...”
—He seemed reasonably clever for a human, yet I have never encountered anyone so strange. He truly is a fitting superior for you.
“Raise your hand if you’re a Skeleton Warlord who wants to be erased for running his mouth.”
After a brief silence, the Skeleton Warlord answered by chanting another spell.
—Grow, Skeleton Skeleton!
They say even a dog at a village school can recite poetry after three years. Now he could do it without being told.
Crack. Crack-crack-crack.
The Griffon killed by Team Leader Choi, along with the monsters brought down by the combined attacks of the Hunters and undead, gained new life and rose from their dead bodies.
There were two hundred of them.
The range also seemed wider than during the first attempt. Even distant undead monsters came under the Skeleton Warlord’s control and began attacking their former allies.
“Wow. You were capable of this?”
—Wow. Was this commander capable of this?
—...Actually, this commander was not capable of quite this much. But for some reason, an enormous amount of mana is surging through me now that I am here!
“Sure. Great.”
I gave up trying to understand this bizarre named monster.
As long as the result was good, that was all that mattered. Trying to figure it out right now would only give me a headache.
—Give me more. More legions!
I couldn’t see him because he was inside my Inventory, but I was certain his fleshless skull was trembling with excitement.
I sighed and tightened my grip on my spear.
“I was already planning to.”
—Do you have a way?
“I do.”
The method for increasing the number of undead was simple.
“Kill them all.”
—Kahaha! You truly are a wicked and ignorant human!
The bastard was getting cheeky, but this time, I had to agree with at least part of what he said.

Flamefire Path.
Whoooosh!
A path of flame opened with every step.
Black robes. Staffs hung with dangling skulls.
Their eye sockets were empty, and patches of unrotted flesh still clung to their bodies.
The three beings, each looking as though it had stepped straight out of a nightmare, sent their thoughts to one another.
—There is a problem.
—The undead monsters are slipping out of our control. They are helping the humans and attacking the legion.
—Why?
They were not asking how their control had been broken. The three beings already knew the answer to that question.
—A higher undead. One more powerful than us.
All monsters had a hierarchy, but the undead were ruled by strength more absolutely than any other kind.
If their control had been stolen, it could only be the work of a higher existence.
—But...
—How is that possible?
None of the three beings could answer.
How could an existence more powerful than them be here, seizing control of the undead and helping the humans?
—Could it be that person?
—Absurd. Have you forgotten the command that person gave us when sending us here?
—Kill the humans. Create more undead and a greater legion, then kill more. More humans.
Recalling their command, the three beings fell into confusion.
If that person—the Arch Lich—was not responsible, then who could possibly possess greater control than they did?
—Was there a necromancer among the humans?
—I sensed nothing.
—Humans reject and despise death. That cannot be. Even if one were among them, they would be nothing compared to us.
Unmistakable hostility permeated their thoughts because they, too, had once been necromancers who suffered humanity’s rejection and contempt.
But that had happened in the distant past, in another dimension.
Drifting across the boundless ocean of death, they had met a boatman named the Arch Lich. After gaining new power, they were finally on the verge of becoming the Liches they had longed to be.
But...
—What a shame.
—If only our transformation had been completed. If only there had been more death in this land.
—Then we would not have lost control, either.
The three beings could not hide their regret.
They had been great necromancers while alive, but they had yet to complete their transformation into Liches.
They had been reborn in the bodies of dead mages, but one week was far too short to absorb enough death energy to become full-fledged Liches.
—That is why that person sent all three of us.
—If this mission fails, that person will be disappointed.
—That person might even take back the power they gave us.
That was what the three beings feared most.
If they wanted to earn the Arch Lich’s favor, they had to overcome this crisis somehow.
Even if it meant expending a tremendous amount of power.
—There is no other choice.
—Are you suggesting we combine our strength?
—Yes. If the three of us combine our strength, even an unidentified higher undead will no longer be able to steal control from us.
—Hmm. Fine.
—Do you agree?
—I agree.
The three beings, who had been competing for the Arch Lich’s favor, finally reached an agreement.
Without hesitation, they began chanting necromantic spells.
—Valencia. Madrid.
—Bayern. Munich.
—Stoke. City.
The energy of death flowing from the three beings spread through the air.
The green grass turned black, and the soldiers of the People’s Liberation Army within range clutched their throats and collapsed.
“Ghk!”
“Guhhh!”
Whoooosh.
As the humans breathed their last, death energy flowed from their bodies and seeped into every part of the monsters.
—Kyaaaaaaah!
—Gwoooooar!
The air trembled with the powerful mana carried in their savage cries. Their strength was beyond comparison with that of ordinary monsters.
Only after sensing their strengthened control and the greater power of the monsters under their command did the three beings stop chanting.
—Kikikikik.
—Success.
—We consumed an enormous amount of power... but this is more than enough.
Just as the three beings smiled in satisfaction at their newly empowered legion—
Boom!
Far away, a monster’s limbs flew through the air amid a thunderous explosion.
The three beings watched the flames rise and exchanged thoughts.
—There appears to be a flame mage. Not bad.
—He is still only human. Deploy the Skeleton Mages in force.
—Good idea.
A short while later, flames erupted again, and the three beings looked at one another.
—What was that just now?
—Our control was severed. It was not stolen.
—He erased them? Impressive.
—But is he truly a mage? His movements seem far too fast...
—Let us deploy the ogre unit.
—I’ll see your ogres and raise you Dullahans.
—Dullahans, too? Then who will protect us?
—He is right. Dullahans would be excessive. The strengthened ogres will be enough.
—That is true.
Three minutes later, a grim atmosphere hung over the three beings’ skulls.
—It was severed.
—Again?
—I told you we should send the Dullahans.
—What is that thing? It does not seem to be a mage.
—J-Just send the Dullahans first!
—Th-Then we shall do so.
The three beings watched as the more than twenty Dullahans assigned as their escort force rushed away. Then they quietly began searching for another point of agreement.
—Hmm. It is unlikely that such a thing will happen, but just in case...
—I had a similar thought.
—Should we create a Death Knight?
—We have already consumed too much power. A Death Knight, too? We do not have suitable materials, and it would take a long time.
—Given the urgency, we can simply choose the most useful one available. If the three of us combine our strength, it will be possible.
—Th-Then should we try?
But the three beings’ plan to create a Death Knight was shattered less than ten minutes later.
Whoosh! Boom!
Even with bodies reduced to little more than bone, they could feel the searing heat.
“Fucking bastards. There’s a shitload of them.”
Crunch!
The three beings watched a figure tear through the monster army with a spear engulfed in hellfire and hurriedly began chanting spells.
Their once slow, dragging voices became as fast as rap.
—Omnehasoyu!
—Yenwigajike!
But before they could complete their spells, the young human—impossible to identify as either a flame mage or a warrior—had already arrived right in front of them.
“Oh, nice to meet you.”
—O-Omnehasoyu!
—Y-Yes, Yenwigajike!
The young man, Jin Taekyung, cocked his head.
“Hello. Entertainment Weekly? Are you idiots?”

chapters.title: Chapter 382
paragraphs: Strike the head, and the body falls.

Once I captured the three who appeared to be the leaders, the undead under their control stopped moving like wind-up dolls. Deprived of its commanders, the monster army scattered. Some were killed, while others fled.
“Arch Lich?”
At my question, the three kneeling figures nodded.
I wasn’t sure whether things that were already dead and reduced to bones could still be called “guys,” but whatever.
I stroked each of the three skulls in turn and continued.
“When someone talks to you, you’re supposed to answer. Are you putting on airs just because you’re dead?”
They answered before I had even finished speaking.
—Yes. Yes. It is an Arch Lich.
—What you heard was correct, honored human.
—Indeed.
“Hmm. An Arch Lich. That’s a monster I’ve never heard of before... But which one of you answered informally at the end?”
—That one!
—How dare he speak so casually to the great human!
Whip! Whip!
Two bony fingers pointed at the third.
His companions’ lightning-fast betrayal left the accused skull trembling.
—No! This is a despicable false accusation!
“...Doesn’t sound like a false accusation to me.”
If he was going to lie, he could at least change the way he talked.
After glancing around, I pulled that out of my Inventory.
“Bones. Snack time.”
It was a skull with a strange black sheen, flames flickering in its empty eye sockets.
—...Bones? If you insist on giving me a nickname, call me Warlordmon like before.
“Why? You’re a skeleton, so Bones. It fits perfectly.”
—How dare you insult this commander!
“Fine. Forget it, then.”
Just as I was about to put it back in my Inventory, the Skeleton Warlord shouted indignantly.
—Thank you for the meal!
“What an honest little guy.”
Honest children deserved rewards. Liars deserved punishment.
“All right. Have a taste.”
—Thank you, slightly less wicked human. But how much may I eat...?
“Just a little, like before.”
—Hmm. I would like more, but very well.
Even snacks were too much if you gave them out too often. After expressing its slight disappointment, the Skeleton Warlord opened its jaws wide toward the trembling figure.
—Come here.
—E-Eek! No!
—Yes!
The change began with the Skeleton Warlord’s decisive shout.
Whoooosh!
That was still amazing, even after seeing it once before.
Black mist poured from the kneeling figure’s body and streamed into the Skeleton Warlord as though being sucked up by a vacuum cleaner.
—Gaaaaah!
And that wasn’t the only change.
As more of the black mist—the substance the Skeleton Warlord called death energy—flowed out, the figure’s complexion grew steadily paler.
Or rather, its bones did.
Meanwhile, the Skeleton Warlord’s black sheen grew deeper and richer.
—S-Stop!
—Heh heh heh. What delicious death energy.
—Nooo!
—This commander shall take it all. Deeeath energy!
Crack!
—Hrk!
“Cut the ‘deeeath energy’ crap. Where did you even learn something like that?”
—...Are you really in a position to say that?
“Anyway, stop eating.”
—Why?!
“You’ll get fat.”
The Skeleton Warlord was momentarily lost for words. I tucked it inside my clothes and looked at its victim.

When I had first seen the creature, its bones had been dark and grimy. Now, half of its skeleton had turned white. Perhaps because so much of its death energy had been drained, the green flames in its eye sockets flickered unsteadily.
—Hrk... H-Hrk...
At the sight of their weakened companion, sucked dry to the bone, the other two anxiously clacked their teeth.
—Ask anything of us, great ruler of flame.
—Please, I beg of you. Accept the loyalty of this insignificant being, Orpheus von Maximus Valencia Bayern.
“...You’re undead, not a bidet.”
They must have been desperate not to lose their power. Not that I minded them being so cooperative.
“All right. If there’s anything you haven’t told me yet, scrape the bottom of the barrel and spill every last bit of it. If you feed me so much as one lie...”
—We will tell you everything!
—Please, I beg of you! Grant this false and insignificant being permission to speak the truth!
—I-I’ll talk.
Apparently unwilling to become bone broth, all three skeletons threw themselves enthusiastically into the interrogation.
They told me everything that had happened, from the Arch Lich’s first appearance a week ago to the events of today. Once they had finished, I frowned for effect.
“You’re sure?”
—Yes, great human!
—I swear upon the River of Death!
—N-Not a single word was false.
As all three skulls nodded furiously, the Skeleton Warlord cut in.
—They speak the truth.
“Did they pay you off? How can you guarantee that?”
—They swore upon the River of Death. For beings such as us, that is an absolute vow. It can never be broken.
“Hmm.”
The guy was usually as frivolous as dust in the wind. Hearing it speak with such gravity made me think it probably wasn’t lying.
Besides, the three of them had no reason to scheme in a situation like this.
“All right. I believe you.”
—Thank you! Thank you so much!
—Hrk, hrk! I shall serve you with all my heart, my king!
—I-I mean, I too shall swear loyalty to you, honored human. I swear upon the River of Death that I will never again commit such an act—
Crunch!
The last skeleton faltered before it could finish.
His trembling green eye light shifted back and forth between the fist embedded in his chest and me.
—W-Why?
“What do you mean, why?”
—I-I, loyalty, swear, River of Death...
“Too late.”
A voice so cold it hardly sounded like mine slipped between my lips.
“It’s too late to undo what you’ve done.”
Countless people had died here today.
Even regular troops armed with firearms and Hunters had been unable to stop them, so there was no telling how many civilians the monster army had killed over the past week.
“I don’t need your loyalty. Especially not from bastards like you.”
The moment I released the Scorching Yang Qi I had drawn up from my dantian—
Whoosh!
Extreme Yang energy erupted from the fist lodged between its shattered ribs. Blue-white Force radiating unimaginable heat coiled around its entire body.
Rooooar!
I watched the green flames in its eye sockets flicker like candles in the wind, then go out.
I also saw the other two figures spring to their feet and begin chanting spells.
—Jazuchawa Umbado...!
—Vargan Mahra...!
Whoooom.
A wind of magical power swirled around them. Just as their sinister spell was about to be completed, I casually said,
“Devour them. Both of them.”
As though it had been waiting for those very words, the Skeleton Warlord sprang from between the folds of my clothes and opened its jaws wide.
—Gladly.
—Varsaba... Eek!
—N-No!
The monsters screamed in a final, desperate bid to live—or rather, to continue existing as undead.
Their wishes meant nothing. The Skeleton Warlord’s pull was stronger and faster than ever.
Whoooosh! Gulp!
The Skeleton Warlord swallowed an enormous quantity of death energy in a single bite, and its skull shuddered.
A moment later, the two skeletons, completely drained of energy, collapsed into piles of bone.
Ding. Ding. Ding.

System —You have successfully completed the unexpected Quest, Unexpected Attack! —You have caused the monster army to collapse! This is truly an outstanding achievement! —As a Quest Reward, you have acquired the Title Undead Hunter! —You have acquired a considerable amount of EXP and Fame! —Level Up!
Only once?
In the past, I would have leveled up several times without difficulty. But now that I had reached Level 120, it seemed the amount of EXP I needed had increased.
Not that I did it for the EXP.
I had merely done what needed to be done, but I couldn’t help feeling a little disappointed.
After all, the stronger I became, the more useful I would be in the battles ahead.
The same goes for that guy.
I looked at the Skeleton Warlord while thinking to myself.
Thanks to the enormous amount of death energy it had absorbed, the power emanating from it was on a completely different level from when we had first met.
—Hmm. Hoooo...
Black mist billowed through the holes in its skull where its nose, ears, and eyes should have been.
Its violet eye flames burned like torches, and its smooth surface gleamed with a deep black luster. A moment later, its crazed laughter thundered through my head.
—Kaha! Kahahahaha!
“Turn down the volume. You’re loud.”
—Wicked human. This time, this commander offers you his profound gratitude.
“You should. Who do you think fed you?”
—Fed me?! Are you implying that this body is some sort of pet?!
“Close enough. Isn’t it?”
—Don’t be absurd!
“Oh? Bones, come here.”
I held out my hand. The skull immediately sprang into the air and landed in my palm.
As a reward, I gently scratched it between the eyes.
“Good boy, Bones. Aren’t you adorable?”
The skull trembled.
—H-How could this happen?! How could this commander be treated like this by a mere human?!
“You say no with your mouth, but your body is honest.”
—I am the master of the Black Forest and the commander of the great undead army. Do not humiliate this body!
“A commander who’s nothing but a head?”
—What?! This paltry body can be restored whenever I wish, so long as I expend enough death energy!
“Really? Then why haven’t you restored it yet?”
—...Because even if I did, some lunatic human would just smash it again.
“Oh, correct.”
The toothless Skeleton Warlord ground its jawbones together, its eye flames narrowing.
—Why, wicked human?
“Why what?”
—There must be some ulterior motive behind feeding me—no, behind granting me such immense power. You clearly have some dark scheme in mind. Tell me the truth!
I thought for a moment before answering.
“Hmm. Because you’re a fucking scrub.”
—What?
“You can’t beat me anyway. If I’m going to keep a scrub around, it might as well be a stronger, more useful one. That’ll make you easier to put to work. Don’t you agree?”
“All right. Get back inside. People are coming.”
I put the Skeleton Warlord, frozen in shock, back into my Inventory and stood.
The airport duty-free corridor would normally have been crowded with employees and passengers. Now it was empty and dark, and three people were walking toward me.
Two of them were familiar.
“Mr. Jin Taekyung.”
“Mr. Jin.”
They were Team Leader Choi, who looked relatively unscathed, and Xiao Shen, an A-rank Hunter from China’s Public Security Armed Forces Department.
A fair amount of time had passed since the battle ended, but Xiao Shen was still covered in blood and dust, his face haggard with exhaustion.
“There you are.”
I exchanged a look of greeting with Team Leader Choi before making an excuse.
“Yes. I had something to take care of.”
“Please speak casually with me. Fuc—no, Mr. Jin, you are the hero who saved me, my comrades, and even the people of Zhonghua.”
Was that my imagination, or had he almost called me Lord Fuck just now?
Whether he knew what I was thinking or not, Xiao Shen continued in an extremely respectful tone.
“Fortunately, with the help of the two gentlemen from the Peace Guild, we were able to defeat the monsters. I would like to take this opportunity to thank you once again.”
“Oh, sure. It was nothing. I only did what anyone should have.”
I waved my hands modestly and stole a glance at Team Leader Choi.

I had been worried the Integrated Language Pack might malfunction and make him notice something strange. But since I was currently speaking with Xiao Shen, it seemed Team Leader Choi was hearing my words in Chinese as well.
“But who is the gentleman beside you...?”
He was the only unfamiliar face among the three.
The gray-haired, middle-aged man who had been silently listening to our conversation extended his hand.
“I am Wei Fenghu, Minister of National Defense under the Central Military Commission. It is a pleasure to meet you, Mr. Jin.”
“Minister of National Defense...”
“My rank is general.”
“Ah.”
I understood that he was a big deal, but I had no idea what that rank actually meant.
Perhaps he had read my thoughts, because Team Leader Choi whispered from beside me in a voice barely louder than an ant.
“Four-star. Four-star.”
“Ah. Ahhh! You’re a general! It’s a pleasure to meet you!”
I had been a four-star once, too. That game I played as a kid had been a lot of fun. The sequel had bombed spectacularly, though.
Wei Fenghu clasped my hand, a faint smile touching his lips.
“You are full of youthful vigor. I have many things I would like to ask you, but shall we talk while we walk?”
“Sure.”
I started after Wei Fenghu, then paused.
“Where are we going?”
“To the operations headquarters. I have a jet waiting.”
“What? Headquarters? A jet?”
“That is correct. Everyone is waiting for you there, Mr. Jin.”
Everyone? Who?

chapters.title: Chapter 383
paragraphs: The jet Wei Fenghu had prepared looked nothing like what I had imagined.
It’s spacious. And fancy.
Through the partly open cabin door, I could see a luxurious table and one of those so-called chairman’s chairs.
Team Leader Choi, who was standing beside me, informed us that the business jet we were looking at cost nearly one hundred billion won per plane, then added,
“I never expected to see an aircraft reserved for state guests here.”
“That is only natural. The two of you are state guests of our country.”
“Ah.”
“Thanks to you, we were able to save countless soldiers and Hunters. None of us—not even me—will ever forget the help you gave us today.”
“...Ah, yes.”
I would have preferred it if they dealt with the fine dust and historical distortions first.
Still, I boarded the jet, privately hoping China was a more conscientious country than I gave it credit for.
The waiting pilot saluted us—or, more precisely, Wei Fenghu—with crisp, disciplined movements.
“You have arrived, Comrade Minister of National Defense.”
“Are we ready?”
“This aircraft and all its escorts are ready. We await your order.”
I wondered what he meant by “escorts,” but then I looked through the window and saw five sleek fighter jets on the runway, their lights blinking as though signaling us.
What the hell are those?
I’d only ever seen things like that in war movies. Were we flying off to fight a battle or something?
Wei Fenghu saw my eyes widen and explained.

“The details have not yet been made public...but as you know, Sichuan Province is currently in a state of war. Magical interference has disrupted communications, and attacks by flying monsters are frequent. An escort is essential for our safety.”
“Is that really true?”
The situation was more serious than I’d thought.
The Wyvern had only attacked us in passing while raiding Chengdu International Airport. But if the same thing was happening throughout Sichuan Province, that changed everything.
“I wish I were lying.”
Perhaps merely thinking about the current situation exhausted him. Wei Fenghu, who seemed to have aged considerably in a short time, leaned back into the soft seat.
“It seems we must part ways here. We will meet again soon, Senior Colonel Xiao Shen.”
Unlike us, Xiao Shen had not boarded the aircraft. He stood rigidly at attention and saluted.
“Yes, Comrade Minister of National Defense. I will complete my mission as quickly as possible and rejoin you. And, gentlemen...”
“Good. I expect great things from you.”
Perhaps because he had achieved such impressive accomplishments, a pleased smile passed across Wei Fenghu’s lips as he looked at the promising young Hunter.
Team Leader Choi gave him a polite bow. I waved.
“See you next time. You fought really well today.”
It was only one sentence.
But the moment Xiao Shen heard my words, his eyes grew as wide as serving trays. His body trembled as though he had been electrocuted, and then he shouted at the top of his lungs.
“Th-Thank you! I will devote myself to every task with the utmost loyalty, so that I never disappoint you, Mr. Jin!”
“...You don’t need to go that far.”
“May your august self remain safe! Loooyalty!”
“‘August self’? What are you—”
Whack!
“Urk!”
That looked like a textbook example of poor judgment.
He’d saluted so hard that the edge of his hand struck him in the eyebrow.
As I stared dumbfounded at Xiao Shen clenching his teeth against the pain, the cabin door closed and our business jet began to take off.
“That guy is, well... How should I put it? He’s quite a character.”
Wei Fenghu gave a quiet laugh at my awkward observation.
“Can you blame him? His idol praised him.”
“Excuse me?”
“Many young Hunters in our country admire you, Mr. Jin. He is no exception.”
What the hell? Was I a Korean Wave star?
Come to think of it, for a four-star general with enough power to make birds fall from the sky, Wei Fenghu seemed unusually attentive to his subordinates.
Or maybe Xiao Shen was simply that promising.
Ah, but...
—Team Leader. How important is the Minister of National Defense under the Central Military Commission, exactly? I’m not very familiar with the structure over here.
Team Leader Choi flinched at my Sound Transmission, then replied through Message Magic.
—If you compare it to our country, he is the Minister of National Defense. Of course, this is China, and Wei Fenghu is the current Chairman’s right-hand man, so his power is considerably greater.
—Ah.
So he’s a lot like me. I’m the Minister of gukbap.
One special serving of sundae-guk was enough to handle three bowls of rice.
Of course, Wei Fenghu could probably erase three cities with a single pointed finger.
And now, that powerful figure of the People’s Republic of China was leaning his upper body toward us and asking,
“It seems we have much to discuss during the flight. Would you not agree?”
Team Leader Choi and I nodded solemnly and opened our mouths.
“Of course. First, I would like to ask what exactly is happening in Sichuan—”
“But do you happen to have any boiled eggs and soda? I’m hungry after fighting so hard.”
Apparently, they didn’t.
“We do.”
They actually did.
The People’s Republic of China.
As its formal name suggested, the people of this vast and imposing nation still adhered to socialism as their national ideology.

About twenty years ago, the Chairman at the time—who had cemented the foundations of his dictatorship by securing lifelong rule—died during the Great Cataclysm. Power then passed to a far more moderate administration, but the substance of the system remained unchanged.
—What was the dead Chairman’s name again? Pingping? Paengpaeng?
Team Leader Choi, who had been chiming in as Wei Fenghu spoke, silently moved his lips. His poker face was astonishing.
—Just so you know, saying something like that here could get you into serious trouble.
—That’s why I’m using Sound Transmission—no, Message Magic.
—I’m telling you to be careful. Some exceptional mages of A rank or higher can eavesdrop on Message Magic.
—Anyway, what was his name? Pingping or Paengpaeng? If you don’t tell me, I won’t be able to sleep tonight.
—...Pingping.
You were going to answer me in the end anyway.
Now that I was finally satisfied, I listened closely to Wei Fenghu’s words.
“No one could have predicted it.”
Sichuan Province was enormous, both in area and in population, with tens of millions of residents.
And it had all begun in Gaoping District, part of Nanchong City—one of the roughly twenty administrative divisions in Sichuan Province.

“As you know, our country has more than ten times as many Gates as other nations. That made us one of the countries hit hardest during the Great Cataclysm, and we have managed them with corresponding rigor ever since.”
But human power could not control even natural disasters, and the Monster Wave was a calamity far worse than any natural disaster.

“We received word that the mana levels in Gaoping District had suddenly spiked exactly thirteen minutes after the first signs appeared. And by the time Lei Fei, head of the Public Security Armed Forces Department stationed in Sichuan Province, arrived at the scene with the Hunters under his command...everything was already too late.”
“Lei Fei?”
The name was unfamiliar. Yet for some reason, a memory surfaced.
That video Team Leader Choi showed me at the Guild House before we left.
I still remembered it vividly. A city plunged into utter chaos beneath the glow of a hologram, and one man at the head of the Hunters, cutting his way through the monsters.
His weapon had shone with a dazzling aura.
“I think I’ve seen him before. Was he the man in the video you sent us...?”
“That is correct.”
Wei Fenghu hesitated, then continued with a faint sigh.
“He was one of our country’s S-rank Hunters. Of course, neither of you would have known about him.”
We wouldn’t have known?
There were only twenty S-rank Hunters in the entire world. Each of them was an absolute powerhouse.
The fame and status they enjoyed far surpassed even those of a Supreme Peak master in Murim.
The internet, news, and social media were their stages, while microphones and cameras followed them like shadows.
The common people of Murim regarded martial artists with equal parts wariness and curiosity, but modern people saw Hunters as objects of pure admiration. They were global celebrities.
And we’re supposed to have never heard of an S-rank Hunter?
Wei Fenghu had phrased it indirectly, but his meaning was clear.
Team Leader Choi’s gaze met mine in midair. At that moment, we were thinking the same thing.
An undisclosed S-rank Hunter.
No—to be precise, an S-rank Hunter deliberately concealed by the Chinese government.
I’d only ever heard rumors about this. So they were true?
An S-rank Hunter was practically the face of a nation.
But unlike the weak, who struggled desperately to avoid being underestimated, the strong concealed their claws.
China was already known to possess two S-rank Hunters. Clearly, it had no intention of revealing the full extent of its strength.
Perhaps the same was true of the world’s other major powers.
Good grief. Even after surviving the Great Cataclysm, they’re still playing this kind of game of nerves.

It was pathetic, but at the same time, I thought I could understand it. Diplomacy. Politics. I felt as though I had caught a glimpse of the truths of a world I had never known, and the feeling was strange.
Team Leader Choi, however, was sharper than I was.
“You said he ‘was’ one of your country’s S-rank Hunters. That sounded like the past tense.”
Wei Fenghu answered with a devastated expression.
“...Lei Fei disappeared a week ago, when the first Monster Wave began. The Hunters of the Public Security Armed Forces Department under his command vanished with him.”
“Are you certain he is only missing? Could he perhaps...”
“We could not confirm his death. After that video was recorded, the monster known as the Lich—no, the Arch Lich—blocked all communications and surveillance with mana.”
Team Leader Choi and I both groaned.
At our reaction, Wei Fenghu asked in a hoarse voice,
“Do you also believe Lei Fei is dead?”
“Hmm.”
Missing for a week in the middle of that hellscape? The outcome was practically a foregone conclusion.
Team Leader Choi shot me a look, so I cautiously began,
“Well, you never know what might happen to someone, but...”
“The other experts said there was a one-hundred-percent chance he was dead. Useless windbags, every last one of them.”
Come on. They sound like real experts to me.
Anyone who confidently claimed Lei Fei was still alive after seeing that situation deserved to be fired on the spot. That was simply the truth.
“But I disagree. Lei Fei—my boy—is certainly alive.”
“I hope so too, but realistically speaking...”
“He is my only nephew. My sister was sickly from childhood and died in childbirth. I took in her baby before he was even weaned and raised him as my own son.”
“Excuse me?”
His nephew? He raised him like a son? What the hell was this?
As I sat frozen like a statue, Wei Fenghu asked me with damp eyes,
“What were you about to say? After ‘realistically speaking.’”
Fuck. This is the worst crisis I’ve ever faced.
The words lodged in my throat. I barely managed to force them out.
“I was going to say that, realistically speaking, there’s still a chance he might be alive.”
“Is that so? Is that really true?”
“Ah, yes. But the odds are extremely slim—”
“Thank you, Mr. Jin!”
“No, General. Commander. Supreme Leader. Please hold on and let me finish...”
He seized my hand.
Too late. Wei Fenghu was no longer listening. Instead, he clasped my hand between both of his, his eyes brimming with tears.
“May I ask you one favor?”
I really wish you wouldn’t.
Contrary to my desperate hopes, a few seconds later, the one sentence I had expected pierced my heart.
“If you happen to meet that boy someday, could you bring him back to me?”
“I beg you.”
Over Wei Fenghu’s shoulder, I saw Team Leader Choi shaking his head.
What if I’d just been firm from the start? I regretted it, but it was too late.
In the end, there was only one answer I could give.
“I will. But...”
“Mr. Jin.”
“Yes?”
“You need not say it. I am already prepared for what may happen.”

Wei Fenghu wiped his eyes with his sleeve. In an instant, he was no longer a middle-aged man worried about his family. He had become the Minister of National Defense under the Central Military Commission once more.
“This is enough. No one else was willing to step forward, but you have given me your word, Mr. Jin. I can rest easier now.”
“I can’t promise anything.”
“I did not need someone’s boastful guarantee. What I needed was a thread of hope.”
Just as Wei Fenghu murmured those words, the aircraft began to descend, accompanied by a sudden sensation of floating.
Outside the window, beneath a blanket of deep darkness, I could see rugged mountain ridges, lights moving without pause, and military vehicles.
“It seems we have arrived.”
I stared out at the landscape as though possessed, then asked,
“Where are we?”
“A temporary operations headquarters.”
“No. That’s not what I meant.”
“Hmm?”
“For some reason, that mountain feels strangely familiar.”
“That cannot be. As far as I know, you have never visited our country... Ah, perhaps you saw it in a photograph?”
“A photograph?”
“It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. That would certainly be possible.”
With a faint smile, Wei Fenghu continued,
“Temporary operations headquarters. Welcome to Mount Qingcheng.”

sentences.text: The jet Wei Fenghu had prepared looked nothing like what I had imagined.
It’s spacious.
And fancy.
Through the partly open cabin door, I could see a luxurious table and one of those so-called chairman’s chairs.
Team Leader Choi, who was standing beside me, informed us that the business jet we were looking at cost nearly one hundred billion won per plane, then added,
“I never expected to see an aircraft reserved for state guests here.”
“That is only natural.
The two of you are state guests of our country.”
“Ah.”
“Thanks to you, we were able to save countless soldiers and Hunters.
None of us—not even me—will ever forget the help you gave us today.”
“...Ah, yes.”
I would have preferred it if they dealt with the fine dust and historical distortions first.
Still, I boarded the jet, privately hoping China was a more conscientious country than I gave it credit for.
The waiting pilot saluted us—or, more precisely, Wei Fenghu—with crisp, disciplined movements.
“You have arrived, Comrade Minister of National Defense.”
“Are we ready?”
“This aircraft and all its escorts are ready.
We await your order.”
I wondered what he meant by “escorts,” but then I looked through the window and saw five sleek fighter jets on the runway, their lights blinking as though signaling us.
What the hell are those?
I’d only ever seen things like that in war movies.
Were we flying off to fight a battle or something?
Wei Fenghu saw my eyes widen and explained.
“The details have not yet been made public...but as you know, Sichuan Province is currently in a state of war.
Magical interference has disrupted communications, and attacks by flying monsters are frequent.
An escort is essential for our safety.”
“Is that really true?”
The situation was more serious than I’d thought.
The Wyvern had only attacked us in passing while raiding Chengdu International Airport.
But if the same thing was happening throughout Sichuan Province, that changed everything.
“I wish I were lying.”
Perhaps merely thinking about the current situation exhausted him.
Wei Fenghu, who seemed to have aged considerably in a short time, leaned back into the soft seat.
“It seems we must part ways here.
We will meet again soon, Senior Colonel Xiao Shen.”
Unlike us, Xiao Shen had not boarded the aircraft.
He stood rigidly at attention and saluted.
“Yes, Comrade Minister of National Defense.
I will complete my mission as quickly as possible and rejoin you.
And, gentlemen...”
“Good.
I expect great things from you.”
Perhaps because he had achieved such impressive accomplishments, a pleased smile passed across Wei Fenghu’s lips as he looked at the promising young Hunter.
Team Leader Choi gave him a polite bow.
I waved.

It was only one sentence.

His body trembled as though he had been electrocuted, and then he shouted at the top of his lungs.

I will devote myself to every task with the utmost loyalty, so that I never disappoint you, Mr.
Jin!”
“...You don’t need to go that far.”
“May your august self remain safe!
Loooyalty!”
“‘August self’?
What are you—”
Whack!
“Urk!”
That looked like a textbook example of poor judgment.
He’d saluted so hard that the edge of his hand struck him in the eyebrow.
As I stared dumbfounded at Xiao Shen clenching his teeth against the pain, the cabin door closed and our business jet began to take off.
“That guy is, well...
How should I put it?
He’s quite a character.”
Wei Fenghu gave a quiet laugh at my awkward observation.
“Can you blame him?
His idol praised him.”
“Excuse me?”
“Many young Hunters in our country admire you, Mr.
Jin.
He is no exception.”
What the hell?
Was I a Korean Wave star?
Come to think of it, for a four-star general with enough power to make birds fall from the sky, Wei Fenghu seemed unusually attentive to his subordinates.
Or maybe Xiao Shen was simply that promising.
Ah, but...
—Team Leader.
How important is the Minister of National Defense under the Central Military Commission, exactly?
I’m not very familiar with the structure over here.
Team Leader Choi flinched at my Sound Transmission, then replied through Message Magic.
—If you compare it to our country, he is the Minister of National Defense.
Of course, this is China, and Wei Fenghu is the current Chairman’s right-hand man, so his power is considerably greater.
—Ah.
So he’s a lot like me.
I’m the Minister of gukbap.
One special serving of sundae-guk was enough to handle three bowls of rice.
Of course, Wei Fenghu could probably erase three cities with a single pointed finger.
And now, that powerful figure of the People’s Republic of China was leaning his upper body toward us and asking,
“It seems we have much to discuss during the flight.
Would you not agree?”
Team Leader Choi and I nodded solemnly and opened our mouths.
“Of course.
First, I would like to ask what exactly is happening in Sichuan—”
“But do you happen to have any boiled eggs and soda?
I’m hungry after fighting so hard.”
Apparently, they didn’t.
“We do.”
They actually did.
The People’s Republic of China.
As its formal name suggested, the people of this vast and imposing nation still adhered to socialism as their national ideology.
About twenty years ago, the Chairman at the time—who had cemented the foundations of his dictatorship by securing lifelong rule—died during the Great Cataclysm.
Power then passed to a far more moderate administration, but the substance of the system remained unchanged.
—What was the dead Chairman’s name again?
Pingping?
Paengpaeng?
Team Leader Choi, who had been chiming in as Wei Fenghu spoke, silently moved his lips.
His poker face was astonishing.
—Just so you know, saying something like that here could get you into serious trouble.
—That’s why I’m using Sound Transmission—no, Message Magic.
—I’m telling you to be careful.
Some exceptional mages of A rank or higher can eavesdrop on Message Magic.
—Anyway, what was his name?
Pingping or Paengpaeng?
If you don’t tell me, I won’t be able to sleep tonight.
—...Pingping.
You were going to answer me in the end anyway.
Now that I was finally satisfied, I listened closely to Wei Fenghu’s words.
“No one could have predicted it.”
Sichuan Province was enormous, both in area and in population, with tens of millions of residents.
And it had all begun in Gaoping District, part of Nanchong City—one of the roughly twenty administrative divisions in Sichuan Province.
“As you know, our country has more than ten times as many Gates as other nations.
That made us one of the countries hit hardest during the Great Cataclysm, and we have managed them with corresponding rigor ever since.”
But human power could not control even natural disasters, and the Monster Wave was a calamity far worse than any natural disaster.
“We received word that the mana levels in Gaoping District had suddenly spiked exactly thirteen minutes after the first signs appeared.
And by the time Lei Fei, head of the Public Security Armed Forces Department stationed in Sichuan Province, arrived at the scene with the Hunters under his command...everything was already too late.”
“Lei Fei?”
The name was unfamiliar.
Yet for some reason, a memory surfaced.
That video Team Leader Choi showed me at the Guild House before we left.
I still remembered it vividly.
A city plunged into utter chaos beneath the glow of a hologram, and one man at the head of the Hunters, cutting his way through the monsters.
His weapon had shone with a dazzling aura.
“I think I’ve seen him before.
Was he the man in the video you sent us...?”
“That is correct.”
Wei Fenghu hesitated, then continued with a faint sigh.
“He was one of our country’s S-rank Hunters.
Of course, neither of you would have known about him.”
We wouldn’t have known?
There were only twenty S-rank Hunters in the entire world.
Each of them was an absolute powerhouse.
The fame and status they enjoyed far surpassed even those of a Supreme Peak master in Murim.
The internet, news, and social media were their stages, while microphones and cameras followed them like shadows.
The common people of Murim regarded martial artists with equal parts wariness and curiosity, but modern people saw Hunters as objects of pure admiration.
They were global celebrities.
And we’re supposed to have never heard of an S-rank Hunter?
Wei Fenghu had phrased it indirectly, but his meaning was clear.
Team Leader Choi’s gaze met mine in midair.
At that moment, we were thinking the same thing.
An undisclosed S-rank Hunter.
No—to be precise, an S-rank Hunter deliberately concealed by the Chinese government.
I’d only ever heard rumors about this.
So they were true?
An S-rank Hunter was practically the face of a nation.
But unlike the weak, who struggled desperately to avoid being underestimated, the strong concealed their claws.
China was already known to possess two S-rank Hunters.
Clearly, it had no intention of revealing the full extent of its strength.
