chapters.title: Chapter 384
paragraphs: Mount Qingcheng.
A sacred Taoist site steeped in ages past.
Anyone who stood before its stern, overwhelming peaks would be struck speechless.
But I was amazed for an entirely different reason.
It’s definitely different...but it looks so similar.
Mount Qingcheng in Murim. Mount Qingcheng in the modern twenty-first century.
The two worlds I had experienced resembled each other in many ways—their terrain, languages, people’s features, and even their ways of life.
At one point, I had even wondered whether Murim might be the distant past of the modern world.
But it wasn’t.
The butterfly effect? There was no way something I had only ever seen in movies had actually happened.
The two worlds were certainly similar, but there were subtle differences between them, and their histories were different as well.
The world of Murim was also smaller than the modern one, with no five oceans or six continents.
People with colored eyes lived in far-off foreign lands, but that was all. The center of that world was a continent ruled by a vast Great Nation.
Perhaps the Zhonghua the Chinese never tired of going on about was Murim itself.
But why did even this have to be similar?
I had barely returned from the Three-Gate Bloodbath, which had mercilessly drenched Sichuan Province in blood, only to find myself at Mount Qingcheng in modern-day Sichuan.
I couldn’t tell whether it was a simple coincidence or some terrible twist of fate.
I only hoped the similarities didn’t extend that far...
“Mr. Jin?”
“Mr. Jin Taekyung.”
“Ah.”
I raised my head like someone waking from sleep.
Wei Fenghu and Team Leader Choi had already gotten off the business jet and were looking at me strangely.
“Sorry. I got distracted by the scenery for a moment.”
“It is so dark, yet you can still appreciate the magnificent scenery of Mount Qingcheng. You truly possess extraordinary mana, Mr. Jin.”
That wasn’t exactly wrong, but now that I had reached the Supreme Peak realm, I could see through most darkness with my eyesight alone, without relying on internal energy.
When I nodded with a complicated expression, Wei Fenghu gazed at me in admiration.
“Now I understand why Korea has kept you hidden so carefully, Mr. Jin. You are indeed worthy of being called an S-rank Hunter—the face of your nation.”
“Excuse me? I’m still officially A-rank.”
“There is no need to hide it. Our country has already ascertained the situation to some extent.”
Before I could respond, Wei Fenghu continued without pause.

“To become an S-rank Hunter, one must attain enlightenment through relentless mental discipline and arduous training. Our country also endured countless trials and errors to cultivate the Hunters we have today...but for someone as young as you to have reached such a realm, the Korean government must have given you its full support.”
“Of course, Mr. Choi beside you is also an excellent Hunter. With the two of you here together, I feel greatly reassured.”
What kind of hearty gukbap nonsense was that?
Team Leader Choi and I exchanged a brief glance and reached a silent agreement.
Keep your mouth shut.
Let’s just go.

Apparently, this misunderstanding had arisen because I had reached my current level in such an absurdly unrealistic way. But if they had already decided to slap that label on me, there was no reason for us to peel it off for them.
Besides, convincing Wei Fenghu otherwise right here would be a pain.
“Hmm. I think there’s been a slight misunderstanding, but I’ll explain everything bit by bit when the time comes.”
“What is there to misunderstand? We both know how things stand.”
“Even the Chairman already knows about the matter. When you meet him, do not bother denying it. Just accept it as it is.”
Aware of what?
I let out a quiet laugh.
Speaking of the Chairman...
He was like a king, holding more than a billion people and the economy and military of the People’s Republic of China in the palm of his hand.
Even now that I had reached the Supreme Peak realm, he felt both close and impossibly distant to someone like me, whose modern-day common sense remained rooted to the bone.
I wonder if I’ll get to see him once this is all over.
Well, what did it matter? That was a question for much later.
Even without my raid pay, my weekly salary was a staggering ten billion won. As far as I was concerned, he was simply a generous employer.
I got to save people and make money. Two birds with one stone.
“I’ll do that. If I meet him.”
“Good. Then let us go meet him.”
“Excuse me?”
“Did I not tell you? He is waiting in the underground bunker right now.”
What the hell is going on?
I stared blankly at Wei Fenghu’s retreating back, then hurried over to Team Leader Choi and whispered,
“D-Did you hear that?”

“Yes, I did. But I find it rather surprising as well. For the Chairman of China to leave the safety of Beijing and come all the way here... It seems his public reputation is at least partly deserved.”
“To hell with his reputation. China’s Jongseok—Jongseok!”
“Not Jongseok, General Secretary! The Chairman!”
“Hmm? What did you just say?”
“Nothing, Minister.”
When Wei Fenghu suddenly glanced back, Team Leader Choi politely covered for us. Then he turned to me with the most grave and earnest expression I had ever seen on his face.

“Mr. Jin Taekyung. You must not make that kind of verbal mistake in front of the Chairman. Understood? Especially not Jongseok. Don’t even mention it. It sounds like the name of some high school classmate.”
“Huh? How did you know?”
I think Team Leader Choi just muttered fuck.
Must be my imagination.
I took a deep breath and repeated the words to myself.
Not Jongseok. General Secretary. The Chairman of China.
Unlike Team Leader Choi, who had been born into the highest tier of nobility, I was an ordinary citizen to my core.
Whatever feelings I normally had toward China, my heart pounded at the thought of meeting the leader of one of the ten most powerful nations in the world.
Just don’t make a mistake. Especially not Jongseok.
Ten minutes later, deep inside an underground bunker, I shook hands with the leader of the People’s Republic of China under the gazes of the important figures gathered there.
“Pleased to meet you, Mr. Jin. This old man is Xiao Yang, Chairman of the People’s Republic of China.”
Good. Not even a hint of Jongseok.
Having cleared that hurdle, I opened my mouth at ease.
“Welcome.”
Ah, fuck.
Chairman of the Chinese Communist Party’s Central Military Commission. General Secretary. And the head of state who stood at the apex of more than a billion people.
Xiao Yang.
His voice directed at the people was gentle, while strength filled his eyes.

“As you all know, I am unfortunately neither a military expert nor an outstanding general. I am merely a schemer who entered politics at an early age and managed to fulfill one small ambition only after reaching the age of seventy.”
It was astonishing to hear the leader of the country with the fourth-largest territory and largest population on Earth call himself a schemer.
So this is what Team Leader Choi meant by the public perception of him?
I felt as if I had a rough idea of what kind of person he was.
Perhaps it was merely a mask he wore in front of others. Perhaps it was hypocrisy.
But at least from the old man speaking before all of us now, including me—Xiao Yang, the Chairman of China—I sensed a kind of qi utterly unlike either of those things.

“Please do your utmost. Save as many of our people as you can, and bring this terrible disaster to an end as quickly as possible. If you do, I will express gratitude worthy of what you and your countries have done, and I will long remember the aid you have given us.”
The truth was, I knew nothing about the life that old man had lived or the policies he had pursued.
But I wanted to give him considerable credit for reaching out to countries around the world to save his own people.

“That is all this old man has to say. Please do not concern yourselves with complicated matters such as politics. I earnestly ask that you find the best way to resolve this crisis with the fewest possible sacrifices.”
The old statesman who had devoted his entire life to politics turned toward one man.
“Minister of National Defense Wei Fenghu. My old friend.”
“Yes, respected Chairman Comrade.”
“Do you want full authority over the Central Military Commission?”
Wei Fenghu hesitated for a moment, then nodded gravely.
“I do.”
“You could use that power well. But I must refuse.”
“...Chairman Comrade?”
“Bring me the orders once this meeting is over. I will assume full authority—and full responsibility—for everything that follows.”
For a moment, I wondered why China’s Jongseok was acting like that.
Then I understood. He was declaring that he would shoulder everything himself.
Watching from beside me, Team Leader Choi murmured,
“He’s a good leader.”
I quietly shook my head.
“No. To me, you’re the best, Team Leader Choi.”
“Mr. Jin Taekyung...”
“So please raise my Guild settlement percentage.”
“Mr. Jin Taekyung...”
The same words, yet a completely different feeling.
Team Leader Choi gave me a look that said, Of course you’d say that, you bastard, and shook his head. Just then, the secretary announced,
“The Chairman is departing.”
At the secretary’s announcement, everyone rose from their seats. It was the least courtesy owed to a head of state.
“I wish you all good fortune in battle.”
The Chairman addressed every person present, meeting each one’s eyes in turn. Naturally, I was no exception.
Unfortunately, I was the very last.
“Mr. Jin.”
A faint smile touched the Chairman’s lips as he looked at me.
“I have very high expectations of you, Mr. Jin. Although this is a contract through which we each receive what we need, I hope you will prioritize human life under all circumstances.”
Was it my imagination, or was his farewell much longer than the ones he had given everyone else?
Feeling the others’ eyes on me, I nodded.
“Understood.”
“Please lend us your considerable strength.”
The Chairman turned to leave, only to pause after a step. Then he casually tossed out one last remark.
“Welcome.”
“Then I will take my leave.”
Once the senior Chinese officials accompanying the Chairman had disappeared, I collapsed into a chair.
Fuck.
If I died, the cause of death would be death by humiliation.
Even if a monster killed me, I would have the cause of death recorded as death by humiliation.
Aagh! Aaaaaagh!
As I screamed in every direction inside my mind, something firmly stepped on my foot.
It was obviously Team Leader Choi, who was sitting beside me.
“Why?”
Team Leader Choi gave a quiet cough.
“Ahem.”
“What is it?”
“Ahem. People. People.”
“Oh.”
I looked around and finally realized that a dozen or so men and women of various races were staring at me inside the underground bunker.
Four of them stood out in particular.
Those people are...
A Chinese man and woman, and two Western men, one tinged green and the other blue.
I could feel it from the moment our eyes met—the enormous energy coiled within their bodies.
Rather than being surprised, I felt that it was only natural. Anyone who knew the identities of those four would have thought the same.
S-rank Hunters.
People whose very existence made headlines. The individuals who stood at the pinnacle of the countless Hunters around the world.
The faces I had grown sick of seeing on television and in commercials were right in front of me.
And now one of them rose and held out his hand.
“Nice to meet you. I’m... Ah, do you not speak English? I can cast translation magic for you.”
I had never expected him to approach me first.
Still dazed, I took his hand and answered,
“No, it’s fine.”
“Oh, listen to that pronunciation. I’d believe you were American.”
He was a middle-aged Black man, a giant well over two meters tall. His blue eyes gleamed as he asked,
“You seem to know who I am. Am I right?”
How could I not?
I was even more nervous than I had been when facing Chairman Xiao Yang.
“Of course. Magic Johnson.”
The title of Archmage, bestowed on only three people in the entire world.
And among those three, the Black man standing before me—Magic Johnson—was the War Mage, the one most specialized in combat.
I’m actually talking to Magic Johnson. I never thought I’d live to see the day.
As I thought that coming here had been the right choice in more ways than one, the world’s greatest War Mage smiled broadly and spoke to me.
“Haha. Thank you for recognizing me. Actually, I’ve known about you for a while.”
“Y-You know me?”
“Of course. Even my youngest daughter, who started elementary school this year, knows Lord Fuck.”
Just how far has that damn nickname spread?
I wondered what Lord Fuck would be called in the English-speaking world.
Fuck Guy? Fuck Man?
The thought of Magic Johnson’s youngest daughter knowing me by that name did not make me happy in the slightest.
Apparently, I wasn’t the only one displeased.
“What an utterly vulgar nickname. Though I suppose it suits a mere A-rank Hunter like you.”
The Chinese man who had just turned thirty, or perhaps was about to, watched me with his arms folded.
“Isn’t that right, you peninsula bangzi?”
Team Leader Choi had no chance to stop me.
My voice had already come out like a prerecorded response.
“What the hell are you talking about, you mainland chink bastard?”

sentences.text: Mount Qingcheng.
A sacred Taoist site steeped in ages past.
Anyone who stood before its stern, overwhelming peaks would be struck speechless.
But I was amazed for an entirely different reason.
It’s definitely different...but it looks so similar.
Mount Qingcheng in Murim.
Mount Qingcheng in the modern twenty-first century.
The two worlds I had experienced resembled each other in many ways—their terrain, languages, people’s features, and even their ways of life.
At one point, I had even wondered whether Murim might be the distant past of the modern world.
But it wasn’t.
The butterfly effect?
There was no way something I had only ever seen in movies had actually happened.
The two worlds were certainly similar, but there were subtle differences between them, and their histories were different as well.
The world of Murim was also smaller than the modern one, with no five oceans or six continents.
People with colored eyes lived in far-off foreign lands, but that was all.
The center of that world was a continent ruled by a vast Great Nation.
Perhaps the Zhonghua the Chinese never tired of going on about was Murim itself.
But why did even this have to be similar?
I had barely returned from the Three-Gate Bloodbath, which had mercilessly drenched Sichuan Province in blood, only to find myself at Mount Qingcheng in modern-day Sichuan.
I couldn’t tell whether it was a simple coincidence or some terrible twist of fate.
I only hoped the similarities didn’t extend that far...
“Mr.
Jin?”
“Mr.
Jin Taekyung.”
“Ah.”
I raised my head like someone waking from sleep.
Wei Fenghu and Team Leader Choi had already gotten off the business jet and were looking at me strangely.
“Sorry.
I got distracted by the scenery for a moment.”
“It is so dark, yet you can still appreciate the magnificent scenery of Mount Qingcheng.
You truly possess extraordinary mana, Mr.
Jin.”
That wasn’t exactly wrong, but now that I had reached the Supreme Peak realm, I could see through most darkness with my eyesight alone, without relying on internal energy.
When I nodded with a complicated expression, Wei Fenghu gazed at me in admiration.
“Now I understand why Korea has kept you hidden so carefully, Mr.
Jin.
You are indeed worthy of being called an S-rank Hunter—the face of your nation.”
“Excuse me?
I’m still officially A-rank.”
“There is no need to hide it.
Our country has already ascertained the situation to some extent.”
Before I could respond, Wei Fenghu continued without pause.
“To become an S-rank Hunter, one must attain enlightenment through relentless mental discipline and arduous training.

Our country also endured countless trials and errors to cultivate the Hunters we have today...but for someone as young as you to have reached such a realm, the Korean government must have given you its full support.”
“Of course, Mr.
Choi beside you is also an excellent Hunter.
With the two of you here together, I feel greatly reassured.”
What kind of hearty gukbap nonsense was that?
Team Leader Choi and I exchanged a brief glance and reached a silent agreement.
Keep your mouth shut.
Let’s just go.
Apparently, this misunderstanding had arisen because I had reached my current level in such an absurdly unrealistic way.
But if they had already decided to slap that label on me, there was no reason for us to peel it off for them.
Besides, convincing Wei Fenghu otherwise right here would be a pain.
“Hmm.
I think there’s been a slight misunderstanding, but I’ll explain everything bit by bit when the time comes.”
“What is there to misunderstand?
We both know how things stand.”
“Even the Chairman already knows about the matter.
When you meet him, do not bother denying it.
Just accept it as it is.”
Aware of what?
I let out a quiet laugh.
Speaking of the Chairman...
He was like a king, holding more than a billion people and the economy and military of the People’s Republic of China in the palm of his hand.
Even now that I had reached the Supreme Peak realm, he felt both close and impossibly distant to someone like me, whose modern-day common sense remained rooted to the bone.
I wonder if I’ll get to see him once this is all over.
Well, what did it matter?
That was a question for much later.
Even without my raid pay, my weekly salary was a staggering ten billion won.
As far as I was concerned, he was simply a generous employer.
I got to save people and make money.
Two birds with one stone.
“I’ll do that.
If I meet him.”
“Good.
Then let us go meet him.”
“Excuse me?”
“Did I not tell you?
He is waiting in the underground bunker right now.”
What the hell is going on?
I stared blankly at Wei Fenghu’s retreating back, then hurried over to Team Leader Choi and whispered,
“D-Did you hear that?”
“Yes, I did.
But I find it rather surprising as well.
For the Chairman of China to leave the safety of Beijing and come all the way here...
It seems his public reputation is at least partly deserved.”
“To hell with his reputation.
China’s Jongseok—Jongseok!”
“Not Jongseok, General Secretary!
The Chairman!”
“Hmm?
What did you just say?”
“Nothing, Minister.”
When Wei Fenghu suddenly glanced back, Team Leader Choi politely covered for us.
Then he turned to me with the most grave and earnest expression I had ever seen on his face.
“Mr.
Jin Taekyung.
You must not make that kind of verbal mistake in front of the Chairman.
Understood?
Especially not Jongseok.
Don’t even mention it.
It sounds like the name of some high school classmate.”
“Huh?
How did you know?”
I think Team Leader Choi just muttered fuck.
Must be my imagination.
I took a deep breath and repeated the words to myself.
Not Jongseok.
General Secretary.
The Chairman of China.
Unlike Team Leader Choi, who had been born into the highest tier of nobility, I was an ordinary citizen to my core.
Whatever feelings I normally had toward China, my heart pounded at the thought of meeting the leader of one of the ten most powerful nations in the world.
Just don’t make a mistake.
Especially not Jongseok.
Ten minutes later, deep inside an underground bunker, I shook hands with the leader of the People’s Republic of China under the gazes of the important figures gathered there.
“Pleased to meet you, Mr.
Jin.
This old man is Xiao Yang, Chairman of the People’s Republic of China.”
Good.
Not even a hint of Jongseok.
Having cleared that hurdle, I opened my mouth at ease.
“Welcome.”
Ah, fuck.
Chairman of the Chinese Communist Party’s Central Military Commission.
General Secretary.
And the head of state who stood at the apex of more than a billion people.
Xiao Yang.
His voice directed at the people was gentle, while strength filled his eyes.
“As you all know, I am unfortunately neither a military expert nor an outstanding general.
I am merely a schemer who entered politics at an early age and managed to fulfill one small ambition only after reaching the age of seventy.”
It was astonishing to hear the leader of the country with the fourth-largest territory and largest population on Earth call himself a schemer.
So this is what Team Leader Choi meant by the public perception of him?
I felt as if I had a rough idea of what kind of person he was.
Perhaps it was merely a mask he wore in front of others.
Perhaps it was hypocrisy.
But at least from the old man speaking before all of us now, including me—Xiao Yang, the Chairman of China—I sensed a kind of qi utterly unlike either of those things.
“Please do your utmost.
Save as many of our people as you can, and bring this terrible disaster to an end as quickly as possible.
If you do, I will express gratitude worthy of what you and your countries have done, and I will long remember the aid you have given us.”
The truth was, I knew nothing about the life that old man had lived or the policies he had pursued.
But I wanted to give him considerable credit for reaching out to countries around the world to save his own people.
“That is all this old man has to say.
Please do not concern yourselves with complicated matters such as politics.
I earnestly ask that you find the best way to resolve this crisis with the fewest possible sacrifices.”
The old statesman who had devoted his entire life to politics turned toward one man.
“Minister of National Defense Wei Fenghu.
My old friend.”
“Yes, respected Chairman Comrade.”
“Do you want full authority over the Central Military Commission?”
Wei Fenghu hesitated for a moment, then nodded gravely.
“I do.”
“You could use that power well.
But I must refuse.”
“...Chairman Comrade?”
“Bring me the orders once this meeting is over.
I will assume full authority—and full responsibility—for everything that follows.”
For a moment, I wondered why China’s Jongseok was acting like that.
Then I understood.
He was declaring that he would shoulder everything himself.
Watching from beside me, Team Leader Choi murmured,
“He’s a good leader.”
I quietly shook my head.
“No.
To me, you’re the best, Team Leader Choi.”
“Mr.
Jin Taekyung...”
“So please raise my Guild settlement percentage.”
“Mr.
Jin Taekyung...”
The same words, yet a completely different feeling.
Team Leader Choi gave me a look that said, Of course you’d say that, you bastard, and shook his head.
Just then, the secretary announced,
“The Chairman is departing.”
At the secretary’s announcement, everyone rose from their seats.
It was the least courtesy owed to a head of state.
“I wish you all good fortune in battle.”
The Chairman addressed every person present, meeting each one’s eyes in turn.
Naturally, I was no exception.
Unfortunately, I was the very last.
“Mr.
Jin.”
A faint smile touched the Chairman’s lips as he looked at me.
“I have very high expectations of you, Mr.
Jin.
Although this is a contract through which we each receive what we need, I hope you will prioritize human life under all circumstances.”
Was it my imagination, or was his farewell much longer than the ones he had given everyone else?
Feeling the others’ eyes on me, I nodded.
“Understood.”
“Please lend us your considerable strength.”
The Chairman turned to leave, only to pause after a step.
Then he casually tossed out one last remark.
“Welcome.”
“Then I will take my leave.”
Once the senior Chinese officials accompanying the Chairman had disappeared, I collapsed into a chair.
Fuck.
If I died, the cause of death would be death by humiliation.
Even if a monster killed me, I would have the cause of death recorded as death by humiliation.
Aagh!
Aaaaaagh!
As I screamed in every direction inside my mind, something firmly stepped on my foot.
It was obviously Team Leader Choi, who was sitting beside me.
“Why?”
Team Leader Choi gave a quiet cough.
“Ahem.”
“What is it?”
“Ahem.
People.
People.”
“Oh.”
I looked around and finally realized that a dozen or so men and women of various races were staring at me inside the underground bunker.
Four of them stood out in particular.
Those people are...
A Chinese man and woman, and two Western men, one tinged green and the other blue.
I could feel it from the moment our eyes met—the enormous energy coiled within their bodies.
Rather than being surprised, I felt that it was only natural.
Anyone who knew the identities of those four would have thought the same.
S-rank Hunters.
People whose very existence made headlines.
The individuals who stood at the pinnacle of the countless Hunters around the world.
The faces I had grown sick of seeing on television and in commercials were right in front of me.
And now one of them rose and held out his hand.
“Nice to meet you.
Ah, do you not speak English?
I can cast translation magic for you.”
I had never expected him to approach me first.
Still dazed, I took his hand and answered,
“No, it’s fine.”
“Oh, listen to that pronunciation.
I’d believe you were American.”
He was a middle-aged Black man, a giant well over two meters tall.
His blue eyes gleamed as he asked,
“You seem to know who I am.
Am I right?”
How could I not?
I was even more nervous than I had been when facing Chairman Xiao Yang.
“Of course.
Magic Johnson.”
The title of Archmage, bestowed on only three people in the entire world.
And among those three, the Black man standing before me—Magic Johnson—was the War Mage, the one most specialized in combat.
I’m actually talking to Magic Johnson.
I never thought I’d live to see the day.
As I thought that coming here had been the right choice in more ways than one, the world’s greatest War Mage smiled broadly and spoke to me.
“Haha.
Thank you for recognizing me.
Actually, I’ve known about you for a while.”
“Y-You know me?”
“Of course.
Even my youngest daughter, who started elementary school this year, knows Lord Fuck.”
Just how far has that damn nickname spread?
I wondered what Lord Fuck would be called in the English-speaking world.
Fuck Guy?
Fuck Man?
The thought of Magic Johnson’s youngest daughter knowing me by that name did not make me happy in the slightest.
Apparently, I wasn’t the only one displeased.
“What an utterly vulgar nickname.
Though I suppose it suits a mere A-rank Hunter like you.”
The Chinese man who had just turned thirty, or perhaps was about to, watched me with his arms folded.
“Isn’t that right, you peninsula bangzi?”
Team Leader Choi had no chance to stop me.
My voice had already come out like a prerecorded response.
“What the hell are you talking about, you mainland chink bastard?”

chapters.title: Chapter 385
paragraphs: “Isn’t that right, you peninsula bangzi?”
“What the hell are you talking about, you mainland chink bastard?”
A heavy silence fell over the room.

Foreigners like Magic Johnson were using translation magic, but even they couldn’t tell exactly what the original slurs bangzi and chink meant. Team Leader Choi clicked his tongue quietly, while one man’s face hardened like stone.
“What?”
“What, asshole?”
“Say that again, bangzi.”
“Sure. Chink.”
“You fucking—”
“Good. Let’s get this straight. I’m a dog. You’re a chink.”
I watched his face twist violently. Just as he was about to shove back his chair and leap to his feet, the woman sitting beside him raised a hand to stop him.
“Enough.”
She was a beautiful woman in her early twenties, with the same crisp, refreshing air as a soft drink. Her calm voice followed.
“I’d appreciate it if you both kept this within reason.”
Within reason...
I studied her for a moment, then shrugged.
“Well, if you’re asking.”
One of her eyebrows arched slightly, as though my answer had surprised her.
“I heard you were quite a handful, but you’re more agreeable than I expected.”
“I have to be. It’s you asking, after all.”
“So you’ve fallen for my feminine wiles? Ah, being beautiful is such a burden.”
She swept back her long hair with practiced nonchalance, drawing a quiet laugh from me.
“Did you just laugh?”
“You’re more entertaining than I expected, Ms. Faye Chen.”
Faye Chen. That was her name.
I couldn’t let her looks and fresh-faced air fool me into thinking she belonged on the cover of a university brochure. She might never have married, but she was well over fifty.
She was also my senior by decades and one of the heroes of the Great Cataclysm.
“So you knew who I was from the start. Hmm. I thought young people these days wouldn’t recognize me.”
She wasn’t wrong. Compared to other S-rank Hunters, Faye Chen rarely appeared in the media.
There were even persistent rumors that she had changed her identity and was living a new life somewhere out of the public eye.
But I had known about her since I was very young.
“My mother’s been a fan of yours for years. You starred in that romance movie that came out about twenty years ago, didn’t you?”
“Oh, my. That was ages ago. Still, it’s nice to meet someone who remembers it.”
“Would it be all right if I asked for your autograph later? I think my mother would be thrilled if I brought one home.”
“Of course. And from now on, just call me Chen. My full name sounds much too formal. If you want to be even friendlier, you can call me big sister.”
“What? What are you talking about? I looked you up online. You’re five years older than my mother.”
“...You really are a handful. Just as I heard.”
But someone else was being a far greater handful.
“You fucking lowlife—!”
His voice boiled with rage. The man we had briefly forgotten during our conversation glared at me.
“How dare a bangzi from a weak little country look down on me? Do you even know who I am?”
“...Wow. That line was fucking awful.”
Faye Chen propped her chin on one hand and looked between us with interest.
“True. I’ve been wondering for a while now. Do you actually know who this young man is?”
Faye Chen wasn’t the only one waiting for my answer.
Everyone was staring at my mouth except Team Leader Choi, who now looked halfway to enlightenment.
The man huffing like a seven-year-old who had lost an argument. Magic Johnson, the Archmage from the United States. Even the young man from the United Kingdom. Their attendants were no exception.
With everyone watching, I nodded.
“I know. Wu Heixing.”
When it came to media exposure, he competed for first or second place even among S-rank Hunters. There was no way I wouldn’t recognize him.
Wu Heixing—the man who had been picking a fight with me and throwing around the word bangzi—stared at me with wide eyes.
“You knew who I was, yet you still dared behave that way?”
“Even a stray dog would know there’s a human piece of shit among the S-rank Hunters.”
“What, what did you say?”
“What? Everyone knows your hobby is getting attention and your specialty is committing crimes, then manipulating the media afterward.”

“Come to think of it, didn’t you cause some trouble last year? The only drug my country allows me. You posted a raid photo on your official social media with some bullshit like that, then got caught using actual drugs a month later. Was it marijuana?”
“Mr. Jin Taekyung.”
“Don’t stop me, Team Leader Choi.”
“It wasn’t marijuana.”
“What?”
Team Leader Choi abruptly cut in and calmly corrected the Taekyung Wiki.
“It was cocaine and methamphetamine.”
“Oh, I see. Thank you for clarifying.”
“Think nothing of it. Now that things have gone this far, what is there left that I can’t say?”
Look at that enlightened expression.
Leaving behind Team Leader Choi, who had renounced all worldly attachments and was preparing to ascend to immortality, I flashed Wu Heixing a broad smile and continued.
“Damn, how did you think of planting foreshadowing like that? This bastard is at least Wu Heishunwon. Purple Raid.”
“What, what did you say?”

“Come to think of it, there was something else. Five years ago, you got caught drugging and sexually assaulting someone at some club called Burning Moon or whatever. How did you get acquitted? Under Chinese law, it wouldn’t have been strange if you’d been executed two or three times over.”
“I heard a rumor that you’re the son of one of the Communist Party’s highest-ranking officials. Did you buy your way out with money and power? Look at this clever bastard.”
“Shut your fucking mouth! How dare a lowborn bangzi speak to me like that!”
Wu Heixing’s face turned scarlet as he roared. Someone who had been silently watching the whole affair finally spoke.
“You’re noisy.”
An arrogant voice flowed smoothly through the room.
“Frivolous and vulgar. I hear you are descended from a noble Chinese family. Did your elders neglect to teach you proper etiquette?”
Wu Heixing bit his lip when he recognized the speaker.
“Y-You’re...”
“You’re?”
Beneath neatly styled brown hair, faintly green eyes swept slowly over Wu Heixing, then moved away.
“William.”
At the young man’s summons, the graying middle-aged man standing behind him stepped forward.
His shoes were spotless, and the creases of his suit were sharp enough to cut. He stood tall, surveyed the room, and spoke in a pleasant baritone.

“Everyone, rise and show proper respect to His Highness Prince Felix Alexander Louis, Duke of Cambridge, Earl of Strathearn, Baron Carrickfergus, Knight of the Order of the Garter, and Knight of the Order of the Thistle.”
Duke of Cambridge, Earl of Strathearn... Fuck, why does he have so many titles?
At any rate, Prince Felix added solemnly, “You may all simply call me His Highness Prince Felix.”
Look at everyone’s faces. They couldn’t have looked more uncomfortable if they tried.
Of course, the finest expression of all belonged to Wu Heixing, who had just called me lowborn.
Understandable. When it came to social standing, how was he supposed to beat British royalty?
“So, this is...”
“Ah.”
Prince Felix regarded the flustered Wu Heixing and nodded as though something had just occurred to him.
“I see. Are you a stutterer?”
“A-a stutterer?”
“If not, why can’t you speak properly? Did your family neglect to provide you with speech training?”
Long live His Highness the Prince.
I didn’t even need to step in. Having the third person in line to the British throne inject carbonated water straight into my veins made me fizz all the way down to my duodenum.
I was grinning so widely my mouth might split when Prince Felix suddenly turned his gaze on me.
“You there.”
“Hm? Are you talking to me?”
At my question, the middle-aged man behind Prince Felix opened his mouth.

“When His Highness Prince Felix Alexander Louis, Duke of Cambridge, Earl of Strathearn, Baron Carrickfergus, Knight of the Order of the Garter, and Knight of the Order of the Thistle deigns to address you—”
“That will do, William.”
Prince Felix raised a hand, silencing the parrot mid-sentence, then regarded me benevolently.
“I have personally set aside my dignity and intervened because I have always believed that the barriers between social classes must be broken down.”
“What does it matter whether one is lowborn or noble? Beneath God, we are all equal. So do not take that man’s words too much to heart.”
What the fuck is this supposed to mean?
I was momentarily speechless. Team Leader Choi leaned over and whispered discreetly.
“I believe he thinks you really are lowborn, Mr. Jin.”
Has that prince bastard lost his mind?
As I stared at Prince Felix in disbelief, he slowly rose and extended the back of his hand toward me as though it were the most natural thing in the world.
“Come now.”
“Come now? What is it this time?”
The middle-aged man, who might have been either a secretary or a parrot, smiled with satisfaction.
“Kiss the back of his hand and express your gratitude for the benevolence His Highness Prince Felix Alexander Louis has shown you.”
Are these people completely insane?
Did these fucking eighteenth-century bastards take a time capsule here or something?
My head reeled. Then Team Leader Choi’s message magic reached my ear.
—No.
I answered through Sound Transmission.
—What do you mean, no?
—Whatever you’re thinking, no. Just smile and let it go. Prince Felix is already famous for being an eccentric.
—Wouldn’t he become even more famous if I broke the back of his hand right now?
—No. Absolutely not!
—Just the back of his hand. Or maybe only one finger.
—I said no!
I hadn’t known that a message spell could convey this much emotion. Team Leader Choi must have been desperate in his own way.
Fine. He’s a British prince. I can’t do anything about that.
I was swallowing my anger when—
“Hey, Lord Fuck.”
What now?
I looked warily at Magic Johnson, who had suddenly approached me.

I had never expected much from Wu Heixing, who was famous for his anti-Korean sentiment and all kinds of trouble. But the joy of seeing S-rank Hunters I had only watched on television in person was gradually running out.
“...No, please. Don’t call me Lord Fuck. Use my name. Would you like it if I called you Dickson instead of Johnson?”
“Hmm. Now that you put it that way, I see your point. Jin, then?”
“That’s much better. But why?”
“It’s nothing special. I was just wondering—are you really not planning to kiss the prince’s hand?”
That sounds pretty special to me.
I was dumbfounded and immediately asked back.
“Of course not. What is this, the Middle Ages? Would you want to do it if you were me, Johnson?”
“I would.”
“What?”
Enlightenment struck me like a flash of lightning.
I had completely forgotten. Magic Johnson was an American national hero—and a national gay icon.
Time magazine’s choice for “the world’s most influential LGBT person” was making a serious suggestion to me.
“So I was thinking I might express my gratitude to the prince in your place, Jin.”
He really knows how to dress it up.
But unlike Magic Johnson, Prince Felix quietly withdrew the back of his hand.
“Beneath God, we are all equal. Such antiquated customs ought to disappear. Magic Johnson, I shall accept your kind offer another time.”
Is that really something the same bastard who held his hand out to me a minute ago should be saying?
Faye Chen, who had been listening, muttered as though she found it absurd.
“My, he’s shameless. He may be one step above Wu Heixing, even if he hasn’t actually committed any crimes.”
“He’s still better than Wu Heixing. That guy should’ve been executed if the law had been followed.”
“That’s true.”
The arrival of one heavyweight after another had reduced Wu Heixing to a cowering nobody, but sparks flew from his eyes.
“Y-you—you fucking bangzi!”
“Stop going on about bangzi already. Even the national anthem gets tiring by the second verse. The same goes for me going easy on you.”
“...You’re going easy on me? Someone like you?”
He sounded genuinely unable to comprehend the idea, so I nodded.
“Yeah. I’m sure of it now.”
I had a rough idea of Wu Heixing’s level, but he had no idea what kind of person I was.
A fight began with sizing up your opponent. This one was over before it even started.
“So stop picking fights and back off while I’m still asking nicely. Let’s just focus on our own jobs.”
“You’re merely an A-rank Hunter, yet you’ve grown arrogant because Chairman Comrade favors you! You don’t even know how high the sky is—!”
“Ah.”
So that was why he had started this bullshit the moment we met.
The reason was so obvious and childish that a derisive laugh escaped me.
“Damn. You’re way too fucking old for this to be cute.”
“What are you going to do? You wanted all the Chairman’s attention and expectations for yourself, but some Korean guy came along and stole them.”
Realizing I had seen straight through him, Wu Heixing flushed with shame and rage.
By now, everyone in the room was watching us. He must have felt every contemptuous gaze boring into him.
And when people like him found themselves in a situation like this...
They always crossed the line.
My prediction proved correct.
His fingertips slid almost imperceptibly toward his sword hilt.
Broad-minded Chairman Xiao Yang had not asked anyone present to disarm, offering his trust instead. But that consideration was about to become poison to Wu Heixing.
Draw it. Don’t hesitate.
No matter how reckless I seemed, I still observed the bare minimum of propriety.
Until now, I had held back only because I had come to help China at the Chairman’s request. If Wu Heixing drew his weapon, I would finally have an excuse to fuck him up within reason.
That’s it. More. Keep going.
As though I were controlling him, Wu Heixing’s hand crept closer to the sword hilt.
Just as his fingers were about to close around it—
Step. Step.
Several sets of footsteps echoed down the corridor beyond the silent underground bunker.
Wu Heixing’s hand froze at almost the exact moment the tightly shut door opened.
The instant I saw the man who entered alongside Minister of National Defense Wei Fenghu, Wu Heixing vanished completely from my mind.
“I’m rather late. Have I kept everyone waiting?”
He had bold, sharply defined features that looked as though they had been painted with a brush, and a powerful build that even his clothes couldn’t conceal.
He looked like a middle-aged man barely into his forties, but beneath that skin lurked an old tiger and a cunning snake.
Lee Jungryong.
Our eyes met, and a deep smile spread across Lee Jungryong’s lips.

You starred in that romance movie that came out about twenty years ago, didn’t you?”
“Oh, my.
That was ages ago.
Still, it’s nice to meet someone who remembers it.”
“Would it be all right if I asked for your autograph later?
I think my mother would be thrilled if I brought one home.”
“Of course.
And from now on, just call me Chen.
My full name sounds much too formal.
If you want to be even friendlier, you can call me big sister.”
“What?
What are you talking about?
I looked you up online.
You’re five years older than my mother.”
“...You really are a handful.
Just as I heard.”
But someone else was being a far greater handful.
“You fucking lowlife—!”
His voice boiled with rage.
The man we had briefly forgotten during our conversation glared at me.
“How dare a bangzi from a weak little country look down on me?
Do you even know who I am?”
That line was fucking awful.”
Faye Chen propped her chin on one hand and looked between us with interest.
“True.
I’ve been wondering for a while now.
Do you actually know who this young man is?”
Faye Chen wasn’t the only one waiting for my answer.
Everyone was staring at my mouth except Team Leader Choi, who now looked halfway to enlightenment.
The man huffing like a seven-year-old who had lost an argument.
Magic Johnson, the Archmage from the United States.
Even the young man from the United Kingdom.
Their attendants were no exception.
With everyone watching, I nodded.
“I know.
Wu Heixing.”
When it came to media exposure, he competed for first or second place even among S-rank Hunters.
There was no way I wouldn’t recognize him.
Wu Heixing—the man who had been picking a fight with me and throwing around the word bangzi—stared at me with wide eyes.
“You knew who I was, yet you still dared behave that way?”
“Even a stray dog would know there’s a human piece of shit among the S-rank Hunters.”
“What, what did you say?”
“What?
Everyone knows your hobby is getting attention and your specialty is committing crimes, then manipulating the media afterward.”
“Come to think of it, didn’t you cause some trouble last year?
The only drug my country allows me.
You posted a raid photo on your official social media with some bullshit like that, then got caught using actual drugs a month later.
Was it marijuana?”
“Mr.
Jin Taekyung.”
“Don’t stop me, Team Leader Choi.”
“It wasn’t marijuana.”
“What?”
Team Leader Choi abruptly cut in and calmly corrected the Taekyung Wiki.
“It was cocaine and methamphetamine.”
“Oh, I see.
Thank you for clarifying.”
“Think nothing of it.
Now that things have gone this far, what is there left that I can’t say?”
Look at that enlightened expression.
Leaving behind Team Leader Choi, who had renounced all worldly attachments and was preparing to ascend to immortality, I flashed Wu Heixing a broad smile and continued.
“Damn, how did you think of planting foreshadowing like that?
This bastard is at least Wu Heishunwon.
Purple Raid.”
“What, what did you say?”
“Come to think of it, there was something else.
Five years ago, you got caught drugging and sexually assaulting someone at some club called Burning Moon or whatever.
How did you get acquitted?
Under Chinese law, it wouldn’t have been strange if you’d been executed two or three times over.”
“I heard a rumor that you’re the son of one of the Communist Party’s highest-ranking officials.
Did you buy your way out with money and power?
Look at this clever bastard.”
“Shut your fucking mouth!
How dare a lowborn bangzi speak to me like that!”
Wu Heixing’s face turned scarlet as he roared.
Someone who had been silently watching the whole affair finally spoke.
“You’re noisy.”
An arrogant voice flowed smoothly through the room.
“Frivolous and vulgar.
I hear you are descended from a noble Chinese family.
Did your elders neglect to teach you proper etiquette?”
Wu Heixing bit his lip when he recognized the speaker.
“Y-You’re...”
“You’re?”
Beneath neatly styled brown hair, faintly green eyes swept slowly over Wu Heixing, then moved away.
“William.”
At the young man’s summons, the graying middle-aged man standing behind him stepped forward.
His shoes were spotless, and the creases of his suit were sharp enough to cut.
He stood tall, surveyed the room, and spoke in a pleasant baritone.

“Everyone, rise and show proper respect to His Highness Prince Felix Alexander Louis, Duke of Cambridge, Earl of Strathearn, Baron Carrickfergus, Knight of the Order of the Garter, and Knight of the Order of the Thistle.”
Duke of Cambridge, Earl of Strathearn...
Fuck, why does he have so many titles?
At any rate, Prince Felix added solemnly, “You may all simply call me His Highness Prince Felix.”
Look at everyone’s faces.
They couldn’t have looked more uncomfortable if they tried.
Of course, the finest expression of all belonged to Wu Heixing, who had just called me lowborn.
Understandable.
When it came to social standing, how was he supposed to beat British royalty?
“So, this is...”
“Ah.”
Prince Felix regarded the flustered Wu Heixing and nodded as though something had just occurred to him.
“I see.
Are you a stutterer?”
“A-a stutterer?”
“If not, why can’t you speak properly?
Did your family neglect to provide you with speech training?”
Long live His Highness the Prince.
I didn’t even need to step in.
Having the third person in line to the British throne inject carbonated water straight into my veins made me fizz all the way down to my duodenum.
I was grinning so widely my mouth might split when Prince Felix suddenly turned his gaze on me.
“You there.”
“Hm?
Are you talking to me?”
At my question, the middle-aged man behind Prince Felix opened his mouth.

“When His Highness Prince Felix Alexander Louis, Duke of Cambridge, Earl of Strathearn, Baron Carrickfergus, Knight of the Order of the Garter, and Knight of the Order of the Thistle deigns to address you—”
“That will do, William.”
Prince Felix raised a hand, silencing the parrot mid-sentence, then regarded me benevolently.
“I have personally set aside my dignity and intervened because I have always believed that the barriers between social classes must be broken down.”
“What does it matter whether one is lowborn or noble?
Beneath God, we are all equal.
So do not take that man’s words too much to heart.”
What the fuck is this supposed to mean?
I was momentarily speechless.
Team Leader Choi leaned over and whispered discreetly.
“I believe he thinks you really are lowborn, Mr.
Jin.”
Has that prince bastard lost his mind?
As I stared at Prince Felix in disbelief, he slowly rose and extended the back of his hand toward me as though it were the most natural thing in the world.
“Come now.”
“Come now?
What is it this time?”
The middle-aged man, who might have been either a secretary or a parrot, smiled with satisfaction.
“Kiss the back of his hand and express your gratitude for the benevolence His Highness Prince Felix Alexander Louis has shown you.”
Are these people completely insane?
Did these fucking eighteenth-century bastards take a time capsule here or something?
My head reeled.
Then Team Leader Choi’s message magic reached my ear.
—No.
I answered through Sound Transmission.
—What do you mean, no?
—Whatever you’re thinking, no.
Just smile and let it go.
Prince Felix is already famous for being an eccentric.
—Wouldn’t he become even more famous if I broke the back of his hand right now?
—No.
Absolutely not!
—Just the back of his hand.
Or maybe only one finger.
—I said no!
I hadn’t known that a message spell could convey this much emotion.
Team Leader Choi must have been desperate in his own way.
Fine.
He’s a British prince.
I can’t do anything about that.
I was swallowing my anger when—
“Hey, Lord Fuck.”
What now?
I looked warily at Magic Johnson, who had suddenly approached me.
I had never expected much from Wu Heixing, who was famous for his anti-Korean sentiment and all kinds of trouble.
But the joy of seeing S-rank Hunters I had only watched on television in person was gradually running out.
“...No, please.
Don’t call me Lord Fuck.
Use my name.
Would you like it if I called you Dickson instead of Johnson?”
“Hmm.
Now that you put it that way, I see your point.
Jin, then?”
“That’s much better.
But why?”
“It’s nothing special.
I was just wondering—are you really not planning to kiss the prince’s hand?”
That sounds pretty special to me.
I was dumbfounded and immediately asked back.
“Of course not.
What is this, the Middle Ages?
Would you want to do it if you were me, Johnson?”
“I would.”
“What?”
Enlightenment struck me like a flash of lightning.
I had completely forgotten.
Magic Johnson was an American national hero—and a national gay icon.
Time magazine’s choice for “the world’s most influential LGBT person” was making a serious suggestion to me.
“So I was thinking I might express my gratitude to the prince in your place, Jin.”
He really knows how to dress it up.
But unlike Magic Johnson, Prince Felix quietly withdrew the back of his hand.
“Beneath God, we are all equal.
Such antiquated customs ought to disappear.
Magic Johnson, I shall accept your kind offer another time.”
Is that really something the same bastard who held his hand out to me a minute ago should be saying?
Faye Chen, who had been listening, muttered as though she found it absurd.
“My, he’s shameless.
He may be one step above Wu Heixing, even if he hasn’t actually committed any crimes.”
“He’s still better than Wu Heixing.
That guy should’ve been executed if the law had been followed.”
“That’s true.”
The arrival of one heavyweight after another had reduced Wu Heixing to a cowering nobody, but sparks flew from his eyes.
“Y-you—you fucking bangzi!”
“Stop going on about bangzi already.
Even the national anthem gets tiring by the second verse.
The same goes for me going easy on you.”
“...You’re going easy on me?
Someone like you?”
He sounded genuinely unable to comprehend the idea, so I nodded.
“Yeah.
I’m sure of it now.”
I had a rough idea of Wu Heixing’s level, but he had no idea what kind of person I was.
A fight began with sizing up your opponent.
This one was over before it even started.
“So stop picking fights and back off while I’m still asking nicely.
Let’s just focus on our own jobs.”
“You’re merely an A-rank Hunter, yet you’ve grown arrogant because Chairman Comrade favors you!
You don’t even know how high the sky is—!”
“Ah.”
So that was why he had started this bullshit the moment we met.
The reason was so obvious and childish that a derisive laugh escaped me.
“Damn.
You’re way too fucking old for this to be cute.”
“What are you going to do?
You wanted all the Chairman’s attention and expectations for yourself, but some Korean guy came along and stole them.”
Realizing I had seen straight through him, Wu Heixing flushed with shame and rage.
By now, everyone in the room was watching us.
He must have felt every contemptuous gaze boring into him.
And when people like him found themselves in a situation like this...
They always crossed the line.
My prediction proved correct.
His fingertips slid almost imperceptibly toward his sword hilt.
Broad-minded Chairman Xiao Yang had not asked anyone present to disarm, offering his trust instead.
But that consideration was about to become poison to Wu Heixing.
Draw it.
Don’t hesitate.
No matter how reckless I seemed, I still observed the bare minimum of propriety.
Until now, I had held back only because I had come to help China at the Chairman’s request.
If Wu Heixing drew his weapon, I would finally have an excuse to fuck him up within reason.
That’s it.
More.
Keep going.
As though I were controlling him, Wu Heixing’s hand crept closer to the sword hilt.
Just as his fingers were about to close around it—
Step.
Step.
Several sets of footsteps echoed down the corridor beyond the silent underground bunker.
Wu Heixing’s hand froze at almost the exact moment the tightly shut door opened.
The instant I saw the man who entered alongside Minister of National Defense Wei Fenghu, Wu Heixing vanished completely from my mind.
“I’m rather late.
Have I kept everyone waiting?”
He had bold, sharply defined features that looked as though they had been painted with a brush, and a powerful build that even his clothes couldn’t conceal.
He looked like a middle-aged man barely into his forties, but beneath that skin lurked an old tiger and a cunning snake.
Lee Jungryong.
Our eyes met, and a deep smile spread across Lee Jungryong’s lips.

chapters.title: Chapter 386
paragraphs: “I’m rather late. Have I kept everyone waiting?”
Lee Jungryong swept his gaze over the gathered people. Some faces were familiar; others he was seeing for the first time today.
Magic Johnson and Faye Chen, whom he had encountered several times during the Great Cataclysm. The young British prince. And China’s problem child.
Whenever his eyes met theirs, the S-rank Hunters gathered in the underground bunker greeted him first.
“Long time no see, Lee. You’ve grown even more attractive since the last time I saw you. Every time I see you, I feel like confessing my love.”
“Please restrain yourself, Magic Johnson. You’re not my type. Faye Chen here might be, though.”
At Lee’s breezy reply, Faye Chen swept back her long hair.
“Oh my. I had no idea you felt that way about me, Mr. Lee. What a shame I found out so late.”
“What’s there to regret? You’re still in your prime.”
“Thank you for saying that, but the young people will laugh if they hear you. They’ll ask what those old folks think they’re doing.”
“Is that really how it is?”
Under Lee’s gaze, Wu Heixing hurriedly waved his hands in denial.
“N-no, Mr. Lee. Of course not.”
“I’ve heard a great deal about you. Exceptionally talented and, hmm, a young man who’s honest about everything.”
“Th-thank you.”
Wu Heixing bowed his head, looking humbled by the honor.

He normally had bangzi—a derogatory term for Koreans—practically glued to his lips, along with his anti-Korean sentiment. But he lacked the nerve to show that side of himself in front of Lee Jungryong.
A bead of cold sweat rolled down the back of Wu Heixing’s neck.
“I’d heard you were coming, but I never expected you to actually appear.”
“Of course I had to come. When a neighbor is in trouble, shouldn’t we help?”
“It’s an honor to meet you, Mr. Lee.”
Even Magic Johnson and Faye Chen, heroes born of the Great Cataclysm, could not compare to Lee Jungryong.
He was the sworn brother of Cheon Taemin, known as the Jesus of the twenty-first century and the savior of the world. He was also the de facto head of the Ares Guild.
One of the most powerful Guilds in the world. And one of the three strongest among all S-rank Hunters.
Lee Jungryong.
Anyone who stood before him owed him the proper respect.
Even the overbearing Wu Heixing was no exception. Neither was the prince, despite his royal blood.
“Nice to meet you. A pleasure to meet you, Jungryong Lee.”
“Ah. So you’re that prince.”
“How impudent—”
Prince Felix raised a hand to silence his secretary, then inclined his head with elegant restraint.
“Felix. You may call me Felix. It is permitted.”
The Korean that came through the translation device was awkward, and his tone was hard to place.
But with those words, Felix Alexander Louis, third in line to the British throne, made the difference between Lee Jungryong and everyone else perfectly clear.
He had gone so far as to let Lee omit the title His Highness.
Of course, Lee Jungryong did not care in the slightest.
They’re still just brats.
The only people Lee acknowledged were Magic Johnson and Faye Chen.
Whatever their personalities, Wu Heixing and Prince Felix were both hailed as geniuses. But in Lee’s eyes, they were nothing more than chicks that had only just learned to walk.
And the people who truly grated on his nerves were elsewhere.
The Peace Guild.
Lee’s gaze shifted to one side. A deep smile spread across his lips as he looked at the two people standing there in silence.
“I seem to be running into you two rather often these days. Have you both been well?”
At Lee’s greeting, Jin Taekyung and Choi Minwoo glanced at each other and shrugged.
“Not really.”
“Not particularly.”
What?
Lee Jungryong unconsciously faltered.
It had been less than a month since he had last seen them. Yet something had changed dramatically in the way they treated him.
Hostility.
That was it.
The unmistakable hostility and wariness he had sensed from them before were gone.
As Lee studied the two people who stood before him with such calm expressions, he soon realized why.
They’ve grown stronger. So much stronger than before that there’s no comparison.
There was no doubt about it. Choi Minwoo’s qi was far greater and more refined than before—so much so that Lee found himself wondering how he had managed to grow this much in such a short time.
And the other one, Jin Taekyung—
...What is this?
Lee felt it through his skin and sixth sense: the immense qi contained within Jin Taekyung’s body, and the profound stillness in his eyes.
It could mean only one thing.
He crossed the wall.
The shock hit Lee like a blow to the back of the head. He had to struggle with all his might to keep his agitation from showing.
How?
Jin Taekyung had undoubtedly been powerful before. Perhaps he had even stood above the countless A-rank Hunters throughout the world.
He had defeated two Named Monsters by himself. It was only natural that the public and the media had clamored about the birth of a new S-rank Hunter.

But Lee Jungryong had known that Jin had not yet crossed the wall. He had known that it would take the young man a very long time to overcome the barrier blocking his path and become a true powerhouse.
And yet—
How can something this absurd happen?
This went beyond mere surprise.
As Lee met Jin Taekyung’s calm gaze, he remembered emotions he had long forgotten.
Anxiety. Impatience.
It was the first time Lee Jungryong had felt such unease since taking complete control of the Ares Guild.
Only a few months ago, Jin had been someone he found laughable and irritating. Yet that same man had now awakened anxiety and impatience within him.
You bastard...
The smile on Lee’s lips vanished without a trace. Wei Fenghu regarded his hardened expression with puzzlement.
“Mr. Lee? Is something wrong?”
“...It’s nothing.”
“Hmm. Then may we begin the meeting?”
Lee Jungryong nodded without a word, but his gaze remained fixed on one person.
Leaning at an angle against the back of his chair, Jin Taekyung muttered as if to himself.
“Well, it looks like quite a big deal to me.”
“Or not. Whatever.”
Without realizing it, Lee Jungryong clenched his fist.
The meeting in the underground bunker continued for a long time.

The Monster Wave had caused at least hundreds of thousands of casualties over the past week. That alone made it an enormous natural disaster and an unmistakable state of war. It was only natural that every decision had to be made with the utmost caution.
“Therefore, we should divide our forces into five armies and gradually pressure the enemy...”
Someone interrupted Wei Fenghu as he continued with a grave expression.
“Minister of National Defense Comrade.”
“Speak, General Liao.”
The middle-aged man called General Liao wore a uniform weighed down with medals. Stroking his beard, he began to speak.
“Listening to the Minister of National Defense has become too frustrating for me to remain silent. If we keep dragging our feet like this, how long will it take us to deal with those monsters?”
Wow...
His tone was unbelievably obnoxious.
He was speaking that way to Wei Fenghu, the Chairman’s right-hand man and the highest-ranking man with real power in the military.
As though he had read my thoughts, Team Leader Choi sent me a message spell.

└ Choi Minwoo: The Communist Party has factions of its own. General Liao comes from the highest pedigree of the Crown Prince Party, the Communist Party’s largest faction, going back to his grandfather’s generation. It rivals the Shanghai Gang, to which Chairman Xiao and Minister of National Defense Wei Fenghu belong. └ Jin Taekyung: The Crown Prince Party and the Shang...what? └ Choi Minwoo: ...If we must rank them, it means the Crown Prince Party is number one and the Shanghai Gang is number two. └ Jin Taekyung: Oh.
Until now, I had assumed that the Communist Party operated under a strict one-party system. Apparently, they fought among themselves just as fiercely.

└ Jin Taekyung: But is that really allowed? If Chairman Xiao pointed at someone and said, “That man is harmful,” wouldn’t they behead him in Tiananmen Square? └ Choi Minwoo: They do it because they’re allowed to. └ Jin Taekyung: ...Well, when you put it that way, I don’t have much to say. └ Choi Minwoo: The factions reached an agreement. During the Great Cataclysm, the Chairman from the Crown Prince Party made so many mistakes that they couldn’t very well keep holding power. └ Jin Taekyung: Ah. Pingping? └ Choi Minwoo: Yes. Pingping.
That damn Great Cataclysm changed all sorts of things.
While I listened to Team Leader Choi’s explanation, General Liao, a pedigreed Crown Prince Party brat, came out with a brilliant proposal.
“Let’s use nuclear weapons.”
“Let’s submit a formal request to Chairman Xiao and launch dozens of nuclear warheads across Sichuan. Wouldn’t that solve everything nice and cleanly?”
Would you look at this nuclear-crazed lunatic?
Everyone, myself included, stared at one another in disbelief.
Minister of National Defense Wei Fenghu’s expression was the most impressive of all. He looked like a man itching for a handgun as he answered.
“Rejected.”
“Why? Are you ignoring me because I’m not part of the Shanghai Gang?”
“Say something that makes sense. Something that makes sense! What about the people who are still alive or haven’t been harmed? What about the land that would be reduced to a wasteland?”
“The sacrifice of the few for the many is unavoidable!”
I didn’t know about the rest, but the man himself looked like an oxhead.
Magic Johnson, who had been listening quietly, suddenly spoke in his deep voice.
“The damage from a successful nuclear attack would be bad enough, but what will you do if they use teleportation magic to move the warheads? To Beijing, for example.”
“That’s why we have an Archmage like you...”

“Me? Our opponent isn’t an ordinary Lich. If that Arch Lich is more skilled at magic than I am, it could cause a truly irreversible catastrophe. Similar things already happened several times during the early days of the Great Cataclysm, remember?”
“B-but even so... A sacrifice of this scale...”
“Hey. Murderfucker.”
Bang!
That startled me.
Magic Johnson shot to his feet, his bronzed muscles rippling.
“Stop it. I like East Asian men, too. I might have to punish you.”
That’s the scariest threat I’ve ever heard.
General Liao’s face turned deathly pale as he looked around for help. But the officials who seemed to belong to his faction avoided his gaze, as did Wu Heixing, his last possible line of defense.
So that’s how this gets resolved.
His opponent was an American national hero—and a national gay icon.
Everyone seemed desperate not to become one of the East Asian men Magic Johnson liked.
Of course, General Liao’s relentless stream of bullshit had played a major role as well.
“Enough, both of you. Especially you, General Liao. Stop spouting such utter nonsense.”
Under Wei Fenghu’s direction—the Chinese man who had just put down that chink—the meeting proceeded quickly.
After gathering the opinions already raised and settling the arguments, Wei Fenghu secured everyone’s agreement before speaking with a weary expression.

“We will assign the six S-rank Hunters here to six separate fronts. Under the official force organization, each front will receive three Army and Air Force divisions, along with Hunters from the Public Security Armed Forces Department.”
Three Chinese divisions and the Public Security Armed Forces Department.
I didn’t know exactly how many people that meant, but the sheer manpower would be enormous.
When it came to the number of Hunters a country possessed, China was always competing for first or second place.
Of course, the enemy won’t be any pushover either.
The estimated casualties alone numbered in the hundreds of thousands.
If the Arch Lich had resurrected the dead as undead...
Then an almost unimaginable number of enemies would be waiting for us.
“This concludes the meeting. Everyone, move out as soon as possible.”
Wei Fenghu said the exact troop numbers and force organization would be provided in writing. Just as everyone rose from their seats, it happened.
Come see me for a moment.
Someone’s voice pierced my ear.
It wasn’t a message spell. It was unmistakably Sound Transmission.
