Yet that same man had now awakened anxiety and impatience within him.
You bastard...
The smile on Lee’s lips vanished without a trace.
Wei Fenghu regarded his hardened expression with puzzlement.
“Mr.
Lee?
Is something wrong?”
“...It’s nothing.”
“Hmm.
Then may we begin the meeting?”
Lee Jungryong nodded without a word, but his gaze remained fixed on one person.
Leaning at an angle against the back of his chair, Jin Taekyung muttered as if to himself.
“Well, it looks like quite a big deal to me.”
“Or not.
Whatever.”
Without realizing it, Lee Jungryong clenched his fist.
The meeting in the underground bunker continued for a long time.
The Monster Wave had caused at least hundreds of thousands of casualties over the past week.
That alone made it an enormous natural disaster and an unmistakable state of war.
It was only natural that every decision had to be made with the utmost caution.
“Therefore, we should divide our forces into five armies and gradually pressure the enemy...”
Someone interrupted Wei Fenghu as he continued with a grave expression.
“Minister of National Defense Comrade.”
“Speak, General Liao.”
The middle-aged man called General Liao wore a uniform weighed down with medals.
Stroking his beard, he began to speak.
“Listening to the Minister of National Defense has become too frustrating for me to remain silent.
If we keep dragging our feet like this, how long will it take us to deal with those monsters?”
Wow...
His tone was unbelievably obnoxious.
He was speaking that way to Wei Fenghu, the Chairman’s right-hand man and the highest-ranking man with real power in the military.
As though he had read my thoughts, Team Leader Choi sent me a message spell.
└ Choi Minwoo: The Communist Party has factions of its own.
General Liao comes from the highest pedigree of the Crown Prince Party, the Communist Party’s largest faction, going back to his grandfather’s generation.

It rivals the Shanghai Gang, to which Chairman Xiao and Minister of National Defense Wei Fenghu belong. └ Jin Taekyung: The Crown Prince Party and the Shang...what? └ Choi Minwoo: ...If we must rank them, it means the Crown Prince Party is number one and the Shanghai Gang is number two. └ Jin Taekyung: Oh.
Until now, I had assumed that the Communist Party operated under a strict one-party system.
Apparently, they fought among themselves just as fiercely.
└ Jin Taekyung: But is that really allowed?

If Chairman Xiao pointed at someone and said, “That man is harmful,” wouldn’t they behead him in Tiananmen Square? └ Choi Minwoo: They do it because they’re allowed to. └ Jin Taekyung: ...Well, when you put it that way, I don’t have much to say. └ Choi Minwoo: The factions reached an agreement.
During the Great Cataclysm, the Chairman from the Crown Prince Party made so many mistakes that they couldn’t very well keep holding power. └ Jin Taekyung: Ah.
Pingping? └ Choi Minwoo: Yes.
Pingping.
That damn Great Cataclysm changed all sorts of things.
While I listened to Team Leader Choi’s explanation, General Liao, a pedigreed Crown Prince Party brat, came out with a brilliant proposal.
“Let’s use nuclear weapons.”
“Let’s submit a formal request to Chairman Xiao and launch dozens of nuclear warheads across Sichuan.
Wouldn’t that solve everything nice and cleanly?”
Would you look at this nuclear-crazed lunatic?
Everyone, myself included, stared at one another in disbelief.
Minister of National Defense Wei Fenghu’s expression was the most impressive of all.
He looked like a man itching for a handgun as he answered.
“Rejected.”
“Why?
Are you ignoring me because I’m not part of the Shanghai Gang?”
“Say something that makes sense.
Something that makes sense!
What about the people who are still alive or haven’t been harmed?
What about the land that would be reduced to a wasteland?”
“The sacrifice of the few for the many is unavoidable!”
I didn’t know about the rest, but the man himself looked like an oxhead.
Magic Johnson, who had been listening quietly, suddenly spoke in his deep voice.
“The damage from a successful nuclear attack would be bad enough, but what will you do if they use teleportation magic to move the warheads?
To Beijing, for example.”
“That’s why we have an Archmage like you...”
“Me?
Our opponent isn’t an ordinary Lich.
If that Arch Lich is more skilled at magic than I am, it could cause a truly irreversible catastrophe.
Similar things already happened several times during the early days of the Great Cataclysm, remember?”
“B-but even so...
A sacrifice of this scale...”
“Hey.
Murderfucker.”
Bang!
That startled me.
Magic Johnson shot to his feet, his bronzed muscles rippling.
“Stop it.
I like East Asian men, too.
I might have to punish you.”
That’s the scariest threat I’ve ever heard.
General Liao’s face turned deathly pale as he looked around for help.
But the officials who seemed to belong to his faction avoided his gaze, as did Wu Heixing, his last possible line of defense.
So that’s how this gets resolved.
His opponent was an American national hero—and a national gay icon.
Everyone seemed desperate not to become one of the East Asian men Magic Johnson liked.
Of course, General Liao’s relentless stream of bullshit had played a major role as well.
“Enough, both of you.
Especially you, General Liao.
Stop spouting such utter nonsense.”
Under Wei Fenghu’s direction—the Chinese man who had just put down that chink—the meeting proceeded quickly.
After gathering the opinions already raised and settling the arguments, Wei Fenghu secured everyone’s agreement before speaking with a weary expression.
“We will assign the six S-rank Hunters here to six separate fronts.
Under the official force organization, each front will receive three Army and Air Force divisions, along with Hunters from the Public Security Armed Forces Department.”
Three Chinese divisions and the Public Security Armed Forces Department.
I didn’t know exactly how many people that meant, but the sheer manpower would be enormous.
When it came to the number of Hunters a country possessed, China was always competing for first or second place.
Of course, the enemy won’t be any pushover either.
The estimated casualties alone numbered in the hundreds of thousands.
If the Arch Lich had resurrected the dead as undead...
Then an almost unimaginable number of enemies would be waiting for us.
“This concludes the meeting.
Everyone, move out as soon as possible.”
Wei Fenghu said the exact troop numbers and force organization would be provided in writing.
Just as everyone rose from their seats, it happened.
Come see me for a moment.
Someone’s voice pierced my ear.
It wasn’t a message spell.
It was unmistakably Sound Transmission.

chapters.title: Chapter 387
paragraphs: It was already deep into the night by the time we left the underground bunker.
I drew a deep breath, letting the cold air seep into my lungs. As I gazed up at the star-filled sky, thinking of Sichuan in the Murim somewhere out there, a small hand tapped me on the shoulder.
“Coming with me? I’m thinking of having a light drink.”
“Now?”
“Yeah. Just us.”
It was Faye Chen. Two other members of that “us” stood behind her.
One of them spoke in a voice brimming with dignity.
“Lady of the East, might there be any Romanée-Conti among the wine we shall share?”
“I’m no noblewoman, but of course I have some. Do you like wine, Prince?”
Prince Felix answered with a displeased look.
“I told you to call me His Highness Felix, not Prince. And I enjoy wine in moderation. Especially the 1945 Romanée-Conti.”
“I don’t have the 1945 vintage.”
“Then I must decline. I shall be leaving.”
Was this guy actually insane?
As Prince Felix disappeared with his attendants, Faye Chen turned toward the one person left behind.
“You’re coming, right, Johnson?”
Magic Johnson grinned, baring his snow-white teeth.
“I’m sorry. Unfortunately, I think I’ll have to put it off until next time.”
“Why?”
“I might be deployed to the front tomorrow. I’d feel more at ease if I at least prepared my spells with Memorize.”
As expected of an Archmage. Heroes of the Great Cataclysm didn’t become heroes for nothing.
Deeply impressed by Magic Johnson’s attitude, I spoke up.
“I don’t think I can go right now either.”
“No.”
“Why not?”
“You’re neither a prince nor an Archmage.”
“...That’s not how this works.”
Unbelievable. Never mind her completely unreasonable demands—that ajumma was really something else, suggesting drinks at a time like this.
“You just cursed me in your head, didn’t you? You called me a thoughtless ajumma for wanting to drink at a time like this.”
“...How did you know?”
“Oh my, look at how pointlessly honest this boy is.”
Faye Chen poked the tip of my nose with one long finger. She looked like a beautiful woman in her early twenties, but she was actually older than my mother. It felt strange.
“Why don’t you find someone else? Mr. Lee, perhaps...”
“Lee?”
Faye Chen tilted her head slightly. Lee Jungryong had long since disappeared with the Ares Guild members he had brought with him.
“Hmm. He’s rather difficult to deal with. He wasn’t like that during the Great Cataclysm, but he’s turned into such a slippery snake. I can never tell what he’s thinking.”
She had an excellent eye for people.
Faye Chen cast a sidelong glance at another candidate disappearing into the distance before continuing.
“Wu Heixing. He’s far too rude. Drinking with him would ruin the taste.”
I gazed at Wu Heixing’s back as he headed into the deserted forest and answered.
“Nothing we can do, then. You’ll have to drink another time.”
“No. These are exactly the days you drink.”
“It might be our last chance.”
“Ah.”
I thought I understood, at least somewhat, why Faye Chen was looking for a drink.
War wore people down. It also brought unexpected farewells in the form of death.
This was her own eve-of-battle ritual after losing countless comrades during the Great Cataclysm.
By the time this crisis was over, one of us might have crossed the river from which no one ever returned.
“Well, since things have turned out this way, I’ll have to find a new target. Right, handsome young man?”
“I told you I’m not going.”
Faye Chen stared at me incredulously.
“Do you have no shame? I meant that young man over there, not you.”
The handsome young man Faye Chen had singled out—Team Leader Choi—nodded readily, contrary to my expectations.
“If you’re inviting me, it would be my honor.”
“Uh, Team Leader. You’re really going?”
“Of course. When will I ever have another chance to share a drink with Faye Chen? Besides, there are many things I’m curious about.”
Faye Chen giggled.
“I thought you were only handsome, but you’re sweet with words, too. So, what are you so curious about?”
“The Equipment you’re wearing right now. Where did you buy it?”
“...That’s your question?”
“Yes.”
“You’re quite a handful yourself.”
Magic Johnson burst into hearty laughter as he watched Faye Chen heave a deep sigh.
“Ha ha. Miss Chen, shall we all go have a drink together, then?”
“All together? Johnson, didn’t you say you weren’t coming?”
“I did. I have no interest in drinking alone with a woman. But if an attractive man like Mr. Choi here joins us, that changes things.”
“I like men. East Asian men in particular.”
“R-right. Let’s go.”
As expected of Time magazine’s choice for the world’s number-one most influential LGBT person.
I sent Team Leader Choi a Sound Transmission as he was dragged away, stiff as a board.
—Call me if anything happens.
Team Leader Choi looked back at me with mournful eyes, like a cow being led to the slaughterhouse, then disappeared with the two S-rank Hunters.
I looked around before setting off.
This was the direction.
After walking along the dark path for some time, keeping out of sight, I stopped in the pitch-black darkness and spoke.
“Come out.”
After a brief silence, someone’s voice drifted from the darkness.
“...Not bad.”
Rustle.
Wu Heixing emerged with the sound and looked me up and down.
“How did you know?”
“What kind of question was that?” I answered flatly.
“You might as well ask me what one plus one is. That would be harder.”
“Hmm. So you were more capable than I expected.”
“Don’t pretend to praise me now. It’s obvious you’re trying to pull some cheap trick.”
I had hit the nail on the head. Wu Heixing’s face flushed bright red.
In a way, he was remarkably easy to handle. I knew he was well into his thirties, but it was hard to believe anyone could be this simple-minded at that age.
“I-it wasn’t like that. I sincerely...”

“You sincerely think I’m a bangzi. You were pissed because some random Korean who isn’t even officially an S-rank Hunter was getting all the attention instead of you. So you picked a fight with your usual one-dimensional bullshit, but nobody reacted well, and that bangzi turned out to be less of a pushover than you expected. Right?”
I kept firing off words like a machine gun without giving him a chance to answer.
“So now you’re throwing out a few compliments you don’t mean and making friendly gestures, trying to pull some kind of trick... Wait. Is any part of what I just said wrong?”
“Yeah, I’ve met plenty of guys like you. I’ve been smacked in the back of the head so many times that even my useless brain finally started turning.”
When I gave him a contemptuous look, the red-faced Wu Heixing began to stammer.
“I wasn’t trying to pull some other trick.”
“Then what? If you’re thinking of becoming friends with me, fold that idea up neatly and put it away. If you stand next to shit, the smell gets on me too.”
“But what are you doing right now?”
At my quiet question, the hand creeping toward his sword hilt stopped dead.
“Don’t draw it. You’ll get hurt.”
Wu Heixing looked at me with conflicted eyes before blurting out a question.
“You already knew everything... So why did you come along so willingly?”
“Because I had something to ask.”
“What?”
I looked straight into Wu Heixing’s eyes.
“Sound Transmission. Right?”
His rigid expression was answer enough. I’d thought it might be possible, but this was still surprising. Scratching the back of my head, I muttered,
“I guess it is. Well, this is the mainland, so I suppose various martial arts could have survived here. An internal-energy cultivation technique, for example.”
“W-what are you talking about? That was message magic...”
“Oh, please.”
A snort escaped me at the sight of him scrambling to make excuses.
Other people who had never encountered martial arts might not be able to tell the difference, but he couldn’t fool me.
Come see me for a moment.
What had reached my ear near the end of the meeting had unquestionably been Sound Transmission.
I had accepted an invitation I could easily have ignored because Wu Heixing himself had sent it.
“H-how did you know?”
“Why? Was it some secret no one else knew?”
I stared at the flustered Wu Heixing and continued.

“I thought it might be possible, but it’s still fascinating. Didn’t you people wipe out all the martial artists during that whole Cultural Revolution business? I’m impressed that martial arts survived even through that.”
“Shut your mouth!”
“Oh, right. You said your family was powerful. Did the highest-ranking Communist Party officials quietly smuggle it out by abusing their positions?”
His expression sank instantly. I must have been right.

As a foreigner, I didn’t know how serious a problem this was, but I understood the value of an internal-energy cultivation technique—in other words, what was called a mana cultivation technique in the modern era.
If this were the Murim, there would’ve been a bloodbath.
He had been caught secretly hoarding a golden calf like that. Naturally, Wu Heixing wasn’t reacting well.
“It would be wise never to speak of what you just said again.”
“I had no particular intention of doing so, but your tone is pretty damn offensive.”
Wu Heixing glared at me with venomous eyes.
“Would you still act like this after learning who my father is?”
“I don’t know who your father is, but he sounds like he might have been a former Red Guard.”
“Wasn’t your father the one who went around with a sledgehammer in his youth, smashing Confucius’s tomb?”
“You fucking bangzi bastard!”
Flash!
With a furious shout, he shot forward.
An Aura Blade—no, Sword Force—surged from the straight sword already drawn from its sheath and hurtled toward my throat.
Whoosh!
The cool wind scattered my hair. I bent backward until my waist nearly touched the ground, letting the Sword Force pass overhead, then sprang upright and drove my knee into his chin.
Crack!
Teeth and blood flew through the air. As Wu Heixing staggered, I seized both his arms and whispered in his ear.
“I told you not to draw that sword.”
Sizzle. Crack!
“Aaaaaaargh!”
The powerful Scorching Yang Qi coursing through my hands shattered his armor and burned his flesh.
Wu Heixing’s scream struck the qi barrier I had spread around us and went no farther.
“You bastard!”
Whoosh!
This guy had even learned fist-and-foot martial arts. Unlike his shoddy sword technique, this was fairly sharp.
Of course...
Compared to the Murim, the quality of his martial arts is much lower.
Slightly disappointed, I reached out.
Boom!
Internal energy collided with internal energy.
His leg, whipping toward my waist, stopped dead.
Wu Heixing’s eyes trembled with shock and disbelief.
“H-how?”
“I’m good.”
I grabbed his ankle and slammed him into the ground with all my strength.
Whoosh! Boom!
Once more.
Whoosh! Boom!
Again. And again. And again.
Boom! Boom! Craaash!
The ground churned, and rocks and trees were ripped free.
By the time I stopped using him as a human pickaxe, Wu Heixing lay spread-eagled in a huge crater, looking as though his soul had left his body.
“Still, you’ve got a sturdy body, so you’re not hurt that badly.”
“Urgh... ugh...”
“Hey, are you crying?”
“Uuuugh...”
He was completely out of it.
Clicking my tongue, I bent down and searched his pockets.
After rummaging through the pouch enchanted with spatial expansion magic for a while, I finally found what I was looking for.
“Ah, here it is. A high-grade potion.”
System Acquired: Top-Grade Potion
“...No, wait. A top-grade potion? What the hell, you bastard?”
I stared in surprise at the sprawled-out Wu Heixing. Even for an S-rank Hunter, carrying something like this around was absurd.
High-grade potions were rare enough, but top-grade potions appeared maybe once or twice a year.
Their almost unreal price aside, they were so scarce that even people with money couldn’t get their hands on one.
I’ve only ever seen these online, and now there’s one right in front of me.
After a moment’s hesitation, I slipped the top-grade potion into my Inventory. Then I searched his pouch again, found a high-grade potion, and poured it over him.

“I’ve got my settlement payment, so I’ll let you off here. You’ve got plenty to be worried about yourself, so if you go around telling people about what happened today... You know what’ll happen, right?”
“Ugh... uuuugh...”
“Okay. We’ve reached a settlement.”
Just as I finished wrapping things up neatly, the phone in my pocket vibrated.
A short text from Team Leader Choi was waiting for me.
Team Leader Choi └ Team Leader Choi: Mr. Ji nTaekyung, pl ease come quickly.
No, Johnson.

This guy had even learned fist-and-foot martial arts.
Unlike his shoddy sword technique, this was fairly sharp.
Of course...
Compared to the Murim, the quality of his martial arts is much lower.
Slightly disappointed, I reached out.
Boom!
Internal energy collided with internal energy.
His leg, whipping toward my waist, stopped dead.
Wu Heixing’s eyes trembled with shock and disbelief.
“H-how?”
“I’m good.”
I grabbed his ankle and slammed him into the ground with all my strength.
Whoosh!
Boom!
Once more.
Whoosh!
Boom!
Again.
And again.
And again.
Boom!
Boom!
Craaash!
The ground churned, and rocks and trees were ripped free.
By the time I stopped using him as a human pickaxe, Wu Heixing lay spread-eagled in a huge crater, looking as though his soul had left his body.
“Still, you’ve got a sturdy body, so you’re not hurt that badly.”
“Urgh... ugh...”
“Hey, are you crying?”
“Uuuugh...”
He was completely out of it.
Clicking my tongue, I bent down and searched his pockets.
After rummaging through the pouch enchanted with spatial expansion magic for a while, I finally found what I was looking for.
“Ah, here it is.
A high-grade potion.”
System Acquired: Top-Grade Potion
“...No, wait.
A top-grade potion?
What the hell, you bastard?”
I stared in surprise at the sprawled-out Wu Heixing.
Even for an S-rank Hunter, carrying something like this around was absurd.
High-grade potions were rare enough, but top-grade potions appeared maybe once or twice a year.
Their almost unreal price aside, they were so scarce that even people with money couldn’t get their hands on one.
I’ve only ever seen these online, and now there’s one right in front of me.
After a moment’s hesitation, I slipped the top-grade potion into my Inventory.
Then I searched his pouch again, found a high-grade potion, and poured it over him.
“I’ve got my settlement payment, so I’ll let you off here.
You’ve got plenty to be worried about yourself, so if you go around telling people about what happened today...
You know what’ll happen, right?”
“Ugh... uuuugh...”
“Okay.
We’ve reached a settlement.”
Just as I finished wrapping things up neatly, the phone in my pocket vibrated.
A short text from Team Leader Choi was waiting for me.
Team Leader Choi └ Team Leader Choi: Mr.
Ji nTaekyung, pl ease come quickly.
No, Johnson.

chapters.title: Chapter 388
paragraphs: “Hey. Hey.”
Tap. Tap-tap.
Someone prodded Wu Heixing in the side with the tip of a foot. He barely managed to open his eyes, and a large figure looming over him swam into view.
“Uhhh...”
“I’ve got something urgent to take care of, so I have to get going. If anyone comes by, make up a convincing story, will you?”
“Ugh... uuuugh...”
“I poured a potion over you, so quit acting like you’re dying, you bastard. Keep it up and I’ll call Magic Johnson over to make you moan for real. See you!”
Whoosh!
Leaving behind a parting remark that made Wu Heixing’s ass ache just from hearing it, the man sped away and vanished in an instant.
It was only ten minutes or so later that Wu Heixing, still lying spread-eagled on the ground, finally spoke in a voice boiling with rage.
“Jin Taekyung...!”
His broken bones and torn flesh had healed thanks to the high-grade potion, but it couldn’t heal the pain etched deep into his bones—or his wounded pride.
How?
He couldn’t believe it. No matter how agitated he had been, how could he—an S-rank Hunter—have been toyed with so thoroughly?
The fact that Jin Taekyung had seen through his martial arts was shocking, but Wu Heixing took even greater offense at the defeat itself. He had always been fiercely proud of the power he possessed.
Me? Me, of all people?
Wu Heixing had been born with the destiny of a Hunter.

As an infant, his potential had been confirmed through an extraordinarily expensive mana aptitude test, and his family, part of the highest ranks of the Chinese Communist Party, had spared no expense in supporting him.

Enormous wealth and power accumulated through corruption. Raised in the finest environment with the best possible support, Wu Heixing awakened as an A-rank Hunter at the age of twenty. Ten years later, he achieved the astonishing feat of becoming an S-rank Hunter.
And yet...
Then why? Why did I lose to some bangzi bastard from that tiny country?
A strange light flashed in Wu Heixing’s eyes as he glared up at the pitch-black night sky.
His gaze held anger, jealousy, and a trace of fear toward the power Jin Taekyung had displayed.
They were emotions Wu Heixing had been sickeningly familiar with for more than a decade.
He shouted at the man who was now nowhere to be found.
“Was this your doing? Are you trying to torment me even after death?!”
The public and the media cursed Wu Heixing as an irredeemable delinquent even as they praised him as a genius born of Zhonghua. But a tiny handful of people, Wu Heixing included, knew the truth.
There was another—the true genius. And it was precisely because of his genius that they had kept him hidden from the world.
“Answer me, Lei Fei!”
With his overwhelming strength and noble character, Lei Fei had been an insurmountable wall to Wu Heixing.
How flustered—and delighted—Wu Heixing had been when he first heard that Lei Fei had disappeared.
But after only a week, another wall had appeared.
A wall named Jin Taekyung.
“Gaaaaaaaah!”
The bushes shuddered beneath his thunderous cry.
“I know that feeling well.”
At the quiet voice of someone who had approached without making a sound, Wu Heixing sprang upright like lightning.
“Who are you?!”
“That hurts. I thought we already knew each other.”
Step.
A man emerged from the darkness. Wu Heixing’s eyes widened.
“You’re...?”
Beneath the faint moonlight, Lee Jungryong continued with a smile.
“I believe we have something important to discuss. What do you say?”
Ding.
System Circulate Your Qi completed! The realm of Fire Gate Divine Technique has risen slightly!
By the time I finished gathering my qi and opened my eyes, the world outside was growing bright.
As though it had been waiting for that exact moment, the Skeleton Warlord immediately spoke.
“Wicked human. Are you finally awake?”
“I wasn’t asleep, you idiot.”
“Drinking before a battle. Tsk, tsk.”
“It’s not like alcohol can make me sick, so shut up.”
Drinking too much caused alcohol toxins to build up in the body, but any decent martial arts master could drive them out with ease.
And with my formidable Scorching Yang Qi, I had even less to worry about.
Come to think of it, I really did drink a lot. I polished off every bottle Faye Chen brought over on her private jet.
I had definitely gone there to stop Magic Johnson, but I wasn’t entirely sure how things had ended up that way.
“But human, how long do you intend to remain in this stuffy place?”
“I was planning to leave anyway.”
I checked the time. Five-thirty in the morning. It was about time to get ready.
After packing my things in the hotel room assigned as my temporary lodging, I went down to the lobby and found Team Leader Choi drinking coffee.
“Oh, Team Leader.”
“...There you are.”
One glance revealed dark circles beneath his eyes. His skin, usually kept so immaculate that it didn’t have a single blemish, looked rough and dry.
“Did you not sleep?”
“If you were in my position, Mr. Jin, would you have been able to?”
Fair point.
The sight I had witnessed after racing over in response to the most desperate emergency text in the world last night had been nothing short of horrific.
“Hey, Choi. It’s just a drinking game. Come on, be cool and do it once. What do you say?”
“Faye Chen! Please help me, Faye Chen!”
“Hmm... Sorry, but it’s a drinking game. The king’s command is absolute. Isn’t that the rule?”
“Even so, a kiss?! I’ve never played a drinking game before! You didn’t even explain the rules properly!”
“Oh, whatever. Number two will kiss number three on the cheek. That’s my command.”
“Choi. Stay still. I don’t want to cast a binding spell on you.”
“This is absurd... Mr. Jin! Over here, Mr. Jin!”
“Jin. Don’t interfere. I don’t want to cast an offensive spell on you.”
If I had arrived even one minute later, a catastrophe would have occurred.
I had been forced to down an enormous amount of alcohol in exchange for rescuing Team Leader Choi, but I didn’t regret it in the slightest. After all, I had been promised fair compensation.
“You remember the promise you made yesterday, right? About adjusting my settlement ratio.”
“...I remember. Nine to one.”
Team Leader Choi glared at me coldly.
“How could you do that in such an urgent situation? Are you even human?”
“Then go give him a nice, passionate kiss right now. Number two is coming over as we speak.”
He might have been number two, but when it came to being gay, he was number one in the world.
Team Leader Choi spotted Magic Johnson—a huge Black man who had just entered the lobby—and sprayed out his coffee.
“Pfft! Please, please hide me.”
“I think it’s already too late.”
The moment I finished speaking, Magic Johnson spotted us and waved a hand as big as a cauldron lid.
“Hey, gays!”
Wasn’t it supposed to be guys? He must have said it wrong... right?
As Team Leader Choi and I stared at him in disbelief, Magic Johnson approached and burst into hearty laughter.
“Don’t look at me like that. I got a little too excited yesterday and played the tiniest prank.”
“...You were really excited?”
“Ah. That came out wrong.”
“Please watch what you say. You startled me.”
“Haha. Anyway, something came up yesterday.”
“...What came?”
“Huh? No, not that kind of coming.”
“Please watch your words. You really startled me.”
“Please, both of you, stop. I’m afraid someone will hear you.”
Looking utterly resigned, Team Leader Choi downed the rest of his coffee and turned his head.
A group of people had entered through the hotel’s front doors and were walking toward us.
“It’s time to leave, gentlemen.”
Wei Fenghu, the Minister of National Defense, stood at the head of the group. His voice was rigid with tension.
At his signal, an elderly military general handed each of us a folder.
“What are these?”

“Information on your assigned areas and the forces stationed there. Of course, we have already sent them the necessary information and contacted them in advance. From here, you will travel aboard your designated jets.”
This was one of the conveniences of living in a modern age with cutting-edge technology.
A short while later, we followed Wei Fenghu to the temporary airfield, where several familiar faces waited amid heavy security.
“Did you sleep well, young people?”
“You’re late.”

Faye Chen greeted us while stretching her arms high overhead. Perhaps because of what had happened yesterday, Wu Heixing kept his eyes lowered without a word, while Lee Jungryong wore a strange smile.
The Skeleton Warlord, safely stored in my Inventory, spoke in a displeased voice.
“That human is unpleasant for some reason. This commander does not like him one bit.”
“I agree.”
Faye Chen raised an eyebrow at my quiet mutter.
“Hm? What did you say?”
“Nothing. By the way, where’s Prince Felix?”
“He left just before dawn. Apparently, a battle signal came from the area he was assigned.”
“...I see.”
Another battle, less than twenty-four hours after arriving.
The word war suddenly made a corner of my heart clench tight.
Our nationalities and upbringings were different, but knowing that human beings like me were being slaughtered somewhere made my heart heavy.
“Hey, young man.”
“Yes?”
Faye Chen had been staring at me intently. She reached out and gave me a light tap on the shoulder.
“Relax your shoulders. If they’re that heavy, how are you supposed to swing your spear?”
“Don’t blame yourself, and don’t be impatient. You can’t take responsibility for every death.”
Responsibility.
I thought about it for a moment before answering honestly.
“...I don’t know. I’m not sure I can do that.”
“Well, you certainly drank yourself senseless yesterday for someone who feels that way.”
“That was...”
“I know. I’m joking. People like us forget the burden for a little while that way. Our lives might end tomorrow—or even today.”
The content didn’t match her bright voice. The hero who had made her way through the Great Cataclysm with every inch of her body looked up at the sky.
“Ah. Perfect weather for a fight.”
She turned and walked lightly toward the jet, which was ready for takeoff.
Then she left us with one quiet remark.
“Let’s all... see each other alive.”
Her back disappeared inside the aircraft.
Magic Johnson gazed up at the sky for a moment with an oddly sentimental look, then suddenly spoke.
“Hey, Choi.”
“Yes?”
“Relax your butt, too.”
“No, your shoulders. Let’s see each other alive again.”
That sounded suspiciously like his true feelings slipping out.
Magic Johnson laughed heartily at Team Leader Choi’s wary look and boarded the aircraft after Faye Chen.
Wu Heixing followed as though fleeing the scene. Finally, Lee Jungryong, the last one remaining, swept his strange gaze over Team Leader Choi and me.
“Take care of yourselves. It would be a shame to die in a place like this, wouldn’t it? Especially at such a young age.”
What a way for an old man to talk.
It was one hell of an ominous remark.
Team Leader Choi’s face hardened, so I smiled and answered in his place.
“That’s right. Unlike certain people, we’re too young for anyone to call our deaths a good passing.”
“If you do kick the bucket, I’ll make sure to send a generous funeral contribution.”
“I’ll be counting on it.”
After a brief silence, Lee Jungryong tossed out that final remark and led the Ares Guild members away.
Now only Team Leader Choi and I remained.
I stretched as hard as I could, then patted him on the shoulder.
“Let’s go, Team Leader.”
“Yes. We should.”
“No need to be nervous. Relax your butt.”
“...That was a joke. I’m sorry.”
One more joke and he looked ready to kill me.
I was cautiously watching Team Leader Choi’s expression as I boarded the aircraft when it happened.
“Unit—attention!”
A booming shout erupted behind us.
Wei Fenghu stood at attention and saluted us, his half-gray hair fluttering in the wind.
The people filling the airfield followed his lead and raised their hands in salute.
It was a gesture of respect for the heroes going to fight for their families and friends.
Their salutes remained raised until the jet’s door closed and the aircraft dwindled to a distant speck in the sky.
Good grief.
With a send-off like that, how could my shoulders not feel heavy?
I leaned back in my seat, suddenly exhausted.
Then—
Crackle. Crrrackle.
“...swer. Respond. This is...”
A static-filled radio transmission suddenly came from the cockpit, accompanied by an alert that pierced my ears.
Ding.
System A Sudden Quest, The Desperate War Situation, has been generated. You cannot refuse this Quest. Arrive as quickly as possible and defeat the enemies!
Damn it. That’s my life, all right.
I let out a deep sigh, then shouted toward the cockpit.
“Sir, floor it!”
“Where are they?”

The speaker was an old man in his eighties. His face was covered in wrinkles and age spots. His aged body was no longer what it had been in his youth, but his eyes held even greater power than they had back then.
Even through the holographic screen, the old man’s powerful gaze could be felt. Wei Fenghu swallowed hard before answering.
“They have all departed, Chairman Comrade.”
“How is the situation at the front?”
“Because of the magical interference disrupting communications and the barriers, we cannot easily determine the enemy’s movements. However, we are doing everything possible to track them.”
“If the S-rank Hunters arrive...”
“With their strength, they should be more than capable of turning the tide.”
“Don’t jump to conclusions. Do not let your guard down for even a moment. The lives of countless people depend on our decisions.”
“Yes. I will keep that in mind.”
After the brief communication with Minister of National Defense Wei Fenghu ended, Xiao Yang, Chairman of China, sat alone in the vast conference room and sank into thought.
How did things come to this?
It was a catastrophe without precedent since the Great Cataclysm. Despite pouring in vast amounts of manpower and money, they had been unable to stop the monster army centered around the Arch Lich.
He had wanted to avoid causing panic if at all possible, but if they delayed any longer, the opportunity might disappear forever.
That was why Xiao Yang had come here today despite the countless objections within the Communist Party.
“They’re ready.”
“...Connect me immediately.”
At his secretary’s words, Xiao Yang opened his eyes.
Holographic figures began appearing one after another in the empty seats of the spacious conference room.
Fourteen people of different races and genders.
No—fifteen, including Xiao Yang.
Each of them was the leader of a nation, and all belonged to a single body.
The United Nations Security Council.
In a grave voice, the elderly Chairman called the emergency meeting to order.

“Sir, floor it!”
“Where are they?”
The speaker was an old man in his eighties.
His face was covered in wrinkles and age spots.
His aged body was no longer what it had been in his youth, but his eyes held even greater power than they had back then.
Even through the holographic screen, the old man’s powerful gaze could be felt.
Wei Fenghu swallowed hard before answering.
“They have all departed, Chairman Comrade.”
“How is the situation at the front?”
“Because of the magical interference disrupting communications and the barriers, we cannot easily determine the enemy’s movements.
However, we are doing everything possible to track them.”
“If the S-rank Hunters arrive...”
“With their strength, they should be more than capable of turning the tide.”
“Don’t jump to conclusions.
Do not let your guard down for even a moment.
The lives of countless people depend on our decisions.”
“Yes.
I will keep that in mind.”
After the brief communication with Minister of National Defense Wei Fenghu ended, Xiao Yang, Chairman of China, sat alone in the vast conference room and sank into thought.
How did things come to this?
It was a catastrophe without precedent since the Great Cataclysm.
Despite pouring in vast amounts of manpower and money, they had been unable to stop the monster army centered around the Arch Lich.
He had wanted to avoid causing panic if at all possible, but if they delayed any longer, the opportunity might disappear forever.
That was why Xiao Yang had come here today despite the countless objections within the Communist Party.
“They’re ready.”
“...Connect me immediately.”
At his secretary’s words, Xiao Yang opened his eyes.
Holographic figures began appearing one after another in the empty seats of the spacious conference room.
Fourteen people of different races and genders.
No—fifteen, including Xiao Yang.
Each of them was the leader of a nation, and all belonged to a single body.
The United Nations Security Council.
In a grave voice, the elderly Chairman called the emergency meeting to order.

Students at last freed from the college entrance exam were busy either preparing to retake it or having fun, while office workers with dark circles under their eyes packed onto public transportation.
Then, amid that peaceful, ordinary routine, a bombshell no one had seen coming dropped.
Urgent Breaking News—Major Announcement from the United Nations Security Council
The video, just over thirty minutes long, began with Chairman Xiao Yang staring gravely into the camera.
“I stand before you as the ninth Chairman of the People’s Republic of China and a member of the United Nations Security Council to speak about the massive Monster Wave unfolding in Sichuan Province.”
It was a bombshell that seized the world’s attention and shook all of Asia.
One day passed, then two, then three. Even after four days, the situation showed no sign of calming down.
There had been countless incidents and disasters since the Great Cataclysm, but the Monster Wave in Sichuan Province was unprecedented in scale.
Chairman Xiao Yang of China officially declared martial law, and with the approval of the United Nations Security Council, peacekeeping forces were deployed to the front.
The entire world was watching.
The Asian countries bordering China were especially on edge.
Korea was no exception. Once again, the Hunter Issues section of the country’s largest online forum was boiling like a cauldron over hot coals.
Here’s a summary of the situation so far.

There isn’t anyone here who hasn’t watched the Security Council’s major announcement video, right? If there is, go die somewhere. This is a genuine emergency. The supreme leader up north has probably already watched the whole thing on iTube and is lurking on this board, too.
Anyway, so many insect bastards kept asking someone to summarize a situation their own lives depended on that I finally got fed up and wrote this.
1. An unexplained massive Wave occurred in Sichuan Province. Current estimated casualties: at least 300,000.
Of course, that figure is from a week ago, so there’s probably no comparison with the number now. At this point, I doubt accurate statistics are even possible.
2. The Chinese government stepped in, but the scale was far crazier than anyone expected.
A monster army numbering at least in the tens of thousands has gathered around something called an Arch Lich.

The People’s Liberation Army and Air Force got absolutely wrecked, while more than two thousand Hunters from the Public Security Armed Forces Department have gone missing. Magical interference cut off communications and neutralized satellite surveillance, so they can’t even confirm whether those Hunters are still alive.

3. The Chinese government secretly contacted several countries and hired a number of S-rank Hunters to suppress the situation as quickly as possible. United Nations peacekeeping forces were deployed to the front two days ago, and they’re fighting desperately.
The Security Council is posting updates on the fighting, so anyone interested can check them here.
(Link attached.)
Everything below this is just my personal opinion, so feel free to skip it.
4. Anyone with a properly functioning brain already knows this, but the current situation isn’t merely serious. Mainland China is practically hell on earth.

They’re pulling every useful Hunter they can find and sending them to the front. Other Gates are being neglected as a result, and their mana levels are becoming unstable. Prices are also hyperinflating across the board.
The truly frightening thing is that if the front collapses and the monster army advances beyond Sichuan... I’ll leave the rest to your imagination.
5. So go to the supermarket and stock up on emergency food before we’re all completely screwed. Of course, I’m not telling you to hoard supplies and profiteer.
6. It felt like a shame to end it here, so I’m throwing in some national pride.
Our Lord Fuck and the Ares Guild’s Jung Dragon are active on the front. Keep hyping them up as hard as you have been.
Teh end.

The netizens who had been gleefully hammering out comments rushed to the United Nations Security Council website.
The sudden flood of visitors overloaded the site, leaving them waiting for ages. When the announcement finally appeared on the main page, they could only doubt their own eyes and ears.
“...What is that?”
A map showed the opposing lines in the standoff against the monster army. The front formed an oval, with the western side driven deep into it like the tip of an awl.

└ I just checked. It really was breached. └ Is Jin Taekyung dead? How bad are the casualties? └ No, the monsters’ side was breached. └ ?? └ ??? └ The breakthrough was so fast that the updates couldn’t keep up. └ ...Does that even make sense? └ Shut your mouth and pull down the shutters. Today is the Lady of the House’s memorial day...
The battlefield where a fierce clash would soon erupt was packed. An endless wasteland stretched before us, filled with more monsters than I could count.
The wind carried their thick killing intent and stench toward us.
“Fuck me. They sure gathered a lot of them.”
Team Leader Choi, standing beside me, answered my mutter.
“No matter how many we kill, there’s no end to them.”
It was the fourth day since we had been deployed to the western front and the fighting had begun in earnest. There was no trace left of Team Leader Choi’s usually immaculate appearance.
Covered in blood and dust, he regarded me with calm, somber eyes.
“When do we begin?”
“Well, we’ll have to hear what our little commander thinks. Right?”
The last question wasn’t directed at Team Leader Choi.
The twenty-one-year-old “little commander” who had remained at my side the entire time, Xiao Shen, answered.
“I’ll follow Teacher Jin’s orders!”
His sparkling eyes made me snort.
“You’re still calling me Teacher? You were the one who told me to drop the formalities first. I told you to call me hyung instead.”
“A-are you really sure that’s all right?”
“I told you it was fine as long as you were okay with it. But is this really all right in front of your men? You said you’re getting promoted to major general now, didn’t you?”
Xiao Shen shook his head at lightning speed.
“No problem at all! H-hyung, hyung!”
He was frighteningly calm in battle, so I had no idea why he stammered so much in everyday life.
I looked at the Hunters from the Public Security Armed Forces Department lined up behind him. There were roughly a thousand of them.
Their fever-bright eyes shone with admiration and awe for the strong.
Of course, Xiao Shen stood out above all the rest.
“Give the order, h-hyung.”
“The order, huh?”
I suddenly looked up at the sky.
An eagle circled overhead on enormous outstretched wings.
I had a good feeling today, too.
“Follow me. Just as you’ve done until now.”
“Right now.”
I stepped forward as I answered.
Crack.
The ten thousand geun of force concentrated in my toes split the ground like a spiderweb and made it cave inward.
Then, in the next instant—
Boom!
With a deafening roar, I shot forward like a streak of light.
Flamefire Path.
The cold wind heated into a scorching blast.
The earth, the wind, and the scenery streaked past. Then a tremendous roar erupted behind me.
“Charge! Charge!”
“Descendants of Zhonghua! People! Sweep them all away!”
“Waaaaaaah!”
Thud-thud-thud-thud!
Kyaaaauuuuu!
The shouts of humans and the howls of monsters rang across heaven and earth. A tremendous vibration shook the foundations of the world.
At the threshold of that chaos, I swung the White Flame with all my strength.
Fwoooosh!
The Extreme Yang Force surging from the spearhead cut through everything in its path.

chapters.title: Chapter 390
paragraphs: Whoosh!
Hot blood sprayed from severed necks in the wake of the Force.
I stepped on the body of an ogre collapsing like a bundle of straw and soared high into the air. Sunlight warmed the back of my neck.
Perfect weather for a fight.
It was noon, and the battlefield was a wasteland without a single tree.
My shadow fell across the thousand or so monsters gathered below, the sun at my back. Then I plunged toward them, spear sweeping down.
Heavenly Strike.
Boom!
The fire dragon’s claw raked the earth.
A deafening roar split the sky. The ground caved in several meters deep, sending dirt and shattered stone flying in every direction.
A whirlwind of hot air that erupted in the middle of the battlefield transformed into blades and swept across the monsters.
Fwoooosh!
System Ding. Ding. Ding...
Green blood pattered down through the dust-filled haze as System notifications announced the monsters’ deaths.
I gave my hand a casual sweep, dispersing the cloud of dust. The monsters beyond it stared at me in a daze.
“Chirrik?”
“Krruk?”
Their eyes seemed to ask what the hell was happening. I drew a deep breath and shouted with internal energy behind my voice.
“Sweep them away—!”
And then—
“Waaaaaaaaah!”
Along with an ear-deafening roar, more than a thousand Hunters who had arrived before I knew it descended on the monster army like a wave.
Crunch!
Wham!
Watching the monsters crumble without any chance to resist, I became certain of one thing.
We’ve won this battle.
The farming was over. Now it was time to harvest.
I headed toward the Twin-Headed Ogre that appeared to be the boss monster.
For the sake of my precious EXP. No—for the sake of minimizing allied casualties.
“That one’s the leader! Ranged unit!”
“Hey, hey! Hands off! I’ll handle it, so don’t touch a single hair on its head!”
I swear to heaven, I didn’t have even the slightest ulterior motive.
Well, on second thought, there was probably no need to swear.
“You despicable human. Your scheme to claim the spoils is plain to see. You never even tried to hide your greed while slaughtering my army!”
“Shut up and do your job, will you? Hurry up and make the undead slaughter their own kind.”
“I was already going to. Grow, skeletons, gro—huh?”
“What’s wrong?”
“Why isn’t my power working? Is this a bug?”
“...Where did you even pick up a word like that?”
The increasingly modernized Skeleton Warlord answered in a dejected voice.
“It seems the Arch Lich’s control grows stronger the deeper we go. Ah, a commander without an army! I cannot express the depth of my sorrow. At this rate, I’m as good as dead!”
What did this bastard think he was?
I was tired of reminding him that he was already dead. Sighing inwardly, I charged toward the leader.
“It’s a crushing victory! Another crushing victory!”
Xiao Shen shouted, his face flushed red. Team Leader Choi and I had already seen this more than ten times, so by now we simply took it in stride.
Well, I suppose he has reason to be excited.
It had taken barely two hours to annihilate an army of more than a thousand monsters.
And we had done it without a single death. It really was a monumental victory. Under the circumstances, it would have been stranger not to get excited.
“Our only casualties are twenty-three severely wounded and thirty lightly wounded. Ah, this is incredible...!”
Xiao Shen trembled like a puppy desperate to pee and looked at me with shining eyes.
“How can this happen every time?”
“Hmm. Maybe it’s because I’m strong.”
Team Leader Choi gave me a mildly incredulous look.
“Why?”
“Wouldn’t most people say something modest at a time like this? That they were lucky, for example?”
“Most people would. But what can I do when it wasn’t luck? I really am that strong. Right, Shen?”
Xiao Shen nodded at tremendous speed.
“That’s right! You’re the best, hyung!”
“You rascal. You’ve turned flattery into an art form.”
Team Leader Choi shook his head as he watched us play off each other.
“What?”
“Nothing. Then again, this is very much like you, Mr. Jin.”
What was that supposed to mean? Somehow, it sounded unpleasant.
I shrugged and turned to Xiao Shen.
“More importantly, what about headquarters?”
“Ah, I contacted them before the battle began.”
By “contacted,” he meant that he had sent several Hunters under his command ahead as messengers.

In a world like this, one might wonder why anyone was still using messengers, but there was no choice. With magic making communication and satellite surveillance impossible, our only options were to run like hell or use vehicles.
At least we still had various modern conveniences, including flares.
“They’ll take a while, then.”
“They were already following behind us, so it shouldn’t take too long.”
“You’re probably tired, but pitch some tents and let the men rest. The battle ended quickly, but fighting still takes everything out of you.”
“Shouldn’t we take care of at least the large monsters ourselves? They’d probably be difficult for headquarters to move...”
“That’s a fair point.”
By headquarters, he meant the military forces traveling with us.

The Hunters of the Public Security Armed Forces Department, myself included, would defeat the monsters at the front. Then the military forces following behind would “clean up” the area and the monster corpses.
I called it cleaning up because their goal wasn’t to collect byproducts.

It was cleaning in the literal sense. The army assigned to the western front spent most of its time cutting up dead monsters and transporting the remains to the rear so they couldn’t be resurrected as undead.
“Um, hyung.”
“Yeah? What is it?”
“I was too embarrassed to mention this before, but... it seems some of the high-ranking officers have been saying various things.”
“Saying what?”
Xiao Shen studied my expression before whispering cautiously.
“They’re a little dissatisfied with the role they’ve been assigned...”
What the hell was he talking about?
It took me quite a while to understand what Xiao Shen meant. After a long, heavy silence, I spoke with a sinking feeling.
“Don’t tell me they’re saying they want to stop cleaning up monster corpses and win some glory of their own.”
“Yes.”
“Would you look at these crazy bastards.”
The curses came spilling out on their own. Soldiers on the other fronts were dying every day, and these people were sick of cleaning up monster corpses?
Team Leader Choi, who had been listening quietly, spoke in a calm voice.
“Don’t be surprised. A chink did what chinks do.”
That hardly seemed like something he should say in front of nearly a thousand Chinese people, but Chinese people and chinks were, strictly speaking, different races.
Xiao Shen, the representative of all good Chinese people, had turned red with embarrassment.
“I-I’m sorry. But as far as I know, it isn’t all the officers. Only some of them are dissatisfied.”
“Only some of them. Right. But there’s one thing I’d like to know...”
I frowned and pointed over Xiao Shen’s shoulder.
“Does that ‘some’ include the man coming this way?”
In the distance, more than a hundred armored vehicles and tanks were approaching us, kicking up clouds of dust.
Rattle, clunk!

The vehicle driving along the ruined road bounced up and down. Through the window of the military vehicle I was sitting in, I began to see wrecked rice paddies and fields, along with collapsed homes scattered here and there.
Once the cleanup was finished, I—or rather, we—set off for a nearby small city.
“Haha, you’ve truly worked hard, Mr. Jin!”
A paunch even his tightly fastened belt couldn’t hide. A bald crown gleaming beneath the sun.
If not for his military uniform and the three stars on his shoulders, I would never have had any reason to meet the middle-aged man sitting before me.

“I contacted the higher-ups this morning, as it happens. Your victory report has thrown not only the United Nations Security Council but the entire world into an uproar! I don’t know what it means, but apparently Korea calls today the Lady of the House’s memorial day...”
I had heard enough of his nonstop nonsense. Unable to take any more, I cut him off.
“I don’t care whether the Lady of the House is dead or alive. May I ask you one thing?”
“M-Mr. Jin?”
General Liao, commander in chief of the 13th Group Army of the Chengdu Military Region, which comprised seven divisions and brigades, looked at me uneasily.
“Why—why are you acting like this? Did something happen?”
“I heard something strange today, so I’m a little on edge.”
“Who dared upset you, Mr. Jin? Ask me anything.”
“Right. What I wanted to ask was...”
I continued while staring at General Liao’s greasy, glistening face.
“I heard some officers are extremely dissatisfied because they want to distinguish themselves. I was wondering if you knew anything about that.”
“Ahem.”
So he did know.
The fact that he had known and still done nothing about it was so absurd that I felt strangely calm.
Still, he was technically an ally and a three-star general from another country. I asked in the calmest, politest tone I could manage.
“Could I see the faces of those fucking bastards?”
“Ahem!”

“I mean, what kind of lunatics throw a fit about wanting to win glory at a time like this? It’s not as if they’ll go out and fight themselves. They’ll put ordinary soldiers in front of them and wave their command batons around from the rear, won’t they?”
“Ahem!”

“What the hell do they mean, they’re sick of cleaning up monster corpses? Why? Have they seen so many that they’ve grown fond of them and decided they want to become corpses too? Maybe they won’t come to their senses until they actually fucking die. Goddamn bastards.”
“Ahem!”
“If there are officers like that, tell them to come see me. I’ll put Equipment on them and send them to the very front. They’d make perfect meat shields—”
I suddenly stopped in the middle of my tirade. Cold sweat was pouring from General Liao’s forehead like water from a sprinkler.
This man was one of those lunatics too.

I had suspected he wasn’t an ordinary madman ever since he started babbling in that underground bunker about whether or not to launch nukes. Now it was clear that he was insane on an entirely different level.
“...General. Are you in your right mind?”
“I-I mean, we need to show what we can do as well. Just a little...”

“What more do you need to show anyone? We’ve been advancing steadily without taking casualties. The Hunters clear the path ahead, and the army follows behind to clean up and rescue civilians. We’re doing a good job. What more are you trying to prove?”
Crack.
At the sight of me popping my knuckles, General Liao hurriedly waved his hands.
“Now, now! Let’s not use informal speech with each other. Considering both my age and my rank, I’m not someone who should be treated this way by you, Mr. Jin.”
“How about I treat you to a bowl upside the head?”
“Wh-what did you say?”
“Nothing. You heard me wrong. Anyway, I understand. Don’t entertain any foolish ideas. From now on, we advance slowly, minimize casualties, and rescue civilians. Understood?”
Why was this man reacting like that?
The moment I saw General Liao’s eyes rolling around instead of answering, a chill ran down my spine.
No way...
“Have you already given the order?”
“W-well, the thing is, I’m currently implicated in a military procurement corruption scandal. This is the point where I need to accomplish something on my own...”
“You fucking bastard!”
Bang!
My kick tore the armored door from its hinges. The driver in the front seat hurriedly slammed on the brakes.
Screeeech!
“Eek!”
General Liao curled into a ball and trembled as he answered in a stammer.
“I-I thought there might be monsters in the small city we’re heading toward, so I deployed some of the Public Security Armed Forces Hunters we were holding in reserve...”
I didn’t need to hear any more. Before I could press him for details, a tremendous roar rang out from the city, now close ahead.
Boom!
A massive explosion. Flames and smoke shot into the sky.
And then—
System Ding.
A System notification announced a Sudden Quest.

chapters.title: Chapter 391
paragraphs: Zhang Wei, commander of the Sichuan Province Public Security Armed Forces Department’s 2nd Company, had remained in the rear, and the operation had made him uneasy from the very beginning.
Go ahead with the army and occupy the city? That’s different from Colonel Xiao’s orders.
His doubts had only deepened when they deliberately bypassed their allies fighting up ahead and continued their advance.
“Colonel Wang, are you certain our regimental commander agreed to this operation?”
The middle-aged senior officer frowned at Zhang Wei’s question.
“Why do you want to know?”
“No matter how I look at it, something feels wrong. Our regimental commander clearly ordered us to conserve our strength in the rear and guard headquarters...”
“Ah, you mean that little regimental commander.”
Zhang Wei’s expression hardened at the officer’s mocking tone toward Xiao Shen.
“Regimental Commander Xiao Shen holds the same rank as you, Colonel Wang. And he’ll soon be promoted to major general.”

“That child knows nothing about the world. He was simply lucky. As if awakening as an A-rank Hunter wasn’t enough, he even made the promotion list thanks to that Korean bastard’s exploits. Considering how quickly he’s risen through the ranks, I wonder if he has some useful guanxi in political circles.”
“He may be young, but he’s exceptionally capable. He’s also highly respected—he’s close enough to us to treat us like brothers.”
The senior officer stroked the command baton in his hand.
“I know perfectly well that Hunters don’t care about rank. But this is wartime. This order came from General Liao, the commander.”
“From the commander himself...?”
“That’s right. So if you don’t want to obey, you may turn back now. Just remember that doing so would constitute disobedience.”

“We’re merely trying to speed up our advance. Given the circumstances, it’s unlikely there are any monsters left behind, but if there are, we’ll wipe them out and rescue any civilians in danger. That’s all. Understood?”
Zhang Wei remained silent for a long moment before nodding and withdrawing.

The Public Security Armed Forces Department was generally treated as a separate organization outside the military, but this was wartime. Defying General Liao, commander of the western front, would not be a wise choice.
“What did he say?”
Zhang Wei answered his subordinate’s hushed question.
“He said it’s an easy operation, so we should shut up and follow him. If we refuse, it’s disobedience.”
“Do you believe him?”
“If you mean the first part, of course not. But the second part is probably true. What do you think?”

“Of course I don’t believe him. That bastard Colonel Wang has no ability of his own. He only made it this far because of his guanxi with the Crown Prince Party. Everyone says he’s General Liao’s obedient dog.”
“And this order came from that very General Liao. Even if something stinks, we have no choice but to endure it for now.”
“...Damn it.”
“But Colonel Wang might be telling the truth. Most of the monsters in the surrounding area should be fighting our allies. With our current forces, we can handle a few stragglers.”
Zhang Wei looked around.

In addition to the hundred Hunters, including himself, they had more than twenty tanks and five hundred infantrymen. Three attack helicopters flew overhead, scouting their surroundings as they advanced.
Please, let there be no serious casualties.
Perhaps Zhang Wei’s wish reached the heavens, because what he feared did not happen.
They entered a small town near Suining with every sense alert. Monsters had devastated the place, but the ruined downtown was utterly silent.
The occasional goblin or Orc sprang out at them, but none posed any real threat.
“Kieeeek!”
Slash!
After killing a dozen or so monsters at the head of the column, Zhang Wei relaxed a little.
“Even monsters of different species are appearing separately. They must have strayed from their groups.”
“Just as I expected. What did I tell you?”
The officer’s arrogant tone grated on him, but this was still preferable to the alternative.
Zhang Wei silently nodded, only to stop short at the senior officer’s next words.
“You want us to split up?”
“That’s right. Under these circumstances, we should find the survivors as quickly as possible.”
“But, Colonel Wang, we haven’t even been inside the city for an hour. We should advance a little farther toward the center before—”
“Watch your insolence.”
“Excuse me?”
“You Hunters may be better at fighting, but I’m several steps ahead of you when it comes to tactics. I currently hold command authority, so shut your mouth and follow my orders.”
“Didn’t you hear me? Shall I give the order to your men myself?”
“...I’ll do it.”
“You have a detailed map, I assume. We’ll meet in the central square in two hours.”
The officer gave Zhang Wei an obnoxious smile and was about to climb into an armored vehicle when—
Whoooosh! Boom!
Zhang Wei blinked blankly.
He wiped his face with one hand, and his palm came away covered in sticky blood.
It was unmistakably human, a vivid crimson. The officer’s body, its upper half gone without a trace, toppled from the armored vehicle.
Thud.
A suffocating silence fell.
Zhang Wei was the first to recover.
“Everyone, prepare for battle—!”
“Monster! A monster has appeared!”
“Tank!”
“The regimental commander has been killed!”
The Hunters of the Public Security Armed Forces Department were the first to react to those shouts. The soldiers took a moment longer to grasp what had happened.
And waiting for them, already thrown into utter chaos by the sudden death of their commander, was an even more horrific death.
Whoooosh!
A single sound tore through the air.
A beam of light shot forward at an invisible speed and swept through the soldiers advancing in orderly ranks and files.
Boom-boom-boom!
It burst dozens of people like balloons before finally piercing the armored vehicle moving under infantry escort.
The streak of light punched through the vehicle’s hardened shell and bored deep inside.
The moment Zhang Wei saw it, he roared like thunder.
“Everyone, get clear!”
But before his voice could reach them, the deafening roar that erupted in the next moment swallowed everything.
BOOM!
The armored vehicle erupted in a flash of red and a cloud of black smoke. Hundreds—thousands—of fragments became blades that tore through everything around them.
Countless soldiers and lower-ranking Hunters who had failed to react in time collapsed like bundles of straw.
Their lifeless bodies did not so much as twitch.
“W-what the hell...?”
Zhang Wei bellowed at the people frozen like statues.
“Spread out! Everyone, spread out! Get as far away from the tanks and armored vehicles as possible!”
But the soldiers, experiencing combat for the first time in their lives, had gone rigid. The unseen enemy did not let their confusion go to waste.
Whoooooosh!
The sound of death came again.
This time, however, there was more than one streak of light.
Boom! Boom-boom-boom!
“Aaaaaagh!”
Flames surged upward, and screams flooded the air.
The more than twenty armored vehicles and tanks were rendered useless in no more than an instant.
The three attack helicopters circling overhead were also reduced to countless fragments and crashed to the ground.
Boom! Clatter-clatter-clatter.
Amid a horrific scene that could only be called a sea of corpses and blood, Zhang Wei felt a chill run down his spine.
At least A-rank monsters. And there aren’t just one or two.
Ironically, it was the most accurate judgment Zhang Wei made that day.
Sssssss.
Between dark alleys and collapsed buildings. Atop the roof of a building still engulfed in flames.
Ten figures that had appeared like black mist stared down at the hundreds of surviving humans with burning violet eyes.
When Zhang Wei saw them mounted on warhorses that had been stripped to the bone, a word escaped his lips like a groan.
“...Death Knights.”
Knights who had once been noble, only to be corrupted by black magic.
The very Death Knights who had vanished alongside the Lich after the Great Cataclysm had appeared.
Ten of them.
The first word that came to Zhang Wei’s mind was death.
Is this where it ends?
Death Knights were beings that surpassed A-rank monsters.
A hundred Hunters and a military force still remained, but Zhang Wei already knew.
There was no escaping the net they had cast.
But...
“I have no intention of dying quietly.”
Zhang Wei was not the only one who felt that way.
Unlike the soldiers, who were too frightened even to hold their guns properly, the Hunters of the Public Security Armed Forces Department raised their weapons with determination in their eyes.
“You don’t have to go this far.”
One of the platoon commanders answered Zhang Wei’s quiet words bluntly.
“And you’re allowed to?”
“I’m sorry. I shouldn’t have brought you here.”
“You didn’t bring us. We followed you. We’ve survived more than ten times thanks to you, so I’d say we were due for something like this.”
He spoke as though it were nothing, but he couldn’t hide the tremor in his voice.
Zhang Wei licked his parched lips as he stared at the ten motionless Death Knights.
“Fight with everything you have, and make sure at least one of you survives. That’s all I have to say.”
A thunderous cheer answered him.
The Hunters cast off their fear, their eyes shining like morning stars.
If they had wanted safe, prosperous lives, they could have chosen another path.

But they had joined the Public Security Armed Forces Department instead of becoming bodyguards for wealthy businessmen or working as mercenaries because of their honor and sense of responsibility as Hunters.
This was a fight they could never retreat from.
“Let’s go! Sons and daughters of the people, descendants of Zhonghua!”
Zhang Wei had just finished shouting with all his strength and was about to charge the nearest Death Knight when—
Rrrrrumble!
It was almost instinctive.
The ground shook violently, and a vast, overwhelming energy washed over them. Every surviving human turned toward it, terror making their hair stand on end.
There, where all their gazes converged, a black knight slowly crossed the ruined city center.
Red eyes flashed beneath a helmet pulled low over its face. The breath of death spilled from its bloodless lips.
“Sar, Garosh.”
Words in a language of the Demon Realm that no one could understand.
Yet in the next instant, Zhang Wei realized what they meant.
Kill them all.
The ten Death Knights charged from every direction, reflected in Zhang Wei’s widened eyes.
Slash!
The slaughter began.
Splash.
A hoof stripped to bare bone stepped into a pool of blood.
The black knight gazed down at the corpse of Zhang Wei, the middle-aged Hunter who had resisted to the very end. The approaching Death Knights knelt before him on one knee.
“Lord. Your next command.”
His next command.

Whoosh! Slash!

sentences.text: Zhang Wei, commander of the Sichuan Province Public Security Armed Forces Department’s 2nd Company, had remained in the rear, and the operation had made him uneasy from the very beginning.
Go ahead with the army and occupy the city?
That’s different from Colonel Xiao’s orders.
His doubts had only deepened when they deliberately bypassed their allies fighting up ahead and continued their advance.
“Colonel Wang, are you certain our regimental commander agreed to this operation?”
The middle-aged senior officer frowned at Zhang Wei’s question.
“Why do you want to know?”
“No matter how I look at it, something feels wrong.
Our regimental commander clearly ordered us to conserve our strength in the rear and guard headquarters...”
“Ah, you mean that little regimental commander.”
Zhang Wei’s expression hardened at the officer’s mocking tone toward Xiao Shen.
“Regimental Commander Xiao Shen holds the same rank as you, Colonel Wang.
And he’ll soon be promoted to major general.”
“That child knows nothing about the world.
He was simply lucky.
As if awakening as an A-rank Hunter wasn’t enough, he even made the promotion list thanks to that Korean bastard’s exploits.
Considering how quickly he’s risen through the ranks, I wonder if he has some useful guanxi in political circles.”
“He may be young, but he’s exceptionally capable.
He’s also highly respected—he’s close enough to us to treat us like brothers.”
The senior officer stroked the command baton in his hand.
“I know perfectly well that Hunters don’t care about rank.
But this is wartime.
This order came from General Liao, the commander.”
“From the commander himself...?”
“That’s right.
So if you don’t want to obey, you may turn back now.
Just remember that doing so would constitute disobedience.”
“We’re merely trying to speed up our advance.
Given the circumstances, it’s unlikely there are any monsters left behind, but if there are, we’ll wipe them out and rescue any civilians in danger.
That’s all.
Understood?”
Zhang Wei remained silent for a long moment before nodding and withdrawing.
The Public Security Armed Forces Department was generally treated as a separate organization outside the military, but this was wartime.
Defying General Liao, commander of the western front, would not be a wise choice.
“What did he say?”
Zhang Wei answered his subordinate’s hushed question.
“He said it’s an easy operation, so we should shut up and follow him.
If we refuse, it’s disobedience.”
“Do you believe him?”
“If you mean the first part, of course not.
But the second part is probably true.
What do you think?”
“Of course I don’t believe him.
That bastard Colonel Wang has no ability of his own.
He only made it this far because of his guanxi with the Crown Prince Party.
Everyone says he’s General Liao’s obedient dog.”
“And this order came from that very General Liao.
Even if something stinks, we have no choice but to endure it for now.”
“...Damn it.”
“But Colonel Wang might be telling the truth.
Most of the monsters in the surrounding area should be fighting our allies.
With our current forces, we can handle a few stragglers.”
Zhang Wei looked around.
In addition to the hundred Hunters, including himself, they had more than twenty tanks and five hundred infantrymen.
Three attack helicopters flew overhead, scouting their surroundings as they advanced.
Please, let there be no serious casualties.
Perhaps Zhang Wei’s wish reached the heavens, because what he feared did not happen.
They entered a small town near Suining with every sense alert.
Monsters had devastated the place, but the ruined downtown was utterly silent.
The occasional goblin or Orc sprang out at them, but none posed any real threat.
“Kieeeek!”
Slash!
After killing a dozen or so monsters at the head of the column, Zhang Wei relaxed a little.
“Even monsters of different species are appearing separately.
They must have strayed from their groups.”
“Just as I expected.
What did I tell you?”
The officer’s arrogant tone grated on him, but this was still preferable to the alternative.
Zhang Wei silently nodded, only to stop short at the senior officer’s next words.
“You want us to split up?”
“That’s right.
Under these circumstances, we should find the survivors as quickly as possible.”
“But, Colonel Wang, we haven’t even been inside the city for an hour.
We should advance a little farther toward the center before—”
“Watch your insolence.”
“Excuse me?”
“You Hunters may be better at fighting, but I’m several steps ahead of you when it comes to tactics.
I currently hold command authority, so shut your mouth and follow my orders.”
“Didn’t you hear me?
Shall I give the order to your men myself?”
“...I’ll do it.”
“You have a detailed map, I assume.
We’ll meet in the central square in two hours.”
The officer gave Zhang Wei an obnoxious smile and was about to climb into an armored vehicle when—
Whoooosh!
Boom!
Zhang Wei blinked blankly.
He wiped his face with one hand, and his palm came away covered in sticky blood.
It was unmistakably human, a vivid crimson.
The officer’s body, its upper half gone without a trace, toppled from the armored vehicle.
Thud.
A suffocating silence fell.
Zhang Wei was the first to recover.
“Everyone, prepare for battle—!”
“Monster!
A monster has appeared!”
“Tank!”
“The regimental commander has been killed!”
The Hunters of the Public Security Armed Forces Department were the first to react to those shouts.
The soldiers took a moment longer to grasp what had happened.
And waiting for them, already thrown into utter chaos by the sudden death of their commander, was an even more horrific death.
Whoooosh!
A single sound tore through the air.
A beam of light shot forward at an invisible speed and swept through the soldiers advancing in orderly ranks and files.
Boom-boom-boom!
It burst dozens of people like balloons before finally piercing the armored vehicle moving under infantry escort.
The streak of light punched through the vehicle’s hardened shell and bored deep inside.
The moment Zhang Wei saw it, he roared like thunder.
“Everyone, get clear!”
But before his voice could reach them, the deafening roar that erupted in the next moment swallowed everything.
BOOM!
The armored vehicle erupted in a flash of red and a cloud of black smoke.
Hundreds—thousands—of fragments became blades that tore through everything around them.
Countless soldiers and lower-ranking Hunters who had failed to react in time collapsed like bundles of straw.
Their lifeless bodies did not so much as twitch.
“W-what the hell...?”
Zhang Wei bellowed at the people frozen like statues.
“Spread out!
Everyone, spread out!
Get as far away from the tanks and armored vehicles as possible!”
But the soldiers, experiencing combat for the first time in their lives, had gone rigid.
The unseen enemy did not let their confusion go to waste.
Whoooooosh!
The sound of death came again.
This time, however, there was more than one streak of light.
Boom!
Boom-boom-boom!
“Aaaaaagh!”
Flames surged upward, and screams flooded the air.
The more than twenty armored vehicles and tanks were rendered useless in no more than an instant.
The three attack helicopters circling overhead were also reduced to countless fragments and crashed to the ground.
Boom!
Clatter-clatter-clatter.
Amid a horrific scene that could only be called a sea of corpses and blood, Zhang Wei felt a chill run down his spine.
At least A-rank monsters.
And there aren’t just one or two.
Ironically, it was the most accurate judgment Zhang Wei made that day.
Sssssss.
Between dark alleys and collapsed buildings.
Atop the roof of a building still engulfed in flames.
Ten figures that had appeared like black mist stared down at the hundreds of surviving humans with burning violet eyes.
When Zhang Wei saw them mounted on warhorses that had been stripped to the bone, a word escaped his lips like a groan.
“...Death Knights.”
Knights who had once been noble, only to be corrupted by black magic.
The very Death Knights who had vanished alongside the Lich after the Great Cataclysm had appeared.
Ten of them.
The first word that came to Zhang Wei’s mind was death.
Is this where it ends?
Death Knights were beings that surpassed A-rank monsters.
A hundred Hunters and a military force still remained, but Zhang Wei already knew.
There was no escaping the net they had cast.
But...
“I have no intention of dying quietly.”
Zhang Wei was not the only one who felt that way.
Unlike the soldiers, who were too frightened even to hold their guns properly, the Hunters of the Public Security Armed Forces Department raised their weapons with determination in their eyes.
“You don’t have to go this far.”
One of the platoon commanders answered Zhang Wei’s quiet words bluntly.
“And you’re allowed to?”
“I’m sorry.
I shouldn’t have brought you here.”
“You didn’t bring us.
We followed you.
We’ve survived more than ten times thanks to you, so I’d say we were due for something like this.”
He spoke as though it were nothing, but he couldn’t hide the tremor in his voice.
Zhang Wei licked his parched lips as he stared at the ten motionless Death Knights.
“Fight with everything you have, and make sure at least one of you survives.
That’s all I have to say.”
A thunderous cheer answered him.
The Hunters cast off their fear, their eyes shining like morning stars.

This was a fight they could never retreat from.

Rrrrrumble!
