chapters.title: Chapter 392
paragraphs: Damn it. Faster. Faster.
Whoooooosh!
I squeezed out every last ounce of strength and pushed my movement technique to its limit. The scenery blurred past as the ruined city rapidly drew closer.
But I knew how it had ended before I even arrived. No—I should say someone told me.
Beep.

System ??? has completed its objective and disappeared. Sudden Quest, Unexpected Assault, has been canceled. You failed to complete the Quest. As a failure penalty, a random stat decreases by 10. Strength decreases by 10.
The moment I heard the System notification, the tension wound tight inside me abruptly snapped.
It wasn’t because I had failed the Quest or because my stat had decreased. It was because I knew what the notification meant.
The deepening silence as I approached the city—and the sight that greeted me moments later—turned my suspicion into certainty.
Blood was everywhere, and horribly mangled corpses lay strewn across the ground. Even I, after countless battles had made me accustomed to death, froze for a moment.
Slaughter.
Yes. This was slaughter. They had blown people apart, torn them to pieces, and crushed them.
The evidence that living human beings had been hunted down and killed like ants made it hard to breathe.
If even I, a complete stranger from another country, felt this way, the grief and rage of the Public Security Armed Forces Department Hunters arriving behind me were beyond words.
“Zhang Wei! Langlang!”
“W-Who the hell did this? Who the hell...? Sob...”
“No! Aaaaaah!”
These were comrades who had entrusted their backs to one another. Among the cold bodies lying before them were their siblings and lovers.
Amid the endless wailing and shouting, one person who had been standing in silence suddenly stepped forward.
Thud. Thud.
Perhaps his hollow footsteps sounded especially loud because his face, so unlike its usual self, was utterly numb and devoid of emotion.
Team Leader Choi, standing beside me, called my name quietly.
“Mr. Jin.”
“I know. Me too.”
Some things had to be done even when you wanted no part of them. This was one of those times. I forced the words past my lips.
“Shen.”
“Xiao Shen!”
Thud. Thud. Thud.
Even my forceful shout failed to stop him. Xiao Shen merely kept walking toward some unknown place, searching for the killers who had murdered his subordinates.
In the end, I had to walk up and grab him by the shoulder.
Smack.
“Stop.”
A dry, lifeless voice emerged.
“...Let go. I have to go.”
“Where?”
“Where?”
Xiao Shen looked around with empty eyes before continuing.
“I don’t know. But they must be somewhere.”
“I have to go after them. No matter what it takes, I’ll find them and have my revenge.”
For a moment, I couldn’t speak.
The person before me wasn’t Xiao Shen. He was me, a few years ago.
That was why I couldn’t bring myself to say what needed to be said.
Because I know how he feels.
He wanted to kill, and he probably wanted to die too.
The deaths of those close to you left behind more than rage and grief. The survivor was burdened with guilt heavier than both combined.
The guilt left behind by a hundred lives was far too much for a twenty-one-year-old to bear.
Damn it.
I swallowed the curse lingering on the tip of my tongue and tightened my grip on his shoulder.
“You’re too late.”
“It’s already too late. We can’t find them right now. That isn’t a guess. I’m certain.”
The System notification had told me as much. There was no possibility of a mistake.
Xiao Shen stared into my unwavering eyes and murmured blankly.
“I’m too late. I really am too late.”
“I don’t want to admit it either, but... yes. That’s the reality.”
I thought he would finally unleash all the rage and grief he had been holding back.
I thought he would wail and smash everything in sight, just as I had a few years ago.
But I was wrong. The monsters weren’t the only targets of Xiao Shen’s revenge.
Rattle-rattle. Thud.
The tanks were only now entering the city.
Xiao Shen watched the advancing column grow from distant specks into looming vehicles, his eyes blazing like fire.
“Then I suppose I’ll have to kill that bastard, at least.”
There was no question who that bastard meant.
General Liao. The man responsible for issuing this goddamn order.
One worthless command from him had killed a hundred Hunters and hundreds of soldiers. Even I thought he deserved to pay for it.
But...
“Fuck. I’m sorry.”
Feeling wretched, I reached out.
Xiao Shen sensed something was wrong and tried to dodge, but my hand moved like flowing water and brushed his acupoints before he could escape.
Tap. Tap-tap!
The Paralysis Acupoint, the Mute Acupoint, and the Sleep Acupoint.
Xiao Shen’s entire body went rigid, his voice was sealed, and a deep sleep began to overtake him.
His eyelids trembled as he fought desperately against the drowsiness pouring over him.
“For now... get some proper sleep. Their deaths weren’t your fault.”
Sshk.
At last, his eyelids closed tight. The final look in Xiao Shen’s eyes held an unmistakable question.
Why? How come?
And Xiao Shen wasn’t the only one asking it.
“Regimental Commander!”
“Jin Taekyung, you!”
Whoooooosh! Shing!
Along with furious shouts, five sounds of air being split apart rang out.
They were A-rank Hunters under Xiao Shen’s command, men called company commanders.
I swept a hand toward them as they charged without hesitation.
Boom!
Compressed air exploded outward, forcing the weapons hurtling toward me to veer away.
The company commanders barely managed to block the palm force tearing through the air, their bodies skidding backward across the ground.
It was fortunate that I had restrained my strength. If I had truly steeled myself, things would not have ended this easily.
“Everyone, calm down. I didn’t want to go this far either.”
“Kgh!”
“What the hell do you think you’re doing?!”
“How dare you lay a hand on the regimental commander...!”
“This is how you repay his kindness?!”
As the atmosphere turned hostile, Team Leader Choi stepped forward and spoke quietly.
“Mr. Jin is only repaying that kindness.”
“W-What did you say?”
“If we had left him alone, the enraged Regimental Commander Xiao would have killed General Liao.”
“...General Liao deserves to die. Even if our regimental commander hadn’t done it, we would have taken matters into our own hands.”
“I agree. But I can’t say how your country’s Central Committee would view it—especially the Crown Prince Party, to which General Liao belongs.”
“He is the supreme commander responsible for an entire front. Killing him would not remain a personal matter.”
Team Leader Choi looked over the Public Security Armed Forces Department Hunters one by one.
They were a force nearly a thousand strong. I hadn’t thought that far ahead, but if they became entangled in an incident like this, they wouldn’t escape the consequences either.
“I won’t tell you to forget what happened today. I’m only saying that now is not the time.”
I felt the hostility begin to subside.
Team Leader Choi’s words were both practical and grounded in emotion. One of the company commanders who had not joined the attack finally spoke.
“I agree. Killing that bastard right now would be easy, but... dealing with the aftermath would not.”
“Remember this. General Liao isn’t the only reason our brothers died.”
He surveyed the horrific sea of corpses and blood, then ground his teeth.
“Let’s wait. Just a little while. Our time will come soon.”
“Haaah.”
“...Damn it all!”
Some looked to the sky and lamented. Others struggled to contain the grief and fury boiling inside them.
But it was clear that they had all reached the same unspoken agreement.
Once the situation had finally settled, Team Leader Choi let out a relieved sigh.
“That’s one less thing to worry about. I’m glad you stopped Regimental Commander Xiao, Mr. Jin.”
“...It was nothing.”
Fortunate. Was this really something we should call fortunate?
Even though I knew there had been no other choice, a bitter taste lingered in my mouth. I knew the rage and grief Xiao Shen must have felt.
“More importantly, it seemed there were survivors.”
“There was a middle-aged couple and one child. They apparently fainted from extreme tension, so they’re being moved somewhere else to rest for now.”
“Are there any other survivors?”
“We’ll find them soon enough.”
Team Leader Choi frowned and looked over my shoulder as he continued.
“Once that utterly incompetent commander gives the order, at least.”
Rattle-rattle.
The armored vehicle advancing with a deafening racket stopped about twenty meters ahead of us.
A moment later, the plump General Liao emerged under heavy guard.
“W-What in the world...?”
At the horrific sight before him, his already fair complexion turned deathly pale.
He doubled over and retched for a long while. The sight filled me with disgust, but it also made me think that perhaps he was human after all.
You bastard. I guess you do feel guilty.
Everyone there had probably thought the same thing.
But General Liao’s next words reminded me of something I had forgotten.
People like him always managed to exceed the limits of imagination.
“N-No. The operation wasn’t supposed to fail!”
The world seemed to slow down.
As though in slow motion, I saw shock and fury spread across the faces around me.
I saw Team Leader Choi reach for me and heard his urgent shout.
“Mr. Jin!”
But it was already too late.
By the time he called my name, I had crossed the twenty-odd meters between us and appeared before General Liao.
An operation. An operation...
I couldn’t suppress the incredulous laugh that escaped me.
I reached toward the man staring up at me as though he had seen a ghost.
Crack! Crunch!
It was over in an instant.
With pure physical strength, without putting so much as a thread of internal energy behind it, I broke both his arms and crushed his kneecaps.
Be grateful I still have one shred of reason left.
His jaw dropped. His eyes bulged.
Then he screamed like a pig being slaughtered.
“Aaaaaaaaargh!!!”
I spat at him as he rolled his eyes back, collapsed to the ground, and convulsed in pain, then turned away.
I didn’t forget to address the staff officer staring at me as though his soul had left his body.
“Report me to your superiors if you’ve got a fucking problem, you bastards.”
Shaking his head, Team Leader Choi approached with a high-grade potion.
The chair was enormous and grotesque.
That was only natural. It had been fashioned from human and monster bones.
Yet it was neither as grotesque nor as terrifying as its owner.
Tap. Tap-tap.
A fleshless finger tapped the skull decorating the armrest.
The figure was well over three meters tall, with a massive frame. The black robe draped over it rippled like mist.
It resembled a king seated upon a throne, and that description was not far from the truth.
The Arch Lich.
It was a being worthy of being called the lord of the undead—a king who ruled over death.
But the Arch Lich itself did not think so. There was another who was the true king, while it was merely that king’s loyal servant.
But...
Was it still too soon?
The Arch Lich felt a sudden pang of regret.

It possessed truly formidable magical power, but it was still far weaker than the strength it had once possessed. On top of that, the situation on the battlefield was proving more difficult than expected.
After silently sinking into thought, the Arch Lich opened its mouth.
“Are you listening, my servant?”
The being prostrated in the darkness answered.
“Yes, my lord.”
“Pull back the front line. We’ll draw the human army in.”
“I obey.”
“Go. Carry my command to every legion within the reach of my power.”
The black knight rose and slowly withdrew.
At the final moment, the Arch Lich’s chair was reflected in his eyes, which burned red.
Tap. Tap-tap.
The skull decorating its armrest was far too small to have belonged to an adult.

The man responsible for issuing this goddamn order.
One worthless command from him had killed a hundred Hunters and hundreds of soldiers.
Even I thought he deserved to pay for it.
But...
“Fuck.
I’m sorry.”
Feeling wretched, I reached out.
Xiao Shen sensed something was wrong and tried to dodge, but my hand moved like flowing water and brushed his acupoints before he could escape.
Tap.
Tap-tap!
The Paralysis Acupoint, the Mute Acupoint, and the Sleep Acupoint.
Xiao Shen’s entire body went rigid, his voice was sealed, and a deep sleep began to overtake him.
His eyelids trembled as he fought desperately against the drowsiness pouring over him.
“For now... get some proper sleep.
Their deaths weren’t your fault.”
Sshk.
At last, his eyelids closed tight.
The final look in Xiao Shen’s eyes held an unmistakable question.
Why?
How come?
And Xiao Shen wasn’t the only one asking it.
“Regimental Commander!”
“Jin Taekyung, you!”
Whoooooosh!
Shing!
Along with furious shouts, five sounds of air being split apart rang out.
They were A-rank Hunters under Xiao Shen’s command, men called company commanders.
I swept a hand toward them as they charged without hesitation.
Boom!
Compressed air exploded outward, forcing the weapons hurtling toward me to veer away.
The company commanders barely managed to block the palm force tearing through the air, their bodies skidding backward across the ground.
It was fortunate that I had restrained my strength.
If I had truly steeled myself, things would not have ended this easily.
“Everyone, calm down.
I didn’t want to go this far either.”
“Kgh!”
“What the hell do you think you’re doing?!”
“How dare you lay a hand on the regimental commander...!”
“This is how you repay his kindness?!”
As the atmosphere turned hostile, Team Leader Choi stepped forward and spoke quietly.
“Mr.
Jin is only repaying that kindness.”
“W-What did you say?”
“If we had left him alone, the enraged Regimental Commander Xiao would have killed General Liao.”
“...General Liao deserves to die.
Even if our regimental commander hadn’t done it, we would have taken matters into our own hands.”
“I agree.
But I can’t say how your country’s Central Committee would view it—especially the Crown Prince Party, to which General Liao belongs.”
“He is the supreme commander responsible for an entire front.
Killing him would not remain a personal matter.”
Team Leader Choi looked over the Public Security Armed Forces Department Hunters one by one.
They were a force nearly a thousand strong.
I hadn’t thought that far ahead, but if they became entangled in an incident like this, they wouldn’t escape the consequences either.
“I won’t tell you to forget what happened today.
I’m only saying that now is not the time.”
I felt the hostility begin to subside.
Team Leader Choi’s words were both practical and grounded in emotion.
One of the company commanders who had not joined the attack finally spoke.
“I agree.
Killing that bastard right now would be easy, but... dealing with the aftermath would not.”
“Remember this.
General Liao isn’t the only reason our brothers died.”
He surveyed the horrific sea of corpses and blood, then ground his teeth.
“Let’s wait.
Just a little while.
Our time will come soon.”
“Haaah.”
“...Damn it all!”
Some looked to the sky and lamented.
Others struggled to contain the grief and fury boiling inside them.
But it was clear that they had all reached the same unspoken agreement.
Once the situation had finally settled, Team Leader Choi let out a relieved sigh.
“That’s one less thing to worry about.
I’m glad you stopped Regimental Commander Xiao, Mr.
Jin.”
“...It was nothing.”
Fortunate.
Was this really something we should call fortunate?
Even though I knew there had been no other choice, a bitter taste lingered in my mouth.
I knew the rage and grief Xiao Shen must have felt.
“More importantly, it seemed there were survivors.”
“There was a middle-aged couple and one child.
They apparently fainted from extreme tension, so they’re being moved somewhere else to rest for now.”
“Are there any other survivors?”
“We’ll find them soon enough.”
Team Leader Choi frowned and looked over my shoulder as he continued.
“Once that utterly incompetent commander gives the order, at least.”
Rattle-rattle.
The armored vehicle advancing with a deafening racket stopped about twenty meters ahead of us.
A moment later, the plump General Liao emerged under heavy guard.
“W-What in the world...?”
At the horrific sight before him, his already fair complexion turned deathly pale.
He doubled over and retched for a long while.
The sight filled me with disgust, but it also made me think that perhaps he was human after all.
You bastard.
I guess you do feel guilty.
Everyone there had probably thought the same thing.
But General Liao’s next words reminded me of something I had forgotten.
People like him always managed to exceed the limits of imagination.
“N-No.
The operation wasn’t supposed to fail!”
The world seemed to slow down.
As though in slow motion, I saw shock and fury spread across the faces around me.
I saw Team Leader Choi reach for me and heard his urgent shout.
“Mr.
Jin!”
But it was already too late.
By the time he called my name, I had crossed the twenty-odd meters between us and appeared before General Liao.
An operation.
An operation...
I couldn’t suppress the incredulous laugh that escaped me.
I reached toward the man staring up at me as though he had seen a ghost.
Crack!
Crunch!
It was over in an instant.
With pure physical strength, without putting so much as a thread of internal energy behind it, I broke both his arms and crushed his kneecaps.
Be grateful I still have one shred of reason left.
His jaw dropped.
His eyes bulged.
Then he screamed like a pig being slaughtered.
“Aaaaaaaaargh!!!”
I spat at him as he rolled his eyes back, collapsed to the ground, and convulsed in pain, then turned away.
I didn’t forget to address the staff officer staring at me as though his soul had left his body.
“Report me to your superiors if you’ve got a fucking problem, you bastards.”
Shaking his head, Team Leader Choi approached with a high-grade potion.
The chair was enormous and grotesque.
That was only natural.
It had been fashioned from human and monster bones.
Yet it was neither as grotesque nor as terrifying as its owner.
Tap.
Tap-tap.
A fleshless finger tapped the skull decorating the armrest.
The figure was well over three meters tall, with a massive frame.
The black robe draped over it rippled like mist.
It resembled a king seated upon a throne, and that description was not far from the truth.
The Arch Lich.
It was a being worthy of being called the lord of the undead—a king who ruled over death.
But the Arch Lich itself did not think so.
There was another who was the true king, while it was merely that king’s loyal servant.
But...
Was it still too soon?
The Arch Lich felt a sudden pang of regret.
It possessed truly formidable magical power, but it was still far weaker than the strength it had once possessed.
On top of that, the situation on the battlefield was proving more difficult than expected.
After silently sinking into thought, the Arch Lich opened its mouth.
“Are you listening, my servant?”
The being prostrated in the darkness answered.
“Yes, my lord.”
“Pull back the front line.
We’ll draw the human army in.”
“I obey.”
“Go.
Carry my command to every legion within the reach of my power.”
The black knight rose and slowly withdrew.
At the final moment, the Arch Lich’s chair was reflected in his eyes, which burned red.
Tap.
Tap-tap.
The skull decorating its armrest was far too small to have belonged to an adult.

chapters.title: Chapter 393
paragraphs: War is a succession of battles.
When a battle that has left countless deaths and rivers of blood finally ends, victory and defeat are decided. The survivors gather in one place and prepare for tomorrow’s battle.
That was why the commanders of the eastern and western fronts in Sichuan Province had gathered together.
“The casualties are too high.”
The first to break the silence was a middle-aged soldier who looked to be in his forties. His uniform caked with dried blood, he continued in a weary voice.
“We barely managed to hold the high ground, but we lost more than three thousand troops today alone.”
A victory that had left nothing but wounds.

Three thousand troops was an enormous loss in itself, but the greater problem was that Hunters accounted for more than thirty percent of the dead, including the commander and several high-ranking officers.
Even considering the threefold disparity in troop strength, the blow was devastating.
“Has headquarters sent a reply?”
“Yes. They held an internal meeting and said they’d dispatch a new commander before dawn.”
“That’s a relief, at least. Then do you happen to know who the new commander will be...?”
As they spoke amid the somber atmosphere, someone abruptly cut in.
“A relief? Do you all really think so?”
The words of someone who had remained silent carried weight. Even more so when that person was a living hero of the Great Cataclysm and an S-rank Hunter.

“Half the command staff, including the commander, were torn apart by flying monsters. The troops under them panicked, driving the casualties even higher. Can you really call any part of that a relief?”
The people flinched beneath the gaze filled with an irresistible aura.
“W-Well, the thing is...”
“The fact that you’re trying to make excuses means you know I’m right. But...”
A chilling voice slipped between red lips.
Faye Chen’s gaze swept across the room, then stopped abruptly on one man.
“Why don’t you have any excuses?”
After a brief silence, Wu Heixing swirled the liquor in his crystal glass.
“Why should I?”
“Why? Well...”
Faye Chen’s eyes darkened.
“Maybe because some fucking idiot abandoned his assigned position, giving the flying monsters waiting for that exact moment the chance to tear command headquarters apart?”
“...I went to support the front line.”

Wu Heixing’s answer was nothing more than a pathetic excuse. When he abandoned the rear, the troops on the front line under Faye Chen’s command had been successfully holding back the endless assault of the monster army.

“Oh, right. There was that, too. You charged deep into enemy territory like some clueless brat because you wanted all the glory, and the formation collapsed. Those kids who went after you to save your ass—did you even know they never found their bodies?”
“People live and die on the battlefield all the time.”
“Of course. It happens all the time.”
Faye Chen continued quietly.
“People like you dying without anyone knowing used to be even more common. Come to think of it, the world has gotten pretty nice. If this had been during the Great Cataclysm...”
But Faye Chen never got to finish.
Crack! Crash!
A sharp crack rang out as crystal shards flew in every direction.
Having crushed the glass in his hand, Wu Heixing slowly rose to his feet.
“That’s enough.”
“Enough? You’re getting awfully informal with me.”
“There’s a limit to how much I’ll tolerate, Faye Chen.”
“Go on, then. Keep talking. Just remember—the more casual your tone gets, the shorter your lifespan becomes.”
“How dare some Hong Konger who’s practically a traitor—!”
“Ah. If you mean the Hong Konger who cleaned up the front line you shat all over, then yes, I suppose that’s me.”
Whoooooosh.
The tremendous auras pouring from the two of them engulfed the room. The pressure was so overwhelming that the others could barely breathe.
Then, in the next instant, the brief standoff between the two S-rank Hunters ended as a mocking smile touched Faye Chen’s lips.
“You’re scared and exhausted, but you still want the glory. That’s why you’re growing more desperate by the day, isn’t it?”
“What?”

“Kid, that’s what war does. It drives people to the brink and tests them. You need a strong mind to endure a hell like this. Of course it’s hard for a spoiled child like you who’s always done whatever he pleased.”
Wu Heixing’s face twisted grotesquely. Every word out of Faye Chen’s mouth had struck home.
“An S-rank Hunter? So what? Mentally, you’re nothing but a seven-year-old child. In a war like this, we’d be better off without someone like you.”
“Shut up! What the hell do you know...?”
“What do I know? You’re asking me that?”
Faye Chen’s derisive snort made Wu Heixing’s face flush bright red.
He had been born with wealth and power in both hands, but his opponent was a war hero who had fought her way through the Great Cataclysm.
The media discriminated against Faye Chen for being from Hong Kong, but when it came to experience, she was someone Wu Heixing could never hope to match.
“Why aren’t you answering?”
Wu Heixing clenched his teeth, refusing to respond, and swept his gaze around the room.
No one had bothered to say anything aloud, but the looks in their eyes resembled Faye Chen’s.
These fucking bastards...!
Even more infuriating was that some of them belonged to the Crown Prince Party and had close ties to Wu Heixing.
The Crown Prince Party was the largest faction within the Chinese Communist Party. As a blood descendant of one of its most prominent leaders, Wu Heixing felt betrayed to the bone.
“I’ll remember what happened today. Every last bit of it.”
Leaving those furious words behind, Wu Heixing turned away.
As he departed reeking of liquor, Faye Chen’s quiet voice flew after him and struck him squarely in the back.
“Remember this, too. Today is the last day I’ll tolerate a child’s reckless bravado. If this happens again... I won’t forgive you.”
Grind.
Wu Heixing returned to his quarters grinding his teeth. The first thing he did was smash everything in sight.
Boom! Boom-boom-boom!
“Fucking Hong Kong bitch! Fucking traitorous bastards!”
The expensive luxury furnishings he had brought over on his private jet despite the chaos shattered into pieces.
He spent a long while stomping and smashing everything within reach, screaming like a madman. At last, breathing heavily, Wu Heixing threw himself onto the bed.
“Damn it.”
His anger refused to subside.
Far from fading, it burned hotter the more he thought about it. His heart pounded so violently that his vision nearly went white.
How dare they treat me like this?
He had been born into the family of one of the most powerful men in China and had risen all the way to this point.
Once he became an S-rank Hunter, the world had belonged to him.
No matter what major disaster he caused, the worst that happened was being summoned by his father and scolded a few times. He had never cared about the criticism from the public or opposing factions.
I’m Wu Heixing. Wu Heixing!
An S-rank Hunter was the face of a nation, another name for its national power. No matter how harshly public opinion condemned him, that fact remained unchanged.
That was reality.
Was that why he had become more passionate about media interviews and parties than smelly, dirty raids? Why he had stopped training and started using drugs?
But the first war of his life was chaos. Watching the monster armies surge forward without end, day after day, left him struggling to breathe.
For someone who had followed an elite path paved with diamonds, it was an unbearably harsh environment.
On top of that, one person’s influence lingered behind Wu Heixing’s repeated mistakes.
Jin Taekyung.
The second wall he had encountered in his life—and one far greater than Lei Fei, the object of his long-standing jealousy.
The shadow Jin Taekyung cast was vast and dark.
The fear carved deep into Wu Heixing’s mind by that one-sided defeat would never leave him as long as Jin Taekyung remained.
Right. As long as that peninsula bangzi doesn’t disappear...
An inscrutable light flashed in Wu Heixing’s eyes as he stared at the ceiling.
He smiled, recalling the conversation he had shared with Lee Jungryong on the night of his crushing defeat. His boiling anger had already vanished without a trace.
Just wait and see. We’ll find out who gets the last laugh.
Once his mind calmed, the fatigue he had temporarily forgotten came rushing back and weighed down his eyelids. As drowsiness overcame him, Wu Heixing suddenly thought:
Damn it. How many more battles like today’s are we going to have to fight?
A short while later, Wu Heixing fell fast asleep, unaware that countless monster armies were withdrawing from the front lines under cover of the pitch-dark night.
The mass withdrawal was taking place simultaneously across every front in Sichuan Province.
“...Phew.”
Xiao Shen let out a sigh, his eyes red and bloodshot.
He had spent the night with his Sleep Acupoint struck and had only regained consciousness two hours ago.
The moment he opened his eyes, he had gone berserk, shouting that he was going to kill General Liao. Team Leader Choi and I had sweated bullets trying to calm him down.
“Xiao Shen, are you all right?”
“Yeah. Have you calmed down a little?”
Xiao Shen answered.
“Yes. I couldn’t put any strength into my body when I first woke up, but I’m fine now. I’ve got more than enough strength to rip that bastard’s head off.”
Calm, my ass.
Still, despite what he said, only his fists were trembling. It didn’t look like he planned to play golf with General Liao’s head right this second, so I breathed a little easier.
“I’ll say it again. I didn’t want to do that to you. The timing was just bad.”
Xiao Shen was silent for a moment before nodding.
“I know, hyung. I also know you stepped in for me.”
“When did you hear about that?”
“The company commanders came and told me. They said you flew into a rage and broke General Liao’s arms and legs.”
“...It wasn’t exactly something I should’ve done after stopping you. But, well, that’s how it turned out.”
Team Leader Choi cut in stiffly.
“If you knew you shouldn’t do it, why did you?”
“Well, uh... I lost my head for a moment.”
“We’re fortunate the current situation is so chaotic. Otherwise, this could have become a serious problem.”
“Lucky for us, then. If things weren’t like this, that bastard would’ve died by my hand already.”
An incompetent commander was more frightening than an enemy.
General Liao had thrown away nearly a thousand lives, then started whining about a failed operation and military glory. He deserved to die.
“It all worked out. His injuries are almost healed thanks to the potion, and they have plenty of reasons to feel guilty themselves, so they’ll quietly let it slide.”

“Grudges last a long time, Mr. Jin. He’s a high-ranking general in the Central Military Commission and a blue-blooded scion of the Crown Prince Party, notorious for holding grudges. There’s every chance this will cause trouble later.”
“What can we do? The water’s already spilled. We’ll deal with it if trouble comes.”
Team Leader Choi was shaking his head in disbelief at my nonchalant answer when Xiao Shen spoke in a low voice.
“Don’t worry. What you’re concerned about, Mr. Choi, won’t happen.”
“Hm?”
“Xiao Shen, have you heard something?”
“Not so much heard...”
After a moment’s hesitation, Xiao Shen shook his head, his expression stiff.
“Um... it’s merely my personal opinion.”
What was that suspicious smell?
Team Leader Choi and I were staring at Xiao Shen doubtfully when—
“M-M-M-May I come in?”
“Did an earthquake hit your vocal cords? Come in.”
Only then did the person who had been pacing outside the tent cautiously step inside.
It was a familiar face—one of General Liao’s closest staff officers.
He was also the man who had pissed himself the day before when he saw me break his superior’s limbs.
“Well, if it isn’t the great nation’s little pants-pisser. What brings you here?”
“S-S-S-Spit it out already. What are you trying to say? Please, just speak properly.”
The staff officer flinched, swallowed hard, and answered.
“A-A guest has arrived.”
“A guest?”
“Yes.”
“Who? Are visitors even allowed here?”
It can’t be Mom and Hayeon, can it?
That absurd thought had just crossed my mind when the staff officer’s answer came flying at me.
“Magic Johnson, a Hunter from the United States, has come to see you.”
I could feel Team Leader Choi clench his butt beside me.

General Liao had thrown away nearly a thousand lives, then started whining about a failed operation and military glory.
He deserved to die.
“It all worked out.
His injuries are almost healed thanks to the potion, and they have plenty of reasons to feel guilty themselves, so they’ll quietly let it slide.”
“Grudges last a long time, Mr.
Jin.
He’s a high-ranking general in the Central Military Commission and a blue-blooded scion of the Crown Prince Party, notorious for holding grudges.
There’s every chance this will cause trouble later.”
“What can we do?
The water’s already spilled.
We’ll deal with it if trouble comes.”
Team Leader Choi was shaking his head in disbelief at my nonchalant answer when Xiao Shen spoke in a low voice.
“Don’t worry.
What you’re concerned about, Mr.
Choi, won’t happen.”
“Hm?”
“Xiao Shen, have you heard something?”
“Not so much heard...”
After a moment’s hesitation, Xiao Shen shook his head, his expression stiff.
“Um... it’s merely my personal opinion.”
What was that suspicious smell?
Team Leader Choi and I were staring at Xiao Shen doubtfully when—
“M-M-M-May I come in?”
“Did an earthquake hit your vocal cords?
Come in.”
Only then did the person who had been pacing outside the tent cautiously step inside.
It was a familiar face—one of General Liao’s closest staff officers.
He was also the man who had pissed himself the day before when he saw me break his superior’s limbs.
“Well, if it isn’t the great nation’s little pants-pisser.
What brings you here?”
“S-S-S-Spit it out already.
What are you trying to say?
Please, just speak properly.”
The staff officer flinched, swallowed hard, and answered.
“A-A guest has arrived.”
“A guest?”
“Yes.”
“Who?
Are visitors even allowed here?”
It can’t be Mom and Hayeon, can it?
That absurd thought had just crossed my mind when the staff officer’s answer came flying at me.
“Magic Johnson, a Hunter from the United States, has come to see you.”
I could feel Team Leader Choi clench his butt beside me.

chapters.title: Chapter 394
paragraphs: As expected, the mainland was on an entirely different scale.
I’d been told this was a small city, but its size and population far exceeded anything I had imagined once we entered it.
That also meant quite a few buildings had survived the monster army’s rampage intact.
This one included.
At the entrance to the municipal hospital, which was currently serving as a temporary headquarters, a tall white Hunter spotted Team Leader Choi and me and approached.
“I’ve been waiting for you.”
“Did Magic Johnson send you...?”
“Yes. My name is Michael Johnson. Feel free to call me Michael.”
“Ah, sure.”
Is everyone over there named Johnson? Is there some kind of Johnson family reunion in L.A.?
Still wondering, I shook Michael’s hand.
He beamed at me.
“What?”
“I’m a huge fan of yours. Lord Fuck.”
“...I’d appreciate it if you called me Jin instead of Lord Fuck.”
“Why? I’d love a nickname like that.”
“Then should I call you Little Johnson?”
Michael’s face turned dead serious.
“Nope.”
Look how firm he is.
I stared at him in disbelief.
“It’s the same principle. So please call me Jin.”
“Ah, okay.”
That Lord Fuck nickname is really spreading to every corner of the globe.

Cheon Taemin had defeated the Demon King, been hailed as the savior of the twenty-first century, and earned the incredibly badass title Slayer. Even if I killed a Demon God instead of a Demon King, I’d probably still be Lord Fuck.
At best, I might evolve into Lord Fuuuck.
“Don’t take it too hard. Lord Fuck has a certain warmth and charm to it, don’t you think?”
“Team Leader, are you making fun of me?”
“Of course not.”
Team Leader Choi let out a quiet laugh, and Michael called out to him.
“Choi. You came too.”
“You know me?”
“Of course. Word of how much Johnson likes you has already spread throughout the Guild.”
I jabbed Team Leader Choi in the ribs as his expression darkened.
“Don’t take it too hard. Johnson’s Johnson likes you, Team Leader.”
“...Mr. Jin. You just said Johnson twice.”
“Did I? Must’ve slipped out.”
Pretending not to notice Team Leader Choi’s sharp glare, I asked Michael, “Where’s Johnson?”
“Ah, I’ll show you.”
We followed him inside. The moment we entered the lobby, the murmuring abruptly died away, and every eye in the room swung toward us.
I’d heard that a few civilians rescued during the night were here, but since this was a temporary headquarters, the place seemed to be filled almost entirely with soldiers.
“The whole atmosphere changes when Jin shows up.”
“I was already famous, but I’m probably a little more famous after yesterday.”
“Oh, did you kill a Named Monster or something?”
I shrugged at Michael’s question.
“Something like that.”
Considering General Liao’s position within the military, he was a Named Monster in his own right.
His side had issued a gag order, but somehow the rumor had spread everywhere. Everywhere I went, I could hear soldiers whispering under their breath.
“Did you hear? Yesterday, Mr. Jin did something to the commander...”
“I heard the story, but wasn’t it just a rumor?”
“They say it’s true. The Hunters confirmed it, and apparently so did one of the headquarters operations staff. Rao Yang heard the whole thing loud and clear.”
“Huh. If that’s true, I’m disappointed in Mr. Jin.”
“Me too. I thought he was a hero of the people.”
The reaction was exactly what I’d expected.
Birds of a feather flock together, and people always side with their own.
Naturally, the soldiers wouldn’t be too happy about me mauling their direct superior...
“He shouldn’t have stopped at breaking the man’s limbs. He should’ve ripped his head off.”
“Exactly. How many people died because of that pig bastard?”

“I heard he took a huge cut from the latest defense procurement scandal too. That’s why he’s keeping quiet and letting this slide even after getting his arms and legs broken. Following Mr. Jin around is the only way he can pick up a few scraps of military glory and save his own skin.”
“That thieving son of a bitch. A bastard like him should be hanged in Tiananmen Square.”
...What? They seem to like me quite a lot.
It wasn’t just the enlisted soldiers. Even the officers were whispering among themselves.
They called General Liao an incompetent pig who had sacrificed his troops. Some said they finally understood why they were still using canteens manufactured during the Chinese Civil War.

Combined with General Liao’s existing reputation, everything that had recently come to light opened the floodgates. Remarks that could have gotten them arrested for insulting a superior poured out one after another.
“The mood is favorable. At this rate, we shouldn’t have to worry about the consequences.”
Team Leader Choi spoke as he walked beside me. Still dazed, I answered, “Yeah. If I’d known, I would’ve hit him a few more times.”
“Hmm. I do still have a few high-grade potions left.”
“Look at you, Team Leader. You’re getting good at jokes.”
“I wouldn’t say I was entirely joking.”
“Huh?”
What’s gotten into this guy all of a sudden?
Team Leader Choi stared straight at me as I struggled to process his unexpected response.

“Mr. Jin, you are indisputably an S-rank Hunter. You’re the dream and symbol of ordinary citizens, as well as a celebrity with enormous public support. General Liao, on the other hand, is the embodiment of the corrupt establishment. Anyone who tries to come after you will have to be prepared to pay an enormous price.”
“So you’re saying it wouldn’t matter if I hit him a little harder?”
“There would still be consequences, but someone like General Liao, who is already on the verge of ruin, won’t be able to drag you down with him.”
“Seriously? Just a few hours ago, you were telling me not to cause trouble.”
“Even the best sports car will crash if all you do is step on the accelerator. You need someone beside you to hit the brakes, like me. And...”
Team Leader Choi continued in a low voice.
“Sometimes you also need to maintain the track so the sports car can run properly. Like now.”
“Too many people witnessed what happened yesterday. If the gag order was bound to fail anyway, I thought it would be better to spread the story as quickly as possible.”
It didn’t take long for the question mark in my head to turn into an exclamation point.
“Team Leader, did you...?”
Team Leader Choi smiled at my slack-jawed expression.
“Getting ahead of the story and spreading the version most favorable to us. It’s a method Vice Guild Master Lee Jungryong often uses.”
Now everything fit together.
I’d wondered how the rumor had spread so quickly that the gag order was already meaningless. Team Leader Choi had clearly laid the groundwork in advance.
The Hunters from the Public Security Armed Forces Department already despised General Liao, so getting them to cooperate must have been easy. As for the soldiers...
He paid them.
In the end, it always came down to money. Team Leader Choi had paid people to talk, and they had spread the rumor in whatever way was most favorable to us.
Besides, wasn’t the military a place crawling with microphones and loudspeakers?
Rumors spread fast.

Ten people opened their mouths, a hundred people heard them, and those hundred passed the story on to a thousand more. Add a generous sprinkling of MSG along the way, and before long the inflated rumor became accepted as fact.
But he thought of all that and pulled it off overnight?
I gazed at Team Leader Choi with newfound respect.
“Team Leader Choi, are you Zhuge Kongming? Zhang Liang?”
“This was nothing special.”
“Team Leader Come, I think I’m about to Choi.”
“...Stop it.”
While we talked, Michael, who had been walking ahead of us, came to a stop.
Knock, knock.
“Johnson. It’s Michael.”
Two auras, one large and one small, stirred beyond the door marked VIP Private Room. Then a deep, cheerful voice called from inside.
“Oh, come on in.”
“You heard him. My job ends here, so I’ll be going.”
Michael shrugged at us and stepped aside.
Team Leader Choi’s butt had already clenched tight, so I opened the sliding door for him.
Rattle.
Two people came into view.
“Haha! So we meet again, charming young men!”
The first was a huge Black man who strode toward us and extended a hand as large as a pot lid—Magic Johnson.
And then...
“Eek!”
A plump pig recoiled in horror the moment he saw me.
I glanced at General Liao, whose double chin was quivering, then took Magic Johnson’s hand and whispered, “When did you get here?”
“About... thirty minutes ago?”
“What about the southern front you’re in charge of? And why didn’t you come find us right away? Why are you sitting around with this guy?”
“Hold on. I’ll answer your questions one at a time. But first, I need to say hello to Choi.”
Snatch.
Like a hawk swooping down on its prey, Magic Johnson seized Team Leader Choi’s hand and greeted him warmly.
“How have you been? Did you think about me a lot?”
Team Leader Choi’s answer was one hundred percent sincere. He must have thought about all kinds of things on the way here.
But since Magic Johnson had no idea what the answer meant, it was more than enough to set his heart aflutter.
“Oh! Then you’re just like me. We have so much in common, don’t we?”
We’re probably very different when it comes to which gender we like.
“Anyway, it’s good to see you again.”
His gaze dripping with lingering affection, Magic Johnson finally ended his reunion with Team Leader Choi and answered my earlier question.
“And Jin, if you’re worried about the southern front I’m in charge of, don’t be. Nothing will go wrong just because I stepped away for a little while.”
“It sounds like the war is going quite well.”
“Hmm. I’m not sure about that. Still, it is encouraging that the monster armies are retreating from every front.”
“Oh, the monster armies are retreating... What?”
Team Leader Choi and I turned to each other and blinked as though we’d rehearsed it.
What the hell was he talking about?
Team Leader Choi recovered before I did and asked Magic Johnson, “This is the first we’ve heard of it. Mr. Johnson, could you tell us what happened?”
“It’s exactly as I said. The monster armies turned tail during the night. When we looked into it, the same thing had happened on every front.”
“But we didn’t detect any movement on our side.”
“Ah, let me correct myself. The western front is the exception.”
“Why is that?”
“What? Hahaha!”
Magic Johnson let out a booming laugh and clapped me on the shoulder.

“Because this western front has penetrated deeper into enemy territory than any other. I don’t know what kind of scheme the Arch Lich is plotting, but the western front is already an open highway. The monsters here have already retreated as far as they can.”
“Oh.”
I’d momentarily forgotten.
Unlike the other fronts, which were advancing little by little under Army and Air Force cover, I had simply killed and smashed everything in my path as I pushed forward.
I did tear through them with unstoppable momentum, but did we really get that far?
Magic Johnson laughed loudly at my bewildered expression.
“That doesn’t sound like the Genghis Khan of the twenty-first century. You’ve accomplished an incredible military feat. Why not smile a little?”
“It’s far too early to relax and smile. But never mind the monster armies pulling back. Why are you here?”
“I came to see Choi.”
“I’m kidding.”
Look how pale Team Leader Choi’s gotten. One more joke and his sphincter might rupture.
“I’m taking some personnel away temporarily, so I had to deliver the written orders to the commander.”
“You’re taking people away? Where?”
“Chengdu. A military conference has been convened.”

chapters.title: Chapter 395
paragraphs: “Follow me.”
Magic Johnson led us to none other than the hospital rooftop.
After sweeping my eyes across the empty landing pad, where there wasn’t a helicopter or jet in sight, I asked,
“There’s nothing here.”
“Nope. I’m here.”
Magic Johnson’s answer was short and simple, but what it implied was anything but.
Team Leader Choi’s eyes widened slightly. He seemed to have reached the same conclusion I had.
“Mr. Johnson. You don’t mean...”
“That’s right. We’re going to travel by teleportation magic.”
Teleportation. In other words, instant travel.
Magic Johnson spoke as casually as if he were suggesting a ride on a tricycle, but everyone knew teleportation magic was infamous for its extreme difficulty.
The finicky conditions required to cast it were one thing. If the coordinates were even slightly off, you could easily wind up dead.
A single misstep could mean ending up fused with an apple tree or a boulder. Horrifying.
“Can’t we just take a jet?”
“Nope.”
Magic Johnson answered firmly and narrowed his eyes.
“Hey, Jin. You don’t actually distrust me, do you? I’m Magic Johnson. Do I have to show you before you’ll believe me?”
You saying that somehow makes it sound even stranger.
Whether he intended to show me teleportation magic or his Johnson, I didn’t care. I just wanted to travel peacefully by jet.
Team Leader Choi noticed my pleading expression and spoke up.
“Mr. Johnson, as you know, this area is within the Arch Lich’s sphere of influence. Magic is being disrupted, and even communications are unreliable.”
“Ah, so that’s what this is about. I thought it was something else.”
Magic Johnson let out a quiet laugh.
“How do you think I got here?”
“Huh?”
“Don’t tell me...”
“That’s right. I teleported. There was a little interference, but it wasn’t enough to hold Magic Johnson back.”
Snap!

Magic Johnson snapped his fingers, and a pillar of flame erupted from thin air. He cast the spell as naturally as breathing—a striking contrast to the mages of the Public Security Armed Forces Department, who had been unable to use magic properly because of the interference.
“You could do that from the beginning?”
“Of course not. Until now, I could still manage most ordinary spells despite the interference, but teleportation is too dangerous. I didn’t even dare attempt it.”
“Then...”

“The Arch Lich. His power had been gradually weakening. In particular, a considerable portion of the interference disappeared after last night. Though communications still seem to be a complete mess.”
It was something he could say—and pull off—only because he was one of just three archmages in the entire world.
Magic Johnson flashed his white teeth and held out a hand to us.
“That should be enough to earn your trust, don’t you think?”
“Well, if you put it that way.”
I took his hand without much hesitation, but Team Leader Choi quietly stepped back.
“Team Leader Choi?”
“I’ll stay here.”
“Why, Choi?”
“There are still matters I need to handle. Besides, given how little influence I have in the discussion, attending in person or hearing about it afterward will make little difference.”
Team Leader Choi always assessed the situation coolly. If he couldn’t change the course of events himself, he pulled lower-priority work forward and dealt with that instead.
I wanted to tell him that he was mistaken, but I quietly nodded.
He wasn’t wrong.
Even the S-rank Hunters whose opinions carried weight were ultimately mercenaries from other countries—borrowed blades.
That was why Chairman Xiao Yang and Minister Wei Fenghu had made it clear that overall command remained in their hands.
“Choi’s dropping out? This can’t be happening! Jin has no Charm!”
I really want to drive a nail through him. Then again, maybe this is for the best.
After whining for quite some time, Magic Johnson said goodbye to Team Leader Choi with a deeply disappointed expression.
“Can’t be helped. See you next time, Choi.”
“Take care.”
“Take care of what? It’ll be over in an instant.”
Magic Johnson shrugged and turned to me.
“Hey, Jin. Ready?”
“Yes.”
“Hold my hand tight. Don’t let go.”
“...Why are we interlocking fingers? Can’t I just hold your palm?”
Isn’t this the sort of thing couples do?
As a guy in his late twenties who had been single his entire life, I couldn’t help feeling uncomfortable about interlocking fingers with a huge Black man.
Magic Johnson spoke gently when he saw my reluctance.
“You can let go if you want. But if you lose your grip during the journey, you might die.”
Thinking of my first love from childhood, I clutched Magic Johnson’s hand tightly.
“Let’s go, darling.”
Magic Johnson’s expression turned stern.
“Sorry, but Jin isn’t my type. You don’t have to squeeze that hard, so could you ease up?”
“...Oh. Right.”
“Then, here we go.”
Just as I opened my mouth to answer—
Whoooooosh!
Gasp!
My breath caught, and the taut air constricted around my entire body.
Through my blurring vision, Team Leader Choi wavered like a mirage before vanishing.
The earth and sky flipped upside down.
Then, at last, came an overwhelming sense of release.
“Hah!”
I expelled the breath I had been holding and inhaled deeply. Cool air filled my lungs. I blinked, and my briefly clouded vision cleared.
It felt as if barely a second had passed, yet an entirely different landscape and different people stood around me.
“Our final guest has arrived.”
Wei Fenghu, Minister of National Defense under China’s Central Military Commission, approached and patted me on the shoulder. He looked as though he had aged ten years in the past week.
“Everyone is waiting. Let us go inside together.”
“W-wait a second.”
“Yes?”
“Don’t come any closer...”
“Uweeeeeegh!”
Splash!
For the record, I’m fairly tall. About two heads taller than Wei Fenghu.
As I emptied my stomach over the thinning crown of the old general’s head, Magic Johnson’s voice reached me.
“Ah, I forgot to mention that the motion sickness gets worse. I’m sorry, Jin. I’m sorry, Wei Fenghu.”
“You should’ve told me that sooner—uweeeeeegh!”
It took a little longer before I was able to attend the meeting.
A holographic recording played in the darkness of a vast conference room.
The footage showed exactly what one person had seen: a complicated control panel, clouds scattering beyond reinforced glass, and tiny specks appearing far below as the aircraft descended.
The things covering the ground surged forward like waves, with no ranks or formation.
Monsters.
It wasn’t difficult to tell that the footage came from a fighter pilot’s perspective. Wearing a head-mounted camera, the pilot radioed someone.
“This is YANU-4885. I repeat, YANU-4885. Target confirmed. Locked on.”
“You are cleared to fire.”
Crackle. Crackle.
The transmission was riddled with static, but the words were clear enough. The pilot took a deep breath and carried out the mission without hesitation.
Rumble.
The fighter trembled slightly as one of its missiles launched. It dwindled into a speck as it streaked toward the center of the advancing monster army—
Whoosh!
A black vortex abruptly appeared in the empty air above the monsters and swallowed the missile.
“Hngh!”
The pilot gasped and hurriedly pressed a red button on the control panel.
But then—
Boom! Crackle.
The footage cut out amid a thunderous roar that suddenly crashed through the room.
The hologram disappeared, and Minister Wei Fenghu spoke with a grave expression.
“What do the rest of you make of it?”
Magic Johnson lit a cigar before answering.
“Teleportation magic. The missile was transported above the fighter.”
“Mr. Johnson, could you do the same?”
After a moment of thought, Magic Johnson answered.
“It wouldn’t be difficult. But I’m not confident I could do it that quickly or accurately.”
“Even for an archmage such as yourself?”
Magic Johnson gave a slight nod and exhaled cigar smoke.

He, too, was an S-rank Hunter who had accomplished feats that would go down in history. He must have been proud of his abilities, so he couldn’t have been pleased to learn that he had been outdone by a monster called the Arch Lich.
But this meeting wasn’t about protecting anyone’s pride.
We had to face reality.
“Then we can’t count on fire support. If we launch anything too powerful and it gets redirected, the result could be catastrophic.”
Faye Chen continued, lightly touching her wineglass with one slender finger.
“I expected as much, but now that it’s come to this, we have no choice but to settle the matter on the ground.”

“If matters continue as they are, the tide of battle will gradually improve. The royal guard of the British Empire, led by this prince, has crushed the monster army. More importantly, that wine you are drinking—is it perhaps a 1945 Romanée-Conti?”
“No.”
“Hm. You don’t know how to drink.”
Faye Chen glared at Prince Felix.

“Oh, my. What is this child talking about? Get a grip. The British Empire was dissolved long ago, and the monsters didn’t retreat because you won a few battles. They retreated because of that fellow sitting across from you.”
Prince Felix glanced at me.
“I heard that you distinguished yourself greatly on the Western Front...but are all those stories truly accurate?”
What, does he think I’m lying?
I stared at Prince Felix incredulously.
“Then they’re true, aren’t they? What, you think I made it all up? If you don’t want to believe me, don’t.”
“Your great achievements may be worthy of praise, but your words and conduct are remarkably insolent. You will refer to me as His Highness and always speak respectfully.”
I readily complied with his demand.
“His Highness, did you eat your fish and chips wrong?”
“Hmm. A man of matchless courage, yet utterly lacking in manners.”
Utterly lacking in manners, my ass. Maybe I should make sure he’s lacking one ball, too.
For the record, the guy I’d beaten up about a week ago kept his mouth firmly shut and wouldn’t even meet my eyes.
It’s nice that he’s quiet, but something about it feels off.
Given Wu Heixing’s stupidity, I’d expected him to come at me at least a few more times. Either he was more cowardly than I’d thought, or I had misjudged him.
More importantly, someone else in the room bothered me far more than Wu Heixing did.
“You’ve been awfully quiet. Don’t you have anything to say?”
Lee Jungryong—the snake coiled in wait—smiled gently.
“Thank you for your concern, but I’m fine. A mercenary’s virtue is following the employer’s wishes without comment.”
“Oh, is that so?”
“It’s a simple principle.”
I smiled back.
“But for someone who says that, your performance has been a little lackluster. Things on the northern front don’t seem to be going very well. Was that your employer’s wish too?”
At my words, silence descended over the room as if everyone had been doused with cold water.
As every gaze turned toward him, Lee Jungryong stroked his chin.
“I find that remark unpleasant. Ares Guild and I did our best.”
“Your best? Really?”
“We fought ten battles over the past week and won nine of them. Although we unfortunately suffered one defeat, I would call that an impressive military record.”
Ten battles, nine wins, one loss. By the numbers, it was certainly an impressive record.
But two days ago, when Team Leader Choi and I heard about the defeat on the northern front, we had both let out hollow laughs.
What a sly old man.
Lee Jungryong was one of the strongest men in the world—or, even by Murim standards, an incredibly powerful martial artist.
Given his personality, there was no chance he had revealed the full extent of his abilities. He had to be even stronger than the public believed.
And someone like that had the nerve to say—
Unfortunately suffered one defeat, my ass.
I couldn’t speak for anyone else, but I was certain.
If Lee Jungryong had taken the field and still lost, then the defeat had been intentional from beginning to end.
The members of Ares Guild had withdrawn intact despite the staggering casualties around them. They were living proof.
Though since I can’t prove anything, I suppose it’s still only a suspicion.
That was also why Lee Jungryong could remain so relaxed. He loosely crossed his arms.
“I regret the defeat that day, but I would appreciate it if you refrained from making hasty accusations. There was a clear reason for our loss.”
“A clear reason?”
“Who could have expected a Death Knight to appear under those circumstances? Once the commander died, the ensuing confusion became impossible to control.”
“If you mean the Death Knights...”
“I heard they appeared on the Western Front last night as well. Is that not so?”
His words brought something to mind.
The testimony of the civilian couple rescued from the small city.
Ten Death Knights had slaughtered nearly a thousand troops, while their leader, the Black Knight, had left without killing the couple for some unknown reason.
That Black Knight had bothered me ever since I heard their story.
“Then among the ones that appeared on the northern front, was there perhaps—”
My question to Lee Jungryong never reached its end.
Urgent footsteps raced down the corridor, and someone who looked like a Chinese officer burst through the door.
Bang!
“Huff, huff. Emergency! Emergency!”
He continued while gasping for breath.
“We have received word that the monster army has advanced! Fighting has broken out on every front!”
“...What?”

Teleportation.
In other words, instant travel.
Magic Johnson spoke as casually as if he were suggesting a ride on a tricycle, but everyone knew teleportation magic was infamous for its extreme difficulty.
The finicky conditions required to cast it were one thing.
If the coordinates were even slightly off, you could easily wind up dead.
A single misstep could mean ending up fused with an apple tree or a boulder.
Horrifying.
“Can’t we just take a jet?”
“Nope.”
Magic Johnson answered firmly and narrowed his eyes.
“Hey, Jin.
You don’t actually distrust me, do you?
I’m Magic Johnson.
Do I have to show you before you’ll believe me?”
You saying that somehow makes it sound even stranger.
Whether he intended to show me teleportation magic or his Johnson, I didn’t care.
I just wanted to travel peacefully by jet.
Team Leader Choi noticed my pleading expression and spoke up.
“Mr.
Johnson, as you know, this area is within the Arch Lich’s sphere of influence.
Magic is being disrupted, and even communications are unreliable.”

Magic Johnson let out a quiet laugh.
“How do you think I got here?”
“Huh?”
“Don’t tell me...”
“That’s right.
I teleported.
There was a little interference, but it wasn’t enough to hold Magic Johnson back.”
Snap!

“Of course not.

I didn’t even dare attempt it.”
“Then...”

In particular, a considerable portion of the interference disappeared after last night.
Though communications still seem to be a complete mess.”
It was something he could say—and pull off—only because he was one of just three archmages in the entire world.

“Well, if you put it that way.”

“Team Leader Choi?”
“I’ll stay here.”
“Why, Choi?”
“There are still matters I need to handle.

Team Leader Choi always assessed the situation coolly.
If he couldn’t change the course of events himself, he pulled lower-priority work forward and dealt with that instead.
I wanted to tell him that he was mistaken, but I quietly nodded.
He wasn’t wrong.
Even the S-rank Hunters whose opinions carried weight were ultimately mercenaries from other countries—borrowed blades.
That was why Chairman Xiao Yang and Minister Wei Fenghu had made it clear that overall command remained in their hands.
“Choi’s dropping out?
This can’t be happening!
Jin has no Charm!”
I really want to drive a nail through him.
Then again, maybe this is for the best.
After whining for quite some time, Magic Johnson said goodbye to Team Leader Choi with a deeply disappointed expression.
“Can’t be helped.
See you next time, Choi.”
“Take care.”
“Take care of what?
It’ll be over in an instant.”
Magic Johnson shrugged and turned to me.
“Hey, Jin.
Ready?”
“Yes.”

Don’t let go.”
“...Why are we interlocking fingers?

Isn’t this the sort of thing couples do?
As a guy in his late twenties who had been single his entire life, I couldn’t help feeling uncomfortable about interlocking fingers with a huge Black man.
Magic Johnson spoke gently when he saw my reluctance.
“You can let go if you want.
But if you lose your grip during the journey, you might die.”
Thinking of my first love from childhood, I clutched Magic Johnson’s hand tightly.
“Let’s go, darling.”
Magic Johnson’s expression turned stern.
“Sorry, but Jin isn’t my type.

chapters.title: Chapter 396
paragraphs: The Black Knight raised his head and looked up at the sky.
A clear blue expanse without a single cloud. But to the Black Knight’s eyes, which had long since lost their light, it appeared only as a dark, murky gray.
How dark.
The thought left him feeling strangely unsettled. Dark? What did darkness even mean?
He had always been the Black Knight. A being born from darkness could not understand what darkness was.
But this... What is it?
Light and sunlight. A child laughing brightly. Someone’s hand stroking his head...
Several words and inexplicable scenes flashed through his mind in succession, leaving him confused.
If not for the call from one of his subordinates a moment later, the Black Knight would have stood there for a long time.
“Lord.”
“Please.”
Black armor as dark as night covered his entire body. Green lights flickered between the slits of the helmet covering his head.
Two Death Knights dismounted from their skeletal warhorses and knelt on one knee. They continued in flat, emotionless voices.
“Give us—”
“your orders.”
Ah.
The Black Knight recalled something he had briefly forgotten: the command given by the lord he served.
“Go. Advance in all directions, trample everything, and kill them all. Offer me mountains of corpses and seas of blood.”
His lord’s commands were absolute. With even his soul bound to that lord, the Black Knight faithfully obeyed.
He had appointed the ten Death Knights under his command to lead five legions, then personally taken the vanguard of one legion and come here.
But why this place, of all places?
The Black Knight gazed at the small city in the distance.
It was a place he remembered. The place where the unfamiliar word child had suddenly come to mind, and where he had sensed an enormous power whose nature he could not identify.
But the Black Knight had no idea why he had come here.
“Lord?”
“Lord?”
After silently looking down at his subordinates, the Black Knight finally gave his command.
“Advance.”
“Your command.”
“We obey.”
Having received the answer they had been waiting for, the Death Knights mounted their skeletal warhorses and raised their enormous spears high.
Pitch-black demonic qi surged from the spearheads, and the monsters packed across the broad plain let out shrill howls.
—Kik. Kikikikik.
—Graaaargh!
There were Skeletons that had died so recently that flesh still clung to their bones, small monsters such as goblins and Orcs, and large monsters such as Trolls and ogres.
By a rough estimate, they numbered in the tens of thousands. Overhead, flocks of Gargoyles and Wyverns cast enormous shadows across the land.
“Rally.”
“Do it.”

At the next command, roughly two hundred Dullahans formed ranks. Holding their severed heads in one hand and weapons in the other, they sat astride beasts made of white bone, their eyes gleaming with a vicious light.
“Prepare.”
“for the charge.”
The two Death Knights took position at the tip of the legion. Their spearheads, raised as if to pierce the sky, slowly descended to point toward the city.
A city of humans. But soon, it would become a city of the undead—a land of death.
“Public Security Armed Forces Department, assemble!”
“F-fuck! Monsters! They’re here!”
“Sound the alarm and report to command immediately!”
Wheeeeeeng!
The humans’ shouts and the wail of the emergency siren carried on the wind.
But the order had already been given. Nothing could stop the undead legion now that it had begun its advance.
Boom. Boom. Boom.
The ranks and files were arranged with military precision.

Death Knights and Dullahans led the way, with highly mobile Lycanthropes and other monsters holding the front line. Large monsters such as ogres, Trolls, and Golems advanced behind them like a colossal wall.
The monsters capable of using bows and magic had already moved to the rear.
The Black Knight was the one who had devised the discipline and formations ordinary monsters lacked.
Where did I learn such things?
Setting the question aside once more, the Black Knight opened his mouth.
“Follow.”
At its master’s will, the skeletal warhorse beneath him began to move.
Clip-clop. Clip-clop.
Hooves of white bone trampled the new shoots beneath them. The undead legion blanketing the vast breadbasket advanced slowly behind its commander.
Tremors shook the earth. The legion moved forward like a slow swell, then became a wave of bones sweeping across the plain.
Thudthudthudthudthud!
—Graaaargh!
Tens of thousands of monsters roared as one.
At the head of the monsters surging toward the city, the Black Knight shot forward like a streak of light.
“That one’s the leader!”
“Ranged units! Prepare!”
“Tanks, stay calm! The armored units will intercept him alongside the Hunters!”
Tanks, armored units, Hunters.
The Black Knight heard the humans’ shouts and, astonishingly, understood them perfectly.
He even knew what command would come next.
“Begin concentrated fire!”
Rat-a-tat-tat-tat!
Boom-boom-boom!
Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh!
It was dazzling. Flames, ice, and flashes of light erupted from all across the city.
Some attacks came crashing down in graceful arcs. Others flew in nearly straight lines, aimed at the Black Knight and the undead knights following behind him.
“Ah.”
Even in a world dyed gray, the light they gave off was enchanting and familiar. The Black Knight felt an inexplicable stirring within him and reached out.
Shrring.
The greatsword strapped to his back slid free.
Before the shells, magic, and arrows could reach him, the pitch-black blade carved through the air in every direction.
Kraaaash!
A gale of magical power swept across the battlefield. Space split apart. Spells blazing with brilliant mana went out like candle flames, and arrows shattered to pieces.
Everyone in the city watched as light was devoured by darkness.
The same thought flashed through Choi Minwoo’s and Xiao Shen’s minds.
This is...
Impossible to stop.
An insight approaching certainty.
Then, in the next moment, a pitch-black flash leaped across space and struck the Hunters.
KABOOM!
A thunderous roar rang out as though the sky itself had split apart.

Dozens of Tower Shields shattered, and sprays of blood burst into the air. Having cut down three A-rank Hunters and twenty B-rank Hunters with a single sword stroke, the Black Knight stared at the frozen humans through glowing red eyes.
From beneath his low-drawn helmet came the chilling voice of the dead.
“Aksar. Garosh.”
Kill them all.
The Demon Realm words had been the last thing heard by those who died here the previous day.
And...
They were the Black Knight’s command to the legion behind him.
“Your command.”
“We obey.”
Two Death Knights appeared to his left and right. A hundred Dullahans charged in behind them, becoming a sharp awl that pierced the human wall.
Krrrunch!
An ambush?

Emergency reports had come in from every front. Wei Fenghu roared, demanding to know what had happened, but the only answer he received was that communications with every front had been completely severed.
“Completely severed? They may have been unstable, but haven’t we still been able to connect since last night?”
The communications officer answered, drenched in cold sweat.
“W-we don’t know why, but the communications interference has grown even stronger. The emergency report that just arrived was confirmed to be from approximately thirty minutes ago.”
What? Thirty minutes?
If that was true, the attacks had begun while the meeting was in progress.
And since the report had barely made it through the interference, it might not have been thirty minutes ago. It could have been an hour.
Magic Johnson muttered with his face gone rigid.
“That can’t be. It wasn’t nearly this bad before I left...”
Suddenly, the words Magic Johnson had spoken before leaving the city flashed through my mind.
“The Arch Lich’s power is gradually weakening. A considerable portion of the interference has disappeared since last night in particular.”
Wrong.
The Arch Lich’s power over the surrounding area hadn’t weakened. He had merely made it look that way.

Little by little, without giving anything away. Then, by withdrawing the legion, he had made it seem as if the range of his influence had shrunk dramatically—so that we could let our guard down even a little more.
This is...
A meticulously laid trap.
I didn’t know how the Arch Lich had realized the S-rank Hunters were gone. What mattered was that he had seized that brief opening and sent the monster legions forward.
The thought of the horrific slaughter we had witnessed the day before now unfolding across every front made my stomach churn even worse than it had during my first teleportation.
But this time, instead of throwing up, I grabbed Magic Johnson and said,
“Teleport.”
“What?”
“Teleport. Hurry!”
I expected Magic Johnson to use magic immediately. But his answer was nothing like what I had expected.
“Jin. Take a jet.”
“What? A jet? Why are you suddenly...? We’ll be too late.”
“It’s too risky right now.”
“Why? You know the coordinates of the hospital rooftop where we were earlier.”
Magic Johnson shook his head.
“The coordinates aren’t the problem. If we attempt to teleport like this...we could both die.”
In my desperation, I had momentarily forgotten about the Arch Lich’s magical interference. There was no way the bastard who had laid such a trap would kindly allow us to teleport.
Magic Johnson continued in a subdued voice.
“Ten minutes. Twenty at most. Take the jet, Jin.”
“...A lot of people will die in that time.”
“Yes. But if you get yourself killed for nothing during the teleportation, there’ll be even more casualties.”
An S-rank Hunter was a strategic weapon capable of turning the tide of a war.

Even if I arrived late, I might still be able to save some people. But if something went wrong during the teleportation, there would be no saving me or the countless people left without reinforcements.
Magic Johnson was worried about me, but he was also pointing that out.
“It’s brave, but foolish.”
“The jet will be ready for takeoff soon. We don’t have time for this.”
Through the bulletproof glass covering one wall of the conference room, I could see pilots crossing the runway and boarding their aircraft.
I could also see the backs of the other S-rank Hunters, who had already left the conference room.
I watched in silence, then suddenly spoke.
“You said it was possible, right?”
“What?”
“Teleporting missiles, like in the hologram footage we saw earlier.”
Magic Johnson’s eyes widened.
“Jin, don’t tell me...”
“There’s no need for you to risk yourself too, Johnson. Sending me alone will be enough.”
“Good God. Are you crazy? I explained it to you, and you still don’t understand!”
“I understand perfectly. I’m prepared to take that risk.”
His lips moved as though he were about to say something, but then he suddenly slammed his fist down on the table.
Bang!
The expensive hardwood shattered beneath the force of his blow.
“Damn it! Fuck this whole goddamn mess!”
I let out a quiet laugh as I watched Magic Johnson mutter curse after curse.
I already knew what his reaction meant.
“I can take that as permission, right?”
“Yes, you insolent little brat.”
His bloodshot eyes fixed on me.
He looked ready to unleash another torrent of abuse.
Magic Johnson was genuinely furious—and at the same time, deeply saddened.
“Listen, Jin. I...”
“I know. You have people you need to protect too. I’m sorry to ask this of you.”
“...Damn it. Is sending you to the hospital rooftop enough?”
“Yes. That’s enough.”
Swoosh.
Magic Johnson clenched his teeth and pressed his thick palm against my chest.
As though taking every possible precaution, his mana slowly began to envelop my body, unlike the first time he had teleported me.
“Ten percent. That’s your chance of survival. There’s a ninety percent chance you could die.”
Ten percent...
I raised my head and looked up at the sky beyond the window.
A clear blue expanse without a single cloud. Was Murim somewhere in the distant universe beyond that sky? Were they waiting for me?
At that moment, a thought suddenly occurred to me, and the corners of my mouth lifted.
“That’s not bad. Ten percent is enough.”
“What?”
A dazzling mass of light burst forth. Feeling warmth envelop my entire body, I continued.
“It’s probably a thousand times higher than the odds of crossing dimensions.”
I wondered what expression Magic Johnson was wearing by then.
I wanted to know, but unfortunately, I could no longer see his face. A blinding flash filled my vision, and a rough, powerful force sucked me through the warping space.
Whoooosh!

Ah.

His lord’s commands were absolute.
With even his soul bound to that lord, the Black Knight faithfully obeyed.
He had appointed the ten Death Knights under his command to lead five legions, then personally taken the vanguard of one legion and come here.
But why this place, of all places?
The Black Knight gazed at the small city in the distance.
It was a place he remembered.
The place where the unfamiliar word child had suddenly come to mind, and where he had sensed an enormous power whose nature he could not identify.
But the Black Knight had no idea why he had come here.

“Lord?”

“We obey.”

By a rough estimate, they numbered in the tens of thousands.
Overhead, flocks of Gargoyles and Wyverns cast enormous shadows across the land.

“Do it.”
At the next command, roughly two hundred Dullahans formed ranks.
Holding their severed heads in one hand and weapons in the other, they sat astride beasts made of white bone, their eyes gleaming with a vicious light.

The two Death Knights took position at the tip of the legion.

A city of humans.
But soon, it would become a city of the undead—a land of death.

Monsters!
They’re here!”

Wheeeeeeng!
The humans’ shouts and the wail of the emergency siren carried on the wind.
But the order had already been given.
Nothing could stop the undead legion now that it had begun its advance.
Boom.
Boom.
Boom.
The ranks and files were arranged with military precision.
Death Knights and Dullahans led the way, with highly mobile Lycanthropes and other monsters holding the front line.
Large monsters such as ogres, Trolls, and Golems advanced behind them like a colossal wall.
The monsters capable of using bows and magic had already moved to the rear.
The Black Knight was the one who had devised the discipline and formations ordinary monsters lacked.
Where did I learn such things?
Setting the question aside once more, the Black Knight opened his mouth.
“Follow.”
At its master’s will, the skeletal warhorse beneath him began to move.
Clip-clop.
Clip-clop.
Hooves of white bone trampled the new shoots beneath them.
The undead legion blanketing the vast breadbasket advanced slowly behind its commander.
Tremors shook the earth.
The legion moved forward like a slow swell, then became a wave of bones sweeping across the plain.
Thudthudthudthudthud!
—Graaaargh!
Tens of thousands of monsters roared as one.
At the head of the monsters surging toward the city, the Black Knight shot forward like a streak of light.
“That one’s the leader!”
“Ranged units!
Prepare!”
“Tanks, stay calm!
The armored units will intercept him alongside the Hunters!”
Tanks, armored units, Hunters.
The Black Knight heard the humans’ shouts and, astonishingly, understood them perfectly.
He even knew what command would come next.
“Begin concentrated fire!”
Rat-a-tat-tat-tat!
Boom-boom-boom!
Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh!
It was dazzling.
Flames, ice, and flashes of light erupted from all across the city.
Some attacks came crashing down in graceful arcs.
Others flew in nearly straight lines, aimed at the Black Knight and the undead knights following behind him.
“Ah.”
Even in a world dyed gray, the light they gave off was enchanting and familiar.
The Black Knight felt an inexplicable stirring within him and reached out.
Shrring.
The greatsword strapped to his back slid free.
Before the shells, magic, and arrows could reach him, the pitch-black blade carved through the air in every direction.
Kraaaash!
A gale of magical power swept across the battlefield.
Space split apart.
Spells blazing with brilliant mana went out like candle flames, and arrows shattered to pieces.
Everyone in the city watched as light was devoured by darkness.
The same thought flashed through Choi Minwoo’s and Xiao Shen’s minds.
This is...
Impossible to stop.
An insight approaching certainty.
Then, in the next moment, a pitch-black flash leaped across space and struck the Hunters.
KABOOM!
A thunderous roar rang out as though the sky itself had split apart.
Dozens of Tower Shields shattered, and sprays of blood burst into the air.
Having cut down three A-rank Hunters and twenty B-rank Hunters with a single sword stroke, the Black Knight stared at the frozen humans through glowing red eyes.
From beneath his low-drawn helmet came the chilling voice of the dead.
“Aksar.
Garosh.”
Kill them all.
The Demon Realm words had been the last thing heard by those who died here the previous day.
And...
They were the Black Knight’s command to the legion behind him.
“Your command.”
“We obey.”
Two Death Knights appeared to his left and right.
A hundred Dullahans charged in behind them, becoming a sharp awl that pierced the human wall.
Krrrunch!
An ambush?
Emergency reports had come in from every front.
Wei Fenghu roared, demanding to know what had happened, but the only answer he received was that communications with every front had been completely severed.
“Completely severed?
They may have been unstable, but haven’t we still been able to connect since last night?”
The communications officer answered, drenched in cold sweat.

Thirty minutes?
If that was true, the attacks had begun while the meeting was in progress.
And since the report had barely made it through the interference, it might not have been thirty minutes ago.
It could have been an hour.
Magic Johnson muttered with his face gone rigid.

Suddenly, the words Magic Johnson had spoken before leaving the city flashed through my mind.
“The Arch Lich’s power is gradually weakening.
