Wrong.
The Arch Lich’s power over the surrounding area hadn’t weakened.
He had merely made it look that way.
Little by little, without giving anything away.
Then, by withdrawing the legion, he had made it seem as if the range of his influence had shrunk dramatically—so that we could let our guard down even a little more.

A meticulously laid trap.
I didn’t know how the Arch Lich had realized the S-rank Hunters were gone.
What mattered was that he had seized that brief opening and sent the monster legions forward.
The thought of the horrific slaughter we had witnessed the day before now unfolding across every front made my stomach churn even worse than it had during my first teleportation.
But this time, instead of throwing up, I grabbed Magic Johnson and said,
“Teleport.”
“What?”
“Teleport.
Hurry!”
I expected Magic Johnson to use magic immediately.
But his answer was nothing like what I had expected.
“Jin.
Take a jet.”
“What?
A jet?
Why are you suddenly...?
We’ll be too late.”
“It’s too risky right now.”
“Why?
You know the coordinates of the hospital rooftop where we were earlier.”

chapters.title: Chapter 397
paragraphs: Team Leader Choi—or rather, Choi Minwoo—thought,
What should I do?
His heart pounded wildly, but his mind was ice-cold.

Only thirty minutes had passed since the battle began. The hastily constructed defensive line had collapsed the instant the fighting started, then been torn apart as the highest-grade monsters slipped through the gaps and ran rampant without meeting any resistance.
Just like now.
Crunch!
Sharp fangs tore savagely into a human throat.
The Lycanthrope tossed aside the Hunter, whose last breath escaped in a wheeze, and let out a roar.
—Awooooooo!
Those became the Lycanthrope’s final words.
Whoosh! Slash!
Its gray fur turned red as its body toppled sideways. Choi Minwoo took its head off with a clean strike, then bent backward without a moment to catch his breath.
Whoooooom! Crack!
The blow missed him by a handspan.
An ax blade rippling with ominous magical power grazed past Choi Minwoo and smashed the heads of two nearby Orcs.
The headless knight, a Dullahan, attacked the human in front of it without the slightest hesitation, despite having killed fellow monsters.
Swoooooosh! Slash!
—Krrk!
“Guh!”
As the enormous halberd swept back and forth, the humans and monsters caught within its reach were hacked to pieces.
A Dullahan was an A-rank monster that required three Hunters of the same rank to handle safely.
But Choi Minwoo slipped past its attack and thrust out his sword without hesitation.
Now!
A short exhalation.
Then a strike like a flash of light.
Thud!
The blade, enchanted with three different spells and forged by a Master Artisan, pierced the Dullahan through the shoulder.
It might not feel pain, having already died once and become undead, but its body was still human.
The muscles and tendons in its right arm were severed, and the halberd dropped heavily to the ground. Choi Minwoo did not miss the opening.
Shhhhhk!
A white blade of aura cleaved the Dullahan in half at the waist. It must not have been dead for long, because rotten blood sprayed from its collapsing body and splattered across Choi Minwoo’s face.
But despite the overpowering stench stabbing at his nose, he did not so much as twitch an eyebrow.
Choi Minwoo was gripped by the tension of the battlefield, cold reason, and a faint exhilaration.
That makes ten.
That was how many A-rank monsters Choi Minwoo had defeated by himself today. Including those of lower grades, the number had to be well over fifty.
Was I always this strong?
If he answered that question honestly, the answer was no.
Perhaps because of the Arch Lich’s influence, the monsters he had encountered in China were slightly stronger and far more ferocious.
Even so, Choi Minwoo had been able to distinguish himself in such a chaotic battle because he had been blessed with two strokes of luck.
The first was—
The Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique.
The Mana Cultivation Method he had learned directly from Jin Taekyung.
Choi Minwoo had his doubts about Jin Taekyung’s claim that it was a family heirloom passed down through generations. But he had no doubt whatsoever that it was an outstanding secret technique.

The Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique allowed him to control his energy reliably while greatly improving how he distributed his strength. The immense mana he had gained while learning it also gave him the stamina to keep fighting without tiring easily.
And his second stroke of luck was—
—Gwoooooar!
Boom!
A length of rebar swung with berserk force and smashed through the concrete road.
Choi Minwoo stepped on the ogre’s thick arm and sprang upward, bringing his sword down with all his strength.
Thrust!
The aura-infused blade split the ogre’s crown as easily as tofu.
Thud.
The four-meter giant dropped to its knees with a heavy crash. Standing on the dead creature’s shoulder, Choi Minwoo quickly swept his gaze over his surroundings.
He’s not here.
Screams and death filled the hellish scene on every side.
But the monster was nowhere to be seen. The monster who had displayed unbelievable power the moment the battle began—the commander of the monster army and leader of the Death Knights.
Where the hell is he?
Choi Minwoo clearly remembered the Black Knight sweeping aside dozens of Hunters with a single blow.
If the creature had truly committed itself to the battle, the humans might have been annihilated before they lasted even thirty minutes.
But for some reason, the Black Knight had not appeared again.
Was it the monster’s arrogance? Did it consider the battle too insignificant to warrant its involvement?
Choi Minwoo could not understand it. But the Black Knight’s absence was both his second stroke of luck and his final chance to make a decision.
We have to retreat.
The urban battle had already lost all meaning. The monster army, numbering around ten thousand, had already covered the city like a swarm of ants. Among them were more than a hundred A-rank monsters.
The humans were outmatched in both numbers and strength.

Nearly half of the thousand Hunters from the Public Security Armed Forces Department who had held the front line were already dead or wounded. And more than half of the damned People’s Liberation Army had thrown down their weapons and fled before the monsters even reached them.
The armored units, reduced to heaps of scrap metal, and the air force, becoming prey for the flying monsters, were simply more of the same.
Rat-a-tat-tat-tat-tat! Boom!
A state-of-the-art combat helicopter lost its balance and plunged from the sky, exploding in flames. Around a dozen soldiers caught in the flying debris died without even having time to scream.
It was a horrifying sight, but they were fortunate in one respect: their deaths had been painless.
A moment later, the monster horde began tearing everyone else apart indiscriminately.
—Kraaaaaaang!
Whoom! Crack!
The foreleg of a Saber Tiger, carrying several tons of force, crushed a soldier’s limbs and burst his head.
The soldiers of the People’s Liberation Army were nowhere near as fast as Hunters, and the rifles they carried were little better than slingshots against the monsters.
Choi Minwoo clenched his teeth at the merciless slaughter unfolding before him.
Get a grip. You can’t save all of them.
He did not hypocritically preach about sacrificing the few for the many. He simply faced the situation with a cold eye and prepared himself to play the villain.
Could we have stopped them if he’d come?
Jin Taekyung suddenly came to mind, but that was nothing more than futile regret.
Even after he hounded the communications officer into frantically transmitting emergency signals, there had been no response.
A carefully planned surprise attack combined with thorough communications interference.
For now, all he could do was hope that one of the countless glass bottles cast into the sea would somehow reach Jin Taekyung.
Thud!
Choi Minwoo drove his sword into the chest of a charging Minotaur and shouted,
“Xiao Shen!”
His mana-infused voice pierced through the screams and thunderous crashes and reached one person’s ears.
Covered in wounds and blood as he fought back the endless stream of monsters, Xiao Shen answered with a battle cry.
“Speak!”
“Withdraw the Public Security Armed Forces Department. We have to retreat now!”
“What? But if we retreat now...”
Choi Minwoo already knew what the young Hunter was about to say.
Retreats—and the pursuits that followed—were when the greatest number of casualties occurred.
Especially in a situation like this. If the Hunters serving as the last line of defense withdrew, the People’s Liberation Army would fall straight into the monster army’s grasp.
“If we’re surrounded, it’s all over. Do you understand? Take the surviving Hunters and the rear units and get out of the city while you still can!”
“...Mr. Choi.”
“I know what you’re thinking. But we have no other choice.”
Xiao Shen squeezed his eyes shut without realizing it.
He knew what the situation was. No—he understood it better than almost anyone.

The tide had turned sharply against them from the moment the battle began, and the humans had been driven all the way back to the hospital they were using as a temporary command center. If the monsters completed their encirclement—
Annihilation.
His deliberation felt long, but only a moment passed.
Xiao Shen opened his eyes and shouted with all his strength as he deflected the attacks raining down on him.
“Retreat! All Public Security Armed Forces Department personnel, withdraw immediately! The North Gate is open!”
In wartime, the orders of a commander like Xiao Shen were absolute.
All the more so when the military leadership, including General Liao, had not even shown their faces.
Good.
The soldiers might not have much hope, but the Hunters’ odds of survival would rise dramatically. If Xiao Shen made the right calls, many of them might break through the encirclement and survive.
Yes. This is enough.
Feeling his heart grow lighter, Choi Minwoo launched himself forward.
Not toward the North Gate, which the monsters had yet to block, but toward the People’s Liberation Army being slaughtered by the monsters.
It feels like I’m going to kill myself.
Why had he made this choice? Even he could not understand it.
Still...
For a man heading to his death, he felt surprisingly good.
Perhaps because dark clouds had gathered overhead, the wind was cool. And behind him, he had companions who would die alongside him, so he would not have to die alone.
Choi Minwoo suddenly spoke.
“Why didn’t you retreat?”
Xiao Shen, who should have been heading toward the North Gate, gave him a faint smile.
“What about you, Mr. Choi?”
“...I asked first.”
“Then I suppose I should answer first. Public Security Armed Forces Department!”
At the regimental commander’s call, the roughly three hundred Hunters following behind him let out a thunderous shout.
“To eliminate monsters and protect the people from every threat!”

“This is why we do not retreat. The 325 members of the Sichuan Province Public Security Armed Forces Department’s 1st Regiment, led by Regimental Commander Xiao Shen, have come to protect the people!”
Xiao Shen continued in a quiet voice.
“Now it’s your turn to answer, Mr. Choi.”
Choi Minwoo silently gazed at the thousands of monsters drawing closer, then suddenly muttered,
“Shit. There sure are a lot of them.”
“That’s probably what he would have said. Then he would have fought harder than anyone else and won in the end.”
It was true. He had always been that way.
He had never backed down, no matter the situation, and he had never given up. Choi Minwoo had watched him longer and more closely than anyone else, so he knew.
That man, Jin Taekyung, was a hero of the new age. Choi Minwoo could never work miracles the way he did.
But still—
“It’s embarrassing.”
“What?”
“Jin Taekyung is technically my subordinate, you see. At a time like this, his superior ought to lead by example.”
Choi Minwoo burst into laughter, loudly enough to leave Xiao Shen bewildered.
His heart felt as light as a dandelion seed, and an unfamiliar power unlike anything he had ever felt before surged through his body as he shot toward the enemy.
Mr. Jin. I’ll see you later.
If I survive today, as soon as possible.
If I die, as late as possible.
Let’s meet then.
Hissssss.
The blade of his sword, filled with aura brighter and more radiant than ever, pointed toward the enemies.
The suicide squad of more than three hundred Hunters roared loud enough to deafen the ears, their fighting spirit surging as they shot forward behind him like arrows.
“Waaaaaaaaah!”
Two Death Knights who had been leading thousands of monsters in the slaughter of the People’s Liberation Army looked down from their skeletal warhorses at the pitiful human force.
—Aksar. Garosh.
A moment later, the black wave swallowed the single white pebble.
The outcome had been decided from the beginning. Yet at the end of that battle, more fiercely fought than any before it, one man’s sword had never lost its light.
The two Death Knights dropped to one knee before the Black Knight watching them.
—In the battle—
—we achieved victory.
—Today, this glory—
—we offer to our Lord.
Their voices were clipped and devoid of intonation. Even at the news of victory, the Black Knight merely nodded without interest.
It had gone as expected. The humans had been unable to stop his mighty legion and had collapsed in a single stroke.
But if asked whether everything had unfolded according to the Black Knight’s wishes, the answer would have been no.
Those humans from before.
After breaking through the city and forcing the humans to retreat at the start of the battle, the Black Knight had turned his warhorse wherever the whim took him.
For some reason, he had returned to the strangely familiar place from the previous day, where he found something small.
Human? No. Not human. A child. And this is a shoe.
Memories and words surfaced one after another.
As the Black Knight had thought, it was a child’s shoe—a tiny infant’s shoe lost in the chaos and left behind without anyone realizing it had fallen.
The infinitely small, dirt-covered shoe seemed strangely familiar. Looking at it made his chest ache.
Hm? My chest aches?
What an unfamiliar expression.

The Black Knight’s body had been incapable of feeling pain from the beginning. His master had personally created him and bestowed a powerful blessing upon him. Naturally, he never tired and felt no pain.
More importantly, this was no time to be swayed by something so trivial.
—Lord.
—Is something wrong?
He did not know why he had done it.
The Black Knight tucked the shoe into a gap in his armor and changed the subject.
—No. Rather, quite a few humans managed to escape alive.
—We apologize.
—It was our failure.
—There must be a reason.
The Death Knights bowed their heads deeply.
—The humans’ resistance—
—was fiercer than expected.
—In exchange—
—we gained a small prize.
As if they had been waiting for those words, the densely packed monsters parted left and right to open a path.
A Troll approached cautiously, lowered the two figures slung over its shoulders, and stepped back.
The Black Knight’s eyes flickered as he regarded the “small prize.”
—They are humans.
—Yes.
The two loyal retainers answered in unison, then continued.
—Reap their souls yourself—
—and make them servants of our Lord.
—If you do so, Lord—
—you will grow even mightier.
They were right. Those two humans possessed rich, enticing souls.
If he personally reaped their souls and took them as subordinates, they would be reborn as even greater warriors. They might even prove worthy of commanding an entire force.
But—
Why?
The Black Knight realized that he was hesitating.
This was obviously something he had to do. Powerful subordinates would strengthen the legion, and strengthening the legion was an act of loyalty and devotion to the King of Death he served.
So why was he hesitating?
What is making me hesitate?
Ordinarily, he would have held back if something felt wrong. But the Black Knight had experienced this same confusion far too often of late.
The fact that he had forced himself to reach out might have been an act of defiance against himself.
—I will accept your suggestion.
Then, just as the Black Knight reached toward the two humans to reap their souls—
“I’ve been thinking about it carefully.”
A voice rang out through the air, and the Black Knight raised his head.
Someone stood atop the half-burned, half-collapsed hospital, framed by sunlight streaming through the dark clouds behind him.
“Ten percent is surprisingly high when you think about it. Hmm. Definitely higher than my chances of getting a girlfriend.”
The Black Knight’s eyes narrowed. He recognized that energy. He had sensed it from afar the previous day.
At last, he had come face-to-face with the owner of that immense heat.
—Who are you?
“Me?”
Swish. Tap.
It happened in an instant. The young human dropped rapidly from a dizzying height, yet landed as lightly as a leaf. He pointed to himself with one finger and grinned.
“I’m one damn lucky bastard.”
The next moment, the Black Knight saw it clearly.
The human’s finger shifting to point at him.
And every trace of emotion vanishing from the human’s face.
“You’re, what...”
His voice was cold enough to make even the dead shudder.
“You’re one damn unlucky bastard.”

sentences.text: Team Leader Choi—or rather, Choi Minwoo—thought,
What should I do?
His heart pounded wildly, but his mind was ice-cold.
Only thirty minutes had passed since the battle began.

The hastily constructed defensive line had collapsed the instant the fighting started, then been torn apart as the highest-grade monsters slipped through the gaps and ran rampant without meeting any resistance.
Just like now.
Crunch!
Sharp fangs tore savagely into a human throat.
The Lycanthrope tossed aside the Hunter, whose last breath escaped in a wheeze, and let out a roar.
—Awooooooo!
Those became the Lycanthrope’s final words.
Whoosh!
Slash!
Its gray fur turned red as its body toppled sideways.
Choi Minwoo took its head off with a clean strike, then bent backward without a moment to catch his breath.
Whoooooom!
Crack!
The blow missed him by a handspan.
An ax blade rippling with ominous magical power grazed past Choi Minwoo and smashed the heads of two nearby Orcs.
The headless knight, a Dullahan, attacked the human in front of it without the slightest hesitation, despite having killed fellow monsters.
Swoooooosh!
Slash!
—Krrk!
“Guh!”
As the enormous halberd swept back and forth, the humans and monsters caught within its reach were hacked to pieces.
A Dullahan was an A-rank monster that required three Hunters of the same rank to handle safely.
But Choi Minwoo slipped past its attack and thrust out his sword without hesitation.
Now!
A short exhalation.
Then a strike like a flash of light.
Thud!
The blade, enchanted with three different spells and forged by a Master Artisan, pierced the Dullahan through the shoulder.
It might not feel pain, having already died once and become undead, but its body was still human.
The muscles and tendons in its right arm were severed, and the halberd dropped heavily to the ground.
Choi Minwoo did not miss the opening.
Shhhhhk!
A white blade of aura cleaved the Dullahan in half at the waist.
It must not have been dead for long, because rotten blood sprayed from its collapsing body and splattered across Choi Minwoo’s face.
But despite the overpowering stench stabbing at his nose, he did not so much as twitch an eyebrow.
Choi Minwoo was gripped by the tension of the battlefield, cold reason, and a faint exhilaration.
That makes ten.
That was how many A-rank monsters Choi Minwoo had defeated by himself today.
Including those of lower grades, the number had to be well over fifty.
Was I always this strong?
If he answered that question honestly, the answer was no.
Perhaps because of the Arch Lich’s influence, the monsters he had encountered in China were slightly stronger and far more ferocious.
Even so, Choi Minwoo had been able to distinguish himself in such a chaotic battle because he had been blessed with two strokes of luck.
The first was—
The Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique.
The Mana Cultivation Method he had learned directly from Jin Taekyung.
Choi Minwoo had his doubts about Jin Taekyung’s claim that it was a family heirloom passed down through generations.
But he had no doubt whatsoever that it was an outstanding secret technique.
The Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique allowed him to control his energy reliably while greatly improving how he distributed his strength.
The immense mana he had gained while learning it also gave him the stamina to keep fighting without tiring easily.
And his second stroke of luck was—
—Gwoooooar!
Boom!
A length of rebar swung with berserk force and smashed through the concrete road.
Choi Minwoo stepped on the ogre’s thick arm and sprang upward, bringing his sword down with all his strength.
Thrust!
The aura-infused blade split the ogre’s crown as easily as tofu.
Thud.
The four-meter giant dropped to its knees with a heavy crash.
Standing on the dead creature’s shoulder, Choi Minwoo quickly swept his gaze over his surroundings.
He’s not here.
Screams and death filled the hellish scene on every side.
But the monster was nowhere to be seen.
The monster who had displayed unbelievable power the moment the battle began—the commander of the monster army and leader of the Death Knights.
Where the hell is he?
Choi Minwoo clearly remembered the Black Knight sweeping aside dozens of Hunters with a single blow.
If the creature had truly committed itself to the battle, the humans might have been annihilated before they lasted even thirty minutes.
But for some reason, the Black Knight had not appeared again.
Was it the monster’s arrogance?
Did it consider the battle too insignificant to warrant its involvement?
Choi Minwoo could not understand it.
But the Black Knight’s absence was both his second stroke of luck and his final chance to make a decision.
We have to retreat.
The urban battle had already lost all meaning.
The monster army, numbering around ten thousand, had already covered the city like a swarm of ants.
Among them were more than a hundred A-rank monsters.
The humans were outmatched in both numbers and strength.
Nearly half of the thousand Hunters from the Public Security Armed Forces Department who had held the front line were already dead or wounded.
And more than half of the damned People’s Liberation Army had thrown down their weapons and fled before the monsters even reached them.
The armored units, reduced to heaps of scrap metal, and the air force, becoming prey for the flying monsters, were simply more of the same.
Rat-a-tat-tat-tat-tat!
Boom!
A state-of-the-art combat helicopter lost its balance and plunged from the sky, exploding in flames.
Around a dozen soldiers caught in the flying debris died without even having time to scream.
It was a horrifying sight, but they were fortunate in one respect: their deaths had been painless.
A moment later, the monster horde began tearing everyone else apart indiscriminately.
—Kraaaaaaang!
Whoom!
Crack!
The foreleg of a Saber Tiger, carrying several tons of force, crushed a soldier’s limbs and burst his head.
The soldiers of the People’s Liberation Army were nowhere near as fast as Hunters, and the rifles they carried were little better than slingshots against the monsters.
Choi Minwoo clenched his teeth at the merciless slaughter unfolding before him.
Get a grip.
You can’t save all of them.
He did not hypocritically preach about sacrificing the few for the many.
He simply faced the situation with a cold eye and prepared himself to play the villain.
Could we have stopped them if he’d come?
Jin Taekyung suddenly came to mind, but that was nothing more than futile regret.
Even after he hounded the communications officer into frantically transmitting emergency signals, there had been no response.
A carefully planned surprise attack combined with thorough communications interference.
For now, all he could do was hope that one of the countless glass bottles cast into the sea would somehow reach Jin Taekyung.
Thud!
Choi Minwoo drove his sword into the chest of a charging Minotaur and shouted,
“Xiao Shen!”
His mana-infused voice pierced through the screams and thunderous crashes and reached one person’s ears.
Covered in wounds and blood as he fought back the endless stream of monsters, Xiao Shen answered with a battle cry.
“Speak!”
“Withdraw the Public Security Armed Forces Department.
We have to retreat now!”
“What?
But if we retreat now...”
Choi Minwoo already knew what the young Hunter was about to say.
Retreats—and the pursuits that followed—were when the greatest number of casualties occurred.
Especially in a situation like this.
If the Hunters serving as the last line of defense withdrew, the People’s Liberation Army would fall straight into the monster army’s grasp.
“If we’re surrounded, it’s all over.
Do you understand?
Take the surviving Hunters and the rear units and get out of the city while you still can!”
Choi.”
“I know what you’re thinking.
But we have no other choice.”
Xiao Shen squeezed his eyes shut without realizing it.
He knew what the situation was.
No—he understood it better than almost anyone.
The tide had turned sharply against them from the moment the battle began, and the humans had been driven all the way back to the hospital they were using as a temporary command center.
If the monsters completed their encirclement—
Annihilation.
His deliberation felt long, but only a moment passed.
Xiao Shen opened his eyes and shouted with all his strength as he deflected the attacks raining down on him.
“Retreat!
All Public Security Armed Forces Department personnel, withdraw immediately!
The North Gate is open!”
In wartime, the orders of a commander like Xiao Shen were absolute.
All the more so when the military leadership, including General Liao, had not even shown their faces.
Good.
The soldiers might not have much hope, but the Hunters’ odds of survival would rise dramatically.
If Xiao Shen made the right calls, many of them might break through the encirclement and survive.
Yes.
This is enough.
Feeling his heart grow lighter, Choi Minwoo launched himself forward.
Not toward the North Gate, which the monsters had yet to block, but toward the People’s Liberation Army being slaughtered by the monsters.
It feels like I’m going to kill myself.
Why had he made this choice?
Even he could not understand it.
Still...
For a man heading to his death, he felt surprisingly good.
Perhaps because dark clouds had gathered overhead, the wind was cool.
And behind him, he had companions who would die alongside him, so he would not have to die alone.
Choi Minwoo suddenly spoke.
“Why didn’t you retreat?”
Xiao Shen, who should have been heading toward the North Gate, gave him a faint smile.
“What about you, Mr.
Choi?”
“...I asked first.”
“Then I suppose I should answer first.
Public Security Armed Forces Department!”
At the regimental commander’s call, the roughly three hundred Hunters following behind him let out a thunderous shout.
“To eliminate monsters and protect the people from every threat!”
“This is why we do not retreat.
The 325 members of the Sichuan Province Public Security Armed Forces Department’s 1st Regiment, led by Regimental Commander Xiao Shen, have come to protect the people!”
Xiao Shen continued in a quiet voice.
“Now it’s your turn to answer, Mr.
Choi.”
Choi Minwoo silently gazed at the thousands of monsters drawing closer, then suddenly muttered,
“Shit.
There sure are a lot of them.”
“That’s probably what he would have said.
Then he would have fought harder than anyone else and won in the end.”
It was true.
He had always been that way.
He had never backed down, no matter the situation, and he had never given up.
Choi Minwoo had watched him longer and more closely than anyone else, so he knew.
That man, Jin Taekyung, was a hero of the new age.
Choi Minwoo could never work miracles the way he did.
But still—
“It’s embarrassing.”
“What?”
“Jin Taekyung is technically my subordinate, you see.
At a time like this, his superior ought to lead by example.”
Choi Minwoo burst into laughter, loudly enough to leave Xiao Shen bewildered.
His heart felt as light as a dandelion seed, and an unfamiliar power unlike anything he had ever felt before surged through his body as he shot toward the enemy.
Mr.
Jin.
I’ll see you later.
If I survive today, as soon as possible.
If I die, as late as possible.
Let’s meet then.
Hissssss.
The blade of his sword, filled with aura brighter and more radiant than ever, pointed toward the enemies.
The suicide squad of more than three hundred Hunters roared loud enough to deafen the ears, their fighting spirit surging as they shot forward behind him like arrows.
“Waaaaaaaaah!”
Two Death Knights who had been leading thousands of monsters in the slaughter of the People’s Liberation Army looked down from their skeletal warhorses at the pitiful human force.
—Aksar.
Garosh.
A moment later, the black wave swallowed the single white pebble.
The outcome had been decided from the beginning.
Yet at the end of that battle, more fiercely fought than any before it, one man’s sword had never lost its light.
The two Death Knights dropped to one knee before the Black Knight watching them.
—In the battle—
—we achieved victory.
—Today, this glory—
—we offer to our Lord.
Their voices were clipped and devoid of intonation.
Even at the news of victory, the Black Knight merely nodded without interest.
It had gone as expected.
The humans had been unable to stop his mighty legion and had collapsed in a single stroke.
But if asked whether everything had unfolded according to the Black Knight’s wishes, the answer would have been no.
Those humans from before.
After breaking through the city and forcing the humans to retreat at the start of the battle, the Black Knight had turned his warhorse wherever the whim took him.
For some reason, he had returned to the strangely familiar place from the previous day, where he found something small.
Human?
No.
Not human.
A child.
And this is a shoe.
Memories and words surfaced one after another.
As the Black Knight had thought, it was a child’s shoe—a tiny infant’s shoe lost in the chaos and left behind without anyone realizing it had fallen.
The infinitely small, dirt-covered shoe seemed strangely familiar.
Looking at it made his chest ache.
Hm?
My chest aches?
What an unfamiliar expression.
The Black Knight’s body had been incapable of feeling pain from the beginning.
His master had personally created him and bestowed a powerful blessing upon him.
Naturally, he never tired and felt no pain.
More importantly, this was no time to be swayed by something so trivial.
—Lord.
—Is something wrong?
He did not know why he had done it.
The Black Knight tucked the shoe into a gap in his armor and changed the subject.
—No.
Rather, quite a few humans managed to escape alive.
—We apologize.
—It was our failure.
—There must be a reason.
The Death Knights bowed their heads deeply.
—The humans’ resistance—
—was fiercer than expected.
—In exchange—
—we gained a small prize.
As if they had been waiting for those words, the densely packed monsters parted left and right to open a path.
A Troll approached cautiously, lowered the two figures slung over its shoulders, and stepped back.
The Black Knight’s eyes flickered as he regarded the “small prize.”
—They are humans.
—Yes.
The two loyal retainers answered in unison, then continued.
—Reap their souls yourself—
—and make them servants of our Lord.
—If you do so, Lord—
—you will grow even mightier.
They were right.
Those two humans possessed rich, enticing souls.
If he personally reaped their souls and took them as subordinates, they would be reborn as even greater warriors.
They might even prove worthy of commanding an entire force.
But—
Why?
The Black Knight realized that he was hesitating.
This was obviously something he had to do.
Powerful subordinates would strengthen the legion, and strengthening the legion was an act of loyalty and devotion to the King of Death he served.
So why was he hesitating?
What is making me hesitate?
Ordinarily, he would have held back if something felt wrong.
But the Black Knight had experienced this same confusion far too often of late.
The fact that he had forced himself to reach out might have been an act of defiance against himself.
—I will accept your suggestion.
Then, just as the Black Knight reached toward the two humans to reap their souls—
“I’ve been thinking about it carefully.”
A voice rang out through the air, and the Black Knight raised his head.
Someone stood atop the half-burned, half-collapsed hospital, framed by sunlight streaming through the dark clouds behind him.
“Ten percent is surprisingly high when you think about it.
Hmm.
Definitely higher than my chances of getting a girlfriend.”
The Black Knight’s eyes narrowed.
He recognized that energy.
He had sensed it from afar the previous day.
At last, he had come face-to-face with the owner of that immense heat.
—Who are you?
“Me?”
Swish.
Tap.
It happened in an instant.
The young human dropped rapidly from a dizzying height, yet landed as lightly as a leaf.
He pointed to himself with one finger and grinned.
“I’m one damn lucky bastard.”
The next moment, the Black Knight saw it clearly.
The human’s finger shifting to point at him.
And every trace of emotion vanishing from the human’s face.
“You’re, what...”
His voice was cold enough to make even the dead shudder.
“You’re one damn unlucky bastard.”

chapters.title: Chapter 398
paragraphs: Before attempting teleportation, a thought suddenly occurred to me.
If I put the odds of everything that’s happened over the past two years into percentages, what would they be?
What were the odds that an F-rank Hunter, trudging uphill after being fired from his Guild, would find an old capsule abandoned at a recycling station?
What were the odds that the capsule would turn out to be a passage to another world?
What were the odds that I would begin my second life as the Third Young Master of a frontier martial family—not as a member of the Namgung Family or a direct Disciple of Huashan?
What were the odds that I would survive one war, two bloody massacres, and more brushes with death than I could count...?
After considering all of that, I reached a single conclusion.
“Ten percent is enough after all.”
With that quiet murmur, I reached out.
Seizing an Object Through Empty Space.
Three jiazi of internal energy pulled Team Leader Choi and Xiao Shen toward me. The Death Knights and monsters tried to move, but stopped when their leader raised a hand.
Ignoring them, I checked the two men’s condition. Their breathing was faint, and their qi was so precarious it seemed ready to vanish at any moment.
If I had taken a jet instead of teleporting, I might have been too late forever.
“I would’ve tried even with a one-percent chance. I’m not the kind of guy who dies for nothing.”
Of course, I had also taken out some insurance in case the worst happened. I just hadn’t expected to use it so soon, let alone under circumstances like these.
Open Inventory. Summon.
I paid no attention to the monsters watching me.
The leader saw me pull the item I needed from my Inventory and asked in a flat voice,
“An extradimensional space. Have you learned Magic?”
Shut your fucking mouth.
I swallowed the words hovering on the tip of my tongue. Normally, that would have been quite difficult, but right now, it wasn’t.
I did not want anyone to interfere with me. At least not right now.
Pop.
When I removed the magically sealed stopper, a faint fragrance drifted out. Milky liquid sloshed inside the clear glass bottle.
A Top-Grade Potion.
A miraculous medicine said to heal any injury as long as the patient was still breathing.
Right now, I couldn’t have cared less about the rarity or value of the scant hundred milliliters in that bottle.
I simply thanked Wu Heixing for being both fabulously wealthy and incredibly stupid, then let the potion trickle between the lips of the patient lying there like a corpse.
Hang on a little longer, Shen.
Team Leader Choi came first. Partly because of all the time we had spent together, but even if we had shared no bond at all, I would still have chosen him first.
That was how serious Team Leader Choi’s injuries were.
This is...

His left arm had been torn away from the shoulder. His right ankle was mangled as if something had chewed and swallowed it, while his left leg had been cleanly amputated. Seven ribs were broken, and his spine was fractured.
And...
His right hand, twisted at an unnatural angle, still clutched the hilt of his sword.
The leather strap he had fastened tightly around it so he wouldn’t lose his grip was soaked through with blood.
I silently undid the strap, pried the sword from his crushed hand, and set it beside him.
I didn’t forget to scold him in my head.
Why did you do this? It’s a miracle you’re still alive.
Then the real miracle began.
When I carefully tilted the bottle and administered exactly half of it, a sound like something burning filled the air, and the wounds covering Team Leader Choi’s entire body began to heal.
Hissssss, hissssss—
Bones regrew, severed muscles rejoined, and damaged organs and flesh knitted together.
He recovered even faster than a Troll, the very embodiment of regeneration. As if time itself had been reversed, color finally began returning to Team Leader Choi’s face.
His qi has stabilized too. This should be enough.
I couldn’t have asked for a better result.
The others watching, however, were far less pleased.
“Fearless human.”
“Stop at once.”
“They have been granted the destiny—”
“of becoming subservient to our mighty Lord.”
I silently regarded the two Death Knights who stepped forward in place of their leader.
Clad from head to toe in pitch-black armor, they looked almost like twins. They were roughly the same height, and even their voices were difficult to tell apart.
There was only one obvious difference between them: the weapons at their waists.
One has a mace. The other has a sword.
That was enough to give me my answer. I had solved the question; I could write down the answer later.
Right now, I had another problem to deal with.
“You’ve been through hell too, Shen.”
Xiao Shen wasn’t as badly injured as Team Leader Choi, but his wounds were still severe. I was about to pour the remaining half of the potion into his mouth when—
“Wretched human.”
“This is your final warning.”
“Put down those two humans, step back, and beg for mercy.”
“Then our Lord will take you as his servant.”
“A servant?”
“Yes.”
One of the Death Knights stepped toward me, its voice flat and emotionless. The scabbard secured at its waist swayed with every step.
Clank. Clank. Clank.
One step. Two steps. Three.
There wasn’t a trace of hesitation in its approach.
Thousands of monsters and their leader were watching.
The Death Knight spoke with such confidence that it was hard to believe it was an emotionless undead monster.
“You possess a truly great and radiant soul. Become one of us.”
A great and radiant soul...
Without even raising my head, I continued pouring the potion.
Once the last few drops had fallen into Xiao Shen’s mouth, I stoppered the empty bottle and returned it to my Inventory.
Hissssss, hissssss.
A signal that recovery had begun.
I straightened at the welcome sound I had been waiting for, looked at the Death Knight, and finally said what I’d been wanting to say.
“His left leg.”
“Hm?”
“Team Leader Choi’s left leg. Everything below a point one handspan beneath the knee was gone. Cut off clean. And Xiao Shen—that young kid lost his right arm.”
“Human. What are you trying to say?”
“What am I trying to say?”
I gave it a faint smile.
“If you cut off perfectly good limbs, you should’ve been prepared for what came next.”
And in the next instant—
In the sliver of time left after an instant had been split in half, then split again, the creature was suddenly right in front of me.
No.
It was the other way around.
It hadn’t come to me.
I had gone to it.
“Let’s see that vaunted skill of yours.”
Everything happened at once. The Death Knight tried to draw its sword, and I reached out with my left hand and pressed firmly against the back of its hand.
That was both the beginning and the end.
Shing. Click!
The dark blade had barely cleared its scabbard before it was forced back inside.
By then, my fist had already punched through the creature’s chest.
Crunch!

The Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist, charged with the Scorching Yang Qi of three jiazi, vaporized even the fistful of blood remaining inside the undead monster and blazed up using its long-dead body as kindling.
Whoosh! Rooooar!
Engulfed in flames that refused to die, the Death Knight flailed its arms and turned toward its kin.
It staggered back along the path it had strode down so confidently, then crumbled into ash.
Though thousands of monsters were gathered there, everything went silent as if someone had pressed a mute button.
I took White Flame from my Inventory and slowly began to walk.
Splash. Splash.
Everywhere I looked and everywhere I stepped, there were corpses and blood.
Countless rifles caught against my feet. A soldier in a crooked combat helmet stared at the sky with lifeless eyes.
At least his corpse was still intact.
In what appeared to have been the fiercest part of the battlefield, Hunters from the Public Security Armed Forces Department lay dead, their bodies mangled beyond recognition.
I had spent a full week with the 1st Regiment under Xiao Shen. Among the corpses were several faces I recognized.
So many died. So damn many.
At least three thousand humans had died here today alone.
How many would that number become if I added the dead from all five fronts? If I included the civilians killed in this Monster Wave?
Thud!
I borrowed an unknown Hunter’s spear and drove it deep into the ground. Team Leader Choi’s leather strap, tied securely to the end of the shaft, fluttered in the wind.
Beyond it stood an army of thousands of monsters—and him.
System Lv. 135 Death Knight Lord
Death Knight Lord.
What a grand name. Then again, the monster possessed enough power to live up to it.
The circumstances are different, but I do have another one like him.
I called out to the creature currently setting a new record for silence.
“Let me ask you a favor.”
I expected him to pretend he hadn’t heard, but after a brief hesitation, the Skeleton Warlord answered.
“...A favor? You’re not asking me to fight beside you, are you?”
“Of course not.”
I had never expected that of him, and I didn’t now. The favor I wanted had nothing to do with fighting.
It was about protecting someone.
“Protect the two people behind me. No matter what it takes.”
With my permission, the Skeleton Warlord had been absorbing death qi whenever possible, growing stronger in the process.
As a Named Monster, he should have been capable of handling several ordinary A-rank monsters by himself.
“When this battle is over, I’ll grant you any wish.”
“In that case, there’s nothing I can’t do. But how long am I supposed to protect them?”
“That’s obvious...”
I raised White Flame and pointed it at the Death Knight Lord.
“Until every last one of those bastards is dead.”
“You lunatic...!”
“Too late.”
I pulled the Skeleton Warlord’s skull from my Inventory and tossed it behind me.
Crack. Pop.
As he hurriedly regenerated his body, I stroked the leather strap fluttering from the spear shaft.
How had he felt?
How had they all felt?
What had gone through their minds as they charged toward their deaths?
I couldn’t begin to imagine.
There was only one thing I knew for certain.
“Any bastard who comes past this spear is going to fucking die.”
The fire dragon coiled within my dantian raised its head.
CRUNCH!
Flesh and bone shattered, spraying in every direction.
An ogre’s limbs went flying, while a Troll was engulfed in unquenchable flames before it had a chance to regenerate.
Boom! Slash!
The head of a Lycanthrope baring its fangs exploded.

A Dullahan charged through the spray of foul-smelling brain matter, only to be cleaved in half with a single blow. Its halberd found a new master and shot away with tremendous force, tearing through a Wyvern’s wing.
CRACKLE!
“Kyaaaaaaa!”
Thud-thud-thud!
Blood rained from the sky.
At the same moment, a streak of blue flame cut through the downpour.
Whoooooosh! Slash!
A storm of blood erupted. Whenever the flames streaked through the air, dozens of monsters fell and hundreds recoiled.
And the thousands of monsters...
At some point, they began to be overwhelmed.
They had grown afraid of a single human—and of the line of death he had drawn with a single spear.
“L-Lord.”
For the first time, the Death Knight’s flat, unwavering voice trembled with emotion.
The Black Knight knew perfectly well what his subordinate’s desperate plea meant.
“Make way.”
Between the slits of the deeply lowered helmet, red eyes flickered.
As he advanced, immense magical power rolling off him, he tried to ignore the strange words and scenes that kept surfacing in his mind.
Nothing could take precedence over his creator, his eternal lord.
“Are you listening, my servant?”
At his lord’s voice echoing like a hallucination, the Black Knight quietly replied,
“Yes, my lord.”
Until the very end, he failed to realize one thing.
That his hand was groping somewhere between the plates of his armor.

Shut your fucking mouth.
I swallowed the words hovering on the tip of my tongue.
Normally, that would have been quite difficult, but right now, it wasn’t.
I did not want anyone to interfere with me.
At least not right now.
Pop.
When I removed the magically sealed stopper, a faint fragrance drifted out.
Milky liquid sloshed inside the clear glass bottle.
A Top-Grade Potion.
A miraculous medicine said to heal any injury as long as the patient was still breathing.
Right now, I couldn’t have cared less about the rarity or value of the scant hundred milliliters in that bottle.
I simply thanked Wu Heixing for being both fabulously wealthy and incredibly stupid, then let the potion trickle between the lips of the patient lying there like a corpse.
Hang on a little longer, Shen.
Team Leader Choi came first.
Partly because of all the time we had spent together, but even if we had shared no bond at all, I would still have chosen him first.
That was how serious Team Leader Choi’s injuries were.
This is...
His left arm had been torn away from the shoulder.
His right ankle was mangled as if something had chewed and swallowed it, while his left leg had been cleanly amputated.
Seven ribs were broken, and his spine was fractured.
And...
His right hand, twisted at an unnatural angle, still clutched the hilt of his sword.
The leather strap he had fastened tightly around it so he wouldn’t lose his grip was soaked through with blood.
I silently undid the strap, pried the sword from his crushed hand, and set it beside him.
I didn’t forget to scold him in my head.
Why did you do this?
It’s a miracle you’re still alive.
Then the real miracle began.
When I carefully tilted the bottle and administered exactly half of it, a sound like something burning filled the air, and the wounds covering Team Leader Choi’s entire body began to heal.
Hissssss, hissssss—
Bones regrew, severed muscles rejoined, and damaged organs and flesh knitted together.
He recovered even faster than a Troll, the very embodiment of regeneration.
As if time itself had been reversed, color finally began returning to Team Leader Choi’s face.
His qi has stabilized too.
This should be enough.
I couldn’t have asked for a better result.
The others watching, however, were far less pleased.
“Fearless human.”
“Stop at once.”
“They have been granted the destiny—”
“of becoming subservient to our mighty Lord.”
I silently regarded the two Death Knights who stepped forward in place of their leader.
Clad from head to toe in pitch-black armor, they looked almost like twins.
They were roughly the same height, and even their voices were difficult to tell apart.
There was only one obvious difference between them: the weapons at their waists.
One has a mace.
The other has a sword.
That was enough to give me my answer.
I had solved the question; I could write down the answer later.
Right now, I had another problem to deal with.
“You’ve been through hell too, Shen.”
Xiao Shen wasn’t as badly injured as Team Leader Choi, but his wounds were still severe.
I was about to pour the remaining half of the potion into his mouth when—
“Wretched human.”
“This is your final warning.”
“Put down those two humans, step back, and beg for mercy.”
“Then our Lord will take you as his servant.”
“A servant?”
“Yes.”
One of the Death Knights stepped toward me, its voice flat and emotionless.
The scabbard secured at its waist swayed with every step.
Clank.
Clank.
Clank.
One step.
Two steps.
Three.
There wasn’t a trace of hesitation in its approach.
Thousands of monsters and their leader were watching.
The Death Knight spoke with such confidence that it was hard to believe it was an emotionless undead monster.
“You possess a truly great and radiant soul.
Become one of us.”
A great and radiant soul...
Without even raising my head, I continued pouring the potion.
Once the last few drops had fallen into Xiao Shen’s mouth, I stoppered the empty bottle and returned it to my Inventory.
Hissssss, hissssss.
A signal that recovery had begun.
I straightened at the welcome sound I had been waiting for, looked at the Death Knight, and finally said what I’d been wanting to say.
“His left leg.”
“Hm?”
“Team Leader Choi’s left leg.
Everything below a point one handspan beneath the knee was gone.
Cut off clean.
And Xiao Shen—that young kid lost his right arm.”
“Human.
What are you trying to say?”
“What am I trying to say?”
I gave it a faint smile.
“If you cut off perfectly good limbs, you should’ve been prepared for what came next.”
And in the next instant—
In the sliver of time left after an instant had been split in half, then split again, the creature was suddenly right in front of me.
No.
It was the other way around.
It hadn’t come to me.
I had gone to it.
“Let’s see that vaunted skill of yours.”
Everything happened at once.
The Death Knight tried to draw its sword, and I reached out with my left hand and pressed firmly against the back of its hand.
That was both the beginning and the end.
Shing.
Click!
The dark blade had barely cleared its scabbard before it was forced back inside.
By then, my fist had already punched through the creature’s chest.
Crunch!

The Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist, charged with the Scorching Yang Qi of three jiazi, vaporized even the fistful of blood remaining inside the undead monster and blazed up using its long-dead body as kindling.
Whoosh!
Rooooar!
Engulfed in flames that refused to die, the Death Knight flailed its arms and turned toward its kin.
It staggered back along the path it had strode down so confidently, then crumbled into ash.
Though thousands of monsters were gathered there, everything went silent as if someone had pressed a mute button.
I took White Flame from my Inventory and slowly began to walk.
Splash.
Splash.
Everywhere I looked and everywhere I stepped, there were corpses and blood.
Countless rifles caught against my feet.
A soldier in a crooked combat helmet stared at the sky with lifeless eyes.
At least his corpse was still intact.
In what appeared to have been the fiercest part of the battlefield, Hunters from the Public Security Armed Forces Department lay dead, their bodies mangled beyond recognition.
I had spent a full week with the 1st Regiment under Xiao Shen.
Among the corpses were several faces I recognized.
So many died.
So damn many.
At least three thousand humans had died here today alone.
How many would that number become if I added the dead from all five fronts?
If I included the civilians killed in this Monster Wave?
Thud!
I borrowed an unknown Hunter’s spear and drove it deep into the ground.
Team Leader Choi’s leather strap, tied securely to the end of the shaft, fluttered in the wind.
Beyond it stood an army of thousands of monsters—and him.
System Lv.
135 Death Knight Lord
Death Knight Lord.
What a grand name.
Then again, the monster possessed enough power to live up to it.
The circumstances are different, but I do have another one like him.
I called out to the creature currently setting a new record for silence.
“Let me ask you a favor.”
I expected him to pretend he hadn’t heard, but after a brief hesitation, the Skeleton Warlord answered.
“...A favor?
You’re not asking me to fight beside you, are you?”
“Of course not.”
I had never expected that of him, and I didn’t now.
The favor I wanted had nothing to do with fighting.
It was about protecting someone.
“Protect the two people behind me.
No matter what it takes.”
With my permission, the Skeleton Warlord had been absorbing death qi whenever possible, growing stronger in the process.
As a Named Monster, he should have been capable of handling several ordinary A-rank monsters by himself.
“When this battle is over, I’ll grant you any wish.”
“In that case, there’s nothing I can’t do.
But how long am I supposed to protect them?”
“That’s obvious...”
I raised White Flame and pointed it at the Death Knight Lord.
“Until every last one of those bastards is dead.”
“You lunatic...!”
“Too late.”
I pulled the Skeleton Warlord’s skull from my Inventory and tossed it behind me.
Crack.
Pop.
As he hurriedly regenerated his body, I stroked the leather strap fluttering from the spear shaft.
How had he felt?
How had they all felt?
What had gone through their minds as they charged toward their deaths?
I couldn’t begin to imagine.
There was only one thing I knew for certain.
“Any bastard who comes past this spear is going to fucking die.”
The fire dragon coiled within my dantian raised its head.
CRUNCH!
Flesh and bone shattered, spraying in every direction.
An ogre’s limbs went flying, while a Troll was engulfed in unquenchable flames before it had a chance to regenerate.
Boom!
Slash!
The head of a Lycanthrope baring its fangs exploded.
A Dullahan charged through the spray of foul-smelling brain matter, only to be cleaved in half with a single blow.
Its halberd found a new master and shot away with tremendous force, tearing through a Wyvern’s wing.
CRACKLE!
“Kyaaaaaaa!”
Thud-thud-thud!
Blood rained from the sky.
At the same moment, a streak of blue flame cut through the downpour.
Whoooooosh!
Slash!
A storm of blood erupted.
Whenever the flames streaked through the air, dozens of monsters fell and hundreds recoiled.
And the thousands of monsters...
At some point, they began to be overwhelmed.
They had grown afraid of a single human—and of the line of death he had drawn with a single spear.
“L-Lord.”
For the first time, the Death Knight’s flat, unwavering voice trembled with emotion.
The Black Knight knew perfectly well what his subordinate’s desperate plea meant.
“Make way.”
Between the slits of the deeply lowered helmet, red eyes flickered.
As he advanced, immense magical power rolling off him, he tried to ignore the strange words and scenes that kept surfacing in his mind.
Nothing could take precedence over his creator, his eternal lord.
“Are you listening, my servant?”
At his lord’s voice echoing like a hallucination, the Black Knight quietly replied,
“Yes, my lord.”
Until the very end, he failed to realize one thing.
That his hand was groping somewhere between the plates of his armor.

chapters.title: Chapter 399
paragraphs: Whoosh!
Nothing could stop the spearhead wreathed in Force—not leather that could deflect bullets, nor flesh and bone harder than steel.
Puh-puh-puk!
Big targets came with a bonus. The spearhead punched through the Lycanthrope’s chest and skewered the monsters packed close behind it like meat on a spit.
“Krrgh, k-kek.”
Its wide eyes held a mixture of confusion and indignation.
Its gaze seemed to protest: Why me, out of all these monsters? I never crossed the death line you drew.
“No.”
I quietly pulled on the shaft.
Scrape. The Lycanthrope’s claws raked across the ground as I dragged it over to my side of the spear.
“You crossed it. Just now.”
That was far enough. I yanked the spear free at lightning speed and swept it horizontally across the monsters before me.
Whoosh, KRAAAASH!
Blue flames scorched the air as they surged forward and swallowed the monsters.
Those still alive burned to death screaming, while those already turned undead crumbled to ash.
Ding. Ding. Ding...
System notifications announcing my kills rang out without pause.
How many had fallen to that single strike? Dozens? A hundred?
Rather than count them one by one, I chose to keep moving. My goal had never been to kill some fixed number of monsters.
Annihilation.
Humans and monsters had been locked in this fated struggle to kill or be killed for decades.
Only one species would be able to survive here today, and I would not be the one to fall.
Thud.
I stepped over the spear embedded deep in the concrete. At the same moment, countless monsters retreated as if by prior agreement.
One step. Two steps. Three.
No matter how far I walked, the distance between us did not shrink. For every step I took, they backed away by just as much.
“This is insane...”
Behind me, the Skeleton Warlord muttered as if groaning.
One human was overwhelming an army of thousands of monsters.
Even if this sight wasn’t enough to fill a page in human history, surely it deserved at least a paragraph.
“W-Where are you going?”
“Keep a good eye on those two. I’m not going far anyway.”
More precisely, there was no longer any need for me to go far.
The guest had already arrived. There was no reason to go out and meet him.
He’s finally here.
My guess had been right. The monster army parted left and right like the ebbing tide, revealing him in the distance atop a skeletal horse made entirely of black bones.
Clip-clop. Clip-clop.
He wore pitch-black full plate armor, and a vivid red glow shone beneath his low-set helmet.
He was far smaller than a large monster like an ogre, but the mana pouring from him was immense and powerful.
System Lv. 135 Death Knight Lord
Level 135. It was a number I had never seen on any monster I had faced before.
As the Death Knight Lord approached, slowly gathering speed, a thought occurred to me.
Can I defeat him?
My battle with the Western Heaven Demon Lord in Murim had been a desperate struggle with my life on the line.

If the Western Heaven Demon Lord had intended to eliminate me from the very beginning, if the Heavenly Power Demon had not passed his internal energy to me, if I had not experienced that miraculous recovery from leveling up, if Jeok Cheongang had not awakened and saved me at the critical moment, I would have died three or four times over.
But in the end, I had survived—and grown stronger.
That was when a question had begun circling endlessly through my mind.
How strong am I now?
The System said my martial arts realm and stats had risen.
I had distributed my stats and fought battles just as I always had, but aside from gaining Force, I wasn’t sure what had changed.
I had no real sense of how much stronger I had become.
At some point, it had all become easy and natural.
And now—
Clatter, thud-thud-thud!
As I watched the Death Knight Lord shoot toward me like a gust of wind, I realized the answer.
The immense mana cascading from his body like a waterfall did not shake me in the slightest. That alone told me.
I am...
Whoooooosh!
The wind vanished, replaced by a flash of light. The Death Knight Lord and his skeletal horse charged as one, and the sword in his hand moved.
Dense darkness gathered around the blade and came crashing down, yet the sight unfolded so slowly before my eyes that a single certainty surfaced in my mind.
I am stronger than anyone else on this battlefield.
In that slowed-down world, I thrust out White Flame.
Blue-white flames surged along the spearhead and devoured the darkness.
A roar like the sky splitting apart rang out.
KRAAAASH!
The ground within a radius of several hundred meters caved in, and the hospital that had stood firm for decades collapsed.
Compressed air erupted in layer after layer like a sonic boom, battering and hurling away everything around them.
And at the center of it all stood two beings whom no one else could approach.
Whoosh, whoosh-whoosh-whoosh! KABOOM!
Several times—perhaps dozens—in the blink of an eye.
Whenever blue-white flames and pitch-black darkness collided and mingled, deafening roars and devastating destruction followed.
No human or monster could see the movements of the two beings.
They existed on another level, clashing within a world and time all their own.
Swish!
The silver-white spear in Jin Taekyung’s hand slashed down through empty space.
Blue-white flames tore through space as they poured downward. But the Black Knight did not retreat. He swung his sword.
KABOOM!
The instant the surging mana collided with the flames, the tremendous pressure shattered the Black Knight’s skeletal horse.
But the erasure of Nightmare—his loyal steed and an A-rank monster—was nothing compared to what came next.
Whoooooosh!
A thrown spear with no preparatory motion whatsoever—a veritable flash of light.
The Black Knight twisted aside on instinct. Tremendous heat grazed his chest and tore into the ranks of monsters behind him.
KRAKAKAK! KABOOM!
The spearhead punched through dozens of monsters before slamming into the ground, where it blasted out a massive crater with a thunderous roar.
Before the monsters caught in the aftermath could even scream in terror, Jin Taekyung was already moving toward the Black Knight.
Sshk.
A single step, without sound or presence.
By the time the Black Knight noticed, Jin Taekyung had erased the dozens of meters between them and reached his target. A fist shot toward the Black Knight’s chest.
“Get lost.”
Boom!
Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist. Heat hotter than lava slammed into the armor.

The Black Knight was hurled away at tremendous speed, but he flipped in midair and righted himself. At the same time, his hand tightened around his sword hilt and swept the blade out with tremendous force.
Whoooooosh! Shh-shh-shhk!
Black mana became dozens of lightning bolts that shot toward Jin Taekyung. Each one possessed earth-shaking power.
But Jin Taekyung was already gone.
KRAKABOOM!
Jin Taekyung burst through the cloud of pale dust and extended both hands.
The sword had already changed direction and was slashing down toward the crown of his head, but he caught the blade between his palms as if clasping his hands in prayer.
Empty-Hand Seizes the Blade.
His hands, wreathed in blue flames, and the blade, laden with immense mana, trembled between the two beings.
One blocking. The other pressing forward.
Their fierce deadlock brought the relentless exchange to a momentary halt—until an unexpected intruder broke it.
“You! Human!”
A Death Knight appeared with a shout and brought its mace down toward Jin Taekyung’s back.
Boom!
The Death Knight never even realized when or how it died.
Jin Taekyung’s heel sliced through the air like a blade and blew its head apart, helmet and all.
Thud.
Yet futile though its erasure had been, the attack was not entirely meaningless.
The Black Knight’s red eyes flashed, and the sword in his grasp unleashed more mana than ever before.
The tiniest of openings.
The instant in which Jin Taekyung diverted his internal energy to kill the Death Knight was enough to shatter the balance.
Crunch! Slash!
Blood sprayed into the air.
It was endlessly red—human blood, proof that the Black Knight’s sword had cut across Jin Taekyung’s chest.
A single certainty flashed through the Black Knight’s mind.
It’s over.
Then, in the next instant, Jin Taekyung’s flame-wreathed fist slammed into the Black Knight’s side.
Crack!
The Death Knight Lord’s body jerked.
Like any undead monster incapable of feeling pain, he made no sound, but I could read the question in the red glow visible through the slits of his helmet.
How?
Yeah. That was exactly what his eyes were asking.
I answered flatly.
“You think you’re the only one with armor?”
Boom!
This time, it was the Flame Divine Palm.
Already cracked from the repeated blows, the Death Knight Lord’s armor shattered into fragments.
“That hurt, you son of a bitch.”
Crack!
I seized his gauntleted wrist, twisted it, and snapped it.
I had no idea how much attacks like these mattered against an undead monster, but it was enough to make him drop his sword.
Clank.
The moment the sword hit the ground, the Death Knight Lord was met with a merciless barrage.
Boom! Crack! Bam!
I planted my foot on his instep and unleashed punch after punch.
Shoulder. Arm. Side. Chest.
The Death Knight Lord took dozens of blows in the blink of an eye. He tried to counterattack, but it didn’t matter.
Thud!
“Don’t look so surprised. My armor’s pretty useful too.”
I had the Fire Dragon Armor.
Never thought I’d use it here.
The Fire Dragon Armor was a divine weapon I had obtained after defeating the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
It had been so severely damaged during the battle in Murim that it was still repairing itself, but even at a restoration rate of roughly fifty percent, it had done its job admirably.
Though I nearly died because it couldn’t block the strike completely.
My vision had swum when the sword cut me.
But I had suffered this much pain more times than I cared to remember.
Besides, it was nothing compared to the pain endured by those who had died before me.
“This is...for the people you killed today.”
I put all my strength into a punch and drove it into his face.
A Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist at the eighth level smashed apart the helmet that had withstood everything, revealing his face.
The balance had tipped. One blow. One final strike would be enough to take his life.
“And this is...”
At that moment, my raised fist stopped dead.
I blinked through eyelids clotted with blood. For just an instant, time seemed to stop when my gaze landed on someone’s face.
It was unfamiliar, yet familiar.
With deathly white skin and glowing red eyes, he looked exactly like a certain hero I had seen in a holographic video.
“...Lei Fei?”

My armor’s pretty useful too.”
I had the Fire Dragon Armor.
Never thought I’d use it here.
The Fire Dragon Armor was a divine weapon I had obtained after defeating the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
It had been so severely damaged during the battle in Murim that it was still repairing itself, but even at a restoration rate of roughly fifty percent, it had done its job admirably.
Though I nearly died because it couldn’t block the strike completely.
My vision had swum when the sword cut me.
But I had suffered this much pain more times than I cared to remember.
Besides, it was nothing compared to the pain endured by those who had died before me.
“This is...for the people you killed today.”
I put all my strength into a punch and drove it into his face.
A Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist at the eighth level smashed apart the helmet that had withstood everything, revealing his face.
The balance had tipped.
One blow.
One final strike would be enough to take his life.
“And this is...”
At that moment, my raised fist stopped dead.
I blinked through eyelids clotted with blood.
For just an instant, time seemed to stop when my gaze landed on someone’s face.
It was unfamiliar, yet familiar.
With deathly white skin and glowing red eyes, he looked exactly like a certain hero I had seen in a holographic video.
“...Lei Fei?”

chapters.title: Chapter 400
paragraphs: The moment he first clashed with Jin Taekyung, the black knight knew instinctively.
He’s strong.
The young human before him was extraordinarily powerful. Even if the black knight fought with everything he had, victory was far from certain. His opponent might even be stronger than he was.
As the battle seesawed back and forth, that conviction only deepened.
This will be a difficult fight.
But the black knight neither feared him nor retreated.
He was his lord’s most loyal servant, charged with carrying out his commands.
This was a battle between warriors who had transcended their limits. Even the slightest difference could decide the outcome.
If I don’t give up, an opportunity will come.
The black knight knew that well.
He had repeated those words to himself ever since his childhood training. By surviving countless battles, he had grown into a mighty warrior.
Confusion struck again. The moment his thoughts faltered, his movements became erratic.
And his opponent was neither weak nor careless enough to let such an opening pass.
Whoosh! Slash!
The spearhead tore through dead flesh.
Boom!
Blue flames slammed into his chest.
Amid the almost tangible heat, the black knight suddenly felt something.
Pain.
What is this...?
What unsettled him was not that he could feel pain, but that a sensation which should have been utterly foreign felt so terribly familiar.
What are these memories...?
His chest throbbed. His head pounded.
As the black knight staggered beneath the relentless barrage, memories belonging to someone he could not identify flashed rapidly before his eyes.
Th-This can’t be!
“His mana adaptability is incredible. It’s the highest figure we’ve ever recorded!”
“He must be enrolled in the Zhonghua Development Training program immediately!”
Humans dressed in dazzling white clothes chattered excitedly. Among them stood a middle-aged man in a dark, sharply tailored uniform.
“Zhonghua Development Training? You intend to raise that child as a Hunter?”
“Of course. He is only thirteen, yet his mana adaptability is comparable to Faye Chen’s. He has more than enough potential to become an S-rank Hunter—the greatest Hunter in our nation!”
“I refuse.”
“Pardon?”
“No, Comrade Lieutenant General. What do you mean? This child...”
“Enough.”
The middle-aged man continued in a subdued voice.
“He is my only nephew. I promised my sister I would make him happy, not turn him into a Hunter and put him in danger.”
“Being a Hunter is a noble calling. If that child becomes an S-rank Hunter, it will be a blessing to all our people!”
“I know how noble their work is. But that was how my brother-in-law...”
The middle-aged man suddenly stopped and shook his head.
“Nothing you say will change my mind. If not for the directive from above, I would never have allowed him to be tested. We’re leaving. The rest is up to you.”
“Comrade Lieutenant General! Comrade Lieutenant General!”
Leaving the shouts behind him, the middle-aged man strode over, forced a smile, and held out his hand.
“You’ve been waiting a long time, haven’t you? Come on. Let’s go.”
The black knight—or rather, the person whose memories these seemed to be—took the middle-aged man’s hand.
His own hand was small and pale.
Then a child’s clear voice rang out.
“Uncle.”
“Yes?”
“I... I want to become a Hunter.”
A host of emotions crossed the middle-aged man’s face.
He stared at the child for a long time, biting his lip. When he finally released a troubled sigh, the others approached with markedly brighter expressions.
“Zhonghua Development Training is a project we designed with the utmost care. Its safety measures are rigorous, and its effectiveness is proven. Wu Heixing is the same age, and he’s doing well.”
“If the child changes his mind, we’ll stop the training at any time.”
The oldest-looking man placed a hand on the middle-aged man’s shoulder.
“Please trust us and leave him in our care, Comrade Lieutenant General Wei Fenghu.”
Wei Fenghu. Wei Fenghu...
The name echoed endlessly through the black knight’s mind.
It was so familiar.
He had missed it so much.
Boom!
Did his chest ache because of the blow he had taken, or was there another reason?
As the staggering black knight stared ahead, more memories appeared before his eyes.
“You think you’re the best just because the adults praise you?”
A boy in a bow tie and black suit glared at him with sharp eyes. His polished shoes gleamed.
“Don’t get the wrong idea. I’m the best. You’re second!”
The black knight’s vision tilted to one side, and then an innocent voice rang out.
“Okay. Let’s do that, then.”
“What?”
“I don’t mind being second. Third is fine too, and I wouldn’t care if I came in last.”
The sharp-featured boy’s mouth fell open.
“Are you stupid? You want to be even worse than Zhang Wei, the lowest-ranked trainee in the whole training camp?”
“But Zhang Wei is kind, and he’s always helping others. He’ll become a great Hunter.”
“Y-You’re making fun of me, aren’t you?”
“Huh? No. I just meant that if that’s what you want, then I’m fine with—ah!”
Crash!
It took only an instant to subdue the boy who had suddenly lunged at him. Pinned beneath him, the boy thrashed and shouted.
“I’m the best! Wu Heixing is the best at everything!”
As one memory faded, another surfaced, as though someone were tossing stones one after another into a still pond.
The memories of that unknown person continued to throw the black knight’s mind into confusion.
“Top trainee, , step forward.”
A small number of people filled a vast space.
For some reason, he could not make out the name being called, but his body moved on its own.
Step. Step.
His disciplined strides were long, and his vantage point was much higher.
He had grown into a young man. An older man in uniform approached and pinned a medal to his chest.
It was a familiar face—the same man from the first memory. He leaned closer and whispered.
“Are you certain you won’t regret this?”
“I have no regrets. I never have, and I never will.”
“Most people will never know you exist. You may have to spend your entire life in the shadows.”
“I was taught that a Hunter is also a guardian. Remaining unseen does not diminish my honor.”
“There is something I have not been able to tell you until now.”
The older man’s grip tightened on his shoulder.
“I’m proud of you. Thank you for growing into such a fine man.”
“Thank you, Uncle. No... Father.”
The older man smiled brightly, his eyes glistening with tears.
The instant a single tear rolled down his wrinkled cheek and struck the platform, another memory surfaced.
“Hello? Is anyone here?”
The place he visited on that warm spring day was a small flower shop. As he looked around at the vibrant flowers and peered farther inside, she approached him.
“Welcome!”
Her steps were light and buoyant, her eyes prim and feline.
Her voice was so cheerful and bright.
And she was so beautiful...
The black knight—or rather, a man who had passed through his youthful years and grown more mature—felt his heart pound.
“Are you a customer?”
“N-No, I... I came to buy some fl-flowers.”
“For your parents? Or your girlfriend?”
“My parents. Strictly speaking, they aren’t my parents. It’s my uncle who raised me...”
“I see. You speak so formally, though. Are you a soldier?”
“S-Something like that.”
It was a strange memory. His words kept breaking off, and everything before his eyes repeatedly turned white.
When he came to his senses, he was walking dazedly into a hospital room with a bright bouquet in his arms.
“You fool. I told you there was no need to come when it’s only mild pneumonia... What’s that?”
At Wei Fenghu’s question, he answered blankly.
“Flowers.”
“Is that a get-well gift?”
“Yes.”
“So you bought me chrysanthemums as a get-well gift?”
“Yes... Huh?”
“You ungrateful brat! Hey, you!”
Smack! Smack!
The man laughed even as he was beaten with the bouquet. A quiet laugh escaped him at his own stupidity, and he could not help laughing because she looked like chrysanthemums.
After that, the memories sped by.
He visited the flower shop every day.
“H-Hello!”
“Welcome—oh, you’re back again?”
“Haha.”
“Chrysanthemums, right? The pure white ones.”
Spring, summer, autumn, winter.
By the time all four seasons had passed, they were no longer merely a flower-shop owner and her customer.
“I have something to tell you.”
“What is it?”
“Will you marry me?”
“I’ll make you happy.”
Of all the memories he had seen, that one lasted the longest.
After a silence so long that a single second felt like ten years, or even a hundred, she finally opened her mouth.
“I have something to tell you too.”
“No, before that, give me your answer...”
“I’m pregnant.”
“What?”
Thump. Thump-thump. Thump-thump-thump!
The man’s heart hammered wildly, and the black knight writhed in agony.
“Aaah... Aaaaaah!”
His head hurt as if it were splitting apart, and it felt as though someone were wringing out his insides with their hands.
Along with pain beyond anything he had ever imagined, another memory forced its way into the empty space.
“Waaah! Waaah!”
“Th-This child...”
“Congratulations on becoming a father, honey.”
The birth of a new life.
And its growth.
“Dada. Dada-da!”
“Honey, honey! Did you hear that? Our baby’s already saying ‘Dada.’ Could our baby be a genius?”
“Could you change the diaper?”
“Wait. Let me hear it one more time.”
“Dada! Momma!”
“Hahaha! That’s right! We’re your daddy and mommy!”
The day the baby, bundled in a swaddling cloth and squirming helplessly, succeeded in rolling over.
The day she first crawled on all fours.
The day she took her first steps...
The man was as happy as if the entire world belonged to him.
But it did not take long for those dreamlike days to become a nightmare.
“The magical power level in Gaoping District has spiked!”
“Gaoping District? Keep trying to contact them, and mobilize and deploy the Second Regiment as a precaution.”
“D-Director, we’ve lost communications.”
“What?”
Disaster struck without warning.
The man hurriedly assembled the forces under his command and headed for the source, only to find an unbelievable sight awaiting him.
“Kyaaaaaaa!”
“E-Everyone, run—guh!”
Crunch! KABOOM!
Flames billowed into the sky above the once-peaceful city, while countless monsters slaughtered people on the ground.
Before that unbelievable scene of carnage, in a land overflowing with screams and death, the man drew his sword.
“Public Security Armed Forces Department!”
Zzzzt!
An aura blade surged around his sword, shining brilliantly.
More than a thousand Hunters answered his cry with a deafening roar.
They were humanity’s shield and guardians.
They could not retreat a single step.
“Wipe them all out!”
“Waaaah! Long live the People’s Republic of China!”
With the Five-Starred Red Flag emblazoned on their armor, they surged forward like a wave—only to break apart in sprays of blood instead of white foam.
“Perish in the flames of hellfire. Fire Rain.”
Kiiiiing.
The ash-gray sky opened its maw.
Beneath the falling rain of fire, the man thought of his beloved wife and five-year-old daughter.
And then he came face-to-face with that being.
“If you had run, you could have lived.”
“I’ll kill you.”
“How noble. What is your name, human?”
“...Lei Fei?”
At the sound of Jin Taekyung’s voice, the black knight’s body went rigid.
The dam burst, and everything began to reassemble.
Thirty-six years of memories from his life as a human crashed over him like a tidal wave, blotting out his vision.
—I am... I am...
What in the world was he?
As the black knight trembled in confusion and pain, a thunderous voice rang through his mind.
—You are my most loyal servant and the supreme commander of my legion. Your lord commands you: fulfill your duty until you crumble into ash!
It was a word of power he could not resist.
The red light in his eyes, wavering like a candle in the wind, suddenly blazed.
The black knight—no, Lei Fei—had fallen with only one strike left to finish him.
Now tremendous magical power erupted from his entire body.
KRAAAAAASH!
